Table: value provided → server MUST validate header matches body; value null / not in arguments → server MUST NOT expect the header; client omits header but value is in body → server MUST reject. Note: "servers SHOULD compare the header value and the body value numerically" for integers. Unrecognized Mcp-Param-* headers: "MUST forward it and otherwise ignore it".

"Header names ... are case-insensitive. Clients and servers MUST use case-insensitive comparisons for header names. Header values (such as method names) are case-sensitive." SEP-2243 tests: 'mcp-method: tools/call' MUST accept; 'Mcp-Method: TOOLS/CALL' MUST reject; 'Mcp-Name:  foo ' MUST accept (trim whitespace).

Modern-only server receiving legacy traffic: "HTTP GET or DELETE to the MCP endpoint: respond with 405 Method Not Allowed. An Mcp-Session-Id header on a request: ignore it, and do not mint or echo session IDs. A Last-Event-ID header: ignore it; streams are not resumable." Dual-era: "Servers and clients that need to interoperate with counterparts speaking those protocol versions implement the behavior described in the corresponding revision ... in addition to the version-negotiation fallback described above."

Era detection contract (server side of the client rule): on 400 the client inspects the body; "If the body contains a recognized modern JSON-RPC error, the server speaks a modern version ... If the body is empty or is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error, fall back to initialize." Hence every 400 a dual-era server returns to a modern request MUST carry the JSON-RPC error body (-32020/-32021/-32022/-32602), otherwise dual-era clients will misdetect the server as legacy. Also for 404: "The JSON-RPC error body distinguishes this case from a 404 returned by a legacy HTTP+SSE server".
requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx §Backward Compatibility; §Protocol Version Header; docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning.mdx §Backward Compatibility with Initialization-Based Versions and §Compatibility Matrix

requirements.text: Dual-era server selection: "A dual-era server selects its behavior from how the client opens: A request carrying modern per-request _meta is served statelessly according to this revision. An initialize request selects legacy semantics, scoped to ... the session (HTTP), as specified by the negotiated legacy protocol version. A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently on the same endpoint or process."

HTTP status mapping for per-request metadata errors: "A request missing any required field [io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities] is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request." and MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021): "On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request."

Legacy GET: "The server MUST either return Content-Type: text/event-stream in response to this HTTP GET, or else return HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed, indicating that the server does not offer an SSE stream at this endpoint." If a stream is opened: "The server MUST NOT send a JSON-RPC response on the stream unless resuming"; "The server MAY close the SSE stream at any time."
requirements.source: docs/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports.mdx §Listening for Messages from the Server items 3-4; 2025-11-25 same

requirements.text: Legacy sessions: server "MAY assign a session ID at initialization time, by including it in an Mcp-Session-Id header on the HTTP response containing the InitializeResult"; "The session ID MUST only contain visible ASCII characters (0x21 to 0x7E)"; "Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an Mcp-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400"; "The server MAY terminate the session at any time, after which it MUST respond to requests containing that session ID with HTTP 404 Not Found"; client on 404 "MUST start a new session"; DELETE: "The server MAY respond to this request with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed".

Legacy SSE event IDs: "Servers MAY attach an id field to their SSE events ... If present, the ID MUST be globally unique across all streams within that session—or all streams with that specific client, if session management is not in use." "The server MUST NOT replay messages that would have been delivered on a different stream." 2025-11-25 adds: "The server SHOULD immediately send an SSE event consisting of an event ID and an empty data field in order to prime the client to reconnect" and "If the server does close the connection prior to terminating the SSE stream, it SHOULD send an SSE event with a standard retry field before closing".
requirements.source: docs/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports.mdx §Resumability and Redelivery; docs/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports.mdx §Sending Messages to the Server item 6 and §Resumability and Redelivery

requirements.text: "The server MUST send each of its JSON-RPC messages on only one of the connected streams; that is, it MUST NOT broadcast the same message across multiple streams."

Long-lived subscription streams over HTTP: "The server MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message ... and MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before it." Stream ends when "The client cancels it — close the SSE stream (HTTP)"; server teardown: "it SHOULD send a successful subscriptions/listen response to signal a graceful end ... then close the stream." Cancellation page: "A server MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing a subscriptions/listen request ID when it tears down that subscription stream ... Servers MUST NOT send notifications/cancelled for any other purpose." Logging: request-scoped notifications/message "MUST NOT be sent on the listen stream or on any stream other than the one carrying the response to the request".
403 body for invalid Origin "MAY comprise a JSON-RPC error response that has no id"; non-accepted notification error body "MAY comprise a JSON-RPC error response that has no id".

Deprecated HTTP+SSE (2024-11-05) transport: "New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it" — a dual-era server is not required to host the old SSE/POST endpoint pair; supporting it is only 'should' guidance for servers 'wanting to support older clients'.

gaps.title: Origin validation is skipped when CORS is disabled or AllowedOrigins='*'
gaps.current: VerifyAndSetCORSHeaders exits immediately when not FSettings.CorsEnabled (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:221-222) and only compares the Origin when FSettings.CorsAllowedOrigins <> '*' (line 227). With [CORS] Enabled=0, or AllowedOrigins=*, any browser Origin is accepted (line 257 even emits Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). Matching is exact-string SameText (line 236), so 'http://localhost' does not match 'http://localhost:5173'.
gaps.required: HTTP-02: Origin MUST be validated on all incoming connections; present-and-invalid → 403 (both eras). Validation is a security control independent of whether CORS response headers are emitted.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: none (non-browser clients send no Origin; absent Origin stays allowed). Library consumers: TMCPSettings gains new properties; existing CorsEnabled/CorsAllowedOrigins keep compiling. Operators who set Enabled=0 to 'turn off security' will now get 403 for browser origins not in the list — document; keep AllowedOrigins=* as the explicit opt-out.
gaps.suggestedChange: Split the two concerns in TMCPIdHTTPServer: (1) new function ValidateOrigin(RequestInfo, ResponseInfo): Boolean that always runs (before the endpoint check, as now) — if RawHeaders.Values['Origin'] <> '' and not IsOriginAllowed(Origin) then ResponseNo := 403, ContentType application/json, body '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Origin not allowed"}}' (HTTP-36), Exit False; (2) SetCORSHeaders only when CorsEnabled. Add TMCPSettings.AllowedOrigins ([Security] AllowedOrigins, default 'http://localhost,http://127.0.0.1,https://localhost,https://127.0.0.1' + allow wildcard-port patterns like 'http://localhost:*'), keep CorsAllowedOrigins as an alias that reads the same value for backwards compatibility. IsOriginAllowed: parse scheme://host[:port], compare scheme+host case-insensitively, port exact or '*'. Add 'Vary: Origin' when echoing a specific origin.

gaps.title: MCP-Protocol-Version header is never read; no era/version classification, no 400/-32022
gaps.current: The only occurrence of the header name is in the CORS Allow-Headers list (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:259-260). HandlePostRequest (lines 316-362) never inspects MCP-Protocol-Version nor params._meta; every request is processed identically regardless of version. MCPServer.Types.pas:11 hard-codes MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-06-18' and CoreManager.Initialize (src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:101) always returns it.
gaps.required: Modern: header MUST be present and MUST equal _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] (else 400 + -32020); unsupported version → 400 + -32022 with data.supported/requested. Legacy: invalid/unsupported header → 400; absent header → assume 2025-03-26 (SHOULD legacy / MAY modern-dual-era). Dual-era: a request carrying modern _meta is served statelessly; initialize selects legacy semantics.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: unchanged behaviour when they send a supported legacy version or no header; clients sending an unknown version now get 400 (spec-required). Library consumers: keep MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant (semantics: default legacy negotiated version) and add MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION / MCP_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS; TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest(string,string) retained as a thin overload so TMCPStdioTransport and third-party callers compile unchanged.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add to MCPServer.Types.pas: const MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2026-07-28'; MCP_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS: array[0..3] of string = ('2026-07-28','2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26'); MCP_HEADER_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 'MCP-Protocol-Version'; MCP_ERR_HEADER_MISMATCH = -32020; MCP_ERR_MISSING_CLIENT_CAPABILITY = -32021; MCP_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION = -32022; type TMCPProtocolEra = (peLegacy, peModern); TMCPRequestContext = record ProtocolVersion: string; Era: TMCPProtocolEra; SessionID: string; end. In TMCPIdHTTPServer add function ClassifyRequest(RequestInfo; Body: TJSONObject; out Ctx: TMCPRequestContext; out ErrorJSON: string; out HttpStatus: Integer): Boolean implementing: Header := Trim(RequestInfo.RawHeaders.Values[MCP_HEADER_PROTOCOL_VERSION]); MetaVersion := Body.params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] (if present). If Header = '' then: if MetaVersion <> '' → 400, -32020 'required header MCP-Protocol-Version missing' else Ctx.ProtocolVersion := '2025-03-26', Era := peLegacy. Else if Header not in MCP_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS → 400 + -32022 with data {supported:[...], requested: Header} (valid for both eras; legacy MUST 400, body allowed). Else if Header >= '2026-07-28' (string compare of ISO dates works) → Era := peModern; if MetaVersion <> Header → 400 + -32020. Else Era := peLegacy (ignore _meta). Make the supported list configurable via TMCPSettings.SupportedProtocolVersions ([Protocol] SupportedVersions=...) so operators can pin legacy-only or modern-only. Add ProcessRequest overload: function ProcessRequest(Request: TJSONObject; const Ctx: TMCPRequestContext; out ErrorCode: Integer): string; old overload calls it with a legacy context.

gaps.title: No validation of Mcp-Method / Mcp-Name standard headers (no -32020 path, no Base64 sentinel decoding)
gaps.current: Neither 'Mcp-Method' nor 'Mcp-Name' appears anywhere in src (grep); HandlePostRequest goes straight from Accept sniffing to FJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:337-357). No -32020 constant exists (only -32700..-32603 at lines 95-99 and JsonRpcProcessor.pas:28-32).
gaps.required: Modern requests: Mcp-Method REQUIRED and MUST equal body.method (case-sensitive); Mcp-Name REQUIRED for tools/call & prompts/get (= params.name) and resources/read (= params.uri); values may be '=?base64?...?=' encoded and MUST be decoded (UTF-8) before comparison; invalid Base64 / invalid characters / missing / mismatch → 400 + JSON-RPC error -32020 with the request id. Header-name lookup case-insensitive; trim surrounding whitespace. Not required on notifications or on legacy-era requests.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: unaffected (validation only runs when Era = peModern). Modern SDK clients already send these headers. Library consumers: none (transport-internal); custom managers/tools unchanged.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit src/Server/MCPServer.HttpHeaders.pas (pure functions, unit-testable): function DecodeMcpHeaderValue(const Raw: string; out Value: string; out Err: string): Boolean — Trim; if starts with '=?base64?' and ends with '?=' (case-sensitive) then strict-validate payload (chars [A-Za-z0-9+/], '=' padding only at end, Length mod 4 = 0; do NOT rely on TNetEncoding.Base64 leniency — check before calling TNetEncoding.Base64.DecodeStringToBytes, then TEncoding.UTF8.GetString) else verify every char is 0x20-0x7E or #9 (otherwise Err 'invalid characters'). function ValidateStandardHeaders(RequestInfo: TIdHTTPRequestInfo; Body: TJSONObject; out Err: string): Boolean: Method := Body.GetValue<string>('method'); McpMethod := RequestInfo.RawHeaders.Values['Mcp-Method'] (Indy TIdHeaderList name lookup is case-insensitive — verify with a 'mcp-method' test); missing → Err; Trim(McpMethod) <> Method → Err. If Method in ['tools/call','prompts/get'] then Expected := params.name; if 'resources/read' then Expected := params.uri; when Expected applies: header missing → Err; DecodeMcpHeaderValue fails → Err; decoded <> Expected → Err. In HandlePostRequest, on Err: ResponseNo := 400; ContentType application/json; body := TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.CreateErrorResponse(id, -32020, 'Header mismatch: ' + Err) (make CreateErrorResponse public/class). Run these checks only for requests (has id) with Ctx.Era = peModern; for notifications validate Mcp-Method only if present.

gaps.title: HTTP status is always 200 for JSON-RPC errors; unknown method must be 404, meta/capability/parse errors 400; method-not-found detection is a fragile string heuristic
gaps.current: HandlePostRequestJSON sets ResponseNo := 200 unconditionally (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:553) and HandlePostRequestSSE likewise (line 509). Unparseable bodies also yield 200 with a -32700 body (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:212-217 via HTTP path). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor maps exceptions to -32601 by Pos('not found', E.Message) (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215) — any tool raising e.g. 'File not found' becomes method-not-found; ExecuteMethodCall raises a plain Exception (line 123).
gaps.required: Modern: unknown RPC method → 404 + -32601; missing required _meta fields → 400 + -32602; -32021 → 400; header validation → 400 + -32020; unsupported version → 400 + -32022; every such 4xx MUST carry the JSON-RPC error body (era detection). Both eras: a notification the server cannot accept → HTTP error status (400). Legacy: keep 200 for -32601 (a 404 would be read by legacy clients as 'session terminated' per HTTP-32 and trigger re-initialize).
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: no change (status mapping applied only when Era = peModern, except 400 for unparseable bodies which the legacy spec also allows). Library consumers: introduce EMCPError(Code, Message, Data) in MCPServer.Types; existing custom managers that raise plain Exception keep working (mapped to -32603 as today, but no longer accidentally -32601 when the message contains 'not found' — behaviour change to document). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest(string,string) signature retained.
gaps.suggestedChange: MCPServer.Types.pas: EMCPError = class(Exception) Code: Integer; Data: TJSONObject; end; EMCPMethodNotFound = class(EMCPError). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ExecuteMethodCall raises EMCPMethodNotFound.Create(-32601, ...). ProcessRequest(TJSONObject, Ctx, out ErrorCode) sets ErrorCode from EMCPError.Code (0 on success, -32603 for other exceptions) and includes E.Data as error.data when assigned (needed for -32022 supported/requested and -32021 requiredCapabilities). TMCPIdHTTPServer.HttpStatusForError(Ctx, Code): Integer := case Code of -32601: if Era=peModern then 404 else 200; -32020,-32021,-32022,-32700,-32600: 400; -32602: 400 when the error originated from _meta validation (raise EMCPError with a flag/HttpStatus field so the processor can say '400'), else 200; else 200. Give EMCPError an optional HttpStatus property so any layer can pin the status. Also set ResponseNo := 400 for -32700 parse errors and for array bodies outside 2025-03-26 (-32600).

gaps.title: 202 'with no body' is not guaranteed under Indy (default HTML body) and notifications are never dispatched to managers
gaps.current: HandlePostRequest sets ResponseNo := 202 and returns without setting ContentText/ContentLength (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:343-352). Indy's TIdHTTPResponseInfo generates a default '202 Accepted' body when both ContentText and ContentStream are empty (behaviour of IdCustomHTTPServer WriteHeader/WriteContent — Indy sources are not present in this container, verify with curl -i). The same applies to the empty SSE bodies at lines 294 and 506 and the 204 at line 526. Additionally the notification is never passed to FJsonRpcProcessor (Exit at line 351), and JsonRpcProcessor itself also drops notifications before dispatch (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:174-181), so IMCPCapabilityManager.HandlesMethod('notifications/...') implementations (e.g. CoreManager.pas:51,59) are dead code on both transports.
gaps.required: HTTP-05: accepted notification → 202 with no body (both eras). Legacy notifications/cancelled and notifications/initialized should at least reach the managers so a dual-era server can track legacy session state or honour cancellation (SHOULD, may be ignored).
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: strictly better (clean 202). Library consumers: custom managers start receiving notifications via ExecuteMethod (return value ignored) — a manager that raises on unknown notifications would now log an error instead of nothing; document. No signature changes.
gaps.suggestedChange: For 202/204 responses set ResponseInfo.ContentLength := 0 and ResponseInfo.ContentText := '' explicitly (and ContentType := ''), then verify with curl that the body is empty; if Indy still emits the HTML page, call ResponseInfo.WriteHeader manually after setting ContentLength := 0 so WriteContent is skipped. Dispatch notifications: in HandlePostRequest call FJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessNotification(Body, Ctx) (new method that finds the manager via GetManagerForMethod and calls ExecuteMethod inside try/except with TLogger.Error) before returning 202; only return an HTTP error (400 + JSON-RPC error without id) when the body is not a valid JSON-RPC message.

gaps.title: GET handling: returns 200 JSON 'endpoint info' (neither SSE nor 405) and an empty immediately-closed SSE stream
gaps.current: HandleGetRequest (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:271-314): if Accept contains text/event-stream → 200 text/event-stream with ContentText '' (lines 283-299, plus echo of Mcp-Session-Id at 289-291); otherwise 200 application/json '{"url":..., "transport":...}' (lines 303-313). Modern spec removed the GET stream entirely; the changelog (item 4, item 9) removed GET and Last-Event-ID.
gaps.required: Modern: GET → 405 (SHOULD). Legacy: server MUST either return text/event-stream or 405 — a 200 JSON body violates the legacy MUST. Since 405 is permitted in every revision, a dual-era server can answer 405 unconditionally; legacy SDK clients (TS/Python StreamableHTTP client) treat 405 on GET as 'server offers no standalone stream' and continue.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: 405 is explicitly allowed; clients that currently open the empty stream keep working (they handle 405). The non-standard 'endpoint info' JSON disappears from the MCP endpoint — if anyone relied on it (README does not document it), expose it on a different path (e.g. GET /) or a Settings flag. Library consumers: none.
gaps.suggestedChange: Replace HandleGetRequest body with: ResponseInfo.ResponseNo := 405; ResponseInfo.CustomHeaders.Values['Allow'] := 'POST, OPTIONS'; ContentLength := 0. Same for DELETE (currently the else branch at lines 200-204) — add the Allow header (RFC 9110 requires it on 405). Optionally keep a TMCPSettings.LegacyGetStream: Boolean (default False) that restores the old 'open SSE and close immediately' answer for legacy Accept: text/event-stream GETs; when enabled, do not echo Mcp-Session-Id for modern-era requests. Remove the endpoint-info JSON or move it to a non-MCP path such as '/' guarded by the same Origin check.

gaps.title: SSE responses are buffered (ContentText set once): no incremental streaming, no keep-alive comments, no disconnect-as-cancellation, no long-lived subscriptions/listen stream, Stop() cannot close open streams
gaps.current: HandlePostRequestSSE computes the full response first (FJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest at src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:488) and assigns one string to ResponseInfo.ContentText (line 501); Indy writes it with Content-Length after the handler returns. Nothing can be written to the client while a tool executes; there is no hook for notifications/progress or notifications/message; the connection thread has no way to detect client disconnect (no IOHandler access — Context is not passed to HandlePostRequest*, line 53-55); Stop() (lines 162-170) simply sets Active := False, which would block on any long-lived handler thread. The SSE event format itself is fine ('event: message', 'data: ', LF LF at lines 101-105, 495-499).
gaps.required: HTTP-10/11: notifications related to the request may precede the final response on the same stream; final response terminates the stream. HTTP-14 (MUST): client closing the stream = cancellation; server SHOULD stop work and MUST NOT send further messages. HTTP-35: subscriptions/listen stream stays open, acknowledged first, graceful completion result on shutdown. HTTP-12/13: X-Accel-Buffering: no (already set) and periodic ':' keep-alive comments. Legacy HTTP-15: disconnect is NOT cancellation (era-dependent).
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: unaffected for plain requests (JSON responses recommended by default; SSE only when streaming is needed). Library consumers: IMCPTool.Execute / IMCPResource.Read / IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod signatures unchanged; streaming is exposed through an ambient, optional TMCPRequestContext.Current (threadvar) with SendNotification/IsCancelled/CheckCancelled, so existing tools compile and run as before and new tools opt in. SSE responses use Connection: close, which drops HTTP keep-alive for streamed responses only.
gaps.suggestedChange: Pass Context: TIdContext into HandlePostRequest/HandlePostRequestSSE. New class TMCPSseWriter (src/Server/MCPServer.SseWriter.pas) wrapping TIdContext+TIdHTTPResponseInfo: Open — set ContentType 'text/event-stream', CharSet 'utf-8', Cache-Control no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering no, ContentLength := -1, CloseConnection := True (HTTP/1.1 needs close-delimited body unless chunked; Indy does not chunk-encode IOHandler writes automatically — if keep-alive must be preserved, set TransferEncoding := 'chunked' and frame each write as hex-length CRLF data CRLF, terminating with '0' CRLF CRLF), then ResponseInfo.WriteHeader; WriteEvent(const JSON: string) → Context.Connection.IOHandler.Write('data: ' + JSON + #10#10, IndyTextEncoding_UTF8) (JSON never contains raw newlines when produced by ToJSON); WriteComment → IOHandler.Write(': keep-alive'#10#10); IsConnected → IOHandler.Connected and not IOHandler.ClosedGracefully (call IOHandler.CheckForDisconnect(False) first); Close → Context.Connection.Disconnect. Catch EIdConnClosedGracefully/EIdSocketError on write and mark Cancelled. Ambient context: threadvar CurrentContext in MCPServer.RequestContext.pas with class property TMCPRequestContext.Current; fields Era, ProtocolVersion, ProgressToken, LogLevel, Cancelled: Boolean, OnNotification: TProc<string,TJSONObject>. Execution model in HandlePostRequest: default to application/json; switch to SSE lazily on the first SendNotification (headers not yet written) — requires running the handler so that the response is only committed after execution; simplest: always run ProcessRequest with a sink that buffers until first notification, then Open SSE and flush; if no notification occurred respond JSON. For subscriptions/listen (if implemented by the managers area) the manager returns a marker (e.g. TValue holding a TMCPStreamHandle) and the transport loops: write acknowledged, then WaitFor(FShutdownEvent or handle.Event, 15000ms) → on timeout WriteComment (doubles as disconnect probe), on event flush queued notifications, on disconnect exit (cancellation), on shutdown write completion result then Close. Keep a TThreadList<TMCPSseWriter> FOpenStreams; Stop sets FShutdownEvent, waits up to N seconds for streams to drain, force-disconnects the rest, then FHTTPServer.Active := False. Era rule: mark Cancelled on disconnect only when Ctx.Era = peModern (legacy: log only).

gaps.title: Mcp-Session-Id is echoed unconditionally (modern SHOULD-not) and minted inconsistently for legacy (only on the JSON path, never on the SSE path); non-standard sessionId in InitializeResult; shared FSessionID field is not thread-safe
gaps.current: Session header is read at src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:333 and echoed back at 348-349, 485-486, 548-549 regardless of era. On the JSON path a fresh session id is lifted out of result.sessionId with a Pos('"sessionId"') heuristic and a hard 'as TJSONObject' cast (lines 533-547; EInvalidCast → Indy 500 if a manager returns a string result containing that text, see JsonRpcProcessor.pas:197). The SSE path (used whenever Accept contains text/event-stream, which every conformant client sends) never sets Mcp-Session-Id on the initialize response, so sessions are effectively never established for conformant clients. CoreManager.Initialize adds a non-schema 'sessionId' field to the result and overwrites the single shared FSessionID from every Indy thread (src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:97,126).
gaps.required: Modern (HTTP-27): ignore Mcp-Session-Id; do not mint or echo. Legacy (HTTP-32): minting is MAY; if minted it must be on the InitializeResult response regardless of JSON/SSE path; a server that never terminates sessions never needs 404/400 session errors.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: two valid options — (a) stateless legacy: never mint, ignore incoming ids (clients that still send an old id are unaffected); (b) mint per-initialize with an in-memory session table. Either is spec-conformant; (a) is the smaller change and matches the modern stateless model. Library consumers: TMCPCoreManager.SessionID property can remain (return '' or last minted) — mark deprecated; removing result.sessionId is invisible to spec clients.
gaps.suggestedChange: Option (a) recommended: delete the Mcp-Session-Id echo for Era = peModern; for legacy keep echoing an incoming id (harmless) but stop minting: remove ResultJSON.AddPair('sessionId', ...) from CoreManager.Initialize and remove the Pos('"sessionId"') block from HandlePostRequestJSON. If session-scoped legacy state is wanted later (negotiated version, initialized flag, log level), add TMCPLegacySessionStore (TDictionary<string, TMCPLegacySession> under TCriticalSection, idle expiry) minted in HandlePostRequest when Body.method = 'initialize' and set on BOTH JSON and SSE responses; then honour HTTP-32: unknown id → 404 only for ids this server minted-and-expired (keep a tombstone set) and otherwise be lenient. Guard FSessionID with the store instead of a class field.

gaps.title: SSE event ids: non-atomic global counter (legacy uniqueness MUST at risk) and ids are obsolete in the modern era
gaps.current: GetNextEventID does Inc(FEventIDCounter) on a plain Int64 field (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:416-420) from Indy's per-connection threads; duplicates are possible under concurrent requests, violating the legacy 'MUST be globally unique' rule. Every SSE response emits 'id: N' (lines 492-496). The 2026-07-28 changelog item 9 removes SSE event IDs; Last-Event-ID is (correctly) never read.
gaps.required: Legacy: ids are MAY; if present MUST be unique. Modern: no ids; Last-Event-ID ignored.
gaps.compatImpact: None for clients (ids are optional in legacy, absent in modern). Library consumers: none.
gaps.suggestedChange: Simplest: drop 'id:' lines and remove FEventIDCounter/GetNextEventID entirely (allowed in all revisions; no resumability is implemented anyway). If ids are kept for legacy streams, use TInterlocked.Increment(FEventIDCounter) (System.SyncObjs) or AtomicIncrement, and emit them only when Ctx.Era = peLegacy.

gaps.title: Server binds to all interfaces; Settings.Host is only used for log text
gaps.current: Start sets FHTTPServer.DefaultPort := FPort and Active := True with no Bindings entry (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:155-156), which makes Indy listen on 0.0.0.0 (and, depending on Indy version, ::). FSettings.Host ('localhost' default, MCPServer.Settings.pas:86) is used only in the log line (IdHTTPServer.pas:159) and the removed GET info JSON (line 309).
gaps.required: HTTP-03: when running locally, SHOULD bind only to 127.0.0.1.
gaps.compatImpact: Operators who reach the server from another machine (README mentions 'Remote connections', Cloudflare Tunnel) must set the new BindAddress=0.0.0.0 explicitly — call out in README/changelog. Library consumers: TMCPIdHTTPServer.Port property unchanged; new BindAddress property defaults to 127.0.0.1 unless Settings.Host is a non-loopback name/IP.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add TMCPSettings.BindAddress ([Server] BindAddress, default '127.0.0.1'; also bind '::1' when IPv6 is desired). In TMCPIdHTTPServer.Start: FHTTPServer.Bindings.Clear; with FHTTPServer.Bindings.Add do begin IP := BindAddress; Port := FPort; IPVersion := Id_IPv4 (add a second binding with Id_IPv6 for '::1'); end; keep DefaultPort for HandleQuerySSLPort. Log a warning when BindAddress = '0.0.0.0' and AllowedOrigins = '*'.

gaps.title: CORS Allow/Expose headers do not cover the modern header names and Mcp-Param-*; DELETE not listed; no Vary: Origin
gaps.current: Access-Control-Allow-Headers is 'Accept, Content-Type, Last-Event-ID, Mcp-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id', Allow-Methods 'POST, GET, OPTIONS', Expose-Headers 'Mcp-Session-Id' (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:257-262). Browser-based modern clients sending Mcp-Method / Mcp-Name / Mcp-Param-* (and Authorization) will fail preflight. OPTIONS handler returns 200 with no Content-Length (line 265-269).
gaps.required: Not an MCP MUST per se, but required for the MUST-send headers (HTTP-21/25) to be usable from browser clients when CORS is enabled; Mcp-Param-{Name} names are dynamic.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy browser clients keep working (old names remain listed). Library consumers: none.
gaps.suggestedChange: Allow-Headers := 'Accept, Content-Type, Authorization, Last-Event-ID, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name' and, on OPTIONS preflight, append the request's Access-Control-Request-Headers value verbatim (covers Mcp-Param-*; alternatively '*' when Allow-Origin is '*' and no credentials). Allow-Methods := 'POST, GET, DELETE, OPTIONS'. Expose-Headers keep 'Mcp-Session-Id' (legacy). Add 'Vary: Origin' whenever a specific origin is echoed. Set ContentLength := 0 on the OPTIONS response (204 is also fine).

gaps.title: No Mcp-Param-* validation path and no way for tools to declare x-mcp-header
gaps.current: No 'Mcp-Param' handling in the transport; the schema generator has no attribute for x-mcp-header (out of this area, but the transport needs the binding list). Unrecognized Mcp-Param-* headers are currently ignored, which is what the spec requires for headers the server does not recognize.
gaps.required: HTTP-24 (MAY) feature; if any tool declares x-mcp-header, HTTP-25 validation becomes MUST: header present → decoded value must equal argument (numeric compare for integers, 'true'/'false' for booleans); argument absent/null → header must not be expected; argument present but header missing → reject; invalid characters → reject; all with 400 + -32020.
gaps.compatImpact: None until a tool opts in. Library consumers: new optional attribute (e.g. [SchemaHeader('Region')]) on TMCPToolBase<T> param classes; existing tools unchanged.
gaps.suggestedChange: Transport side: in ValidateStandardHeaders for tools/call, obtain the tool's inputSchema (TMCPRegistry.CreateTool(Name).GetInputSchema, cached per tool name in a TDictionary<string, TArray<THeaderBinding>> guarded by TMonitor; THeaderBinding = record HeaderName, PropertyPath: string; Kind: (hbString, hbInteger, hbBoolean) end, collected by walking 'properties' chains only). For each binding: ArgValue := arguments at path; Header := RawHeaders.Values['Mcp-Param-' + HeaderName]; if ArgValue is nil/TJSONNull then (if Header <> '' → treat as mismatch → -32020) else begin if Header = '' → -32020 'missing Mcp-Param-...'; DecodeMcpHeaderValue; compare: hbInteger → StrToInt64/TryStrToFloat numeric equality, hbBoolean → decoded = 'true'/'false' matching TJSONBool, hbString → exact end. Ignore Mcp-Param-* headers with no binding. Reject bindings that violate the x-mcp-header constraints at registration time (log + drop the annotation) so the server never advertises an invalid tool.

gaps.title: JSON-RPC batch bodies (2025-03-26 legacy) are rejected with a -32700 parse error; modern array bodies should be -32600/400
gaps.current: IsRequestOnlyNotificationsOrResponses accepts arrays (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:453-465) and returns 202 for all-notification batches, but a batch containing requests reaches TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ParseJSONRequest which raises 'JSON-RPC request must be an object' (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:52-56) → reported as -32700 with id null and HTTP 200 (lines 212-217).
gaps.required: HTTP-09: a 2025-03-26 client MAY send batches; server must answer with JSON/SSE responses (MAY be batched). HTTP-08: modern bodies are single messages — arrays are invalid input (400 + -32600 recommended).
gaps.compatImpact: Only 2025-03-26 clients that actually batch (rare; no mainstream SDK does). Library consumers: none.
gaps.suggestedChange: In HandlePostRequest after parsing: if Body is TJSONArray then if Ctx.ProtocolVersion = '2025-03-26' then process each element via ProcessRequest and return a JSON array of the non-empty responses (202 when all were notifications, as now) else ResponseNo := 400 with -32600 'Batching is not supported in protocol version X'. Keep IsRequestOnlyNotificationsOrResponses.

gaps.title: Thread-unsafe counters: TServerStatusResource and FEventIDCounter are incremented from Indy worker threads without atomics; 'active connections' actually counts in-flight requests
gaps.current: TServerStatusResource.IncrementRequestCount/ConnectionOpened/ConnectionClosed use plain Inc/Dec on class vars (src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Server.pas:95-109) and are called once per HTTP request from HandleHTTPRequest (IdHTTPServer.pas:177-179,206), so under keep-alive the value is 'requests in flight', not connections. GetResourceData reads them unsynchronised (lines 139-140). FEventIDCounter: see GAP-HTTP-09.
gaps.required: Not an MCP normative rule; a correctness prerequisite for the concurrent streaming model (multiple SSE streams per client are allowed; HTTP-34 requires per-stream message isolation) and for the legacy unique-id MUST.
gaps.compatImpact: None. Library consumers embedding TServerStatusResource see the same API.
gaps.suggestedChange: Use AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement (System.SyncObjs TInterlocked) for FRequestCount/FActiveConnections; read with AtomicCmpExchange or a volatile read. Either rename the JSON field to activeRequests or derive ActiveConnections from FHTTPServer.Contexts.LockList.Count/UnlockList exposed through a callback. Do the same for any new open-stream registry (TThreadList).

gaps.title: Accept parsing: substring match on the first Accept header only; SSE chosen whenever offered; request with id=null treated as a request and answered with 204/empty stream
gaps.current: AcceptsSSE := Pos('text/event-stream', AcceptHeader) > 0 (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:422-425) — ignores q=0, ignores a second 'Accept:' header line (RawHeaders.Values returns the first). SSE is selected for every request that offers it (line 354), even though nothing is streamed. When ProcessRequest returns '' for a request whose id is null/bool (ExtractRequestID → Empty, JsonRpcProcessor.pas:82-87,174-181) the transport answers 204 (line 524-528) or an empty SSE body (line 506).
gaps.required: HTTP-06: a request MUST get application/json or text/event-stream; nothing else. Server chooses the format; JSON is the cheaper default when no notifications will be sent.
gaps.compatImpact: Clients that currently receive SSE for every call will receive application/json — both are mandatory for clients (2025-03-26 onward). Library consumers: none.
gaps.suggestedChange: Default to application/json; use SSE only when streaming is required (progress/logging/subscriptions per GAP-HTTP-07). Implement AcceptsSSE by iterating all RawHeaders entries named 'Accept', splitting on ',', trimming, and checking media-type = 'text/event-stream' (or '*/*') with q <> 0. If streaming is needed but the client did not offer text/event-stream, fall back to JSON with the final response only. Treat id=null as an invalid request (-32600, 400) rather than a notification.

gaps.title: No authentication hook on the HTTP transport
gaps.current: No Authorization handling anywhere in TMCPIdHTTPServer; README suggests 'claude mcp add ... --header "Authorization: Bearer your-token"' (README.md:353) but the token is ignored.
gaps.required: HTTP-04: servers SHOULD implement proper authentication for all connections (the full OAuth spec is a separate area).
gaps.compatImpact: Opt-in; default open as today. Library consumers: new optional OnAuthenticate event / Settings.BearerToken; no breaking change.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add TMCPIdHTTPServer.OnAuthenticate: TFunc<TIdHTTPRequestInfo, Boolean> (or an IMCPHttpAuthenticator interface) invoked after Origin validation; when it returns False respond 401 with 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer' and a JSON-RPC error body without id. Provide a built-in static-bearer implementation driven by [Security] BearerToken in settings.ini. Never log the Authorization header (current logging at IdHTTPServer.pas:331 logs whole bodies; add a redaction option).

gaps.title: Documentation/config does not describe the dual-era transport (README badge 2025-06-18, no settings for versions/bind/origin)
gaps.current: README.md:6 badge 'MCP-2025-06-18', :30 'Implements MCP specification 2025-06-18 with Streamable HTTP and SSE', :107 'Claude Code (SSE support)'; settings.ini.example has only [Server]/[CORS]/[SSL]; TMCPSettings has no version, bind-address or security-origin keys (src/Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas:83-96).
gaps.required: Derived from HTTP-27/29: operators need to know that GET/DELETE answer 405, sessions are not minted, which versions are served, and how to bind/expose the server.
gaps.compatImpact: None at runtime; new INI keys have defaults so existing settings.ini files keep loading (TIniFile.Read* with defaults, Settings.pas:143-155).
gaps.suggestedChange: Add to settings.ini.example and TMCPSettings: [Server] BindAddress=127.0.0.1; [Protocol] SupportedVersions=2026-07-28,2025-11-25,2025-06-18,2025-03-26; LegacyGetStream=0; [Security] AllowedOrigins=...; BearerToken=. README: update badge to 2026-07-28 (dual-era), document header requirements for modern clients (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name), the 405 on GET/DELETE, stateless sessions, curl examples for both eras, and the BindAddress change.

alreadyConformant: Single configurable MCP endpoint path with 404 for other paths (HTTP-01): src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:184-192 (FSettings.Endpoint, default '/mcp' in src/Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas:89).
DELETE (and any other method) answers 405 (HTTP-27 modern, HTTP-32 legacy MAY): src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:200-204 (only the RFC 9110 'Allow' header is missing).

Origin present-and-not-allowed → 403 when CORS is enabled with an explicit list (HTTP-02 partial): src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:244-251; absent Origin is allowed (non-browser clients), which is correct.
Notification/response-only POST bodies get 202 (HTTP-05, modulo Indy default body — see GAP-HTTP-05): src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:343-352.
Requests are answered with either Content-Type application/json (HandlePostRequestJSON, lines 530-553) or text/event-stream (HandlePostRequestSSE, lines 479-509) (HTTP-06).
UTF-8 in and out (HTTP-07): body read with IndyTextEncoding_UTF8 (line 328); JSON response written via TStringStream(..., TEncoding.UTF8) (line 551); SSE CharSet 'utf-8' (line 480).
SSE stream headers already include Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no (HTTP-12): lines 285-287 and 481-483.

SSE framing is valid per the SSE spec: 'event: message', 'data: <json>', blank-line terminator with LF (lines 101-105, 495-499); the final JSON-RPC response ends the body, so the stream terminates with the response (HTTP-10/HTTP-11 'SHOULD terminate').
Server never sends JSON-RPC requests or unrelated notifications on a response stream (HTTP-10 MUST NOT, HTTP-34): only the single response is ever written (lines 488-501).
Last-Event-ID is never read and no replay is attempted (HTTP-27 modern 'ignore'; HTTP-33 legacy MAY): grep shows the header only in the CORS allow list (line 260).
Session id, when echoed, is a GUID string (visible ASCII, HTTP-32): src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:97.
OPTIONS preflight is handled (lines 194-195, 265-269) and CORS headers are emitted only when CorsEnabled (line 221-222).

HTTP keep-alive is enabled for the POST-per-message model (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:118) and Indy runs each connection on its own thread, which is compatible with per-request SSE streams.
TLS is available via TaurusTLS/OpenSSL (lines 364-408) so the server can be deployed with authentication/transport security as the spec's security section expects.
JSON-RPC parse errors are reported as -32700 with id null (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:209-217), matching the error object rules (only the HTTP status needs to change for modern era).
notes: Indy source is not available in this container (find found no IdCustomHTTPServer.pas), so all statements about Indy internals (default HTML body for empty 202/204, WriteHeader/IOHandler streaming, case-insensitive TIdHeaderList lookup, Bindings default 0.0.0.0) must be verified on the Windows build with curl -i / curl -N before finalising the plan.

Recommended request pipeline order for POST: Origin (403) → endpoint (404) → parse body (400/-32700) → array handling (2025-03-26 batch vs 400/-32600) → notification? (validate Mcp-Method only if present, dispatch, 202 no body) → era/version classification (missing header + _meta → 400/-32020; unknown version → 400/-32022; header ≠ _meta → 400/-32020) → modern standard headers Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name/Mcp-Param-* (400/-32020) → _meta required fields (400/-32602) → dispatch → status mapping (-32601 → 404 modern only; -32021 → 400; else 200) → JSON or SSE.

Era classification key: header value (2026-07-28 or later = modern; 2025-03-26/06-18/11-25 = legacy; absent = legacy 2025-03-26 unless the body carries _meta.protocolVersion, in which case it is a modern request missing its header). Legacy clients do not send MCP-Protocol-Version on the initialize request itself (2025-06-18 lifecycle note: 'on all subsequent requests'), so initialize always arrives header-less and must be treated as legacy.
404 must never be used for legacy-era requests: legacy clients interpret 404 + Mcp-Session-Id as 'session terminated' and re-initialize (HTTP-32 item 4). The -32601 → 404 mapping is modern-era only.

Every 4xx returned to a modern request must carry the JSON-RPC error body (-32020/-32021/-32022/-32602/-32601): dual-era clients use the body to decide whether to fall back to initialize (HTTP-28). An empty 400 would make a modern client think this is a legacy server.

Notifications over HTTP have no defined header requirements in 2026-07-28 ('header requirements for notification POSTs are not defined by this revision'); do not reject a notification for missing Mcp-Method; the only client→server notification in the modern core is notifications/cancelled, which is stdio-only.

Modern era: a POST body that is a JSON-RPC response object is invalid ('The client MUST NOT send JSON-RPC responses'); the spec gives no server rule — recommend 400 + -32600 (id null) for modern era, 202 for legacy era (legacy clients send responses to server requests such as ping/roots/list even though this server never issues them).

Base64 sentinel decoding must be strict: System.NetEncoding.TBase64Encoding silently skips invalid characters, but SEP-2243's conformance table requires 400 + HeaderMismatch for invalid padding or characters; validate the alphabet and length mod 4 before decoding. The markers '=?base64?' and '?=' are case-sensitive and lowercase; a plain value that happens to look like the sentinel is always encoded by clients, so no ambiguity remains after decoding.

SSE event ids and the FEventIDCounter can be removed outright: modern removed them (changelog item 9 'Remove SSE stream resumability and message redelivery (the Last-Event-ID header and SSE event IDs)'), legacy makes them optional, and the server implements no replay.

Dropping the GET stream to 405 is safe for legacy SDK clients: the TypeScript and Python StreamableHTTP client transports treat 405 on their standalone GET as 'no server-initiated stream available' and continue. The MCP Inspector talks to the server through its own Node proxy, so CORS is irrelevant for Inspector testing; CORS only matters for browser pages calling the server directly.

Streaming design implication for the library API: keep IMCPTool.Execute(const Arguments: TJSONObject): TValue and IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod unchanged; expose a threadvar-backed TMCPRequestContext.Current (Era, ProtocolVersion, ProgressToken, LogLevel, IsCancelled, SendProgress, SendLog) so existing custom tools/managers keep compiling and only new code opts into progress/log notifications and cooperative cancellation. Indy runs each connection on its own thread so a threadvar is a safe ambient carrier for the duration of ExecuteMethod.

With Indy, incremental SSE requires writing headers manually (ResponseInfo.WriteHeader after setting ContentLength := -1) and then writing to Context.Connection.IOHandler; because Indy does not chunk-encode IOHandler writes, set CloseConnection := True so HTTP/1.1 clients read until close, or implement chunked framing by hand if keep-alive on streamed responses matters. Periodic ': keep-alive' comment writes double as the disconnect probe that implements 'disconnect = cancellation' (HTTP-14).

TMCPIdHTTPServer.Stop currently just sets Active := False; once long-lived subscriptions/listen streams exist, Stop must signal a shutdown event, write the graceful completion result on each open stream, disconnect, and only then deactivate, otherwise Active := False blocks waiting for handler threads.

Legacy cancellation (notifications/cancelled over HTTP) can legitimately be ignored ('Servers MAY ignore cancellation notifications if ... the request cannot be cancelled'); without sessions there is no safe way to correlate request ids across clients, so a dual-era server should simply log them.

Legacy session policy decision for the orchestrator: stateless legacy (never mint Mcp-Session-Id, ignore incoming ids) is spec-conformant and matches the current effective behaviour for conformant clients; minting sessions is only worthwhile if the lifecycle area wants per-client legacy state (negotiated version when the header is absent, logging/setLevel, initialized flag). If sessions are minted they must be set on both JSON and SSE initialize responses.

Both TMCPStdioTransport and TMCPIdHTTPServer construct their own TMCPJsonRpcProcessor; the new ProcessRequest overload with TMCPRequestContext should be shared so the stdio transport's era handling (server/discover probe, notifications/cancelled) can reuse the same status/error plumbing.

Dead code to clean up while touching the transport: HTTP_NOT_ACCEPTABLE (IdHTTPServer.pas:88) and KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT (line 79) are unused; the JSON body is parsed twice per request (transport line 341 and processor line 48) — pass the parsed TJSONObject into the processor.

Non-spec hardening observed: the non-Taurus SSL path enables TLS 1.0/1.1 (IdHTTPServer.pas:396); full request bodies are logged at Info level (line 331) which will include tool arguments and, if added, bearer tokens — add redaction/level control.

x-mcp-header support depends on the tools/schema area adding an attribute (e.g. [SchemaHeader('Region')]) to MCPServer.Schema.Generator; the transport-side validation (GAP-HTTP-12) should be written against the emitted inputSchema JSON so it also works for hand-built schemas from TMCPToolBase.BuildSchema.

server/discover is a modern MUST ('Servers MUST implement server/discover', versioning.mdx §Protocol Version Negotiation) and carries only _meta (no Mcp-Name); it must pass the same header validation (MCP-Protocol-Version + Mcp-Method: server/discover). Belongs to the lifecycle/core area but the transport must not special-case it.

Suggested conformance test list (curl/Delphi DUnitX against a running server): mcp-method lowercase accepted; Mcp-Method: TOOLS/CALL rejected -32020/400; Mcp-Name with surrounding spaces accepted; missing Mcp-Method on modern request → 400/-32020; header/_meta version mismatch → 400/-32020; MCP-Protocol-Version: 1900-01-01 → 400/-32022 with supported[]; no header + no _meta → served as 2025-03-26; no header + _meta → 400/-32020; unknown method modern → 404/-32601, legacy → 200/-32601; notification → 202 with Content-Length: 0; GET/DELETE → 405 + Allow; Origin: http://evil.example → 403 even with CORS disabled; =?base64?SGVsbG8?= (bad padding) → 400/-32020; Base64 UTF-8 Mcp-Name matching a non-ASCII tool name accepted; client closing an SSE stream mid-tool marks the context cancelled.

gapReports.area: stdio transport, cancellation, progress, shutdown, dual-era probe (server/discover)

requirements.text: "Messages are delimited by newlines, and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines." Each line is exactly one JSON-RPC request, notification, or response.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio.mdx (intro bullet list); /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports.mdx '## stdio'; identical in 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26

requirements.text: "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message."

"The server MAY write UTF-8 strings to stderr for any logging purposes including informational, debug, and error messages." (2025-06-18 wording: "for logging purposes"). Client "SHOULD NOT assume stderr output indicates error conditions" (2025-11-25+).
"MCP uses JSON-RPC to encode messages. JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded."

"The server MUST NOT write JSON-RPC requests to stdout. Server-to-client interactions are carried in InputRequiredResult replies"; patterns: "Servers MUST NOT initiate JSON-RPC requests, and clients do not send JSON-RPC responses."; transports overview: "No other message direction exists".

Server writes three kinds of messages on the single channel: responses correlated by id; request-scoped notifications (notifications/progress, notifications/message); notifications for an active subscriptions/listen request, which "Clients MUST correlate ... using the io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId field in _meta". basic/index: "On notifications delivered via a subscriptions/listen stream, the server MUST include io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId in _meta". "All messages share this single channel; there are no per-request streams."

"All request metadata for the stdio transport is carried inline in the JSON-RPC message body. The protocol version, per-request capabilities, and optional client identity live in _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/*; ... There is no header layer." basic/index: fields io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities are Required and "MUST be included on every request"; "A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params)."

"Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection to establish context (e.g., capabilities, protocol version, client identity). Every request supplies this metadata in its _meta field." Note: "an open connection, such as a STDIO process, is not a conversation or session: clients may interleave unrelated requests on the same transport, and a server must not treat connection or process identity as a proxy for conversation or session continuity."

"Servers SHOULD NOT require that a client reuse the same connection or process to perform related operations." and "Servers SHOULD be prepared to handle requests associated with multiple tasks, threads, or conversations."

2025-03-26 only: "MCP implementations MAY support sending JSON-RPC batches, but MUST support receiving JSON-RPC batches." stdio section: "Messages may be JSON-RPC requests, notifications, responses—or a JSON-RPC batch containing one or more requests and/or notifications." Removed in 2025-06-18 (changelog major change 1: "Remove support for JSON-RPC batching").
Notifications: "The receiver MUST NOT send a response." and "Notifications MUST NOT include an ID."

Requests: "Requests MUST include a string or integer ID. Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be null." Server implication: a message with id:null is neither a valid request nor a notification and should be rejected as Invalid Request (-32600), not silently treated as a notification.

"Error responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to (except in error cases where the ID could not be read due a malformed request)." A null-id error is therefore reserved for unparseable/malformed input.

Logging feature deprecated: "New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it; existing implementations SHOULD migrate to logging to stderr for stdio transports, or to OpenTelemetry". Also "servers MUST NOT emit notifications/message for requests that did not include [io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel]".

"Servers receiving cancellation notifications SHOULD: Stop processing the cancelled request; Free associated resources; Not send a response for the cancelled request". On stdio the client "MUST send a notifications/cancelled notification referencing the request ID" (params.requestId, optional params.reason) — so a server must be able to receive and dispatch it while the request is in flight.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation.mdx '## Behavior Requirements' item 3 and '## Transport-Specific Cancellation'; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2025-11-25/basic/utilities/cancellation.mdx '## Behavior Requirements' item 4 ('Receivers of cancellation notifications SHOULD')

requirements.text: "Servers SHOULD stop work on a cancelled request as soon as practical and MUST NOT send any further messages for it." (no response, no progress, no notifications/message after honoring a cancel).
"Servers MAY ignore cancellation notifications if: The referenced request is unknown; Processing has already completed; The request cannot be cancelled".

"Due to network latency, cancellation notifications may arrive after request processing has completed, and potentially after a response has already been sent. Both parties MUST handle these race conditions gracefully".
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation.mdx '## Timing Considerations'; same heading in 2025-11-25 utilities/cancellation.mdx

requirements.text: "Invalid cancellation notifications SHOULD be ignored: Unknown request IDs; Already completed requests; Malformed notifications" — preserving fire-and-forget semantics (never answer a notification with an error).
"Both parties SHOULD log cancellation reasons for debugging".

"A server MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing a subscriptions/listen request ID when it tears down that subscription stream. Servers MUST NOT send notifications/cancelled for any other purpose." schema: "Servers MUST NOT use this notification to cancel any other request." SEP-2575: on client cancel of a listen request "The server MUST stop sending notifications for that subscription."

Client-side rule with server implication: "The initialize request MUST NOT be cancelled by clients" (2025-03-26..2025-11-25) and, 2025-11-25 only, "For task-augmented requests, the tasks/cancel request MUST be used instead of the notifications/cancelled notification." A server may treat a cancel of initialize as invalid and ignore it (CN-05).

"The server MAY send progress notifications to report the status of requests the client has issued." Opt-in: client puts progressToken in params._meta.progressToken; server sends notifications/progress with params {progressToken, progress, total?, message?}.

"Progress tokens MUST be a string or integer value" and "MUST be unique across all active requests" (client chooses). Server must accept and echo either JSON type unchanged (schema: ProgressToken = string | number).
"The progress value MUST increase with each notification, even if the total is unknown."
"The progress and the total values MAY be floating point."
"The message field SHOULD provide relevant human readable progress information."
"Progress notifications MUST only reference tokens that: Were provided in an active request; Are associated with an in-progress operation".

"Servers receiving a request with a progress token MAY: Choose not to send any progress notifications; Send notifications at whatever frequency they deem appropriate; Omit the total value if unknown". Schema: "The receiver is not obligated to provide these notifications."
"Clients and servers SHOULD track active progress tokens"; "Both parties SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent flooding".

"Progress notifications MUST stop after completion." Patterns overview: "While the request is in flight, the server MAY send notifications scoped to it, such as notifications/progress" — i.e. progress precedes the response on the same channel.

"Servers SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed or reads return end-of-file. This is the primary graceful-shutdown signal and the only portable one, so honoring it reduces the need for forced termination." (Legacy revisions describe the same client procedure — close stdin, wait, SIGTERM, SIGKILL — without an explicit server keyword.)

Client shutdown escalation: "1. Closing the input stream ... 2. Waiting for the server to exit. 3. If the server does not exit within a reasonable time, forcibly terminating the process ... On POSIX systems, forced termination typically escalates from SIGTERM to SIGKILL. On Windows ... TerminateProcess or Job Objects." Server implication: SIGTERM must remain an effective termination signal.
"The server MAY initiate shutdown by closing its output stream to the client and exiting."

"When the server ends a subscription on its own initiative (for example, during shutdown), it SHOULD respond to the original subscriptions/listen request with a completion result before closing the stream." Also "Active subscriptions/listen streams must also be re-established after restart" (client), so the server holds no subscription state across restarts.

"Servers MUST implement server/discover." It "lets a client query a server's supported protocol versions, capabilities, and identity before sending any other requests." Request carries only _meta; result is DiscoverResult {resultType, supportedVersions: string[], capabilities: ServerCapabilities, instructions?, ttlMs, cacheScope, _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'] (SHOULD)}.

"If the server does not implement the requested version (whether the version is unknown to the server, or is a known version the server has chosen not to support), it MUST respond with an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing the versions it does support": error.code -32022, error.data.supported: string[], error.data.requested: string.

Probe semantics a dual-era server must satisfy: "The server returns a DiscoverResult: the server is modern." "The server returns a recognized modern JSON-RPC error such as UnsupportedProtocolVersionError: the server is modern ... Do not fall back to initialize." "The server returns any other error, or does not respond within a reasonable timeout: the server is legacy." "The fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one specific error code: legacy servers respond to unknown pre-initialize requests with implementation-defined errors (commonly -32601 or -32602) or not at all." Hence a dual-era server must answer server/discover with DiscoverResult (or -32022) before any initialize, and must never answer it with -32601/-32602/-32603.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio.mdx '## Backward Compatibility'; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning.mdx '### Compatibility Matrix' rows 'Dual-era | Modern' and 'Legacy | Dual-era'

requirements.text: "A server that wishes to support both legacy clients (which expect an initialize handshake) and modern clients (which use per-request metadata) MAY implement both behaviors." SEP-2575: "Such a server can continue to implement the old initialize RPC to handle legacy clients, while also exposing the new stateless RPCs (server/discover, etc.) for updated clients."
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning.mdx '## Backward Compatibility with Initialization-Based Versions'; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/seps/2575-stateless-mcp.md '### Supporting Multiple Versions'

requirements.text: (Declarative normative text, no RFC keyword.) "A dual-era server selects its behavior from how the client opens: A request carrying modern per-request _meta is served statelessly according to this revision. An initialize request selects legacy semantics, scoped to the stdio process (stdio) or the session (HTTP), as specified by the negotiated legacy protocol version."

"A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently on the same endpoint or process." And "A client that only supports modern versions does not need to probe" — so a modern request (e.g. tools/call with _meta) may be the first message on the process and must be served without initialize.

"The era determination is a property of the server, not of an individual request. Clients SHOULD cache the result for the lifetime of the server process (stdio) ... and MAY persist it across restarts of the same server configuration". Server implication: server/discover must answer identically for the whole process lifetime, including after an initialize has put the process into legacy mode.

Conditional (only if legacy support is ever dropped): "A server that supports only modern versions SHOULD name the protocol versions it supports in any error it returns to an initialize request, on any transport".

Legacy version negotiation that fixes the per-process legacy semantics: "If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports. This SHOULD be the latest version supported by the server." "The initialization phase MUST be the first interaction between client and server." (client obligation; server not required to enforce).

ping (legacy only; removed in 2026-07-28 changelog item 5): "The receiver MUST respond promptly with an empty response"; sender "MAY ... Consider the connection stale; Terminate the connection" on timeout. Server implication on stdio: a ping must be answerable while another request is executing.

gaps.title: Synchronous single-threaded stdio loop: one request blocks stdin reading, no serialized async writer, no concurrency
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas:54-96 — `while not Eof(Input)` → `Readln` → `FJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest` (synchronous, runs the tool on the reader thread) → `Writeln(Output)`/`Flush`. While a tool executes (ToolsManager.pas:120-128 → Tool.Base.pas:158-168) no further line is read, so a `notifications/cancelled` for that request, a legacy `ping`, or any interleaved modern request sits unread in the pipe until the tool returns. stdout is written only from this one thread; there is no writer abstraction any other component could use to emit `notifications/progress`, `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged`, subscription notifications, or a graceful `subscriptions/listen` result. Contrast: the HTTP transport already executes the same processor concurrently on Indy worker threads (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:144,488,522).
gaps.required: Modern: process is not a session; "clients may interleave unrelated requests on the same transport" (ST-08); dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently (DE-06); server must be able to emit request-scoped and subscription notifications on the single channel before/alongside responses (ST-06, PG-09) and observe cancellations while work is in flight (CN-01/CN-02). Legacy: ping "MUST respond promptly" (DE-10) even during a long tool call. Any of this needs (a) a reader that keeps consuming stdin while requests run and (b) a single serialized writer for stdout.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: today's behaviour is functionally correct but latency-bound; after the change they gain prompt ping/cancel. Modern clients: without this, subscriptions/listen, cancellation and progress cannot be implemented on stdio at all (blocker for those features). Library consumers: `TMCPStdioTransport.Create(ManagerRegistry, CoreManager)` and `Run` keep their signatures; custom tools/resources/managers will be executed from worker threads on stdio — they already are on HTTP (Indy), so thread-safe implementations are already the contract, but consumers who relied on strict single-threaded stdio execution need an opt-out (`MaxConcurrentRequests := 1`), which preserves in-order sequential dispatch while still allowing the reader/writer split (so cancel/ping are observed). Shared mutable state in the repo that is not thread-safe today: TServerStatusResource counters use plain Inc/Dec (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Server.pas:95-108) and TMCPCoreManager.FSessionID (CoreManager.pas:97).
gaps.suggestedChange: Unit MCPServer.StdioTransport: (1) add `IMCPMessageWriter = interface  procedure WriteMessage(const Json: string); end` implemented by a `TMCPStdioWriter` that owns a `TCriticalSection` (or a `TThreadedQueue<string>` drained by one writer thread) and performs write+flush of exactly one line per call; (2) `Run` becomes: reader loop on the calling thread reading lines → for notifications call processor synchronously (cheap, must be fast to honour cancel) → for requests enqueue a work item executed on `TTask.Run`/a bounded `TThreadPool` (new property `MaxConcurrentRequests: Integer` default e.g. 8; `1` = sequential compatibility mode) whose completion writes the response through the writer; (3) `TMCPInflightRegistry` (TDictionary<string /*id key*/, IMCPRequestContext> + lock) registered before dispatch and removed after the response is written (or suppressed when cancelled). (4) Expose the writer to managers/tools via the request context (see GAP-CN-01/GAP-PG-01). (5) Keep `Run` blocking until EOF and all in-flight work drained (with a bounded drain timeout so EOF still exits promptly, SD-01). Also mirror the `IMCPMessageWriter` abstraction in MCPServer.IdHTTPServer for the SSE path (cross-area) so tools get the same API on both transports.

gaps.title: notifications/cancelled is never dispatched; no in-flight request registry, no cancellation signal reaches tools; responses are always sent
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:174-181 — any message without `id` is logged (`'Notification received: ' + MethodName`) and `Exit`s; `notifications/cancelled` params (`requestId`, `reason`) are never read, the reason is not logged (CN-06), and nothing is cancelled. No manager registers it (CoreManager.pas:48-53 only handles initialize/notifications/initialized/ping). `IMCPTool.Execute(const Arguments: TJSONObject)` (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:18,41,59,76) and `IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod(Method, Params)` (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:43) carry no cancellation token. The response is unconditionally written (StdioTransport.pas:66-71) even if a cancel arrived. Combined with GAP-ST-01 the cancel for the running request cannot even be read before completion, so the server only ever hits the 'already completed' MAY-ignore case (CN-03).
gaps.required: CN-01: SHOULD stop processing, free resources, not send a response; CN-02 (modern stdio): "MUST NOT send any further messages for it" once cancelled; CN-03/CN-05: ignore unknown/completed/malformed silently; CN-04: handle the late-arrival race gracefully; CN-06: log the reason; CN-07: server-sent notifications/cancelled only for tearing down a subscriptions/listen stream, and a client cancel referencing a listen id MUST stop that subscription's notifications.
gaps.compatImpact: Both eras (same wire format in 2025-03-26..2026-07-28). Legacy clients that time out and send cancel currently get a late response, which they 'SHOULD ignore' — works by accident but wastes server work. Library consumers: no signature break if cancellation is exposed via a thread-local/context accessor rather than changing `IMCPTool.Execute`; tools that never check cancellation keep running to completion (permitted by CN-03 'cannot be cancelled'), but their response is suppressed by the transport, which is a visible behaviour change only when a client actually cancels. Custom `IMCPCapabilityManager` implementations keep compiling because the interface (with its GUID) is left untouched and a new optional interface is probed with `Supports()`.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit MCPServer.RequestContext: `IMCPRequestContext = interface  function GetRequestId: TJSONValue; function GetProtocolVersion: string; function GetEra: TMCPProtocolEra; function GetProgressToken: TJSONValue; function IsCancelled: Boolean; procedure CheckCancelled; {raises EMCPRequestCancelled} procedure ReportProgress(const Progress: Double; const Total: Double = -1; const Msg: string = ''); function GetWriter: IMCPMessageWriter; end` with a `TMCPRequestContext` implementation (cancel flag via TInterlocked, monotonic progress guard) and a thread-local class property `TMCPRequestContext.Current` set by the transport around dispatch. Add `IMCPContextAwareManager = interface ['{new GUID}'] function ExecuteMethodEx(const Method: string; const Params: TJSONObject; const Context: IMCPRequestContext): TValue; end` — processor does `if Supports(Manager, IMCPContextAwareManager, Ex) then Ex.ExecuteMethodEx(...) else Manager.ExecuteMethod(...)`. Add `IMCPCancellableTool = interface ... function ExecuteWithContext(const Arguments: TJSONObject; const Context: IMCPRequestContext): TValue; end` optionally implemented by TMCPToolBase<T>/<T,R> forwarding to Execute (default) so existing subclasses compile unchanged. In TMCPJsonRpcProcessor add `ProcessMessage(const Line: string; const Session: TMCPTransportSession; out Kind: TMCPMessageKind): string` (old `ProcessRequest` kept, delegating): when Method = 'notifications/cancelled' → parse params.requestId (accept string or number, key on JSON text), log reason at Info, call `InflightRegistry.Cancel(id)`; unknown/finished ids and malformed params → log at Debug and return '' (never write an error for a notification, ST-11). Transport: after the worker finishes, `if Context.IsCancelled then discard response else Writer.WriteMessage(response)`; `ReportProgress` becomes a no-op once cancelled (CN-02). Subscription teardown by client cancel (once GAP-ST-07 exists): registry lookup of listen ids → stop stream, send nothing further. Never emit server-side notifications/cancelled except in the listen-teardown path (CN-07) — enforce by giving the writer no generic 'send cancel' API outside TMCPSubscriptionStream.

gaps.title: progressToken ignored; no way for a tool/manager to emit notifications/progress before its response
gaps.current: No code reads `params._meta` (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:185-190 passes `params` through untouched; ToolsManager.pas:96-118 extracts only `name`/`arguments`). There is no API to write a notification to stdout while a request is executing (StdioTransport.pas:64-71 writes exactly one response per request). `TMCPToolsCapability.SupportsProgress/SupportsCancellation` (Types.pas:63-71) and the `tools.supportsProgress:false / supportsCancellation:false` pairs emitted by CoreManager.pas:106-114 are not spec fields in any revision (the tools capability only defines `listChanged`).
gaps.required: PG-01/PG-07: sending progress is MAY, so absence is conformant. But an upgrade that adds long-running tools should implement it, and then PG-02 (token is string|number, echoed verbatim), PG-03 (progress strictly increasing), PG-06 (only for active requests), PG-08 (track tokens; rate-limit), PG-09 (stop after completion) are MUSTs/SHOULDs. Progress must be written on the same channel before the response (ST-06).
gaps.compatImpact: Both eras (identical wire format 2025-03-26..2026-07-28). No effect on clients that send no progressToken. Library consumers: additive API (`TMCPRequestContext.Current.ReportProgress`), no change to `IMCPTool.Execute`; tools that never call it behave exactly as today. Removing the non-standard `supportsProgress/supportsCancellation` keys from the initialize result is a wire change that no known client reads (cross-ref core/lifecycle area).
gaps.suggestedChange: In TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessMessage: read `params._meta.progressToken` (clone the TJSONValue so the JSON type — string vs number — is preserved) into the `TMCPRequestContext`. `ReportProgress` implementation: if no token → return; if cancelled or completed (context sealed by the transport right before writing the response) → return; enforce monotonicity (if Progress <= LastProgress then raise EMCPProgressError in DEBUG / clamp+log in RELEASE); rate limit with `MinProgressIntervalMs` (default 100, property on the transport); build `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/progress","params":{"progressToken":<token>,"progress":<double>,"total":<double>?,"message":<string>?}}` with TJSONObject and hand it to `IMCPMessageWriter.WriteMessage` (stdio: locked stdout; HTTP: SSE `data:` event on the open response, cross-area). Track active tokens in the inflight registry (PG-08). Drop the `supportsProgress/supportsCancellation` fields from `TMCPCoreManager.Initialize` and mark `TMCPToolsCapability` properties deprecated (keep the class so consumer code compiles).

gaps.title: server/discover answered with -32601 (legacy probe outcome); no DiscoverResult, so modern/dual-era clients can never enter modern mode
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:121-123 raises 'Method [server/discover] not found...' because no manager handles it (CoreManager.pas:48-53; ToolsManager.pas:64-67; ResourcesManager.pas:59-64); lines 214-215 map any message containing 'not found' to JSONRPC_METHOD_NOT_FOUND (-32601). Per stdio.mdx '## Backward Compatibility' that is exactly the 'any other error → legacy' outcome, so the current binary is a well-behaved legacy server, but can never be detected as modern. Server identity/version live in TMCPSettings.ServerName/ServerVersion (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas:87-88) and MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-06-18' (Types.pas:11).
gaps.required: DE-01: servers MUST implement server/discover; DE-03: dual-era server must answer it with a DiscoverResult — or a recognized modern error (-32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError with data.supported/data.requested, DE-02) — before any initialize and regardless of process state; DE-07: answer consistently for the whole process lifetime (also after an initialize has selected legacy semantics). Result shape (schema.ts DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult): `resultType:"complete"`, `supportedVersions:string[]`, `capabilities:{tools:{},resources:{}}`, `ttlMs`, `cacheScope:"public"|"private"`, optional `instructions`, `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo:{name,version}` (SHOULD).
gaps.compatImpact: Modern era only; zero effect on legacy clients (they never send server/discover). Library consumers: adding the method inside TMCPCoreManager (or a new TMCPDiscoveryManager registered by default in RunStdioServer/RunHTTPServer) keeps `IMCPCapabilityManager` unchanged; consumers who build their own registry must register the new manager to become dual-era (document in README 'Using as a Library'). Consumers with custom managers that expose extra capabilities need a hook to contribute to `capabilities` — e.g. an optional `IMCPCapabilityDescriber` interface probed with Supports().
gaps.suggestedChange: Add `'server/discover'` to `TMCPCoreManager.HandlesMethod` and implement `Discover(const Params: TJSONObject): TValue` (or new unit Managers/MCPServer.DiscoveryManager.pas) that: (a) validates `params._meta` per ST-07 (missing protocolVersion/clientCapabilities → -32602; unsupported version → -32022 with `data.supported` = modern versions list and `data.requested`); (b) returns TJSONObject {resultType:'complete', supportedVersions:[MCP_MODERN_VERSIONS...], capabilities:{tools:{}, resources:{}} (add listChanged/subscribe only when GAP-ST-07 lands; ask other managers via `IMCPCapabilityDescriber`), _meta:{'io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo':{name:FSettings.ServerName, version:FSettings.ServerVersion}}, ttlMs: 3600000, cacheScope:'public'}; (c) never touches FSessionID/initialize state. Add constants in MCPServer.Types: `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION_2026_07_28 = '2026-07-28'`, `MCP_MODERN_VERSIONS`, `MCP_LEGACY_VERSIONS = ['2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26']`; keep `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` (consumers reference it) as the latest legacy default. Replace the `Pos('not found', E.Message)` heuristic (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215) with typed exceptions (`EMCPMethodNotFound`, `EMCPInvalidParams`, `EMCPUnsupportedProtocolVersion` carrying `data`) so a resource/tool error text containing 'not found' can never surface as -32601 and flip a probing client into legacy mode.
