gaps.title: No per-request era detection and no per-process legacy mode: _meta is ignored, initialize always negotiates '2025-06-18', modern requests are served with legacy semantics
gaps.current: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest never inspects `params._meta` (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:185-190); the only process state is `TMCPCoreManager.FSessionID` set on initialize (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:97,126) and the result always says `protocolVersion: '2025-06-18'` (CoreManager.pas:101; Types.pas:11) regardless of `params.protocolVersion`, so a 2025-03-26 client asking for 2025-03-26 is told 2025-06-18 (violates DE-09 if the server claims 2025-03-26 support) and a 2025-11-25 client is downgraded (allowed). A modern `tools/call` carrying `_meta` (allowed as first message, DE-06) is processed under legacy semantics: no `resultType`, no serverInfo, no -32022/-32602 checks; a modern `ping` would be answered instead of -32601 (ping removed in 2026-07-28). `notifications/initialized` and `initialize` are accepted at any time and repeatedly (CoreManager.pas:57-63).
gaps.required: DE-05: modern `_meta` request → stateless modern semantics; `initialize` → legacy semantics scoped to the stdio process at the negotiated legacy version; DE-06/DE-07: both eras may coexist in one process and the era answer must be stable; DE-09: echo the requested legacy version when supported, else the latest supported legacy version; ST-07/ST-08: modern requests validated from their own `_meta` only, never from process state.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: unchanged behaviour except correct version echo (2025-03-26 clients now get 2025-03-26 and batching per GAP-ST-05; 2025-11-25 clients get 2025-11-25). Modern clients: become servable. Library consumers: `TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest(RequestBody, SessionID)` retained (delegates to the new overload with a default process session); `IMCPCapabilityManager` untouched; new `IMCPContextAwareManager` optional. Consumers that subclass/replace TMCPCoreManager must adopt the new `TMCPTransportSession` object to get per-process negotiation; otherwise they stay legacy-only (still valid).
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit Protocol/MCPServer.Session.pas: `TMCPTransportSession = class  NegotiatedLegacyVersion: string; Initialized: Boolean; Era: TMCPProtocolEra; Lock: TCriticalSection end` — one instance per stdio process (owned by TMCPStdioTransport) and per Mcp-Session-Id on HTTP (cross-area). In TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessMessage: `Era := eraModern if params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] exists else eraLegacy`; modern path: validate required _meta keys (-32602), version ∈ MCP_MODERN_VERSIONS (-32022), build TMCPRequestContext(ProtocolVersion, ClientCapabilities, ProgressToken) and dispatch through a modern method table (server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list, subscriptions/listen; `initialize`/`ping`/`notifications/initialized` → -32601 under modern _meta); legacy path: `initialize` → CoreManager negotiates `params.protocolVersion` ∈ MCP_LEGACY_VERSIONS else latest legacy, stores it in the session, returns it (DE-09); other legacy requests use `Session.NegotiatedLegacyVersion` (policy for legacy requests before initialize: keep today's permissive behaviour and assume the latest legacy version — see notes). Results: add `resultType:'complete'` only on the modern path so legacy responses are byte-compatible with today. Add `Era`/`ProtocolVersion` to IMCPRequestContext so managers (tools/resources) can shape results per era.

gaps.title: SIGTERM is swallowed in stdio mode; stdio loop never observes ShutdownEvent; leak-report dialog can block exit
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/MCPServer.dpr:65-72 installs `SignalHandler` for SIGINT/SIGTERM (lines 180-183) that only calls `ShutdownEvent.SetEvent`; `RunStdioServer` (dpr:114-141) never waits on or polls `ShutdownEvent` — `TMCPStdioTransport.Run` exits only on `Eof(Input)` (StdioTransport.pas:54). Because the handler replaces the default terminate action, SIGTERM from a client following the spec escalation no longer kills the process: the blocked `Readln` is either restarted (BSD `signal()` semantics) or raises EInOutError, which the `except` at StdioTransport.pas:73-95 turns into a spurious `{"id":null,"error":{"code":-32603}}` on stdout and then keeps looping. The client must escalate to SIGKILL. Windows: `ConsoleCtrlHandler` (dpr:47-62) returns True for CTRL_C/CTRL_BREAK (suppresses default exit) but clients use TerminateProcess, so only POSIX is affected. Additionally `ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown := True` (dpr:169) is unconditional; with the default memory manager on Windows a detected leak is reported via a modal dialog at process exit, which would hold the subprocess open after EOF until the client force-kills it.
gaps.required: SD-01: exit promptly on EOF (currently met when no leak dialog appears); SD-02: SIGTERM must terminate the process within a reasonable time; SD-03: server may close stdout and exit; ST-02: no non-MCP output (the spurious null-id error).
gaps.compatImpact: Both eras (legacy lifecycle describes the same SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation). No wire change. Library consumers embedding TMCPStdioTransport in their own .dpr are unaffected by the dpr fix but benefit from `Run` exposing a `Stop`/`RequestShutdown` method they can call from their own signal handler.
gaps.suggestedChange: MCPServer.dpr: in stdio mode either do not install the SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers (leave default terminate action) or make `SignalHandler` set the event AND unblock the reader (POSIX: `__close(0)`; Windows: `CloseHandle(GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE))`) so `Eof(Input)` returns True. TMCPStdioTransport: add `procedure Stop` (sets a volatile FTerminated flag checked by the reader loop, closes stdin handle) and make `Run` honour a `ShutdownEvent: TEvent` property; on EOF/Stop: stop accepting work, drain in-flight requests with a bounded wait (e.g. 2 s), send graceful `subscriptions/listen` completion results for open subscriptions (SD-04, once GAP-ST-07 exists), flush and close stdout, return. Set `ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown := {$IFDEF DEBUG}not HasStdioFlag{$ELSE}False{$ENDIF}` (or route leak reports to stderr via FastMM options) so no dialog can block exit. Log 'Signal received' only to stderr (already the case).

gaps.title: stdin/stdout use Delphi Text I/O with the system ANSI code page on Windows: non-ASCII JSON is not UTF-8 on the wire
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas:57 `Readln(Input, InputLine)` and :68/:89 `Writeln(Output, ...)` use the RTL `Text` records `Input`/`Output`, which decode/encode UnicodeString with the file's code page = `DefaultSystemCodePage` unless `SetTextCodePage` is called; nothing in the repo calls `SetTextCodePage`. On Windows (the primary target per /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/build.bat Win32/Win64 dcc32/dcc64 builds) that is the ANSI ACP (e.g. 1252), so a request containing e.g. 'é' or an emoji in tool arguments is mis-decoded and a response containing them is not UTF-8 (lossy '?'). On Linux the default is UTF-8 so it works there. `Writeln` also emits CRLF on Windows (not a violation: CR is JSON whitespace, but LF-only is what every SDK reader expects). NOTE: verified against RTL semantics, not by compiling — needs a runtime check on Windows with a non-ASCII echo call.
gaps.required: ST-04: "JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded" (both eras); ST-01 newline framing.
gaps.compatImpact: Both eras, Windows builds only. Fix is invisible to clients except that non-ASCII round-trips correctly. Library consumers: internal to `TMCPStdioTransport.Run`; consumers who wrote their own loop with `TMCPJsonRpcProcessor` are unaffected (they own their I/O).
gaps.suggestedChange: Minimal: at the top of `TMCPStdioTransport.Run` call `SetTextCodePage(Input, CP_UTF8); SetTextCodePage(Output, CP_UTF8);` and write with `Write(Output, Json + #10); Flush(Output)` instead of `Writeln`. Preferred (needed anyway for GAP-ST-01): replace Text I/O with `THandleStream` over `GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE/STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE)` (Windows) / fd 0 and 1 (POSIX); read with a `TStreamReader.Create(Stream, TEncoding.UTF8, False /*DetectBOM*/)` line reader (or a manual byte buffer split on #10, stripping a trailing #13); write bytes via `TEncoding.UTF8.GetBytes(Json + #10)` directly to the stream — do NOT use `TStreamWriter` with `TEncoding.UTF8`, which can emit a BOM preamble that is not a valid MCP message. Add a test fixture with a non-ASCII `echo` argument.

gaps.title: Library consumers must remember to set TLogger.UseStdErr themselves; TMCPStdioTransport itself logs and would write to stdout if they forget
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/MCPServer.dpr:161-167 sets `TLogger.UseStdErr := True` (only when `HasStdioFlag`) and then `LogToConsole := True`. `TMCPStdioTransport.Run` itself calls `TLogger.Info` (StdioTransport.pas:50-51,62,70,98) and `TLogger.DoWriteLog` writes with `WriteLn(LogLine)` to stdout whenever `FLogToConsole and not FUseStdErr` (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Logger.pas:177-180). Every tool/manager logs via TLogger (e.g. ToolsManager.pas:243,255; CoreManager.pas:81,133). README '### STDIO Transport' (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/README.md:112-130) says logs go to stderr but the 'Using as a Library' section does not tell consumers to set `UseStdErr`.
gaps.required: ST-02: "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message"; ST-03 stderr logging allowed.
gaps.compatImpact: Both eras. Shipped executable is already correct; the risk is only for library consumers who instantiate `TMCPStdioTransport` in their own program and enable `LogToConsole` — their stdout channel is silently corrupted with log lines. Forcing stderr inside the transport is a behaviour change only for such consumers and only in the direction the spec requires.
gaps.suggestedChange: In `TMCPStdioTransport.Create` set `TLogger.UseStdErr := True` (document it) and add a class-level guard `TLogger.StdoutReserved: Boolean` that `DoWriteLog` checks so console logging can never fall back to `Output` while a stdio transport exists; log a one-time warning to stderr if a consumer flips `UseStdErr` back to False. Update README 'Using as a Library' with an explicit stdio checklist (UseStdErr, no `Writeln` in tools, use `TLogger`). Keep `LogToConsole` default False (Logger.pas:103) so unit-initialization `RegisterTool` logs (Registration.pas:56) stay silent.

gaps.title: Outer stdio exception handler emits an uncorrelated id:null -32603 error for I/O failures and does not stop on a broken stdout
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas:73-95: `ProcessRequest` already catches its own exceptions and returns -32700/-32601/-32603 with the request id (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:204-218), so the outer `except` is reached only for failures outside request processing (Readln/Writeln/Flush EInOutError, logger failures, signal-interrupted reads). It then writes `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":...}}` to stdout — a response that corresponds to no request — and continues the loop; if stdout itself is the broken stream, the nested `Writeln` raises inside the handler and the exception escapes `Run` (dpr:193-195 logs it and the process exits, which is acceptable).
gaps.required: ST-13: error responses carry the request id except when the id could not be read from a malformed request; a transport-level failure is not that case. ST-02: only valid MCP messages on stdout. SD-03: on a closed output stream the server should just exit.
gaps.compatImpact: Both eras. Clients ignore null-id errors in practice (they cannot correlate them), so removing the write changes nothing visible; exiting on EPIPE makes shutdown cleaner.
gaps.suggestedChange: Delete the stdout write from the outer handler: log to stderr with `TLogger.Error`, and if the exception came from the writer (EInOutError on stdout) set FTerminated and break the loop so `Run` returns and the process exits (SD-03). Leave the -32700/null-id parse-error path inside `TMCPJsonRpcProcessor` as the only null-id producer. With GAP-ST-01 the writer thread should treat a write failure the same way (signal shutdown).

gaps.title: JSON-RPC batch arrays rejected with -32700 (2025-03-26 clients MUST be able to send batches)
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:52-56 raises 'JSON-RPC request must be an object' for a TJSONArray; the handler at :209-213 then reports JSONRPC_PARSE_ERROR (-32700) with id null because `JSONRequest` is nil — the wrong code even for an unsupported batch (JSON-RPC prescribes -32600). The HTTP path has array awareness only for the 202/notification check (IdHTTPServer.pas:453-465) and then calls the same processor.
gaps.required: ST-10 (2025-03-26 only): "MUST support receiving JSON-RPC batches"; batching removed from 2025-06-18 onward, so for negotiated versions ≥ 2025-06-18 and for modern requests an array should get -32600 Invalid Request.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy 2025-03-26 clients only (rare in practice; most SDKs never batched). No effect on 2025-06-18+/modern clients other than a more accurate error code (-32600 instead of -32700). Library consumers: internal to the processor; the returned string may now be a JSON array for batch input — consumers who parse the processor's return value as an object must handle that (document; gate on negotiated version so it cannot happen unless they serve 2025-03-26).
gaps.suggestedChange: In `TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessMessage`: if the parsed value is a TJSONArray and `Session.NegotiatedLegacyVersion = '2025-03-26'` → iterate elements, process each (requests and notifications), collect non-empty responses into a TJSONArray, return its JSON or '' if all were notifications (empty array → -32600 per JSON-RPC). Otherwise return `CreateErrorResponse(null, -32600, 'Batching not supported')`. Keep `ParseJSONRequest` for the object case. Decide explicitly whether 2025-03-26 is in `MCP_LEGACY_VERSIONS`; if it is dropped, this gap disappears and `initialize` for 2025-03-26 should negotiate up to 2025-06-18 (DE-09 allows that).

gaps.title: id:null silently treated as a notification; client-sent responses (no method) answered with a -32601 error
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:75-87 `ExtractRequestID` returns TValue.Empty for a present-but-null (or boolean/object) `id`, and :174-181 then treats the message as a notification and drops it without any error. A message with an `id` but no `method` (a JSON-RPC response — which clients MUST NOT send in 2026-07-28 and which this server never solicits since it never sends requests) falls through to :168-171 (MethodName = '') → :121-123 → error response -32601 'Method [] not found' with the same id, i.e. the server answers a response with an error response.
gaps.required: ST-12: request id MUST NOT be null (→ -32600 Invalid Request, id null since the id is unusable); ST-11: never respond to notifications; ST-05/patterns: clients do not send responses — a stray response should be ignored/logged, not answered; ST-13 error-id rules.
gaps.compatImpact: Both eras. Only malformed or stray messages are affected; conformant clients see no change.
gaps.suggestedChange: In `ProcessMessage`: (a) if the object has key `id` whose value is not TJSONString/TJSONNumber → return -32600 with id null; (b) if `method` is absent: if `result` or `error` present → log at Debug and return '' (ignore), else → -32600 with the parsed id; (c) optionally validate `jsonrpc = '2.0'` → -32600. Keep `ExtractRequestID` but add an `out IdPresent: Boolean` (or a `TMCPRequestId` record with `Kind: (ridNone, ridNull, ridString, ridNumber, ridInvalid)`).

gaps.title: No subscriptions/listen support on stdio (ack-first ordering, subscriptionId tagging, cancel-to-stop, graceful close)
gaps.current: No manager handles `subscriptions/listen` (CoreManager.pas:48-53, ToolsManager.pas:64-67, ResourcesManager.pas:59-64); initialize advertises `resources.subscribe:false, listChanged:false` (CoreManager.pas:116-124) so nothing is promised today. There is no server→client notification path at all on stdio (GAP-ST-01). The processor's one-request-one-response model (`ProcessRequest` returns a single string) cannot represent a long-lived request whose response is deferred until teardown.
gaps.required: If subscriptions are offered: `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged` MUST be the first message carrying the subscription id and no notification may precede it (per subscription id, interleaving with other subscriptions allowed); every notification on the stream MUST carry `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId` = listen request id (ST-06); server MUST NOT send notification types not requested; client `notifications/cancelled` referencing the listen id MUST stop the stream (CN-07/SEP-2575); on server-initiated teardown SHOULD send the `subscriptions/listen` result with `resultType:'complete'` and `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId` (SD-04); server-sent `notifications/cancelled` only for tearing down such a stream (CN-07).
gaps.compatImpact: Modern era only (legacy uses resources/subscribe + listChanged capability flags, currently advertised false). Purely additive for clients; only matters once the server advertises `tools.listChanged`/`resources.listChanged`/`resources.subscribe` in DiscoverResult. Library consumers: additive `IMCPSubscriptionSource` hook for managers that can raise list_changed/updated events; no existing API changes.
gaps.suggestedChange: Cross-area with the subscriptions/resources area; stdio-specific mechanics: `TMCPSubscriptionStream` (listen request id, agreed `SubscriptionFilter`, `IMCPMessageWriter`) created by a `TMCPSubscriptionsManager` (implements IMCPContextAwareManager for `subscriptions/listen`, returns a sentinel 'deferred' TValue so the transport does not write a response); on creation immediately write `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged` through the locked writer (guaranteeing ack-first per id since all later notifications for that id go through the same stream object); every notification is built with `params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId']` = cloned listen id; the inflight registry maps listen ids to streams so `notifications/cancelled` stops them (CN-07); `TMCPStdioTransport.Run` on EOF/Stop iterates open streams and writes `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<listenId>,"result":{"resultType":"complete","_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId":<listenId>}}}` before closing stdout (SD-04). Advertise `listChanged`/`subscribe` in DiscoverResult capabilities only when at least one source is registered.

alreadyConformant: ST-01 one message per line, no embedded newlines: responses are produced by `TJSONObject.ToJSON` (compact, escapes control characters) and written with a single `Writeln` — /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas:68 and :89 (error path deliberately built with the JSON writer, comment at :78-80); /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:202,140.

ST-02 nothing but MCP messages on stdout in the shipped executable: the only stdout writes in the tree are StdioTransport.pas:68 and :89 (grep of Writeln/WriteLn across src); the logger is switched to stderr before `LogToConsole` is enabled (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/MCPServer.dpr:161-167) and `TLogger.LogToConsole` defaults to False (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Logger.pas:103), so unit-initialization `TMCPRegistry.RegisterTool` logs (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:56, e.g. Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Echo.pas:46-50) never reach stdout.

ST-03 stderr logging: `WriteLn(ErrOutput, LogLine)` when `FUseStdErr` (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Logger.pas:177-178); README documents 'Log diagnostic messages to stderr' (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/README.md:123). ST-14: the server already logs to stderr rather than via the deprecated `notifications/message` feature.
Per-message flush so the client sees each line immediately: `Flush(Output)` at StdioTransport.pas:69 and :93.

SD-01 exit on EOF: `while not Eof(Input)` (StdioTransport.pas:54) → `Run` returns → `RunStdioServer` frees transport/settings and the program ends (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/MCPServer.dpr:134-140, 188-189); 'STDIO transport stopped - EOF reached' logged at :98.
ST-05 / CN-07 by construction: there is no code path that writes a JSON-RPC request or a `notifications/cancelled` to stdout; the server only ever writes responses (StdioTransport.pas:64-71).
ST-11 notifications never get a response: requests without id return '' (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:174-181) and the transport writes nothing when the result is '' (StdioTransport.pas:66).

CN-03/CN-04/CN-05 degenerate conformance: late or unknown `notifications/cancelled` are logged and ignored, never answered with an error (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:179-180) — the 'processing has already completed' MAY-ignore case.
PG-07: choosing not to send any progress notifications is explicitly permitted; the server currently sends none.
ST-13 for malformed input: unparseable lines get -32700 with id null (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:209-217), the one case where a null id is allowed; `ExtractRequestID` is nil-safe (:69-73).

DE-03 today (as a pure legacy server): `server/discover` yields -32601 'Method [server/discover] not found...' (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:121-123, 214-215), which the 2026-07-28 stdio probe classifies as 'legacy → fall back to initialize', so dual-era clients interoperate with the current binary correctly.
Blank/whitespace-only lines are skipped rather than answered with a parse error (StdioTransport.pas:59-60) — tolerant of clients that emit an extra newline.
Legacy shutdown for the HTTP mode: SIGINT/SIGTERM and Windows console control handlers set `ShutdownEvent`, and `RunHTTPServer` waits on it and stops the server cleanly (dpr:46-72, 101-107, 176-183).
notes: Sandbox limitation: Delphi cannot be compiled here. Findings about RTL Text I/O code pages, CRLF line endings and TStreamWriter BOM preambles (GAP-ST-02) are grounded in documented RTL semantics and must be confirmed with a Windows runtime test (echo tool with 'é'/emoji over --stdio) before/after the fix.

Open design question — `supportedVersions` in DiscoverResult: the versioning page's -32022 example lists both '2026-07-28' and '2025-11-25' under `supported`, but the stdio probe says the client will 'select a mutually supported version from supportedVersions and continue' with per-request _meta. Recommend listing only versions the server serves statelessly (['2026-07-28']) in `supportedVersions`/`data.supported`; legacy versions are reachable only through `initialize` (DE-05). Flag for the core/lifecycle area to decide consistently across stdio and HTTP.

Open design question — legacy requests (no `_meta`) arriving before any `initialize` on the process: the legacy lifecycle makes initialize-first a client MUST and does not require servers to reject; the current code processes them permissively (CoreManager/ToolsManager never check state). 2026-07-28 stdio.mdx warns that such servers 'would process an era-ambiguous method (such as tools/call) under legacy semantics', which is why modern clients are told to probe. Recommendation: keep permissive behaviour (assume the latest supported legacy version) to avoid breaking existing tests/consumers; document it. Alternative: -32600 'initialize required' — stricter but a behaviour change for library consumers' integration tests.

Because clients cache the era per process (DE-07), `server/discover` must keep returning DiscoverResult even after an `initialize` has switched the process to legacy mode, and an `initialize` must keep working after modern requests were served (DE-06 'concurrently'). Do not make era a one-way latch on the process; make it a per-request property with a per-process *legacy negotiated version* side-slot.

Modern-era removals relevant to the stdio dispatcher: `ping`, `logging/setLevel`, `notifications/initialized`, `resources/subscribe` are not modern methods (2026-07-28 changelog items 4-5). Under modern `_meta` they should map to -32601; under legacy they keep working. `notifications/message` must never be emitted for modern requests lacking `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel` (the server never emits it today).

Concurrency facts for GAP-ST-01: `TMCPJsonRpcProcessor` is stateless (only FManagerRegistry) and is already shared across Indy threads; `TMCPToolsManager.FTools` and `TMCPRegistry` dictionaries are read-only after construction; `TMCPCoreManager.FSessionID` and `TServerStatusResource` counters (Resource.Server.pas:95-108, plain Inc/Dec) are not thread-safe and are already racy under HTTP — fix with TInterlocked when introducing stdio concurrency. `TLogger` is lock-protected (Logger.pas:165-198).

The `Pos('not found', E.Message) → -32601` heuristic (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215) is a dual-era hazard: once server/discover exists, any exception text containing 'not found' raised while serving a modern request (e.g. 'Resource not found', 'Tool not found') would be reported as -32601, which a probing client could misread as 'legacy server'. Replace with typed exceptions before shipping GAP-DE-01.

SEP-2575 '### Supporting Multiple Versions' is the design precedent for the dual-era server: keep `initialize` for legacy clients and expose `server/discover` and the stateless RPCs for modern ones on the same process; SEP-2575 'Why is it important for STDIO to be stateless as well?' explains why stdio must not treat process lifetime as a session (matches ST-08 note).

Legacy `ping` from the client is in scope of the blocking-loop gap: with the current loop a ping during a long tool call is answered only after the tool returns; 2025-11-25 ping.mdx lets the client 'Consider the connection stale; Terminate the connection' on timeout. Concurrency (GAP-ST-01) fixes this without any change to `TMCPCoreManager.Ping`.

Windows console control handler returns True for CTRL_C/CTRL_BREAK (dpr:47-62), suppressing default termination; this does not affect MCP clients, which use TerminateProcess/Job Objects, but means a human running `MCPServer.exe --stdio` in a console cannot Ctrl+C it (only Ctrl+Z/EOF works). Consider not installing the handler in stdio mode.

StdioTransport.pas:62 and :70 log the full request and response lines at Info to stderr. Allowed by ST-03, but clients 'MAY capture' stderr, so tool arguments (possibly secrets) end up in client logs; consider Debug level or truncation.

README (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/README.md:112-130 '### STDIO Transport', and 'Using as a Library') should gain: dual-era behaviour (server/discover probe vs initialize), cancellation/progress support and how tools use `TMCPRequestContext.Current`, the `MaxConcurrentRequests` opt-out, the `TLogger.UseStdErr` requirement for embedders, and the exact stdout framing (UTF-8, LF, one message per line).

Timeouts (cancellation.mdx '## Timeouts') apply to the *sender* of requests; since the server never sends requests in the modern era (and sends none today in legacy either), no server-side timeout requirement applies here. If the HTTP transport ever emits legacy server→client requests (sampling/elicitation) that is another area.

The ecosystem's stdio clients (Codex per README:360-373, Claude Desktop, MCP Inspector) all split stdout on '\n' and tolerate a trailing '\r'; switching to LF-only output (GAP-ST-02) is therefore safe and removes a Windows/Linux difference in the byte stream.

gapReports.area: Tools: definitions, JSON Schema 2020-12, annotations, icons, structuredContent, tool errors, x-mcp-header, naming, tools/list envelope (resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope/pagination/ordering), MRTR and progress on tools/call

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx, heading 'Capabilities' (identical sentence in docs/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools.mdx and 2025-06-18); schema.ts ServerCapabilities.tools = { listChanged?: boolean }
requirements.text: "Servers that support tools **MUST** declare the `tools` capability" with shape {"tools": {"listChanged": true|false}}. `listChanged` is the only defined key. Modern era: declared in the server/discover result; legacy era: in the initialize result.

"Servers that declare the `tools` capability **MUST** respond to `tools/list` requests with the set of tools currently available to the requesting client. This set **MAY** be empty and **MAY** change over time ..., but **MUST NOT** vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection. The set **MAY** vary by the authorization presented on the request".

"Servers **SHOULD** return tools in a deterministic order (i.e., the same ordering across requests when the underlying set of tools has not changed). Deterministic ordering enables clients to reliably cache the tool list and improves LLM prompt cache hit rates".

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx, headings 'Result Responses' and 'ResultType'; schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts interface Result ('Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field'); schema.json 2026-07-28: CallToolResult.required=[content,resultType], ListToolsResult.required=[cacheScope,resultType,tools,ttlMs]
requirements.text: "The `result` **MUST** include a `resultType` field to indicate the type of the result." "A `resultType` of `"complete"` indicates the request completed successfully"; "`"input_required"` indicates the request is incomplete and more information is needed". Applies to every tools/list and tools/call result. Legacy servers omit it and clients treat absence as "complete".

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching.mdx, headings 'Cacheable Results' and 'Time-to-Live (TTL) Field'; schema.ts ListToolsResult extends PaginatedResult, CacheableResult { ttlMs: number (@minimum 0); cacheScope: "public"|"private" }
requirements.text: "Servers MUST include caching hints on results with `resultType: "complete"` returned by the following operations: `server/discover`, `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read`"; "Servers **MUST** provide a `ttlMs` value that is `>= 0`"; `cacheScope` is required and is "public" ("appropriate for lists of tools ... when they are identical for all users") or "private". Interim `input_required` results "are not cacheable and carry no caching hints".
"Servers **MUST** apply the same `cacheScope` to all response pages for a given list request." Servers **MAY** return different `ttlMs` per page.

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination.mdx, headings 'Operations Supporting Pagination', 'Implementation Guidelines', 'Error Handling' (same in 2025-11-25/2025-06-18)
requirements.text: `tools/list` supports cursor pagination: request `params.cursor` (opaque string), response optional `nextCursor`. "Servers **SHOULD**: Provide stable cursors; Handle invalid cursors gracefully"; "Invalid cursors **SHOULD** result in an error with code -32602 (Invalid params)." Page size is server-determined; pagination itself is optional (omit nextCursor when complete).

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx, heading 'Tool' (identical in 2025-11-25); schema.ts Tool.inputSchema: { $schema?: string; type: "object"; [key: string]: unknown }
requirements.text: `inputSchema` "**MUST** be a valid JSON Schema object (not `null`)", "Defaults to 2020-12 if no `$schema` field is present", root `type` must be "object" ("Tool arguments are always JSON objects, so `type: "object"` is required at the root"). "For tools with no parameters, use one of these valid approaches: `{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false }` - **Recommended**; `{ "type": "object" }`".

requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts interface Tool (inputSchema/outputSchema doc comments); SEP /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/seps/2106-json-schema-2020-12.md 'Specification'; changelog.mdx minor change 10. Legacy restriction: schema/2025-11-25/schema.ts Tool.outputSchema 'Currently restricted to type: "object" at the root level' and inputSchema limited to $schema/type/properties/required
requirements.text: Modern: "Beyond that, any JSON Schema 2020-12 keyword may appear alongside `type` — including composition keywords (`oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not`), conditional keywords (`if`/`then`/`else`), reference keywords (`$ref`, `$defs`, `$anchor`)"; outputSchema "can be any valid JSON Schema 2020-12" (array/primitive roots allowed). Legacy 2025-06-18/2025-11-25: inputSchema/outputSchema are limited to type/properties/required (+$schema in 2025-11-25) and outputSchema root MUST be `type: "object"`.

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx, headings 'Schema Dialect', 'Implementation Requirements', 'Schema Validation' (same text in docs/specification/2025-11-25/basic/index.mdx; absent from 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26)
requirements.text: "Clients and servers **MUST** support JSON Schema 2020-12 for schemas without an explicit `$schema` field"; "Clients and servers **MUST** validate schemas according to their declared or default dialect. They **MUST** handle unsupported dialects gracefully by returning an appropriate error"; "Schemas **MUST** be valid according to their declared or default dialect"; "Clients and servers **SHOULD** document which schema dialects they support"; "Implementors are RECOMMENDED to use JSON Schema 2020-12".

"Implementations **MUST NOT** automatically dereference `$ref` values that resolve to a network URI." Opt-in fetching "**MUST** be disabled by default"; "Schemas that fail to validate due to an unresolved external `$ref` **SHOULD** be rejected rather than silently treated as permissive"; implementations "**SHOULD** apply reasonable bounds, such as a maximum schema depth, a cap on the total number of subschemas, or a per-validation time budget" when validating composition keywords.

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx, heading 'Tool Names' (identical in 2025-11-25; originates from seps/986-specify-format-for-tool-names.md, whose 64-char/'/' variant was superseded by the spec text)
requirements.text: "Tool names **SHOULD** be between 1 and 128 characters in length (inclusive)." "Tool names **SHOULD** be considered case-sensitive." "The following **SHOULD** be the only allowed characters: uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), underscore (_), hyphen (-), and dot (.)" "Tool names **SHOULD NOT** contain spaces, commas, or other special characters." "Tool names **SHOULD** be unique within a server." Server `name` "**SHOULD NOT** be relied upon for disambiguation".

requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts interfaces Tool, ToolAnnotations, BaseMetadata; docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx heading 'Tool'. (title/outputSchema/_meta since 2025-06-18; icons since 2025-11-25; annotations since 2025-03-26)
requirements.text: Tool definition fields: `name` (required), `title` (optional; "Display name precedence order is: `title`, `annotations.title`, then `name`"), `description` (optional), `inputSchema` (required), `outputSchema` (optional), `icons` (optional), `annotations` (optional: `title`, `readOnlyHint` default false, `destructiveHint` default true, `idempotentHint` default false, `openWorldHint` default true), `_meta` (optional). "clients **MUST** consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers" (hints only).

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx, heading '`icons`'; schema.ts interfaces Icons, Icon (2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28)
requirements.text: Tools MAY carry `icons`: array of `{ src (required URI: HTTPS URL or data: URI), mimeType?, sizes? (e.g. ["48x48"], ["any"]), theme? ("light"|"dark") }`. Clients "**MUST** reject icon URIs that use unsafe schemes" other than HTTPS/`data:` and MUST support image/png and image/jpeg, SHOULD support svg+xml/webp — so a server should only publish https:// or data: PNG/JPEG (optionally SVG/WebP) icons.

"MCP servers **MAY** designate specific tool parameters to be mirrored into HTTP headers using an `x-mcp-header` extension property" (value = name part of `Mcp-Param-{name}`). If used, the value "**MUST NOT** be empty", "**MUST** match HTTP field-name token syntax (`1*tchar`)", "**MUST NOT** contain control characters", "**MUST** be case-insensitively unique among all `x-mcp-header` values in the `inputSchema`", "**MUST** only be applied to parameters with primitive types (integer, string, boolean). Parameters with type `number` are not permitted. Integer values **MUST** be within the safe range ... (−2^53+1 to 2^53−1)", "**MUST** only be applied to properties that are _statically reachable_ from the schema root" (chain of `properties` keys only; not through items/oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not/if/then/else/$ref). Clients "**MUST** reject tool definitions where any `x-mcp-header` value violates these constraints" (tool excluded from tools/list). "Server developers **SHOULD NOT** mark sensitive parameters ... with `x-mcp-header`".

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx, headings 'Standard Request Headers', 'Server Behavior for Custom Headers', 'Server Validation', 'Value Encoding'
requirements.text: On Streamable HTTP, `Mcp-Method` (=method) and `Mcp-Name` (=params.name for tools/call) "are **REQUIRED** for compliance". "Servers **MUST** reject requests with a recognized `Mcp-Param-{Name}` header that contains invalid characters"; "Any server that processes the message body **MUST** validate that encoded header values, after decoding if Base64-encoded, match the corresponding values in the request body. Servers **MUST** reject requests with a `400 Bad Request` HTTP status and JSON-RPC error code `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) if any validation fails." Table: value provided → "Server MUST validate header matches body"; value `null` or parameter absent → "Server MUST NOT expect the header"; client omits header but value in body → "Server MUST reject the request". Servers "**MUST** decode an encoded `Mcp-Name` or `Mcp-Param-{Name}` value" (`=?base64?...?=` sentinel) before comparing; integers "**SHOULD** compare ... numerically".

requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts interface CallToolResult (`content: ContentBlock[]` non-optional; schema.json required=[content,resultType]; 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 required=[content]); docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx heading 'Tool Result' and sub-headings 'Text Content', 'Image Content', 'Audio Content', 'Resource Links', 'Embedded Resources'
requirements.text: A tools/call result MUST contain `content` (array of content blocks, may be empty). Block shapes: text `{type:"text", text}`; image `{type:"image", data (base64), mimeType}`; audio `{type:"audio", data (base64), mimeType}`; resource_link `{type:"resource_link", uri, name, title?, description?, mimeType?, size?, icons?}`; embedded `{type:"resource", resource:{uri, mimeType?, text | blob}}`. "All content types ... support optional annotations" `{audience?: ("user"|"assistant")[], priority?: 0..1, lastModified?: ISO 8601}` and `_meta`. "A tool **MAY** return links to Resources"; "Resources **MAY** be embedded". Note: 2025-03-26 ContentBlock union has no `resource_link`.

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx, heading 'Structured Content'; schema.ts CallToolResult.structuredContent?: unknown. Legacy: 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 tools.mdx 'Structured Content' ("returned as a JSON object") and schema.ts structuredContent?: { [key: string]: unknown }
requirements.text: Modern: "**Structured** content is returned as a JSON value in the `structuredContent` field of a result. This can be any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null) that conforms to the tool's `outputSchema` if one is defined." Legacy (2025-06-18, 2025-11-25): structuredContent MUST be a JSON object; 2025-03-26 has no structuredContent at all.

"If an output schema is provided: Servers **MUST** provide structured results that conform to this schema. Clients **SHOULD** validate structured results against this schema." (i.e. when a tool advertises `outputSchema`, every successful result must carry a `structuredContent` that validates against it.)

"For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block." SEP-2106 strengthens this for non-object values: "servers using array or primitive `structuredContent` MUST also emit a `TextContent` block containing the serialized JSON".

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx, heading 'Error Handling' (same in 2025-11-25; 2025-06-18/2025-03-26 listed 'Invalid arguments' under protocol errors, clarified by seps/1303-input-validation-errors-as-tool-execution-errors.md as backward compatible); schema.ts CallToolResult.isError doc
requirements.text: "**Protocol Errors** indicate issues with the request structure itself ...: Unknown tool; Malformed requests (requests that fail to satisfy CallToolRequest schema); Server errors. They are returned as standard JSON-RPC errors" e.g. `{"code": -32602, "message": "Unknown tool: invalid_tool_name"}`. "**Tool Execution Errors** ...: API failures; Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range); Business logic errors. They are reported in tool results with `isError: true`". schema.ts: "Any errors that originate from the tool SHOULD be reported inside the result object, with `isError` set to true, _not_ as an MCP protocol-level error response ... However, any errors in _finding_ the tool, an error indicating that the server does not support tool calls, or any other exceptional conditions, should be reported as an MCP error response." `isError` "If not set, this is assumed to be false".
"Servers **MUST**: Validate all tool inputs; Implement proper access controls; Rate limit tool invocations; Sanitize tool outputs".

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx, heading 'Input Required Tool Results'; docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr.mdx headings 'Supported Requests', 'Server Requirements (Basic Workflow)', 'Error Handling', 'Security Considerations'; schema.ts InputRequiredResult, InputResponseRequestParams (CallToolRequestParams extends it: inputResponses?, requestState?)
requirements.text: "Servers **MAY** respond to `tools/call` with an `InputRequiredResult`" (`resultType: "input_required"`, `inputRequests?`, `requestState?`). If used: "`inputRequests` keys ... **MUST** be unique within the scope of the request"; values "**MUST** be one of ElicitRequest, CreateMessageRequest, or ListRootsRequest"; "servers **MUST** treat `requestState` as an attacker-controlled input. If `requestState` influences authorization, resource access, or business logic, servers **MUST** protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and **MUST** reject state that fails verification"; "**SHOULD** include ... the authenticated principal ... a short expiry (TTL) ... an identifier for the originating request"; "Servers **MUST** include at least one of `inputRequests` or `requestState` in every `InputRequiredResult`"; "Servers **MUST NOT** send an `inputRequests` that the client has not declared support for in its capabilities"; "Servers **MUST NOT** assume that clients will fulfill the `inputRequests` or retry"; "Servers **MUST NOT** send `InputRequiredResult` responses on any other client requests" (only prompts/get, resources/read, tools/call); "Servers **SHOULD** validate that the data provided by the client is a valid `InputResponses` object"; unexpected parameters "**SHOULD** ignore"; missing info → "**SHOULD** respond with a new `InputRequiredResult`". Legacy era has no MRTR (server-initiated requests instead); a dual-era server must not emit `input_required` to legacy clients.

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress.mdx, headings 'Progress Flow', 'Behavior Requirements', 'Implementation Notes'; basic/index.mdx '_meta' reserved key `progressToken`
requirements.text: A tools/call may carry `params._meta.progressToken` (string or integer). "The server **MAY** then send progress notifications" (`notifications/progress` with progressToken, progress, total?, message?). "Progress notifications **MUST** only reference tokens that: Were provided in an active request; Are associated with an in-progress operation"; "The `progress` value **MUST** increase with each notification"; "Progress notifications **MUST** stop after completion"; both parties "**SHOULD** implement rate limiting". Servers "**MAY**: Choose not to send any progress notifications".

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx, heading '`_meta`', sub-section 'Per-response protocol fields'; schema.ts ResultMetaObject
requirements.text: "Servers **SHOULD** include the following `io.modelcontextprotocol/*` field in every result's `_meta`, unless specifically configured not to do so ...: `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo` (Implementation)". Applies to tools/list and tools/call results (cross-cutting with the lifecycle area). Implementations "**MUST NOT** make assumptions about values" at reserved `_meta` keys; tool-supplied `_meta` must be merged, not overwritten.

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools.mdx, heading 'List Changed Notification' (legacy: 2025-11-25 same heading, sent on the server→client channel)
requirements.text: "When the list of available tools changes, servers that declared the `listChanged` capability **SHOULD** send a notification" `notifications/tools/list_changed` — modern: only "to clients that have opened a `subscriptions/listen` stream with `toolsListChanged: true`". Not required when `listChanged` is not declared.
"Servers that use embedded resources **SHOULD** implement the `resources` capability".

When mapping tool/protocol failures to JSON-RPC codes: "Implementations **MUST NOT** emit any code from this sub-range [-32020..-32099] that is not defined by this specification and **MUST** use defined codes only with their specified meanings"; "New codes **MUST NOT** be allocated in [-32000..-32019]"; "**MUST NOT** emit ... `-32002` ... `-32042`". Defined: -32020 HeaderMismatch, -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapability, -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersion; standard -32700/-32600..-32603.

requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts interface CallToolRequestParams (`arguments?: { [key: string]: unknown }`; identical optionality in 2025-03-26/2025-06-18/2025-11-25); tools.mdx 'Error Handling' (only requests failing the CallToolRequest schema are protocol errors)
requirements.text: Derived from the schema: `params.name` is a required string; `params.arguments` is OPTIONAL. A `tools/call` without `arguments` (e.g. for a zero-parameter tool) satisfies the CallToolRequest schema and MUST be processed normally, not treated as malformed and not allowed to crash. A request whose `arguments` is present but not an object, or whose `name` is missing/not a string, fails the schema and is a protocol error (-32602).

gaps.title: tools/list result lacks resultType, ttlMs and cacheScope
gaps.current: TMCPToolsManager.BuildToolListResponse (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:213-228) emits only {"tools": [...]}. No manager or the processor (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:192-200) adds an envelope.
gaps.required: Modern results MUST carry resultType:"complete"; tools/list MUST additionally carry ttlMs (>=0) and cacheScope ("public"|"private"), same cacheScope on every page. schema.json 2026-07-28 marks all four as required, so a validating modern client rejects the current response.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients tolerate the extra fields: Result in schema.json 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 has additionalProperties:{} (open), so emitting ttlMs/cacheScope unconditionally is safe. Library consumers: custom IMCPCapabilityManager implementations get resultType for free if it is injected in TMCPJsonRpcProcessor; TMCPToolsManager API unchanged, two new optional properties.
gaps.suggestedChange: (1) In TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest, after ExecuteMethodCall, when the request is modern (per-request _meta present / negotiated era from the lifecycle area) and the result object has no 'resultType', add 'resultType':'complete' (and merge _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo, see TL-25) — this covers custom managers. (2) In TMCPToolsManager add published properties ListTtlMs: Integer (default 0) and ListCacheScope: string (default 'public'); BuildToolListResponse adds TJSONNumber(ListTtlMs) as 'ttlMs' and 'cacheScope' always (harmless for legacy). Optionally read defaults from TMCPSettings (ToolsListTtlMs/ToolsListCacheScope in settings.ini). Because the list is static (built once in the constructor) a positive TTL such as 300000 is safe; keep 0 as the conservative default.

gaps.title: tools/call result lacks resultType
gaps.current: TMCPToolsManager.BuildToolCallResponse (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:130-183) never adds resultType; CallToolResult.required = [content, resultType] in schema.json 2026-07-28.
gaps.required: Every modern result MUST include resultType ("complete", or "input_required" for MRTR).
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients ignore/tolerate the extra field (open Result). No library API change if injected centrally.
gaps.suggestedChange: Same envelope injection as GAP-TL-01 (processor-level, era-aware). ToolsManager must set resultType itself only for InputRequiredResult ('input_required', GAP-TL-19) so the processor's 'add if absent' rule leaves it alone.

gaps.title: TMCPToolBase<T,R> results have structuredContent but no content array
gaps.current: TMCPToolBase<T,R>.Execute returns a TJSONObject (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:183-202); BuildToolCallResponse's TJSONObject branch (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:168-181) adds only 'structuredContent' (+ optional isError) — the required 'content' field is absent and no text fallback is produced.
gaps.required: CallToolResult.content is required in every revision (schema.json required=[content] / [content,resultType]); a tool returning structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block (MUST for non-object values per SEP-2106).
gaps.compatImpact: Purely additive on the wire; consumers using TMCPToolBase<T,R> get a valid result. No API change.
gaps.suggestedChange: In BuildToolCallResponse's TJSONObject branch, also add 'content': [ {type:'text', text: JsonResult.ToJSON} ] before 'structuredContent'. Do the same in the new TMCPToolResult path (GAP-TL-15) when SetStructuredContent is used without explicit text.

gaps.title: Unknown tool returns an isError result instead of JSON-RPC -32602
gaps.current: TMCPToolsManager.CallTool (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:245-248) sets ResultValue := 'Error: Tool not found: X' which BuildToolCallResponse turns into {content:[text], isError:true}. Raising a plain Exception would not help: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor maps any message containing 'not found' to -32601 (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215) and everything else to -32603.
gaps.required: "Unknown tool" is a protocol error returned as a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 (both eras).
gaps.compatImpact: Clients that relied on a text result for a missing tool (none spec-conformant) see a JSON-RPC error instead. Library consumers: new exception class is additive; custom managers may adopt it to control error codes.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add to MCPServer.Types (or new MCPServer.Errors.pas): EMCPProtocolError = class(Exception) with property Code: Integer and optional Data: TJSONValue; constants MCP_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMS = -32602 etc. TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest catches EMCPProtocolError first and uses E.Code (and data) in CreateErrorResponse; keep the existing heuristic for other exceptions. TMCPToolsManager.CallTool raises EMCPProtocolError.Create(-32602, 'Unknown tool: ' + ToolName) when FTools.TryGetValue fails.

gaps.title: Malformed tools/call params produce an isError result instead of -32602
gaps.current: ExtractToolNameAndArguments (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:96-118) returns False for nil params / missing or empty name; a non-string name is silently stringified (NameValue.Value) and a non-object 'arguments' is silently treated as absent (line 116-117). CallTool then returns BuildToolCallResponse('Error: Invalid tool parameters') (lines 237-241), i.e. isError:true.
gaps.required: "Malformed requests (requests that fail to satisfy CallToolRequest schema)" are protocol errors (-32602).
gaps.compatImpact: Wire behaviour changes only for invalid requests. No library API change.
gaps.suggestedChange: In ExtractToolNameAndArguments raise EMCPProtocolError(-32602, 'Invalid params: name must be a non-empty string') when Params=nil, name missing, or NameValue is not TJSONString; raise EMCPProtocolError(-32602, 'Invalid params: arguments must be an object') when 'arguments' exists but is not TJSONObject. Keep Arguments=nil (or empty object, see GAP-TL-06) when the key is absent.

gaps.title: tools/call without 'arguments' passes a nil TJSONObject into the deserializer (nil dereference)
gaps.current: ExtractToolNameAndArguments leaves Arguments=nil when the key is absent (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:103, 115-117); TMCPToolBase<T>.Execute / <T,R>.Execute call TMCPSerializer.Deserialize<T>(Arguments) unconditionally (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:162, 189); DeserializeObject iterates 'for Pair in Json do' on the nil object (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:111) — this dereferences nil and is expected to raise an access violation, which ExecuteTool (ToolsManager.pas:122-127) converts into {isError:true, text:'Error executing tool: Access violation ...'}. (Could not compile/run Delphi in this environment; conclusion is from reading the code path.) Even the zero-parameter get_time tool hits this path when a client omits 'arguments', which the schema explicitly allows.
gaps.required: `arguments` is optional in CallToolRequestParams in all revisions; a request without it must be processed normally.
gaps.compatImpact: Fix is invisible to conforming clients; library consumers' tools receive an empty object instead of nil (custom TMCPToolBase.Execute implementations that already guard nil keep working).
gaps.suggestedChange: In TMCPToolsManager.CallTool, when 'arguments' is absent create a local empty TJSONObject (owned by the manager, freed after Execute) and pass it; additionally make TMCPSerializer.DeserializeObject nil-safe (if not Assigned(Json) then Exit after the required-check of GAP-TL-07). Add a unit test/manual test: {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_time"}}.

gaps.title: Tool input validation is incomplete (required not enforced, types silently coerced, hand-written schemas never validated)
gaps.current: TMCPSerializer.DeserializeObject skips properties absent from the JSON (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:130-131) so a missing required parameter silently keeps the default value although the schema advertised it in 'required' (Schema.Generator.pas:93-94, 140-150). Type mismatches are coerced: non-numeric JSON for Integer → StrToIntDef(...,0) (Serializer.pas:199-209), Float → 0, Boolean from any string (lines 224-236), wrong-typed array elements dropped (lines 403-410). Only unknown parameter names (lines 111-118) and enum values (lines 285-288) are rejected. Tools deriving from the non-generic TMCPToolBase (Tool.Base.pas:27-42, BuildSchema/Execute abstract) get no validation at all.
gaps.required: "Servers **MUST**: Validate all tool inputs"; "servers **MUST** validate schemas according to their declared or default dialect"; validation failures are tool execution errors with actionable text (SEP-1303).
gaps.compatImpact: Behaviour change: tools whose callers omitted a parameter that is not marked [Optional] now get isError:true instead of a default value — this is what the advertised schema already promised. Provide TMCPSerializer.StrictMode (default True) as an escape hatch. Custom TMCPToolBase tools unaffected unless they call the new validator.
gaps.suggestedChange: (a) In DeserializeObject, before the property loop, raise EArgumentException('Missing required parameter "%s"') for every writable property without OptionalAttribute that is absent from Json; raise EArgumentException('Parameter "%s": expected integer, got string') on type-kind mismatches instead of StrToIntDef/StrToFloatDef fallbacks. (b) Add MCPServer.Schema.Validator.pas with class function TMCPSchemaValidator.Validate(const Schema: TJSONObject; const Instance: TJSONValue; out Errors: TArray<string>): Boolean covering type, required, enum, properties (recursive), items, additionalProperties, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, pattern (TRegEx), const, nullable type arrays; never resolve $ref (same-document '#/$defs/...' only), depth cap (TL-11). (c) TMCPToolsManager.ExecuteTool validates Arguments against Tool.InputSchema when the tool does not derive from the generic bases (or always, cheap) and returns isError with the joined messages. (d) Document supported dialect (2020-12 subset) in README.

gaps.title: Schema generator maps Integer/Int64 to "number" instead of "integer"
gaps.current: TMCPSchemaGenerator.GetJsonTypeFromRttiType: tkInteger, tkInt64 → 'number' (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas:115).
gaps.required: JSON Schema 2020-12 has a distinct "integer" type; the basic spec's own example uses {"type":"integer","minimum":0}; x-mcp-header MUST only be applied to integer/string/boolean and "Parameters with type `number` are not permitted", so no Integer parameter of this library could ever be header-mirrored; LLM clients may also send 3.5 for a 'number'.
gaps.compatImpact: Emitted schema text changes (consumers snapshotting schemas in tests must update). The deserializer already accepts integers; no runtime behaviour change for clients.
gaps.suggestedChange: Change the mapping to 'integer' for tkInteger/tkInt64 (and tkChar/tkWChar → 'string'). Keep tkFloat → 'number', but map TDateTime/TDate/TTime (RttiType.Handle = TypeInfo(TDateTime) etc.) to 'string' with 'format':'date-time' (and teach ConvertJsonToValue/ConvertValueToJson ISO 8601 via System.DateUtils.ISO8601ToDate/DateToISO8601). Detect Boolean via RttiType.Handle = TypeInfo(Boolean) (also ByteBool/WordBool/LongBool) instead of RttiType.Name = 'Boolean' (line 119).

gaps.title: Nested objects emit no properties and arrays emit empty items; sets emit untyped arrays
gaps.current: GetJsonTypeFromRttiType returns bare 'object' for any tkClass other than TJSONArray (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas:124-128) and GenerateSchema adds 'items': {} for every array (lines 68-69) — although TMCPSerializer can deserialize nested classes, TArray<T> and TList<T> with typed elements (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:242-257, 377-443). tkSet → 'array' with empty items (line 123). Result: LLMs cannot see the shape of nested inputs, and generated outputSchemas under-describe structuredContent.
gaps.required: Schemas MUST be valid 2020-12 (they are) but MUST also describe inputs so the server can 'Validate all tool inputs'; outputSchema is meant to let clients 'validate structured results'. The generator should emit the full shape it knows from RTTI.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive schema detail; no wire-breaking change. Library consumers with nested param classes get richer schemas automatically.
gaps.suggestedChange: Refactor TMCPSchemaGenerator into a recursive GenerateTypeSchema(RttiType, Visited: TList<PTypeInfo>, Depth): TJSONObject: tkClass (non-TJSONValue) → recurse into properties (object with properties/required); TJSONObject/TJSONValue → {} (any); TJSONArray → {type:array}; TRttiDynamicArrayType → items := GenerateTypeSchema(ElementType); TList<T>/TObjectList<T> → items from the 'Add' parameter type (reuse FindAddMethod logic); tkSet → {type:array, items:{type:string, enum:[...]}, uniqueItems:true}; tkRecord → object over fields; cycle guard by Visited/Depth (emit {} on cycle). Share one RTTI→JSON-type table between generator and serializer (GAP-TL-10).

gaps.title: structuredContent produced by TMCPToolBase<T,R> can violate the generated outputSchema
gaps.current: GenerateSchema(R) marks every read/write property as required (Schema.Generator.pas:93-94, 140-150), but TMCPSerializer.Serialize/ConvertValueToJson omits: (a) dynamic-array/TList properties — there is no tkDynArray branch and TList is not a TJSONValue (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:333-374), so array-typed properties that the schema declares as required arrays never appear; (b) nil object properties (Value.IsEmpty → Exit at line 330) declared as required objects; (c) non-Boolean enumerations are serialized through Value.AsBoolean (lines 346-356) while the schema says {type:string, enum:[...]} (lines 87-91, 152-170) — wrong type or EInvalidCast. Only object roots are produced (fine for legacy).
gaps.required: "Servers **MUST** provide structured results that conform to this schema."
gaps.compatImpact: Output for tools using arrays/enums/nil objects in R changes from missing/incorrect fields to correct ones; consumers relying on the current omission are unlikely. No API change.
gaps.suggestedChange: In ConvertValueToJson add tkDynArray (iterate via Value.GetArrayLength/GetArrayElement → TJSONArray), tkClass TList<T>/TObjectList<T> (RTTI 'Count'/'Items' or 'ToArray'), tkSet (array of GetEnumName), tkEnumeration non-Boolean → TJSONString(GetEnumName), tkRecord; emit TJSONNull for nil objects and make the generator mark class/array properties without [Required]... simplest: generator emits 'type':['object','null'] for class-typed properties, or treats nil as absent and does not list class-typed properties in 'required' unless explicitly non-nullable. Add a debug-mode self-check (TMCPSchemaValidator from GAP-TL-07) that validates structuredContent against outputSchema and logs a warning on mismatch.

gaps.title: tools/list order is TDictionary iteration order, not registration order
gaps.current: TMCPRegistry stores factories in TDictionary<string,TMCPToolFactory> and GetToolNames returns FTools.Keys.ToArray (src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:20, 91-96); TMCPToolsManager stores tools in TDictionary<string,IMCPTool> and iterates FTools.Values (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:24, 223). Order is hash-table order: stable within one process run in practice (Delphi's string hash is deterministic) but not the registration order and liable to change whenever an unrelated tool is added or the table grows.
gaps.required: "Servers **SHOULD** return tools in a deterministic order (i.e., the same ordering across requests when the underlying set of tools has not changed)."
gaps.compatImpact: Only the order of the tools array changes. Additive API (TMCPRegistry keeps a TList<string> of names in registration order).
gaps.suggestedChange: Add class var FToolOrder: TList<string> to TMCPRegistry (append on first RegisterTool of a name; GetToolNames returns FToolOrder.ToArray) and FOrder: TList<IMCPTool> (or TList<string>) to TMCPToolsManager; BuildToolListResponse iterates the list. Optionally a SortToolsByName: Boolean property for alphabetical order.

gaps.title: tools/list ignores 'cursor'; invalid cursors return the full list instead of -32602
gaps.current: ExecuteMethod dispatches 'tools/list' to ListTools without Params (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:71-72, 253-257); 'cursor' is never read; nextCursor never emitted (fine, pagination is optional) but a bogus cursor is silently accepted.
gaps.required: "Invalid cursors **SHOULD** result in an error with code -32602 (Invalid params)." Servers SHOULD provide stable cursors if they paginate.
gaps.compatImpact: Only affects clients sending a cursor this server never issued. Additive property ListPageSize.
gaps.suggestedChange: Change ListTools to take Params; read params.cursor; add property ListPageSize: Integer (0 = single page). Cursor = base64 of the start index (or the last tool name for stability); if a cursor is present and cannot be decoded / is out of range raise EMCPProtocolError(-32602, 'Invalid cursor'); emit nextCursor when more tools remain; same ttlMs/cacheScope on all pages (TL-06).

gaps.title: Tool names are not validated; duplicate registrations silently replace or crash at startup
gaps.current: TMCPRegistry.RegisterTool uses AddOrSetValue (last registration silently wins) with no format check (src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:51-57); TMCPToolsManager.RegisterTool uses FTools.Add, so a duplicate reaching it raises EListError during TMCPToolsManager.Create (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:79-82). The registry key (RegisterTool name) and Tool.Name (FName set in the tool constructor) are not checked for consistency.
gaps.required: Names SHOULD be 1..128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.-], no spaces/commas, unique within the server.
gaps.compatImpact: Default behaviour: log a warning only, so existing consumers with non-conforming names keep working; optional strict mode raises. Duplicate detection surfaces as a clear message instead of EListError.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add TMCPToolNaming.IsValid(const Name: string; out Reason: string): Boolean in MCPServer.Tool.Base (regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$); TMCPRegistry.RegisterTool logs TLogger.Warn for invalid names and for re-registration of an existing name (raise EMCPRegistrationError when class var StrictToolNames = True). TMCPToolsManager.RegisterBuiltInTools warns when Tool.Name <> registry name and registers under Tool.Name.

gaps.title: No way to declare annotations (readOnlyHint etc.), icons or _meta on a tool; empty description always emitted
gaps.current: IMCPTool exposes only Name/Title/Description/InputSchema/OutputSchema/Execute (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:11-25); CreateToolJSON emits name, title (only if <> name), description (even when ''), inputSchema, outputSchema (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:185-211). The only attributes are Optional/SchemaDescription/SchemaEnum (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:14-35).
gaps.required: Tool MAY carry annotations {title, readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint}, icons [{src (https:// or data:), mimeType?, sizes?, theme?}], _meta. Optional but expected by modern hosts for confirmation UX.
gaps.compatImpact: Purely additive. Direct IMCPTool implementers are not forced to change: new capabilities go through an optional interface discovered with Supports(). All three base classes gain protected fields/setters.
gaps.suggestedChange: In MCPServer.Tool.Base: TMCPToolAnnotations = record (Title: string; ReadOnlyHint, DestructiveHint, IdempotentHint, OpenWorldHint: TMCPOptionalBool [unset/false/true]); TMCPIcon = record (Src, MimeType, Theme: string; Sizes: TArray<string>); IMCPToolMetadata = interface ['{new GUID}'] function GetAnnotations: TMCPToolAnnotations; function GetIcons: TArray<TMCPIcon>; function GetMeta: TJSONObject; end; implement in TMCPToolBase, TMCPToolBase<T>, TMCPToolBase<T,R> via protected FAnnotations/FIcons/FMeta plus helpers SetReadOnly/SetDestructive/AddIcon(Src, MimeType, Sizes, Theme). Optionally class attributes [ToolAnnotations(...)]/[ToolIcon(...)] read via RTTI. CreateToolJSON: if Supports(Tool, IMCPToolMetadata, Meta) emit 'annotations' (only set hints), 'icons', '_meta' (clone); omit 'description' when empty; reject icon src not starting with 'https://' or 'data:' with a warning.

gaps.title: No typed API for image/audio/resource_link/embedded-resource content, block annotations, per-block _meta or explicit structuredContent
gaps.current: A tool result is a string → single text block (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:148-167), a TJSONObject → structuredContent only (lines 168-181), or a raw TJSONArray passed through verbatim as 'content' (lines 141-147; undocumented in README, and TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithParams is typed string so only the non-generic TMCPToolBase can use it). No helper builds base64 image/audio blocks, resource_link ({uri,name,...}), embedded resources ({resource:{uri,text|blob}}), annotations {audience,priority,lastModified} or result-level _meta.
gaps.required: Content block shapes and optional annotations per TL-17; structuredContent may be any JSON value (modern) or an object (legacy); text fallback SHOULD accompany structured content.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive: existing string/TJSONObject/TJSONArray return paths keep working. TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithParams (string) remains the documented override; a new virtual with a default implementation is added, so existing subclasses compile unchanged.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit MCPServer.Tool.Result.pas: TMCPToolResult = class with AddText(const Text; Annotations: TMCPContentAnnotations = nil), AddImage(const Data: TBytes; const MimeType: string), AddAudio(...), AddResourceLink(const Uri, Name: string; const Description, MimeType, Title: string = ''), AddEmbeddedText(const Uri, Text, MimeType), AddEmbeddedBlob(const Uri; const Data: TBytes; const MimeType), SetStructuredContent(Value: TJSONValue {takes ownership}; AddTextFallback: Boolean = True), property IsError: Boolean, property Meta: TJSONObject, function ToJSON(Era: TMCPProtocolEra): TJSONObject (for legacy 2025-06-18/11-25 refuse non-object structuredContent → drop it, keep text; for 2025-03-26 also omit structuredContent). TMCPToolBase<T> gets 'function ExecuteWithParamsEx(const Params: T; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TMCPToolResult; virtual;' whose default wraps ExecuteWithParams(Params) into a text block (preserving the 'Error:' heuristic); Execute returns TValue.From(TMCPToolResult); BuildToolCallResponse handles TMCPToolResult first. Base64 via System.NetEncoding.TNetEncoding.Base64.EncodeBytesToString (strip line breaks). Document all return forms in README.

gaps.title: isError is inferred from an 'Error:' string prefix or an 'error' key, not declared explicitly
gaps.current: BuildToolCallResponse sets isError when the text StartsWith('Error:') or 'Error executing tool:' (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:151) and, for structured results, when an 'error' member is non-empty (lines 173-174). ExecuteTool turns every exception into 'Error executing tool: ' + Message (lines 122-127). Bundled tools depend on the prefix (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Calculate.pas:68,74; src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.ListFiles.pas:67,92). A legitimate output beginning with 'Error:' is mis-flagged; an error phrased differently is not flagged.
gaps.required: Errors originating from the tool SHOULD be reported with isError:true; the server needs an unambiguous way for tools to signal this.
gaps.compatImpact: Heuristic is retained (documented as legacy convention) so existing consumer tools behave identically; explicit mechanisms are additive.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add EMCPToolError = class(Exception) (MCPServer.Errors.pas); ExecuteTool catches EMCPToolError → isError:true with E.Message (no 'Error executing tool:' prefix), EArgumentException/other Exception → isError:true with 'Error executing tool: ' prefix as today, EMCPProtocolError → re-raise (protocol error). TMCPToolResult.IsError (GAP-TL-15) is the explicit result-level flag. Keep the string heuristic behind TMCPToolsManager.LegacyErrorPrefixDetection: Boolean (default True).

gaps.title: Non-string/non-JSON TValue results yield an empty result object without 'content'
gaps.current: BuildToolCallResponse has branches only for TJSONArray, string and TJSONObject (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:141-181); a custom TMCPToolBase.Execute returning TValue.Empty, an Integer, a Boolean or another object produces {} — invalid CallToolResult (content required).
gaps.required: CallToolResult.content is required in every revision.
gaps.compatImpact: Only affects consumers' hand-written tools returning unusual TValues; they now get a valid text result.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add a final else branch: if ResultValue.IsEmpty then content := [] else content := [{type:'text', text: ResultValue.ToString}]; for TValue holding an arbitrary TObject, serialize via TMCPSerializer to structuredContent + text.

gaps.title: x-mcp-header not supported (no schema annotation, no Mcp-Param-* validation)
gaps.current: TMCPSchemaGenerator recognises only SchemaDescription/SchemaEnum attributes (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas:73-85), so no tool can emit x-mcp-header; TMCPIdHTTPServer reads only Accept and Mcp-Session-Id headers (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:333-337) and never inspects Mcp-Param-*, Mcp-Method or Mcp-Name; CORS Access-Control-Allow-Headers lists only Accept, Content-Type, Last-Event-ID, Mcp-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id (lines 259-260). Integer params currently map to 'number' (GAP-TL-08), which x-mcp-header forbids.
gaps.required: Servers MAY use x-mcp-header; if they do, the value constraints in TL-15 apply and the HTTP server MUST validate Mcp-Param-{Name} headers against the body (400 + -32020 HeaderMismatch), MUST reject invalid characters, MUST decode the base64 sentinel, and MUST NOT expect a header for absent/null values.
gaps.compatImpact: Opt-in per property; no effect on tools that do not use the attribute. Requires GAP-TL-08 first, otherwise modern clients would drop any tool annotating an Integer property. Standard-header (Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name) validation itself belongs to the transport area.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add SchemaHeaderAttribute(Name) in MCPServer.Types; generator emits 'x-mcp-header': Name only for root-level string/integer/boolean properties, validating non-empty, tchar-only (RFC 9110: !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~ and alnum), no CR/LF, case-insensitive uniqueness, and raising EMCPSchemaError at schema build otherwise. Expose TMCPToolsManager.FindTool(const Name: string): IMCPTool and a cached list of header-annotated properties per tool. In TMCPIdHTTPServer.HandlePostRequest (modern requests only): parse method/params.name/arguments; for each annotated property with a non-null value in the body, require header Mcp-Param-{Name} (case-insensitive RawHeaders lookup), decode '=?base64?...?=' (TNetEncoding.Base64, UTF-8), compare (numeric compare for integers, 'true'/'false' for booleans); on mismatch/missing/invalid chars respond HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC error {code:-32020, message:'Header mismatch: ...'}; when the body value is absent or null, ignore the header. Add Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Protocol-Version and the configured Mcp-Param-* names to Access-Control-Allow-Headers (no wildcard patterns allowed).

gaps.title: MRTR (InputRequiredResult) on tools/call not supported; tools cannot see _meta, client capabilities, inputResponses or requestState
gaps.current: IMCPTool.Execute receives only the arguments object (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:18); TMCPToolsManager.ExtractToolNameAndArguments reads only 'name' and 'arguments' (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:96-118); 'inputResponses', 'requestState' and '_meta' (progressToken, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities) are discarded. No result type other than CallToolResult can be produced.
gaps.required: Servers MAY return {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests?, requestState?}; if they do, the MUSTs of TL-23 apply (at least one field; capability check; integrity-protected requestState; no assumption of retry). Must never be emitted to legacy clients.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive. IMCPTool unchanged; a new IMCPRequestContext parameter is provided through the new ExecuteWithParamsEx virtual (GAP-TL-15) and an optional IMCPToolContextAware interface for direct IMCPTool implementers. Legacy clients receive an isError text result instead of an input_required result.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit MCPServer.Tool.Context.pas: IMCPRequestContext = interface with ProtocolVersion: string; IsModern: Boolean; ClientCapabilities: TJSONObject (from params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities']; nil/empty for legacy); ProgressToken: TValue; Meta: TJSONObject; InputResponses: TJSONObject; RequestState: string; function HasClientCapability(const Path: string): Boolean (e.g. 'elicitation.form'). EMCPInputRequired = class(Exception) holding InputRequests: TJSONObject (owned) and RequestState: string, with builders TMCPInputRequests.AddFormElicitation(Key, Message, RequestedSchema) / AddUrlElicitation. TMCPToolsManager.CallTool builds the context from Params, catches EMCPInputRequired: modern → result {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests, requestState} (no ttlMs/cacheScope), after asserting each request's method is allowed by ClientCapabilities (drop or raise -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapability otherwise) and that at least one of the two fields is present; legacy → {content:[text 'This tool requires interactive input that the connected client does not support'], isError:true}. Provide TMCPRequestState.Seal(Payload: TJSONObject; const Key: TBytes; TtlSeconds; const RequestDigest: string): string and Open(...) using THashSHA2.GetHMACAsBytes (System.Hash) + base64url, embedding exp/method/tool-name/args-digest; Open raises EMCPProtocolError(-32602,'Invalid requestState') on failure. Settings: RequestStateKey (random per process if absent).

gaps.title: _meta.progressToken on tools/call is ignored; no way to emit notifications/progress
gaps.current: progressToken is never read (ToolsManager.pas:96-118); the HTTP SSE POST path buffers a single event into ResponseInfo.ContentText (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:470-510) and the stdio loop writes only the final response (src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas:64-71), so notifications cannot precede a result.
gaps.required: Server MAY send notifications/progress; if it does, tokens MUST be active, progress MUST increase, notifications MUST stop after completion, rate limiting SHOULD apply. Choosing not to send is allowed (current behaviour is conformant but the library offers no opt-in).
gaps.compatImpact: Additive; transport change (streaming writes) is owned by the transport area. Tools that never call ReportProgress are unaffected.
gaps.suggestedChange:
IMCPRequestContext.ReportProgress(Progress: Double; Total: Double = -1; const Msg: string = '') enqueues {method:'notifications/progress', params:{progressToken, progress, total?, message?}} into a per-request TThreadedQueue<string> only when a progressToken was supplied; enforce monotonic progress and a min-interval throttle.
