Transports drain the queue: stdio writes each notification line before the response; HTTP SSE handler must switch to streaming writes on AContext.Connection.IOHandler (WriteLn of 'event: message
data: ...

') before writing the final result event.

gaps.title: tools capability is declared with non-standard keys and without listChanged
gaps.current: TMCPCoreManager.Initialize emits capabilities.tools = {supportsProgress:false, supportsCancellation:false} (src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:106-114) mirroring TMCPToolsCapability (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:63-71), which is not actually used to build the JSON. Neither key exists in any revision's ServerCapabilities.tools ({listChanged?: boolean}); schema.json leaves the object open so it is tolerated but meaningless.
gaps.required: "Servers that support tools **MUST** declare the `tools` capability" as {listChanged?: boolean} — legacy in initialize, modern in server/discover (lifecycle area owns the discover result).
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients ignore the unknown keys today and will not miss them. TMCPToolsCapability keeps SupportsProgress/SupportsCancellation (deprecated, unused) and gains ListChanged for source compatibility.
gaps.suggestedChange: Emit tools: {"listChanged": false} (or {}) in both the initialize result and the server/discover result; add ListChanged: Boolean to TMCPToolsCapability and have both code paths build the JSON from it. Set listChanged:true only once a dynamic registry + subscriptions/listen exist.

gaps.title: No rate limiting or access-control hook for tool invocations
gaps.current: TMCPToolsManager.CallTool executes any registered tool unconditionally (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:230-251); TMCPIdHTTPServer has no per-client throttling (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:172-208). Only list_files implements its own path-based access check (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.ListFiles.pas:62-69).
gaps.required: "Servers **MUST**: ... Implement proper access controls; Rate limit tool invocations; Sanitize tool outputs".
gaps.compatImpact: Opt-in hooks/settings; default behaviour unchanged except an optional rate limiter that is off by default. Library consumers get a single interception point for authorization.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add TMCPToolsManager.OnBeforeCallTool: reference to procedure(const Tool: IMCPTool; const Arguments: TJSONObject; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext) (raise EMCPToolError to deny with isError, or EMCPProtocolError(-32602/-32603) for protocol-level refusal) and OnAfterCallTool for output sanitisation/logging. Add a simple thread-safe token bucket keyed by remote IP (TMonitor-protected TDictionary<string,TBucket>) in TMCPIdHTTPServer with settings RateLimitPerMinute (0 = off) returning HTTP 429 with a JSON-RPC -32603 body; for stdio, a global bucket. Document that per-tool authorization is the embedding application's responsibility.

gaps.title: No era-specific shaping of tool definitions/results for legacy sessions
gaps.current: CreateToolJSON and BuildToolCallResponse are version-agnostic (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:130-211); nothing prevents a hand-written TMCPToolBase (BuildSchema/Execute) from advertising an array/primitive outputSchema or returning non-object structuredContent to a 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 client, or resource_link blocks / title / outputSchema / icons to a 2025-03-26 client.
gaps.required: Legacy 2025-06-18/2025-11-25: outputSchema root MUST be type:object and structuredContent MUST be an object; 2025-03-26 has no structuredContent/outputSchema/title/icons and no resource_link content type. Modern: any JSON value/schema.
gaps.compatImpact: Only matters once consumers use the new modern-only flexibility; the generic bases always produce object schemas. Requires the negotiated version to be available to the manager (thread-local request context or IMCPRequestContext).
gaps.suggestedChange: Give the manager the negotiated protocol version (IMCPRequestContext.ProtocolVersion, populated by the processor from _meta for modern requests and from the session for legacy). In CreateToolJSON: if version < 2026-07-28 and outputSchema.type <> 'object' then omit outputSchema; if version = 2025-03-26 omit title/outputSchema/icons/_meta. In result building: if version < 2026-07-28 and structuredContent is not a TJSONObject then drop it (keep the text fallback); if version = 2025-03-26 drop structuredContent and downgrade resource_link blocks to text.

gaps.title: Schema generator lacks title/format/minimum/maximum/default/pattern/additionalProperties/$schema and emits properties:{} for no-parameter tools
gaps.current: GenerateSchema emits only type/properties/required/description/enum/items (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas:31-105); attribute set is Optional/SchemaDescription/SchemaEnum (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:14-35); zero-property classes (TGetTimeParams, src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.GetTime.pas:12-13) yield {type:object, properties:{}} rather than the recommended {type:object, additionalProperties:false}. Property names are always LowerCase(Prop.Name) (line 135-138) with no override, while the deserializer accepts case/underscore-insensitive keys (Serializer.pas:73-91).
gaps.required: Any 2020-12 keyword MAY appear; no-parameter tools should preferably use additionalProperties:false; schemas SHOULD describe constraints so LLMs and validators can use them. (All MAY/recommended.)
gaps.compatImpact: Additive attributes; emitting additionalProperties:false for empty classes is harmless. If additionalProperties:false is ever emitted for non-empty classes, keep the deserializer's lenient key matching or document the tightening. Consumers' existing attribute usage unchanged.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add attributes in MCPServer.Types: SchemaTitle, SchemaFormat('date-time'|'email'|...), SchemaMinimum/SchemaMaximum(Double), SchemaMinLength/MaxLength, SchemaPattern, SchemaDefault(string), SchemaName('jsonName') for explicit property names, class-level SchemaAdditionalProperties(False) and SchemaDialect('$schema URI'); generator emits them; TMCPSchemaValidator (GAP-TL-07) enforces them. Emit additionalProperties:false automatically when a params class has no properties.

gaps.title: Documentation gaps: supported schema dialect, result forms, error conventions
gaps.current: README documents only string-returning TMCPToolBase<T> tools with [Optional]/[SchemaDescription] (README.md:222-283) and the four example tools (README.md:438-443); it does not mention TMCPToolBase<T,R>/outputSchema, the TJSONArray content passthrough, the 'Error:' isError convention, the JSON Schema dialect, or naming rules.
gaps.required: "Clients and servers **SHOULD** document which schema dialects they support"; library consumers need the contract for isError, content blocks, structured output and naming.
gaps.compatImpact: Docs only.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add README sections: 'Tool naming rules', 'Input schema (JSON Schema 2020-12 subset generated from RTTI; supported attributes)', 'Returning results (text / TMCPToolResult / structured output via TMCPToolBase<T,R>)', 'Reporting errors (EMCPToolError vs EMCPProtocolError; legacy Error: prefix)', 'Annotations, icons, x-mcp-header', 'Protocol versions served (2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, 2026-07-28) and per-era differences'.

alreadyConformant: tools/list and tools/call are routed by capability name 'tools' and HandlesMethod (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:59-77).

Tool definitions carry name, optional title (emitted only when it differs from name, matching BaseMetadata semantics), description, inputSchema and, for TMCPToolBase<T,R>, outputSchema (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:185-211; src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:100-106, 227-230).

Generated inputSchema has root type:'object' with 'properties' and 'required' and no '$schema', so it correctly defaults to JSON Schema 2020-12; every emitted keyword (type, properties, required, description, enum, items) is valid 2020-12 (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas:45-50, 66-69, 75-101).

Enum constraints are emitted both from [SchemaEnum] and from Delphi enumeration RTTI, and invalid enum values are rejected with an actionable message (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas:79-91, 152-170; src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:261-291).
Property order inside 'properties' follows declaration order via RTTI GetProperties, so a given tool's schema is stable across requests (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas:56).

The tool set is built once in the constructor from TMCPRegistry and never mutated per request, satisfying 'MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests' (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:46-51, 84-94).

Input-validation failures (unknown parameter, invalid enum value) and exceptions thrown by tool logic are returned as tool execution errors with isError:true rather than protocol errors, in line with SEP-1303 and the CallToolResult.isError guidance (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:111-118, 133-138, 285-288; src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:120-128, 148-167).
isError is emitted as a JSON boolean and omitted when false, which the schema permits ('If not set, this is assumed to be false') (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:161-166, 175-180).
Text content blocks have the correct {type:'text', text} shape (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:156-159).

When a tool returns a TJSONArray it is passed through verbatim as 'content', so image/audio/resource blocks can already be emitted by hand-written tools (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:141-147).

structuredContent is a clone of the tool's TJSONObject and the outputSchema is generated from the same class R, so field names (lower-cased) and primitive types line up for simple classes (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:171; src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:193-195, 227-230; src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:159-173).

Bundled tool names 'echo', 'get_time', 'list_files', 'calculate' satisfy the naming rules (1-128 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_.-]) (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Echo.pas:37, GetTime.pas:32, ListFiles.pas:45, Calculate.pas:48).

Tool name uniqueness is effectively enforced: TMCPRegistry keys by name and TMCPToolsManager.RegisterTool uses TDictionary.Add (src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:55; src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:79-82).

Schemas returned by IMCPTool.GetInputSchema/GetOutputSchema are cloned and freed by the manager, giving a consistent ownership contract for library consumers (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:196-209).

No reserved/forbidden error codes are emitted: only -32700/-32601/-32603 are produced today (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:27-32, 209-217), so nothing in the -32020..-32099 range or -32002/-32042 is misused.

The server never dereferences $ref (no schema validation with $ref support exists), so the 'MUST NOT automatically dereference network $ref' rule is trivially met (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas, src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas).
list_files implements a path-confinement access check on its input (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.ListFiles.pas:62-69), an example of the 'Validate all tool inputs / access controls' MUST at tool level.
notes: Envelope placement: resultType and _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo are cross-cutting (every result), so inject them once in TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest based on the request era; ttlMs/cacheScope are method-specific and belong in TMCPToolsManager (and the resources manager for its list/read methods). Emitting ttlMs/cacheScope unconditionally is safe for legacy clients because Result has additionalProperties:{} (open) in schema.json 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25; resultType could also be emitted unconditionally for the same reason, but keeping it modern-only is cleaner for dual-era tests.

schema.json 2026-07-28 required sets that a validating modern client will enforce: ListToolsResult=[cacheScope, resultType, tools, ttlMs]; CallToolResult=[content, resultType]; Result=[resultType]. ServerCapabilities.tools has no additionalProperties:false in any revision, so the current supportsProgress/supportsCancellation keys are tolerated but meaningless.

Era propagation without breaking IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod(Method, Params): TValue: either (a) a threadvar/`TMCPRequestScope.Current: IMCPRequestContext` set by the processor around ExecuteMethodCall (works for Indy worker threads and stdio), or (b) an additive IMCPCapabilityManagerEx with ExecuteMethodEx(Method, Params, Ctx) that the processor prefers via Supports(). Custom managers written against the old interface keep compiling either way. For modern requests the version is in params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion']; for legacy it is the negotiated session version, which today lives only in TMCPCoreManager (src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:97-101 stores a session id but not the client's requested version).

Thread-safety constraint for any new tool API: tool instances are singletons created once and shared by all Indy worker threads (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:84-94), so per-request state (context, progress, result builders) must be passed as parameters/return values, never stored in tool fields.

JsonRpcProcessor error mapping is string-based ('not found' → -32601, otherwise -32603) (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:209-217); a typed EMCPProtocolError(Code, Message, Data) is the prerequisite for -32602 (unknown tool/invalid params/invalid cursor), -32020 (HeaderMismatch), -32021 (MissingRequiredClientCapability) and -32022. JSON-RPC constants are duplicated in JsonRpcProcessor.pas:27-32 and IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99; centralise them in MCPServer.Types together with the new -32020..-32022 codes.

Tool-logic exceptions vs server errors: ExecuteTool's catch-all (ToolsManager.pas:122-127) also converts genuine server faults (EAccessViolation, EOutOfMemory) into isError results; the spec lists 'Server errors' under protocol errors. Consider mapping EAccessViolation/EOutOfMemory/EInvalidPointer to -32603 while keeping application exceptions as isError. This is a judgement call and was not listed as a gap.

Deserializer leniency: keys are matched case-insensitively and with underscores stripped (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas:73-91), so the wire contract is looser than the advertised schema ('includehidden' vs 'includeHidden' vs 'include_hidden'). Harmless today; if additionalProperties:false or a strict validator is introduced, either keep the leniency (validate after key normalisation) or document the tightening.

Delphi TDictionary iteration order is deterministic for identical insertion sequences within a build, so the current tools/list order is stable within one process run; it is nevertheless neither registration order nor guaranteed across table growth or Delphi versions, hence GAP-TL-11 is rated minor.

TValue.AsBoolean on a non-Boolean enumeration (Serializer.pas:346-356): whether it raises EInvalidCast or yields a bogus boolean depends on the RTL version; either way the output disagrees with the generated {type:string, enum} schema. Could not compile/execute Delphi in this Linux environment; GAP-TL-06 and GAP-TL-10(c) are derived from code reading and should be confirmed with a quick manual test.

Non-object outputSchema/structuredContent (SEP-2106) is modern-only; the generic TMCPToolBase<T,R> always produces objects, so legacy interop is preserved by construction. The new flexibility is only reachable through hand-written TMCPToolBase.BuildSchema/Execute or TMCPToolResult.SetStructuredContent, which is why era-shaping (GAP-TL-23) is minor.

2025-11-25 legacy clients may send Tool.execution.taskSupport expectations and a `task` member in tools/call params (tasks were core-experimental in 2025-11-25 and became the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension in 2026-07-28). Out of scope for this area; the tools manager currently ignores unknown params, which is acceptable because taskSupport defaults to 'forbidden'.

MRTR capability check needs the client's per-request capabilities: elicitation.form / elicitation.url (still active), sampling and roots (deprecated as of 2026-07-28 per SEP-2577 but still allowed during the deprecation window). If a tool needs elicitation and the client did not declare it, return MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021, data.requiredCapabilities) or degrade to an isError text — the spec's MUST is only 'MUST NOT send inputRequests the client has not declared'.

x-mcp-header and CORS: Access-Control-Allow-Headers does not accept prefix wildcards, so browser clients require the concrete Mcp-Param-* names (or '*' for non-credentialed requests); the list can be computed from the registered tools' header-annotated properties at Start. Int64 properties are JSON 'integer' but may exceed the ±2^53 safe range required for header mirroring; the generator should refuse [SchemaHeader] on Int64 or document the limit.

ttlMs choice: the tool list is immutable for the process lifetime and listChanged is not declared, so any positive ttlMs is truthful; the spec's example uses 300000. cacheScope 'public' is correct because the list does not depend on the caller (no authorization/filtering exists). If per-user filtering is ever added via OnBeforeCallTool-style hooks, switch to 'private'.

Suggested new units to keep the library API additive: MCPServer.Errors.pas (EMCPProtocolError, EMCPToolError, EMCPInputRequired, error-code constants), MCPServer.Tool.Result.pas (TMCPToolResult + content builders), MCPServer.Tool.Context.pas (IMCPRequestContext, TMCPRequestState HMAC helper), MCPServer.Schema.Validator.pas (TMCPSchemaValidator). Existing units keep their public signatures; IMCPTool is extended only through optional interfaces (IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPToolContextAware) discovered with Supports().

Structured-text fallback: use compact TJSONObject.ToJSON (no whitespace) in the TextContent block, matching the spec example format; for TMCPToolBase<T,R> this also makes the result readable by 2025-03-26 clients that have no structuredContent.

SEP-986 (the original naming SEP) allowed '/' and capped names at 64 characters; the published spec text (2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 'Tool Names') is the authority: 128 characters and no '/'. Validate against the spec text.

The TMCPTool/TMCPToolsResponse classes in src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:93-111 (InputSchema as string) are unused by the manager; they can stay for source compatibility but should not be extended — the JSON is built directly in TMCPToolsManager.CreateToolJSON.

gapReports.area: Resources, resource templates, prompts, caching, pagination, completion (server side; dual-era 2026-07-28 modern + 2025-03-26/2025-06-18/2025-11-25 legacy)

requirements.text: "Servers that support resources MUST declare the `resources` capability" — modern: inside DiscoverResult.capabilities (server/discover); legacy: inside the `initialize` result. Shape: {"resources": {"subscribe"?: boolean, "listChanged"?: boolean}}; "Serves that support neither `listChanged` or `subscribe` may omit it" -> {"resources": {}}.

`subscribe` now means "whether the server supports resource-specific update notifications for resources requested through subscriptions/listen using the resourceSubscriptions filter"; `listChanged` = "whether the server will emit notifications when the list of available resources changes". "Servers may advertise either feature independently, together or neither."

`subscribe`: "whether the client can subscribe to be notified of changes to individual resources" via `resources/subscribe` (params.uri) / `resources/unsubscribe`; server then sends `notifications/resources/updated` {uri}. "Both `subscribe` and `listChanged` are optional—servers can support neither, either, or both".

"Servers that declare the `resources` capability MUST respond to `resources/list` requests with the set of resources currently available to the requesting client. This set MAY be empty and MAY change over time ..., but MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection. The set MAY vary by the authorization presented on the request".

`resources/list` result = {"resources": Resource[], "nextCursor"?: string} (legacy) and additionally REQUIRED {"resultType": "complete", "ttlMs": number>=0, "cacheScope": "public"|"private"} in modern (ListResourcesResult extends PaginatedResult, CacheableResult; JSON schema required = [cacheScope, resources, resultType, ttlMs]).
requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts ListResourcesResult; schema/2026-07-28/schema.json definitions.ListResourcesResult.required; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § Listing Resources

requirements.text: Resource object: `uri` (required, @format uri), `name` (required), `title`? (2025-06-18+), `description`?, `mimeType`? ("if known"), `size`? ("raw resource content, in bytes (i.e., before base64 encoding)"), `icons`? (2025-11-25+), `annotations`? {audience?, priority? 0..1, lastModified? ISO-8601 (2025-06-18+)}, `_meta`? (2025-06-18+). 2025-03-26 Resource has only uri,name,description,mimeType,size,annotations{audience,priority}.
requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts Resource, Annotations, BaseMetadata, Icons; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § Data Types › Resource, § Annotations; schema/2025-03-26/schema.json definitions.Resource

requirements.text: `resources/read` request params: `uri` (required). Result: {"contents": (TextResourceContents|BlobResourceContents)[]} plus, modern only, REQUIRED `resultType`, `ttlMs`, `cacheScope` (ReadResourceResult extends CacheableResult). "Servers MAY return multiple resource contents in response to a single `resources/read` request."
requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts ResourceRequestParams, ReadResourceRequestParams, ReadResourceResult; schema/2026-07-28/schema.json definitions.ReadResourceResult.required=[cacheScope,contents,resultType,ttlMs]; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § Reading Resources

requirements.text: Text contents = {uri, mimeType?, text} ("text ... must only be set if the item can actually be represented as text (not binary data)"); Blob contents = {uri, mimeType?, blob: base64 string}. Security: "Binary data MUST be properly encoded".
requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts TextResourceContents, BlobResourceContents; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § Resource Contents, § Security Considerations (3)

requirements.text: "Servers MAY also respond to `resources/read` with an `InputRequiredResult` to indicate that additional input is needed before the resource can be read" (MRTR). Supported-request table lists prompts/get, resources/read, tools/call only; "Servers MUST NOT send `InputRequiredResult` responses on any other client requests." "Servers MUST include at least one of `inputRequests` or `requestState` in every `InputRequiredResult`"; "Servers MUST NOT send an `inputRequests` that the client has not declared support for in its capabilities"; requestState "MUST" be treated as attacker-controlled and integrity-protected if it influences authorization.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § Reading Resources; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr.mdx § Supported Requests, § Server Requirements (Basic Workflow)

requirements.text: "If the requested resource does not exist, servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code `-32602` (Invalid Params). Servers SHOULD return `-32603` for internal errors." Example error carries "data": {"uri": ...}; SEP-2164: "The `data` field SHOULD include the `uri` that was not found."
"Servers MUST NOT return an empty `contents` array for a non-existent resource. An empty array is ambiguous".

"Implementations of this protocol version MUST NOT emit these codes: `-32002` — resource not found (2025-11-25 and earlier; replaced by `-32602`)". Also "-32000 to -32019 — legacy ... new implementations SHOULD NOT use codes from this sub-range at all".

"Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Resource not found: `-32002`; Internal errors: `-32603`" (identical wording in 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25). Example: {"code": -32002, "message": "Resource not found", "data": {"uri": ...}}.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources.mdx § Error Handling; .../2025-06-18/server/resources.mdx § Error Handling (line 374); .../2025-03-26/server/resources.mdx § Error Handling (line 334)

requirements.text: "1. Servers MUST validate all resource URIs"; "2. Access controls SHOULD be implemented for sensitive resources"; "4. Resource permissions SHOULD be checked before operations"; modern adds "5. Servers MUST sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks when serving `file://` resources". "Custom URI schemes MUST be in accordance with RFC3986".
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § Security Considerations, § Custom URI Schemes; 2025-11-25 same headings

requirements.text: https://: "Servers SHOULD use this scheme only when the client is able to fetch and load the resource directly from the web on its own"; "For other use cases, servers SHOULD prefer to use another URI scheme, or define a custom one". file://: "MCP servers MAY identify file:// resources with an XDG MIME type, like `inode/directory`".

"When the list of available resources changes, servers that declared the `listChanged` capability SHOULD send a notification: notifications/resources/list_changed". Modern: only delivered on a subscriptions/listen stream where the client set `resourcesListChanged: true` ("the server MUST NOT send notification types the client has not explicitly requested"), tagged with `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`. Legacy: sent unsolicited (HTTP GET SSE stream / stdio).
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § List Changed Notification; schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts ResourceListChangedNotification, SubscriptionFilter; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions.mdx § Opening a Stream

requirements.text: `resources/subscribe` / `resources/unsubscribe` are removed (changelog #4: "Replace the HTTP GET endpoint and `resources/subscribe`/`resources/unsubscribe` with `subscriptions/listen`"). Subscriptions are opened via `subscriptions/listen` params.notifications.resourceSubscriptions: string[]; server "MUST send `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged` as the first message" and delivers `notifications/resources/updated` {"_meta": {"io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId": <listen id>}, "uri"}. A modern client that still sends resources/subscribe hits "If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with `404 Not Found` and a JSON-RPC error with code `-32601`" (HTTP).
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx item 4; .../2026-07-28/server/resources.mdx § Subscriptions; .../2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions.mdx § Acknowledgment; .../2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx § Protocol Version Header

requirements.text: Every result "MUST include a `resultType` field" ("complete" for ordinary results, "input_required" for MRTR interim results); applies to ListResourcesResult, ReadResourceResult, ListResourceTemplatesResult, ListPromptsResult, GetPromptResult, CompleteResult. "Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field."

`resources/templates/list` result = {"resourceTemplates": ResourceTemplate[], "nextCursor"?} (+ modern REQUIRED resultType, ttlMs, cacheScope). ResourceTemplate: `uriTemplate` (required, "A URI template (according to RFC 6570)"), `name` (required), `title`?, `description`?, `mimeType`? ("should only be included if all resources matching this template have the same type"), `icons`?, `annotations`?, `_meta`?.

"Resource templates allow servers to expose parameterized resources using URI templates. Arguments may be auto-completed through the completion API." (ref/resource with uri = the template). Supports pagination and (modern) caching.

"Servers that support prompts MUST declare the `prompts` capability" ({"prompts": {"listChanged"?: boolean}}) — modern in DiscoverResult, legacy "during initialization". Minimum baseline example: {"prompts": {}}.

"Servers that declare the `prompts` capability MUST respond to `prompts/list` requests with the set of prompts currently available to the requesting client. This set MAY be empty and MAY change over time ..., but MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection."

`prompts/list` result = {"prompts": Prompt[], "nextCursor"?} (+ modern REQUIRED resultType, ttlMs, cacheScope; ListPromptsResult extends PaginatedResult, CacheableResult). Prompt: `name` (required), `title`? (2025-06-18+), `description`?, `arguments`?: PromptArgument[] {name (required), title?, description?, required?: boolean}, `icons`? (2025-11-25+), `_meta`?.
requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts ListPromptsResult, Prompt, PromptArgument; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/prompts.mdx § Listing Prompts, § Data Types › Prompt

requirements.text: `prompts/get` params: `name` (required), `arguments`?: {[key]: string}. Result: {"description"?: string, "messages": PromptMessage[]} where PromptMessage = {"role": "user"|"assistant", "content": ContentBlock}; modern adds REQUIRED resultType. GetPromptResult is NOT a CacheableResult (no ttlMs/cacheScope).
requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts GetPromptRequestParams, GetPromptResult, PromptMessage, Role; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/prompts.mdx § Getting a Prompt

requirements.text: Prompt message content types: text {type:'text', text}; image {type:'image', data (base64), mimeType} — "The image data MUST be base64-encoded and include a valid MIME type"; audio {type:'audio', data, mimeType} — "MUST be base64-encoded and include a valid MIME type"; resource_link {type:'resource_link', uri, name, ...Resource fields} (2025-06-18+ only; absent from 2025-03-26 PromptMessage.content); embedded resource {type:'resource', resource: TextResourceContents|BlobResourceContents} — "MUST include: A valid resource URI; The appropriate MIME type; Either text content or base64-encoded blob data". "All content types in prompt messages support optional annotations".

requirements.text: "Servers MAY also respond to `prompts/get` with an `InputRequiredResult` to indicate that additional input is needed before the prompt can be resolved." (GetPromptResultResponse.result: GetPromptResult | InputRequiredResult). Same MRTR server requirements as RS-09.

"Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Invalid prompt name: `-32602` (Invalid params); Missing required arguments: `-32602` (Invalid params); Internal errors: `-32603` (Internal error)".

"Servers SHOULD validate prompt arguments before processing"; "Both parties SHOULD respect capability negotiation"; "Implementations MUST carefully validate all prompt inputs and outputs to prevent injection attacks or unauthorized access to resources."

"When the list of available prompts changes, servers that declared the `listChanged` capability SHOULD send a notification" `notifications/prompts/list_changed` — modern: only "to clients that have opened a `subscriptions/listen` stream with `promptsListChanged: true`".

"Servers MUST include caching hints on results with `resultType: "complete"` returned by the following operations: `server/discover`, `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read`". "Interim results with `resultType: "input_required"` ... are not cacheable and carry no caching hints."
"Servers MUST provide a `ttlMs` value that is `>= 0`" (integer milliseconds; 0 = immediately stale; absent "should only occur in older server versions"; negative ignored by clients).

`cacheScope` is required, value "public" ("does not contain user-specific data ... MAY store and serve ... to any user") or "private" ("Caches MUST NOT be shared across authorization contexts"). Guidance: "`"public"` is appropriate for lists of tools, prompts, and resource templates when they are identical for all users. `"private"` is appropriate for `resources/read` results that depend on the authenticated user, or for filtered list results that vary per user." SEP-2549: "`cacheScope` is required because there is no safe default for older servers."
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching.mdx § Cache Scope Field, § Choosing a Cache Scope; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/seps/2549-TTL-for-list-results.md § Backward Compatibility

requirements.text: "Servers MUST apply the same `cacheScope` to all response pages for a given list request." Each page carries its own ttlMs; "Servers MAY return different `ttlMs` values on different pages".

"Servers MUST be aware that responses with a `"public"` `cacheScope` may be shared between callers even if the Result is coming from an authenticated endpoint." Server implementors "MUST apply appropriate per-primitive access controls, and MUST NOT rely on `cacheScope` alone to prevent unauthorized access".

"A server MAY provide `ttlMs` without advertising `listChanged: true`"; "TTL is a freshness hint, not a guarantee. Servers MAY change the underlying data before the TTL expires." Results of MRTR retries (requests carrying inputResponses/requestState) "MUST NOT be cached" by clients — server still must include fields on complete results.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching.mdx § Interaction with Notifications, § Cache Key, § TTL note

requirements.text: Pagination "uses an opaque cursor-based approach": "The cursor is an opaque string token"; "Page size is determined by the server". Response: "The current page of results; An optional `nextCursor` field if more results exist". Request continues with params.cursor. Operations: `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `prompts/list`, `tools/list`.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination.mdx § Pagination Model, § Response Format, § Request Format, § Operations Supporting Pagination; schema.ts PaginatedRequestParams, PaginatedResult

requirements.text: "Servers SHOULD: Provide stable cursors; Handle invalid cursors gracefully".
"Invalid cursors SHOULD result in an error with code -32602 (Invalid params)."
Clients "MUST NOT" treat an empty-string cursor as end of results ("an empty string is a valid cursor") — therefore a server signals end-of-list only by OMITTING `nextCursor`, never by emitting "".

"Servers SHOULD return tools from `tools/list` in a deterministic order to enable client-side caching" (changelog); by extension stable cursors (PG-02) require a deterministic order for resources/prompts lists too.
"Servers that support completions MUST declare the `completions` capability": {"completions": {}}.

`completion/complete` params: `ref` = {type:'ref/prompt', name} | {type:'ref/resource', uri (URI or URI template)}; `argument` {name, value}; `context`?.{arguments?: {[k]: string}} (context added 2025-06-18; absent in 2025-03-26). Result: {"completion": {"values": string[] ("Must not exceed 100 items"), "total"?: number, "hasMore"?: boolean}} (+ modern resultType; CompleteResult is not cacheable).
requirements.source: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts CompleteRequestParams, CompleteResult, PromptReference, ResourceTemplateReference; /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion.mdx § Data Types, § Completion Results; schema/2025-03-26/schema.ts CompleteRequest (line 1095, no context)

requirements.text: "Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Method not found: `-32601` (Capability not supported); Invalid prompt name: `-32602`; Missing required arguments: `-32602`; Internal errors: `-32603`".

"Servers SHOULD: Return suggestions sorted by relevance; Implement fuzzy matching where appropriate; Rate limit completion requests; Validate all inputs". "Implementations MUST: Validate all completion inputs; Implement appropriate rate limiting; Control access to sensitive suggestions; Prevent completion-based information disclosure".

HTTP: "If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with `404 Not Found` and a JSON-RPC error with code `-32601`" — applies to `resources/subscribe`, `resources/unsubscribe`, and to `prompts/*` / `completion/complete` when those capabilities are not offered.
"Servers SHOULD include the following `io.modelcontextprotocol/*` field in every result's `_meta` ... `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`" (Implementation {name, version}).

Every request "MUST include the required `_meta` fields" (protocolVersion, clientCapabilities); "A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code `-32602` (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be `400 Bad Request`." Note PaginatedRequest.params is non-optional in 2026-07-28 (`params: PaginatedRequestParams`), so a modern `resources/list` with no params object is malformed.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx § `_meta` › Per-request protocol fields; schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts PaginatedRequest (line 1063) vs schema/2025-11-25/schema.ts PaginatedRequest (params?)

requirements.text: Streamable HTTP standard headers: `Mcp-Method` (all requests) and `Mcp-Name` sourced from "`params.name` or `params.uri`" for "`tools/call`, `resources/read`, `prompts/get` requests" are REQUIRED; "Servers that process the request body MUST reject requests where the values specified in the headers do not match the corresponding values in the request body" with `400 Bad Request` and `-32020` (HeaderMismatch); values may be Base64-sentinel encoded (`=?base64?...?=`) and "servers MUST decode encoded values".
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx § Standard Request Headers, § Value Encoding, § Server Validation

requirements.text: Dual-era server rule: "A request carrying modern per-request `_meta` is served statelessly according to this revision. An `initialize` request selects legacy semantics, scoped to the stdio process (stdio) or the session (HTTP), as specified by the negotiated legacy protocol version." "A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently on the same endpoint or process." Consequence for this area: error code (-32602 vs -32002), resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope emission and subscribe-method availability must be selected per request from the negotiated revision.
requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning.mdx § Backward Compatibility with Initialization-Based Versions (after Compatibility Matrix)

gaps.title: No `resultType` on any resources (or other) result
gaps.current: ListResources builds {resources:[...]} only (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:102-117); ReadResource builds {contents:[...]} (:142-172); ListResourceTemplates builds {resourceTemplates:[]} (:186-193). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest wraps whatever the manager returns without adding fields (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:192-200).
gaps.required: Modern: "The `result` MUST include a `resultType` field" — "complete" on every ordinary result, "input_required" on MRTR interim results.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients ignore unknown result fields (Result has [key:string]:unknown in all revisions) so emitting it unconditionally is harmless, but emit only for modern-era requests to stay schema-exact. Library consumers: if injected centrally in the processor, custom IMCPCapabilityManager implementations get it for free with no code change; managers that deliberately return an input_required result must be able to set it themselves (processor must not overwrite an existing key).
gaps.suggestedChange: In MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas, after ExecuteMethodCall and when the request is modern (per-request `_meta` present / negotiated version >= 2026-07-28 from the request-context object the lifecycle work introduces): if ExecuteResult is a TJSONObject and GetValue('resultType') = nil then AddPair('resultType','complete'). Add const MCP_RESULT_TYPE_COMPLETE = 'complete' / MCP_RESULT_TYPE_INPUT_REQUIRED = 'input_required' in MCPServer.Types.pas. Do not add it inside each manager (avoids duplicating it in ToolsManager/ResourcesManager/PromptsManager and covers third-party managers).

gaps.title: `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` missing on resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list
gaps.current: None of the three result builders emit ttlMs/cacheScope (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:102-117, :142-172, :186-193). IMCPResource exposes only URI/Name/Description/MimeType/Read (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas:11-23), so there is no per-resource place to declare freshness or scope.
gaps.required: Modern: "Servers MUST include caching hints on results with `resultType: "complete"` returned by ... `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read`"; "Servers MUST provide a `ttlMs` value that is `>= 0`"; cacheScope required, "public"|"private"; same cacheScope on all pages.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: extra fields are tolerated (Result allows additional keys); emit only in modern era for schema exactness. Library consumers: do NOT add methods to IMCPResource (custom classes implementing the interface directly would stop compiling); add an additive interface and default fields in TMCPResourceBase<T> so existing descendants compile unchanged and get conservative defaults (ttlMs 0, cacheScope 'private').
gaps.suggestedChange: MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas: add `TMCPCacheScope = (csPublic, csPrivate)` and `IMCPCacheableResource = interface ['{new guid}'] function GetTtlMs: Integer; function GetCacheScope: TMCPCacheScope; end;` implemented by TMCPResourceBase<T> via new protected fields FTtlMs: Integer (default 0) and FCacheScope: TMCPCacheScope (default csPrivate) that descendants set in Create. TMCPResourcesManager: add published properties ListTtlMs: Integer (default 0), ListCacheScope: TMCPCacheScope (default csPrivate; the sample dpr sets csPublic + 300000 because the set is fixed at construction and there is no auth), used for resources/list and resources/templates/list; in ReadResource query `Supports(Resource, IMCPCacheableResource, Cacheable)` and fall back to (0, csPrivate). Emit `ttlMs` (TJSONNumber) and `cacheScope` ('public'|'private') only for modern-era requests. Sample values: project://info and project://readme -> FTtlMs := 3600000, FCacheScope := csPublic (static text); logs://recent and server://status -> FTtlMs := 0, FCacheScope := csPrivate (dynamic process telemetry; logs://recent even mutates the buffer on read at /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Logs.pas:209). Document in README that a deployment adding authorization must set csPrivate on anything user-dependent (CA-05).

gaps.title: Resource not found is returned as a successful text result instead of a JSON-RPC error (-32602 modern / -32002 legacy)
gaps.current: ReadResource on unknown URI returns HTTP 200 result {contents:[{uri, mimeType:'text/plain', text:'Error: Resource not found: <uri>'}]} (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:165-170). CreateErrorResponse cannot carry `data` (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:128-144). Trap: ProcessRequest maps ANY exception whose message contains 'not found' to -32601 METHOD_NOT_FOUND (:214-215), so simply raising Exception('Resource not found') would yield the wrong code (and, once the transport maps -32601 to HTTP 404 in modern, the wrong HTTP status too).
gaps.required: Modern: "servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code `-32602` (Invalid Params)" with data.uri (SHOULD, SEP-2164) and "MUST NOT emit" -32002. Legacy (2025-03-26/06-18/11-25): "Resource not found: `-32002`" (SHOULD). Never an empty contents array.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients that today show the 'Error: Resource not found' text will instead receive a JSON-RPC error (-32002) — a behaviour change, but the one the legacy spec asks for and what every official SDK does (SEP-2164 table). Library consumers: custom resources unchanged; custom managers can adopt the new typed exception but are not forced to (generic Exception still maps to -32603).
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.Errors.pas: `EMCPError = class(Exception) Code: Integer; Data: TJSONValue (owned); constructor Create(ACode: Integer; const AMessage: string; AData: TJSONValue = nil)`; constants MCP_ERR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_LEGACY = -32002 in MCPServer.Types (kept only for legacy era). In TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest add `on E: EMCPError do Result := CreateErrorResponse(id, E.Code, E.Message, E.Data)` BEFORE the generic handler and remove/limit the substring 'not found' heuristic to the processor's own 'Method [..] not found' exception (better: raise EMCPError(-32601) from ExecuteMethodCall). In TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource: `if not FResources.TryGetValue(URI, Resource) then raise EMCPError.Create(IfThen(Ctx.IsModern, JSONRPC_INVALID_PARAMS, MCP_ERR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_LEGACY), 'Resource not found', TJSONObject.Create.AddPair('uri', URI))`. The era comes from the shared request context (thread-local `TMCPRequestContext.Current` or an optional `IMCPCapabilityManagerEx.ExecuteMethodEx(Method, Params, Context)` discovered with Supports(), leaving IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod intact for third-party managers). Keep HTTP status 200 for this application-level -32602 (only header/_meta failures mandate 400; a 400 with a non-modern error body would trigger dual-era clients' legacy fallback).

gaps.title: Resource read exceptions are swallowed into the `text` field instead of a -32603 error
gaps.current: ReadResource catches any exception from Resource.Read and returns a success result whose text is 'Error reading resource: ' + E.Message (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:155-163).
gaps.required: "Servers SHOULD return `-32603` for internal errors" (modern MUST-adjacent wording in the same paragraph as the -32602 MUST); legacy "Internal errors: `-32603`".
gaps.compatImpact: Behaviour change for both eras: a failing custom TMCPResourceBase<T>.GetResourceData now produces a JSON-RPC error instead of a text blob (clients will finally see failures as failures). No compile impact.
gaps.suggestedChange: Remove the try/except at ResourcesManager.pas:155-163; let EMCPError propagate as-is and wrap any other Exception as EMCPError.Create(JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR, E.Message). Log at Error level with TLogger before re-raising.

gaps.title: Missing/invalid `uri` param is not rejected with -32602 (nil params crashes)
gaps.current: ReadResource calls Params.GetValue('uri') without checking Params (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:134-138); the processor passes Params = nil when the request has no params object (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:185-188) -> EAccessViolation -> -32603 'Access violation ...'. An empty or non-string uri falls into the 'not found' text path. No URI syntax validation exists anywhere (registry keys are arbitrary strings, /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:59-65).
gaps.required: `uri` is a required param (ResourceRequestParams); "Servers MUST validate all resource URIs"; malformed params -> -32602.
gaps.compatImpact: None for clients that send valid requests. Library consumers: registering a resource whose URI has no RFC3986 scheme would now fail fast at TMCPRegistry.RegisterResource (surface as an exception at startup) — document.
gaps.suggestedChange: In ReadResource: `if (Params = nil) or not (Params.GetValue('uri') is TJSONString) or (URI = '') then raise EMCPError.Create(JSONRPC_INVALID_PARAMS, 'Missing required parameter: uri')`. Add `class function TMCPUriUtils.IsValidUri(const S: string): Boolean` (scheme = ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*: via System.RegularExpressions, no control chars/whitespace) in a small src/Protocol/MCPServer.Uri.pas; call it in TMCPRegistry.RegisterResource (raise EArgumentException) and in ReadResource (-32602 'Invalid resource URI').

gaps.title: `resources/subscribe` / `resources/unsubscribe` handling and advertised `subscribe` flag per era
gaps.current: HandlesMethod does not include subscribe/unsubscribe (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:59-64) so they fall through to 'Method [...] not found' -> -32601 (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:121-123, :214-215) but always with HTTP 200 (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:509, :553). Capability advertised as {subscribe:false, listChanged:false} only in `initialize` (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:116-124); no subscriptions/listen support exists.
gaps.required: Modern: the methods no longer exist; unknown method -> -32601 and (HTTP) 404; subscriptions only via subscriptions/listen with resourceSubscriptions. Legacy: with subscribe:false the server need not implement them (-32601 acceptable). Advertising {subscribe:false, listChanged:false} (or {}) is valid in both eras.
gaps.compatImpact: No client-visible change beyond the HTTP status in modern (transport area). Library consumers unaffected.
gaps.suggestedChange: Keep `resources: {subscribe: false, listChanged: false}` (or `{}`) in both `initialize` and `server/discover`. Do not add handlers for resources/subscribe|unsubscribe. Ensure the transport maps -32601 to HTTP 404 for modern-era requests (cross-reference transport/lifecycle work item; the JsonRpcProcessor should expose the error code to TMCPIdHTTPServer, e.g. ProcessRequest returning a record {Body, ErrorCode} or an out parameter). If listChanged/subscribe are ever enabled, a `TMCPSubscriptionsManager` (subscriptions/listen) is the modern delivery path — out of scope here.

gaps.title: Capabilities are hard-coded in CoreManager rather than derived from the registered managers
gaps.current: TMCPCoreManager.Initialize always emits `tools` and `resources` capabilities (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:106-124) regardless of whether TMCPToolsManager/TMCPResourcesManager were registered (README 'Using as a Library' lets consumers register any subset; /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/README.md lines ~200-215). A consumer that omits TMCPResourcesManager still advertises `resources`, and a future PromptsManager/CompletionManager would have to edit CoreManager to be advertised.
gaps.required: "Servers that declare the `resources` capability MUST respond to `resources/list`"; "Servers that support prompts MUST declare the `prompts` capability"; "Servers that support completions MUST declare the `completions` capability". Both eras (initialize result / DiscoverResult).
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients see the same capability JSON for the default configuration. Library consumers: custom managers that implement the new optional interface become advertisable; those that do not are simply not listed (today they are never listed either), so no break.
gaps.suggestedChange: MCPServer.Types.pas: add `IMCPCapabilityProvider = interface ['{new guid}'] function GetCapabilityJSON: TJSONObject; end;` (returns the value object, e.g. {} or {listChanged:false}). Implement in TMCPToolsManager ({listChanged:false}), TMCPResourcesManager ({subscribe:false, listChanged:false}), TMCPPromptsManager ({listChanged:false}), TMCPCompletionManager ({}). Extend IMCPManagerRegistry with `function GetManagers: TArray<IMCPCapabilityManager>` (additive) and let TMCPCoreManager (initialize) and the new server/discover handler build `capabilities` by iterating managers and Supports(Manager, IMCPCapabilityProvider). Remove the unused TMCPCapabilities/TMCPToolsCapability/'supportsProgress'/'supportsCancellation' keys (not in any revision's ServerCapabilities schema) or keep them only under `experimental`.

gaps.title: Resource descriptor supports only uri/name/description/mimeType; optional fields (title, size, icons, annotations, _meta) unsupported and empty strings are emitted
gaps.current: ListResources emits exactly uri, name, description, mimeType (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:109-114) even when Description/MimeType are '' (ReadResource likewise emits mimeType '' at :153). IMCPResource / TMCPResourceBase<T> have no Title/Size/Icons/Annotations/Meta (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas:11-41).
gaps.required: Resource: `mimeType` "if known" (optional), `title`?, `size`?, `icons`?, `annotations`?, `_meta`? — all optional but part of the data model in both eras (title 2025-06-18+, icons 2025-11-25+).

New fields are optional; 2025-03-26 JSON schema does not set additionalProperties:false, so gating by negotiated version is polish, not a hard requirement. Library consumers: additive protected fields on TMCPResourceBase<T>; no signature changes.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add to TMCPResourceBase<T>: FTitle: string; FSize: Int64 (-1 = unknown); FAnnotations: TJSONObject (nil = none; audience/priority/lastModified); FIcons: TJSONArray (nil = none); FMeta: TJSONObject; expose through an additive `IMCPResourceMetadata` interface (GetTitle, GetSize, GetAnnotations, GetIcons, GetMeta). Add a shared `TMCPResourceJson.Describe(const R: IMCPResource; const Ctx): TJSONObject` helper used by ListResources, resource_link content blocks and (later) templates that adds optional pairs only when non-empty/-1/nil; gate `title`/`_meta` to negotiated version >= 2025-06-18 and `icons` to >= 2025-11-25 (modern always).

gaps.title: Binary (blob) resource contents and multi-part contents are impossible through IMCPResource
gaps.current: IMCPResource.Read returns a single string (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas:17, :91-134); ReadResource always writes one {uri, mimeType, text} item (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:147-157). TResourceContent (Base.pas:43-52) has only Text and is unused.
gaps.required: "Resources can contain either text or binary data": BlobResourceContents {uri, mimeType?, blob: base64}; "Binary data MUST be properly encoded"; "Servers MAY return multiple resource contents in response to a single `resources/read` request."
gaps.compatImpact: Purely additive: IMCPResource and TMCPResourceBase<T>.Read keep working (text path). Existing custom resources need no change. The same content record is reusable for prompt embedded resources.
gaps.suggestedChange: MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas: `TMCPResourceContents = record URI, MimeType: string; Text: string; Blob: TBytes; IsBlob: Boolean; Meta: TJSONObject; class function FromText(...)/FromBytes(...) end;` and additive interface `IMCPResourceReader = interface ['{new guid}'] function ReadContents: TArray<TMCPResourceContents>; end;`. TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource: if Supports(Resource, IMCPResourceReader) use it, else wrap Resource.Read into one text item. Serialize blob with `TBase64Encoding.Create(0).EncodeBytesToString(Bytes)` (line-length 0 -> no CR/LF; the default TNetEncoding.Base64 inserts line breaks every 76 chars, which would corrupt `blob`). Provide `TMCPBinaryResourceBase = class(TInterfacedObject, IMCPResource, IMCPResourceReader)` with abstract `function GetBytes(out MimeType: string): TBytes` and a sample (e.g. server icon PNG) to prove the path; set `size` = Length(Bytes) when known.

gaps.title: Resource templates are not supported (registry is exact-URI only; templates list always empty)
gaps.current: TMCPRegistry stores factories keyed by literal URI (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:21, :59-65, :79-89); ReadResource does an exact TryGetValue (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:150); ListResourceTemplates hard-codes an empty array with the comment 'this server doesn't support resource templates' (:186-193).
gaps.required: Optional feature: `resourceTemplates` entries with `uriTemplate` (RFC 6570), `name`, optional title/description/mimeType/icons/annotations; reads of URIs matching a template must resolve; templates MAY be completed via completion/complete (ref/resource).
gaps.compatImpact: Additive. Existing exact-URI registration path untouched; resources/templates/list keeps returning [] until a template is registered. Both eras use the same wire shape (plus modern caching fields).
gaps.suggestedChange: MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas: `TMCPTemplateVars = TDictionary<string,string>`; `IMCPResourceTemplate = interface ['{new guid}'] function GetUriTemplate: string; GetName; GetTitle; GetDescription; GetMimeType; function Matches(const URI: string; Vars: TMCPTemplateVars): Boolean; function CreateResource(const URI: string; Vars: TMCPTemplateVars): IMCPResource; end;` plus `TMCPResourceTemplateBase` implementing RFC 6570 level 1/2 matching (`{var}` -> `([^/]+)`, `{+var}` -> `(.+)`, `{/var}`, `{?var}` optional) by compiling the template to a System.RegularExpressions.TRegEx with named groups, percent-decoding captured values. MCPServer.Registration.pas: `TMCPResourceTemplateFactory = reference to function: IMCPResourceTemplate; class procedure RegisterResourceTemplate(const UriTemplate: string; Factory)`; `GetResourceTemplateURIs`; `CreateResourceTemplate`. TMCPResourcesManager: FTemplates: TList<IMCPResourceTemplate>; ListResourceTemplates emits them (with pagination/caching fields); ReadResource: exact lookup first, then first template whose Matches succeeds; else not-found error. Sample: `logs://{level}` returning filtered logs via TLogBuffer.GetLogs(100, Level) (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Logs.pas:160).

gaps.title: Prompts capability entirely missing (no prompts/list, prompts/get, no prompt abstraction)
gaps.current: No unit handles 'prompts/list' or 'prompts/get'; TMCPRegistry knows only tools and resources (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:13-36); CoreManager never advertises `prompts` (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:103-124); MCPServer.dpr registers only Core/Tools/Resources managers (/home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/MCPServer.dpr:84-91, :125-132). A client sending prompts/list gets -32601 via the 'not found' substring path (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214), which is the correct answer for a server that does not offer prompts.
gaps.required: Prompts are a MAY feature, but once offered: capability declared; prompts/list -> {prompts[], nextCursor?, (modern) resultType, ttlMs, cacheScope}; prompts/get -> {description?, messages[{role, content}], (modern) resultType}; content blocks text/image/audio/resource_link/resource; -32602 for unknown prompt or missing required argument; -32603 internal; MRTR (modern MAY); listChanged notifications only if advertised.
gaps.compatImpact: Fully additive: new units, new TMCPRegistry methods, new manager registered in the dpr and documented in README. Existing tools/resources code and consumer code untouched. Legacy clients (2025-03-26) must not receive `resource_link` content, `title` or `icons` — gate by negotiated version. prompts/get result must NOT carry ttlMs/cacheScope (not a CacheableResult).

gaps.title: No way for a resource or prompt to return an InputRequiredResult (MRTR)
gaps.current: Managers can only return a TJSONObject result or raise; no representation of input_required/inputRequests/requestState exists (IMCPResource.Read: string at /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas:17; ReadResource builds only contents at ResourcesManager.pas:142-172).
gaps.required: Modern MAY: resources/read and prompts/get MAY answer with {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests?, requestState?}; MUST include at least one of the two; MUST NOT include inputRequests the client did not declare capability for (from `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`); requestState is attacker-controlled and MUST be integrity-protected when it affects authorization; MUST NOT be sent on any other method.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive. Only resources/prompts/tools that raise the new exception are affected; in legacy era the manager converts it to a -32603 error (legacy servers would instead have issued a server-initiated elicitation request, which this server never supported).
gaps.suggestedChange: Shared with tools/call: in MCPServer.Errors.pas add `EMCPInputRequired = class(Exception) InputRequests: TJSONObject (owned, may be nil); RequestState: string; end;` and `TMCPInputResponses` accessor on the request context (params.inputResponses / params.requestState). TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource and TMCPPromptsManager.GetPrompt catch EMCPInputRequired and (modern only) return {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests?, requestState?} WITHOUT ttlMs/cacheScope; verify each inputRequests[*].method against the client capabilities in the request context (elicitation/sampling/roots) and drop/raise -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapability otherwise. Provide `TMCPRequestState.Sign/Verify` helper (HMAC-SHA256 with a per-process secret, System.Hash.THashSHA2.GetHMAC) so consumers do not hand-roll integrity protection.

Registration API for library consumers (TMCPRegistry.RegisterResource + factory, TMCPResourceBase<T>) is a clean extension point that the suggested additive interfaces (IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPPrompt) can build on without changing IMCPResource: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas:15-36; /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas:11-41
notes: Era selection is per request: a request with modern `_meta` is served under 2026-07-28 rules; an `initialize` handshake pins legacy rules for that HTTP session / stdio process (versioning.mdx § Backward Compatibility). The resources/prompts managers therefore need the negotiated revision and the client capabilities at execution time. Recommend ONE shared mechanism (thread-local `TMCPRequestContext.Current` set by TMCPJsonRpcProcessor, or an additive `IMCPCapabilityManagerEx.ExecuteMethodEx(Method, Params, Context)` discovered with Supports()) so IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod keeps its signature for third-party managers.

Error-code matrix for 'resource not found': modern MUST -32602 (+ data.uri SHOULD) and MUST NOT -32002; legacy 2025-03-26/06-18/11-25 SHOULD -32002. Clients of 2026-07-28 SHOULD still accept -32002, so a lazy single-code implementation would 'work', but the modern MUST NOT makes the dual-code switch mandatory for conformance.

Trap in the current processor: any exception message containing 'not found' is turned into -32601 (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214). Once the transport maps -32601 to HTTP 404 for modern requests (streamable-http.mdx), a naive 'Resource not found' exception would become a 404 that dual-era clients may misread as a legacy server. Introduce typed EMCPError before touching the managers.

HTTP status for application-level -32602 (resource not found, invalid cursor, unknown prompt, missing prompt argument) should stay 200: the spec only mandates 400 for malformed `_meta`/header errors, and streamable-http § Backward Compatibility says clients fall back to `initialize` on a 4xx whose body is not a recognized modern error (-32020/-32021/-32022).

ttlMs/cacheScope are only required in the modern era; they are not part of any legacy Result schema. Since legacy JSON schemas do not set additionalProperties:false they would be tolerated, but gating them (like resultType) keeps legacy responses byte-identical to today's, which is the safest compatibility story.

Recommended cache values for the built-ins: project://info and project://readme -> ttlMs 3600000, cacheScope public (static strings); logs://recent -> ttlMs 0, private (dynamic, and GetResourceData mutates the buffer at Resource.Logs.pas:209 — consider dropping that access-log side effect); server://status -> ttlMs 0, private (live telemetry). resources/list and resources/templates/list -> public with e.g. 300000 in the sample server (set fixed at construction, no auth); library default should be (0, private) which can never be wrong (CA-05).
GetPromptResult and CompleteResult are NOT CacheableResult — do not add ttlMs/cacheScope there. InputRequiredResult interim results also carry no caching hints.

Pagination is optional; the simplest conformant behaviour is 'never emit nextCursor, reject any supplied cursor with -32602' because the server never issued one. If a page size is configurable, keep 0 = unlimited as default so all existing clients see one page. Make list order deterministic (sort by uri/name or preserve registration order) — TDictionary.Values order is unspecified, which also hurts client-side caching keyed on list content.

Field availability by legacy revision (gate optional emission): `title` on Resource/ResourceTemplate/Prompt/PromptArgument and `_meta` on Resource/contents: 2025-06-18+; `icons`: 2025-11-25+; `annotations.lastModified`: 2025-06-18+; `resource_link` content in PromptMessage: 2025-06-18+ (2025-03-26 PromptMessage.content = text|image|audio|resource only); completion `context.arguments`: 2025-06-18+. Legacy JSON schemas leave additionalProperties open, so this gating is polish rather than a MUST.

Base64 in Delphi: System.NetEncoding.TNetEncoding.Base64 inserts CR/LF every 76 characters; use `TBase64Encoding.Create(0)` (CharsPerLine = 0) or `TNetEncoding.Base64String` (Delphi 12) for `blob` / image `data` so the value is a single-line base64 string as the schema expects (@format byte).

Modern `PaginatedRequest.params` is required (schema.ts 2026-07-28 line 1063: `params: PaginatedRequestParams`) because `_meta` is required, so `resources/list` without params is malformed -> -32602/400 in the modern era. This is enforced by the shared `_meta` validation (lifecycle area), not by the resources manager; the manager must still tolerate Params = nil for legacy requests.

Subscriptions: modern `resources/updated` requires `subscriptions/listen` streams with `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged` first and `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId` on every notification; legacy needs an HTTP GET SSE stream or stdio push. Since the server advertises listChanged:false / subscribe:false in both eras, nothing is required now; note that TMCPIdHTTPServer.HandleGetRequest opens and immediately closes an SSE stream (IdHTTPServer.pas:271-300), so even legacy list_changed delivery is not possible today — keep the flags false until a subscriptions manager exists.

Streamable HTTP `Mcp-Name` header for resources/read is sourced from `params.uri`; resource URIs routinely contain characters outside the plain-ASCII token set (':' '/' are fine, but spaces/non-ASCII must be Base64-sentinel encoded), so the transport validation must decode `=?base64?...?=` before comparing with the body (XC-04).

MRTR is shared across tools/call, prompts/get and resources/read; design the EMCPInputRequired exception + requestState HMAC helper once (Protocol layer) and reuse in ToolsManager, PromptsManager and ResourcesManager. Servers MUST NOT emit inputRequests for capabilities the client did not declare in `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`, so the request context must expose them.

Library-compat design rule for this whole area: never add members to IMCPResource, IMCPTool, IMCPCapabilityManager or IMCPManagerRegistry that would force third-party implementers to change (Delphi interfaces are not open for extension); use new GUID'd interfaces discovered with Supports(), new protected fields with safe defaults in TMCPResourceBase<T>/TMCPToolBase<T>, and additive class methods on TMCPRegistry. New units (MCPServer.Errors, MCPServer.Pagination, MCPServer.Prompt.Base, MCPServer.PromptsManager, MCPServer.CompletionManager) are opt-in; MCPServer.dpr, MCPServer.dproj (DCCReference list at /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/MCPServer.dproj:131-150) and build.bat search paths (`src\Prompts` must be added to the -U list at /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/build.bat) need updating.

The repo has no test project (only LICENSE, README.md, build.bat, generate-ssl-cert.bat, settings.ini.example, src). Suggest a DUnitX project exercising TMCPJsonRpcProcessor end-to-end for: resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope present on modern list/read results and absent on legacy; -32602 vs -32002 by era with data.uri; -32603 on read exception; -32602 on missing uri and on any cursor; blob base64 round-trip; prompts/get -32602 on unknown prompt and missing required argument; prompts/get result has no ttlMs.

TMCPServerStatusResource.SetNamePrefix re-registers a URI in TMCPRegistry at runtime (Resource.Server.pas:72-93); it only affects managers constructed afterwards, so RS-04 (no per-connection variation) is not violated, but document that registry changes after manager creation are not reflected (or add TMCPResourcesManager.Refresh + listChanged support later).

Open question for the orchestrator: whether prompts, resource templates and completion are in scope for this release (all three are MAY features). If yes, the suggested designs above are additive and share the pagination/caching/error plumbing with tools, so building the plumbing first (GAP-RS-01/02, GAP-CA-01, GAP-PG-01) makes each optional feature roughly one unit of work.

requirements.text: "Servers MUST send server-to-client requests (such as roots/list, sampling/createMessage, or elicitation/create) using the MRTR pattern. The previous pattern of server-initiated requests is no longer supported." Reinforced by patterns/index.mdx: "Servers MUST NOT initiate JSON-RPC requests"; stdio.mdx: "The server MUST NOT write JSON-RPC requests to stdout"; streamable-http.mdx: "The server MUST NOT send independent JSON-RPC requests on this stream."
requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr.mdx (top Note); basic/patterns/index.mdx (Overview); basic/transports/stdio.mdx (Receiving Messages); basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx (Receiving Messages)

requirements.text: "Servers MAY send InputRequiredResult responses on the following client requests: prompts/get, resources/read, tools/call." tools.mdx: "Servers MAY respond to tools/call with an InputRequiredResult"; same sentence in resources.mdx for resources/read and prompts.mdx for prompts/get.
requirements.source: mrtr.mdx (Supported Requests); server/tools.mdx (Input Required Tool Results); server/resources.mdx (Reading Resources); server/prompts.mdx (Getting a Prompt)

requirements.text: "Servers MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult responses on any other client requests." (i.e. not on tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list, server/discover, completion/complete, subscriptions/listen).

"inputRequests keys are server assigned identifiers and MUST be unique within the scope of the request." "inputRequests values are request objects that MUST be one of ElicitRequest, CreateMessageRequest, or ListRootsRequest" (each is {method, params}).
requirements.source: mrtr.mdx (Server Requirements (Basic Workflow) item 2); schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts InputRequest/InputRequests

requirements.text: "If a client request contains a requestState field, servers MUST treat requestState as an attacker-controlled input. If requestState influences authorization, resource access, or business logic, servers MUST protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and MUST reject state that fails verification. Integrity protection MAY be omitted only when tampering can cause nothing worse than request failure."

"To prevent replay, servers SHOULD include the following inside the integrity-protected requestState payload and verify each on receipt: the authenticated principal ...; a short expiry (TTL) ...; an identifier for the originating request, e.g. the method name and a digest of its salient parameters". Warning: "Servers for which a given requestState must be consumed at most once ... MUST enforce that invariant server-side."

"Servers MUST include at least one of inputRequests or requestState in every InputRequiredResult response." Schema: InputRequiredResult { resultType: "input_required"; inputRequests?; requestState?: string }.

"Servers MUST NOT send an inputRequests that the client has not declared support for in its capabilities. For example, if a client does not declare support for elicitation, the server MUST NOT include any elicitation/create requests." basic/index.mdx: "If processing a request requires a capability the client did not include in io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities, the server MUST return a MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) whose data.requiredCapabilities lists the missing capabilities. On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request." schema: "Servers MUST NOT infer capabilities from prior requests."
requirements.source: mrtr.mdx (Server Requirements item 7); basic/index.mdx (_meta, Per-request protocol fields); schema.ts RequestMetaObject.clientCapabilities, MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY = -32021, MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError

requirements.text: "Servers MUST NOT assume that clients will fulfill the inputRequests or retry the original request. Servers MAY choose to return an InputRequiredResult on multiple attempts at the same request". Retry is an independent request: "The JSON-RPC id MUST be different between the initial request and the retry" (client side) and "the server processing the retry does not need any information beyond what is directly present in the retry request".

"Servers SHOULD validate that the data provided by the client is a valid InputResponses object and that the information inside can be correctly parsed. Protocol errors (malformed JSON, invalid schema, internal server errors) SHOULD return a JSON-RPC error response with an appropriate error code and message."
"If additional, unexpected parameters are provided in the InputResponses object, the server SHOULD ignore any information it does not recognize or need."

"If the client fails to send all the information requested in a previous InputRequests, and the missing information is necessary for the server to process the request, the server SHOULD respond with a new InputRequiredResult requesting the missing information again, rather than returning an error."

"The result MUST include a resultType field to indicate the type of the result." "Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field." Values: "complete" for ordinary results, "input_required" for InputRequiredResult; "Extensions MAY add additional ResultType values. The set of supported ResultType values MUST be created from the set defined in the core protocol and include any additional values of supported extensions that are advertised via capabilities."
requirements.source: basic/index.mdx (Responses; ResultType); schema.ts Result.resultType; changelog.mdx (Major changes 8)

requirements.text: SEP-2322: InputRequiredResult "MAY be sent either as a standalone response or as the final message on an SSE stream, although implementations are encouraged to prefer the former. If using an SSE stream, servers MUST NOT send any message on the stream after the incomplete response message." streamable-http.mdx: "The final JSON-RPC response SHOULD terminate the stream."
requirements.source: seps/2322-MRTR.md (Protocol Requirements for Ephemeral Workflow, Server Behavior); streamable-http.mdx (Receiving Messages)

requirements.text: Legacy sessions know nothing of resultType/InputRequiredResult: in 2025-03-26..2025-11-25 server-to-client requests are JSON-RPC requests on an SSE stream ("The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications before sending the JSON-RPC response"), and "Both parties MUST: Respect the negotiated protocol version; Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated." versioning.mdx: "An initialize request selects legacy semantics, scoped to the stdio process (stdio) or the session (HTTP), as specified by the negotiated legacy protocol version." => a dual-era server MUST NOT emit InputRequiredResult (resultType input_required) to a legacy-era client.

requirements.source: client/elicitation.mdx (User Interaction Model Warning; Form Mode Security); identical text in 2025-11-25/client/elicitation.mdx; 2025-06-18: "Servers MUST NOT use elicitation to request sensitive information"

requirements.text: "Servers MUST NOT send elicitation requests with modes that are not supported by the client." "an empty capabilities object is equivalent to declaring support for form mode only" (elicitation: {} == {form: {}}). In 2026-07-28 the capability is declared per request in _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities; in 2025-11-25 during initialize; in 2025-06-18 elicitation is `object` (form only, no mode field).

"All elicitation requests MUST include the following parameters: mode (optional for form, defaults to form), message." "Form mode elicitation requests MUST either specify mode: \"form\" or omit the mode field, and include ... requestedSchema." "URL mode elicitation requests MUST specify mode: \"url\", a message, and include ... url"; "The url parameter MUST contain a valid URL." requestedSchema is "limited to flat objects with primitive properties only" (string/number/integer/boolean/enum incl. multi-select arrays).
requirements.source: client/elicitation.mdx (Elicitation Requests; Form Mode Elicitation Requests; Requested Schema; URL Mode Elicitation Requests); schema.ts ElicitRequest, PrimitiveSchemaDefinition

requirements.text: "Servers MAY request information from a user during the processing of a client request, by sending an InputRequiredResult containing an elicitation/create request." Client result inside inputResponses is ElicitResult {action: accept|decline|cancel; content?}. For URL mode, action accept "does not mean that the interaction is complete"; on retry "the server determines from the echoed requestState (or its own stored state) whether the out-of-band interaction has completed, and either returns the final result or responds with another InputRequiredResult."
