requirements.source: client/elicitation.mdx (Elicitation Requests; URL Mode Elicitation Requests; Response Actions)

requirements.text: "Servers SHOULD NOT assume that elicitation requests will always succeed, and MUST handle cases where the user declines or cancels the elicitation, or where the client fails to process the request."

"Servers MUST bind elicitation requests to the client and user identity"; "if state is stored, servers implementing elicitation MUST securely associate this state with individual users ... State storage MUST be protected against unauthorized access; For remote MCP servers, user identification MUST be derived from credentials acquired via MCP authorization when possible (e.g. sub claim)"; "Servers MUST NOT rely on client-provided user identification without server verification".
requirements.source: client/elicitation.mdx (Security Considerations 1; Statefulness; Identifying the User)

requirements.text: Safe URL Handling — servers requesting elicitation: "MUST NOT include sensitive information about the end-user ... in the URL"; "MUST NOT provide a URL which is pre-authenticated to access a protected resource"; "SHOULD NOT include URLs intended to be clickable in any field of a form mode elicitation request"; "SHOULD use HTTPS URLs for non-development environments". Phishing: "The MCP Server MUST verify the identity of the user who opens the URL before accepting information" and "MUST ensure that the user who started the elicitation request ... is the same user who completes the authorization flow"; "MUST ensure that the mechanism to determine the user's identity is resilient to attacks where an attacker can modify the elicitation URL." OAuth: "MCP servers MUST NOT rely on URL mode elicitation to authorize users for themselves"; "The MCP server MUST NOT transmit credentials obtained through URL mode elicitation to the MCP client."
requirements.source: client/elicitation.mdx (Safe URL Handling; Phishing; URL Mode Elicitation for OAuth Flows)

requirements.text: "Servers SHOULD validate received data matches the requested schema" (Form Mode Security 3).

2026-07-28 removes the 2025-11-25 URLElicitationRequiredError and elicitationId: "Implementations of this protocol version MUST NOT emit these codes: ... -32042 — URL elicitation required (2025-11-25 only)." changelog 11: removes notifications/elicitation/complete and the elicitationId field; "Servers needing to correlate an elicitation across retries encode their own identifier in requestState." (Legacy 2025-11-25: server MAY return -32042 only when URL mode elicitation is required and MAY send notifications/elicitation/complete.)
requirements.source: basic/index.mdx (Error Codes); changelog.mdx (Minor changes 11); 2025-11-25/client/elicitation.mdx (URL Elicitation Required Error; Completion Notifications)

requirements.text: Roots: "New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it; existing implementations SHOULD migrate to passing directories or files via tool parameters, resource URIs, or server configuration." Earliest removal: first revision released on or after 2027-07-28. If used: "servers send an InputRequiredResult containing a roots/list request"; servers SHOULD "Check for roots capability before usage". notifications/roots/list_changed is removed in 2026-07-28 (changelog 5).
requirements.source: client/roots.mdx (Warning; Listing Roots; Implementation Guidelines); deprecated.mdx (Deprecated table); changelog.mdx (Major changes 5)

requirements.text: Sampling: "New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it; existing implementations SHOULD migrate to integrating directly with LLM provider APIs." If used: "Servers MUST NOT send tool-enabled sampling requests to Clients that have not declared support for tool use via the sampling.tools capability"; "Servers SHOULD avoid using [includeContext thisServer/allServers] ... and SHOULD NOT use them unless the client declares sampling.context capability"; "Servers MUST ensure that when replying to a stopReason: toolUse, each ToolUseContent item is responded to with a ToolResultContent item with a matching toolUseId, and that the user message contains only tool results".
requirements.source: client/sampling.mdx (Warning; Tools in Sampling; Capabilities Note; Security Considerations 6)

requirements.text: SEP-2577 Capability negotiation during the deprecation window: "Implementations that encounter deprecated capabilities MUST still handle them correctly. Implementations SHOULD emit a warning (e.g., in logs or developer tooling) when deprecated capabilities are negotiated. New implementations SHOULD NOT add support for deprecated features unless needed for backward compatibility with existing counterparts." "During the deprecation period, wire-level behavior is unchanged."

Logging: "New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it; existing implementations SHOULD migrate to logging to stderr for stdio transports, or to OpenTelemetry for structured observability." stdio.mdx: "The server MAY write UTF-8 strings to stderr for any logging purposes"; "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message."
"Servers that emit log message notifications MUST declare the logging capability" ({"capabilities": {"logging": {}}}). Same sentence in 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25.

"To receive log messages for a specific request, include io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in the request's _meta. The server MUST NOT emit notifications/message for a request that does not include this field." "When the field is present, the server MAY send notifications/message notifications at or above the requested level on the response stream of that request, before the final response. notifications/message is request-scoped: the server MUST NOT deliver it on a subscriptions/listen stream or on any stream other than the one carrying the response to the request that set the log level." logging/setLevel is removed (changelog 5).
requirements.source: server/utilities/logging.mdx (Per-request log level); schema.ts RequestMetaObject["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]; changelog.mdx (Major changes 5)

requirements.text: "If the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel value carried in a request's _meta is not a recognized log level, the server SHOULD reject that request with a standard JSON-RPC error: Invalid log level: -32602 (Invalid params)". Legacy: for logging/setLevel "Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Invalid log level: -32602" (only meaningful when logging capability is advertised; otherwise -32601 per schema MethodNotFoundError: "one gated behind a server capability the server did not advertise").
"Log messages MUST NOT contain: Credentials or secrets; Personal identifying information; Internal system details that could aid attacks" (applies to any notifications/message ever emitted).

"The client sends a subscriptions/listen request with a notifications filter specifying which event types it wants to receive. The server MUST NOT send notification types the client has not explicitly requested." Filter fields: toolsListChanged, promptsListChanged, resourcesListChanged (booleans), resourceSubscriptions (string[]); all optional. subscriptions/listen "replaces the former resources/subscribe RPC and the HTTP GET endpoint".
requirements.source: basic/patterns/subscriptions.mdx (Opening a Stream; Notification Filter); schema.ts SubscriptionFilter, SubscriptionsListenRequestParams; changelog.mdx (Major changes 4)

requirements.text: "The server MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message carrying the subscription's ID in _meta under io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId, and MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before it. On stdio ... this ordering is defined per subscription ID and not per channel: messages belonging to other subscriptions MAY be interleaved before it." "The notifications field in the acknowledgment reflects the subset the server agreed to honor. Notification types the server does not support are omitted."

"On notifications delivered via a subscriptions/listen stream, the server MUST include io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId in _meta so the client can correlate the notification with the originating subscription request." "The value is the JSON-RPC ID of the subscriptions/listen request." (schema NotificationMetaObject: RequestId, absent on request-scoped notifications such as progress).
requirements.source: basic/index.mdx (_meta, Per-response protocol fields); basic/patterns/subscriptions.mdx (Receiving Notifications); schema.ts NotificationMetaObject

requirements.text: Graceful closure: "When the server ends a subscription on its own initiative (for example, during shutdown), it SHOULD respond to the original subscriptions/listen request with a completion result before closing the stream." Result: {"resultType":"complete","_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId": <listen id>}} — schema SubscriptionsListenResult makes _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId REQUIRED.
requirements.source: basic/patterns/subscriptions.mdx (Cancellation; Graceful Closure); schema.ts SubscriptionsListenResult, SubscriptionsListenResultMetaObject; schema/2026-07-28/examples/SubscriptionsListenResult/listen-closed.json

requirements.text: "A server MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing a subscriptions/listen request ID when it tears down that subscription stream (see Subscriptions). Servers MUST NOT send notifications/cancelled for any other purpose." schema: "On stdio, the server also sends this notification, solely to terminate a subscriptions/listen stream ... Servers MUST NOT use this notification to cancel any other request."

Client cancellation of a listen stream: HTTP — "Closing the SSE response stream MUST be treated by the server as cancellation of that request ... The server SHOULD stop work on the cancelled request as soon as practical and MUST NOT send any further messages for it." stdio — client sends notifications/cancelled referencing the listen request id; "Servers receiving cancellation notifications SHOULD: Stop processing the cancelled request; Free associated resources; Not send a response for the cancelled request"; "Servers MAY ignore cancellation notifications if: The referenced request is unknown; Processing has already completed". "On stdio, if the connection is terminated and then re-established, the client MUST re-send subscriptions/listen ... the server holds no subscription state across reconnections."
requirements.source: basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx (Cancellation); basic/transports/stdio.mdx (Cancellation); basic/patterns/cancellation.mdx (Behavior Requirements); basic/patterns/subscriptions.mdx (Graceful Closure)

requirements.text: HTTP long-lived streams: "When initiating an SSE stream, servers SHOULD include the X-Accel-Buffering: no header"; "For long-lived streams — in particular the subscriptions/listen response stream — servers are encouraged to periodically emit an SSE comment line (a line beginning with a colon, e.g. :\r\n) as a keep-alive." "Resumable SSE streams via Last-Event-ID are not supported." Request-scoped notifications (progress, message) "are not delivered on the listen stream".

"When the list of available tools changes, servers that declared the listChanged capability SHOULD send a notification to clients that have opened a subscriptions/listen stream with toolsListChanged: true" (notifications/tools/list_changed); identical for prompts (promptsListChanged) and resources (resourcesListChanged; resources/updated for resourceSubscriptions). resources capability: "subscribe: whether the server supports resource-specific update notifications for resources requested through subscriptions/listen using the resourceSubscriptions filter"; "Servers may advertise either feature independently, together or neither."
requirements.source: server/tools.mdx (Capabilities; List Changed Notification); server/prompts.mdx; server/resources.mdx (Capabilities; Subscriptions)

requirements.text: Unimplemented methods (e.g. subscriptions/listen, resources/subscribe, logging/setLevel, tasks/*): MethodNotFoundError -32601 — "a server returns this error when a client invokes a method the server does not implement — either a genuinely unknown method, or one gated behind a server capability the server did not advertise". On HTTP (modern): "If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with 404 Not Found and a JSON-RPC error with code -32601."

Legacy (2025-03-26..2025-11-25): "servers that declared the listChanged capability SHOULD send a notification" (notifications/resources/list_changed, notifications/tools/list_changed); resources/subscribe only if subscribe capability declared; GET SSE stream: "The server MUST either return Content-Type: text/event-stream in response to this HTTP GET, or else return HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed, indicating that the server does not offer an SSE stream at this endpoint." Modern-only servers: "HTTP GET or DELETE to the MCP endpoint: respond with 405 Method Not Allowed" (SHOULD).
requirements.source: 2025-06-18/server/resources.mdx (Capabilities; List Changed Notification; Subscriptions); 2025-06-18/server/tools.mdx (List Changed Notification); 2025-11-25/basic/transports.mdx (Listening for Messages from the Server item 3); 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx (Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions)

requirements.text: "Extensions are advertised in the extensions field of capabilities, which is a map of extension identifiers to per-extension settings objects. Extension identifiers MUST follow the _meta key naming rules, with a mandatory prefix." "Each extension specifies the schema of its settings object; an empty object indicates support with no additional settings." Servers advertise in server/discover result capabilities.extensions; clients in _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities.extensions on each request. "Extensions are always disabled by default and require explicit opt-in from the developer." The extensions field does not exist in the 2025-06-18 / 2025-11-25 schemas.
requirements.source: basic/versioning.mdx (Extension Negotiation); docs/extensions/overview.mdx (Negotiation; SDK Implementation Note); schema.ts ServerCapabilities.extensions, ClientCapabilities.extensions; changelog.mdx (Minor changes 1); grep of schema/2025-11-25/schema.ts and schema/2025-06-18/schema.ts (no `extensions?` field)

requirements.text: "If one party supports an extension but the other does not, the supporting party MUST either revert to core protocol behavior or reject the request with an appropriate error. Extensions SHOULD document their expected fallback behavior." Extension resultType values may only be used when the extension is advertised via capabilities (see MRTR-13).

Tasks extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks: "A server that has negotiated this extension MAY return CreateTaskResult in lieu of a standard result (e.g. CallToolResult) in response to any supported request [tools/call] at its own discretion and on a per-request basis." "A server that returns the standard CallToolResult shape — i.e., never elects to create a task — remains fully spec-compliant under this extension."
requirements.source: seps/2663-tasks-extension.md (Capability Negotiation; Supported Methods; Backward Compatibility); docs/extensions/tasks/overview.mdx

requirements.text: "A server MUST NOT return CreateTaskResult to a client that did not include the extension capability on its request, regardless of prior declarations." "If a server is unable to service a request to a client that does not declare this extension capability without returning CreateTaskResult, the server MUST return an error with the code -32021 ... data.requiredCapabilities.extensions['io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks']". "Servers MUST set resultType to \"task\" when returning a CreateTaskResult ... MUST NOT set resultType to \"task\" on result types other than CreateTaskResult."

If implemented: "A server MUST NOT return CreateTaskResult until the task is durably created"; tasks/get "MUST" return the status-specific Task shape (working | input_required + inputRequests | completed + result | failed + error | cancelled), resultType "complete"; tasks/update: "the server MUST acknowledge the request with an empty result", "SHOULD ignore any inputResponses ... not currently outstanding"; tasks/cancel: "The server MUST acknowledge the request with an empty result", cooperative; errors: "Invalid or nonexistent taskId: -32602 ... Servers MUST return this error for tasks/get ... SHOULD ... for tasks/update and tasks/cancel"; "-32021 ... MUST return this error for non-declaring clients issuing tasks/get, tasks/update, and tasks/cancel" and for non-declaring clients requesting taskIds on subscriptions/listen; "Each request key in inputRequests MUST be unique over the lifetime of a single task"; "The failed status MUST NOT be used to represent non-JSON-RPC errors" (isError results are completed); HTTP: "the client MUST set the Mcp-Name header ... to the value of params.taskId"; security: task IDs "MUST generate them with sufficient entropy"; "Servers MUST perform authentication and authorization checks on each task-related request"; "notifications/progress and notifications/message notifications MUST NOT be sent on the subscriptions/listen stream for a task"; MRTR before task: "SHOULD resolve all MRTR exchanges synchronously before responding with a CreateTaskResult".
requirements.source: seps/2663-tasks-extension.md (Task Creation; Task Polling; Task Update Requests; Task Cancellation; Task Status Notifications; Streamable HTTP: Routing Headers; Error Handling; Security Implications; Composition with MRTR)

requirements.text: Cross-era: under 2025-11-25 "Servers MUST NOT treat this capability as enabling tasks under that protocol version"; "Servers MUST treat clients declaring only the legacy [tasks.*] capability as non-declaring with respect to this extension"; "tasks/result is removed; clients calling it MUST receive -32601"; "The task parameter on CallToolRequest is removed; servers MUST ignore it"; servers "MUST NOT continue to advertise the legacy capabilities under any protocol version that includes this extension." Reserved: tasks/ prefix, notifications/tasks/ prefix, resultType "task".

gaps.title: No per-request context (era, _meta, clientCapabilities, transport) reaches managers/tools — root enabler for every MUST in this area
gaps.current: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest(RequestBody, SessionID) (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:146-224) extracts only id/method/params and calls IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod(Method, Params) (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:265-270, JsonRpcProcessor.pas:113-126). params._meta is never read; nothing knows whether the caller is a legacy session (initialize, CoreManager.pas:70-140) or a modern request; IMCPTool.Execute(Arguments) (src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:18) and IMCPResource.Read (src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas:247) receive no context either. Tool instances are singletons shared across Indy worker threads (ToolsManager.pas:245-248), so context cannot be stored on the tool.
gaps.required: Servers MUST NOT rely on undeclared client capabilities and MUST NOT infer them from prior requests (MRTR-08); MUST NOT emit notifications/message without io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel (LG-03); MUST honor only the requested notification filter (SUB-01); MUST only use negotiated capabilities in legacy sessions (MRTR-15).
gaps.compatImpact: Library consumers: keep IMCPCapabilityManager, IMCPTool, IMCPResource GUIDs and signatures unchanged; add opt-in extension interfaces so existing custom managers/tools/resources compile and behave identically (they simply never see the context). Legacy clients: no wire change.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit Protocol/MCPServer.RequestContext.pas: IMCPRequestContext = interface with ProtocolVersion: string; Era: TMCPProtocolEra (peLegacy, peModern); ClientCapabilities: TJSONObject (read-only, may be nil for legacy pre-initialize); ClientInfo: TJSONObject; LogLevel: string; RequestID: TValue; InputResponses: TJSONObject; RequestState: string; Transport hooks (IMCPNotificationSink for streams). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor builds it from params._meta (modern) or from the CoreManager's negotiated legacy session (legacy). Add IMCPCapabilityManagerV2 = interface(IMCPCapabilityManager) ['new GUID'] function ExecuteMethodEx(const Method: string; const Params: TJSONObject; const Context: IMCPRequestContext): TValue; processor does `if Supports(Manager, IMCPCapabilityManagerV2, V2) then V2.ExecuteMethodEx(...) else Manager.ExecuteMethod(...)`. Same pattern for tools: IMCPContextAwareTool ['GUID'] function ExecuteWithContext(const Arguments: TJSONObject; const Context: IMCPRequestContext): TValue; TMCPToolBase/TMCPToolBase<T>/<T,R> implement it by default as Execute(Arguments) and expose a protected virtual ExecuteWithParams overload taking Context. Never store context in a field of the singleton tool; pass it as a parameter (or a threadvar as last resort).

gaps.title: Error plumbing cannot express -32021 (MissingRequiredClientCapability) with data.requiredCapabilities, nor -32602 for invalid input
gaps.current: CreateErrorResponse(RequestID, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage) (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:128-144) has no `data` member; error code selection is by substring: Pos('not found', E.Message) → -32601, else -32603 (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:211-217); only five constants exist (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:27-32, duplicated in IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99). No -32602 is ever emitted; HTTP status is always 200 (IdHTTPServer.pas:509,553).
gaps.required: MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities (basic/index.mdx _meta; schema MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError), HTTP 400; invalid logLevel / malformed inputResponses → -32602; error responses MAY include data.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive; existing consumers raising plain Exception keep getting -32603/-32601 as today. Legacy clients unaffected. (HTTP status mapping itself belongs to the transport area.)
gaps.suggestedChange: In MCPServer.Types.pas add consts MCP_ERROR_HEADER_MISMATCH = -32020; MCP_ERROR_MISSING_CLIENT_CAPABILITY = -32021; MCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION = -32022; and class EMCPJsonRpcError = class(Exception) with Code: Integer and Data: TJSONObject (owned), plus helpers EMCPMissingClientCapability.Create(const RequiredCapabilities: TJSONObject) and EMCPInvalidParams.Create(const Msg). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest catches `on E: EMCPJsonRpcError` first and emits code + data verbatim; CreateErrorResponse gains an optional `Data: TJSONObject` parameter. Expose the resulting code to the transport (e.g. ProcessRequest returns a record {Body: string; ErrorCode: Integer}) so IdHTTPServer can map -32021/-32022/-32020 → 400 and -32601 → 404 for modern requests.

gaps.title: No way for a tool or resource to return an InputRequiredResult (MRTR) — elicitation is impossible in the modern era
gaps.current: TMCPToolsManager.CallTool (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:386-407) always wraps the TValue into a CallToolResult via BuildToolCallResponse (286-339): string → content/isError, TJSONObject → structuredContent, TJSONArray → content. TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource (src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:538-591) always returns contents[]. IMCPTool.Execute returns TValue (Tool.Base.pas:18), TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithParams returns string (Tool.Base.pas:49), IMCPResource.Read returns string (Resource.Base.pas:247). No type for inputRequests/requestState exists anywhere in src/. There is no prompts manager at all.
gaps.required: Servers MAY answer tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get with {"resultType":"input_required","inputRequests":{key:{method,params}},"requestState":string} containing at least one of the two fields, keys unique per request, values restricted to elicitation/create | sampling/createMessage | roots/list; MAY return it repeatedly; the retry arrives as a NEW request carrying inputResponses/requestState.
gaps.compatImpact: Purely additive for library consumers: existing TMCPToolBase<T>/TMCPToolBase<T,R>/TMCPResourceBase<T> subclasses keep compiling; MRTR is opt-in via a new exception type or a new return type. Legacy clients never see it (see GAP-MRTR-04). This is the only sanctioned path to elicitation for modern clients, so although MAY, it is the headline feature of the upgrade.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit Protocol/MCPServer.Mrtr.pas: TMCPInputRequiredResult = class (InputRequests: TJSONObject map; RequestState: string; function ToJSON: TJSONObject builds resultType input_required and raises if both are empty — MRTR-07); EMCPInputRequired = class(Exception) carrying an owned TMCPInputRequiredResult so any tool/resource/prompt code can `raise EMCPInputRequired.Create(Result)`. TMCPToolsManager.CallTool and TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource (and the future PromptsManager.GetPrompt) catch EMCPInputRequired (only in ExecuteTool/Read — not in list methods) and return its JSON as the result. Provide builders: TMCPInputRequests.AddElicitationForm(key, message, schema: TJSONObject), AddElicitationUrl(key, message, url), AddSampling(key, params), AddRoots(key); enforce key uniqueness (MRTR-04) via TDictionary. Extend TMCPToolBase<T> with protected `InputResponses: TJSONObject` / `RequestState: string` accessors taken from the IMCPRequestContext passed by the manager (GAP-CTX-01), plus helper `function ElicitResultFor(const Key: string): TMCPElicitResult` (see GAP-EL-01). Keep the SSE path unchanged: HandlePostRequestSSE (IdHTTPServer.pas:470-510) already emits exactly one event, satisfying MRTR-14.

gaps.title: No enforcement that inputRequests only use capabilities the client declared on THIS request (elicitation form/url, sampling(.tools), roots) and no -32021 path
gaps.current: Client capabilities are never parsed: CoreManager.Initialize only logs clientInfo (CoreManager.pas:83-95) and discards params.capabilities; modern _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities is never read (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:185-190 only passes params through).
gaps.required: "Servers MUST NOT send an inputRequests that the client has not declared support for"; elicitation {} means form only; "Servers MUST NOT send elicitation requests with modes that are not supported by the client"; "Servers MUST NOT send tool-enabled sampling requests to Clients that have not declared ... sampling.tools"; when the request cannot proceed without the capability → -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities (HTTP 400).
gaps.compatImpact: Only affects consumers who opt into MRTR. Legacy sessions: capability snapshot comes from initialize params and is stored in the session/process (allowed for legacy semantics); modern: from each request's _meta and never cached.
gaps.suggestedChange: In TMCPToolsManager (and ResourcesManager) before serializing an EMCPInputRequired: for each inputRequests value check Context.ClientCapabilities — 'elicitation/create' requires capabilities.elicitation present; mode 'url' additionally requires elicitation.url; mode 'form'/absent requires elicitation.form or an empty elicitation object; 'sampling/createMessage' requires sampling (and sampling.tools when params.tools present); 'roots/list' requires roots. On failure raise EMCPMissingClientCapability with data {"requiredCapabilities": {"elicitation": {"url": {}}}} (shape per schema/2026-07-28/examples/MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError/missing-elicitation-capability.json). Store the legacy initialize `capabilities` object in TMCPCoreManager (new property ClientCapabilities: TJSONObject, cloned) so the same check runs for legacy sessions if legacy elicitation is ever added; for modern requests read _meta per request only.

gaps.title: No integrity-protected requestState helper (HMAC/AEAD, TTL, principal, request digest)
gaps.current: Nothing in src/ signs, verifies or even reads params.requestState; ExtractToolNameAndArguments (ToolsManager.pas:252-274) ignores every param except name/arguments. TMCPSettings (src/Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas) has no secret-key setting.
gaps.required: "servers MUST treat requestState as an attacker-controlled input ... MUST protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and MUST reject state that fails verification"; SHOULD embed and verify principal, TTL, and originating-request identifier (method + digest of salient params).
gaps.compatImpact: Additive helper; no effect on consumers who do not use MRTR. Operators running multiple instances behind a load balancer must configure a shared key (new settings.ini [Security] RequestStateKey); a per-process random key is generated (and logged as a warning) when absent.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit Core/MCPServer.RequestState.pas: TMCPRequestState with class function Seal(const Payload: TJSONObject; const Context: IMCPRequestContext; const Method: string; const ArgsDigest: string; TTLSeconds: Integer): string — serializes {p: payload, m: method, d: ArgsDigest, u: principal-or-'', exp: unix} as base64url (System.NetEncoding TBase64URLEncoding) and appends '.' + base64url(HMAC-SHA256) via System.Hash.THashSHA2.GetHMACAsBytes(Data, Key, SHA256); class function Open(const Token: string; const Context; const Method; const ArgsDigest; out Payload: TJSONObject): Boolean using constant-time compare, checking exp, m, d and u. ArgsDigest = SHA-256 of canonical JSON of params.arguments (or uri). On verification failure: raise EMCPInvalidParams('Invalid request state') (-32602) or, per MRTR-12, return a fresh InputRequiredResult without trusting the state. Key source: TMCPSettings.RequestStateKey (base64), else random 32 bytes at startup. Document that single-use semantics (one-time redemption) are the tool author's responsibility.

gaps.title: No era gating: an InputRequiredResult (and resultType) must never be sent to a legacy-era client; resultType must be added for modern-era results
gaps.current: All results are emitted verbatim from managers (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:192-200); there is no notion of era, and no resultType is ever added. MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION is the single constant '2025-06-18' (Types.pas:237) echoed by Initialize (CoreManager.pas:101).
gaps.required: Legacy: "Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated" — legacy clients do not understand resultType/input_required (they would treat the object as a CallToolResult lacking `content`). Modern: "The result MUST include a resultType field"; "Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field."
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Inspector default) keep receiving byte-identical results if resultType is only injected for modern-era requests. Library consumers who raise EMCPInputRequired get a defined legacy fallback instead of a broken response.
gaps.suggestedChange: In TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest: when Context.Era = peModern and the result is a TJSONObject without 'resultType', AddPair('resultType','complete') (InputRequiredResult already carries 'input_required'). In TMCPToolsManager/ResourcesManager: when an EMCPInputRequired escapes under Context.Era = peLegacy, convert it — tools: CallToolResult {content:[{type:text,text:'This tool needs additional input (elicitation: <message>) which requires MCP 2026-07-28; please supply the information as tool arguments'}], isError:true}; resources: -32603 internal error or a text content explaining the same. Optionally (not recommended, see notes) implement legacy in-stream elicitation/create over SSE later. Add a unit test matrix: modern tools/call → input_required; legacy tools/call → isError text.

gaps.title: Structural guarantee that InputRequiredResult is only produced for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get
gaps.current: Once EMCPInputRequired exists, any manager method (e.g. a custom IMCPCapabilityManager implementing tools/list) could leak it; today the generic handler turns unknown exceptions into -32603 (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:204-218), which is accidentally correct.
gaps.required: "Servers MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult responses on any other client requests."
gaps.compatImpact: None for consumers; defensive.
gaps.suggestedChange: Catch EMCPInputRequired only inside TMCPToolsManager.CallTool, TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource and TMCPPromptsManager.GetPrompt; in TMCPJsonRpcProcessor treat any EMCPInputRequired that reaches it as an internal error (-32603, message 'InputRequiredResult not permitted for method X') and log it; document in README that custom managers must not return resultType input_required except from those three methods.

gaps.title: inputResponses parsing/validation semantics (ignore unknown keys, re-request missing keys, handle decline/cancel, validate against requestedSchema)
gaps.current: params.inputResponses is silently dropped (ToolsManager.pas:264-273 reads only name/arguments) — consistent with 'ignore unrecognized' but provides no parsed access, no ElicitResult model, no schema validation.
gaps.required: SHOULD validate InputResponses; SHOULD ignore unknown entries; SHOULD answer missing-but-necessary info with a new InputRequiredResult rather than an error; MUST handle decline/cancel; SHOULD validate content against requestedSchema.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive helper API; no wire impact.
gaps.suggestedChange: In Protocol/MCPServer.Mrtr.pas: TMCPInputResponses wrapper over the TJSONObject with TryGetElicit(key, out R: TMCPElicitResult): Boolean (Action: accept|decline|cancel, Content: TJSONObject), TryGetSampling(key, out TJSONObject), TryGetRoots(key, out TJSONArray); malformed value (not an object / bad action) → raise EMCPInvalidParams (-32602); unknown keys ignored. Provide TMCPElicitSchema.Validate(Content, RequestedSchema): TArray<string> covering type, required, enum/oneOf/anyOf-const, minLength/maxLength, minimum/maximum, minItems/maxItems, format email/uri/date/date-time. Pattern documented in README: if TryGetElicit fails or Action <> accept, either finish with an isError result or raise a new EMCPInputRequired (MRTR-12).

gaps.title: No elicitation API: form/URL request builders, mode gating, restricted schema builder, URL-mode safety rules
gaps.current: No elicitation code exists in src/. (The absence of -32042/elicitationId/notifications/elicitation/complete is conformant for 2026-07-28.)
gaps.required: Elicitation requests MUST carry message (+ requestedSchema for form; + url for url mode; mode 'url' explicit); schema restricted to flat primitives; MUST NOT use form mode for secrets; MUST NOT put sensitive data or pre-authenticated links in URLs; MUST NOT send unsupported modes; MUST NOT emit -32042 in modern era.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive; library consumers get TMCPElicitation helpers; nothing existing changes.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit Protocol/MCPServer.Elicitation.pas: TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder (AddString(name, title, description, required, minLength, maxLength, format, default), AddNumber/AddInteger(min,max,default), AddBoolean(default), AddEnum(values, titles?), AddMultiSelect(values, minItems, maxItems)) producing {type:object, properties, required}; TMCPElicitation.Form(message, schema) → {method:'elicitation/create', params:{mode:'form', message, requestedSchema}} and TMCPElicitation.Url(message, url) → {mode:'url', message, url} with a guard that url is absolute and, unless settings allow, https; TMCPElicitResult parser (accept/decline/cancel). Mode gating is done in the manager (GAP-MRTR-02). Add a README section 'Elicitation (MCP 2026-07-28)' with the dual-era caveat and the security rules (no secrets via form; bind URL flows to the authenticated user; never pre-authenticate URLs).

gaps.title: io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in modern _meta is not validated (SHOULD reject unknown values with -32602)
gaps.current: _meta is never inspected (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:185-190). No notifications/message are emitted anywhere, so LG-03 is trivially met, but an invalid level value is accepted silently.
gaps.required: "If the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel value carried in a request's _meta is not a recognized log level, the server SHOULD reject that request with ... -32602 (Invalid params)". The MCP Inspector stamps logLevel=debug on every modern request by default (docs/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/protocol-eras.mdx, Logging/Modern), so the key WILL appear in practice.
gaps.compatImpact: None for legacy; modern clients sending a bogus level get -32602 instead of silent acceptance.
gaps.suggestedChange: In the _meta parser (GAP-CTX-01): if 'io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel' is present and not in ['debug','info','notice','warning','error','critical','alert','emergency'] raise EMCPInvalidParams('Invalid log level'). Store the level on IMCPRequestContext.LogLevel for information only. Do NOT add a `logging` capability, `logging/setLevel` handling, or `notifications/message` emission (deprecated, LG-01); keep TLogger → stderr/file. Optionally log a TLogger.Debug once per process that a client requested protocol logging which this server does not provide.

gaps.title: No warning when deprecated capabilities are negotiated (roots/sampling in client capabilities, or a legacy logging/setLevel call)
gaps.current: CoreManager.Initialize ignores params.capabilities (CoreManager.pas:83-95); logging/setLevel from a legacy client yields -32601 'Method [logging/setLevel] not found' (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:121-123, 214-215) with no diagnostic.
gaps.required: SEP-2577: "Implementations SHOULD emit a warning (e.g., in logs or developer tooling) when deprecated capabilities are negotiated."
gaps.compatImpact: Log-only; no wire change.
gaps.suggestedChange: In TMCPCoreManager.Initialize (legacy) and in the modern _meta parser: if clientCapabilities contains 'roots' or 'sampling', TLogger.Warning('Client declares deprecated capability %s (SEP-2577); this server does not use it'). Keep -32601 for logging/setLevel and resources/subscribe (capability not advertised) but log at Info level that the method is unsupported/deprecated.

gaps.title: subscriptions/listen not implemented and no long-lived stream infrastructure (HTTP SSE stays open; stdio interleaving)
gaps.current: subscriptions/listen falls through GetManagerForMethod → nil (ManagerRegistry.pas:171-184) → '-32601 Method [subscriptions/listen] not found' with HTTP 200 (IdHTTPServer.pas:553). HandlePostRequestSSE writes one event into ResponseInfo.ContentText and returns (IdHTTPServer.pas:470-510) — Indy sends the whole response after the handler returns, so no stream can stay open and nothing can be pushed later. Stdio loop is strictly synchronous Readln→ProcessRequest→Writeln (StdioTransport.pas:611-653) with no output lock and no way to write asynchronous notifications. X-Accel-Buffering: no is already set (IdHTTPServer.pas:287,483).
gaps.required: If the server offers the method: MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged first with _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId = listen request id and only the agreed filter subset; MUST tag every stream notification with subscriptionId; MUST NOT send unrequested types; SHOULD send completion result {resultType:'complete',_meta:{subscriptionId}} on server-initiated teardown; MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing the listen id when tearing down; HTTP client disconnect = cancellation (MUST NOT write further); stdio notifications/cancelled → stop; keep-alive SSE comments encouraged. If NOT offered: -32601 (and HTTP 404 in modern era — transport area).
gaps.compatImpact: Not offering listen is compliant because CoreManager advertises resources.subscribe=false/listChanged=false and tools has no listChanged (CoreManager.pas:106-124) and lists are static. But the MCP Inspector's modern-era 'Subscribe' button sends subscriptions/listen and expects an acknowledgment (protocol-eras.mdx, Resource subscriptions/Modern), and modern hosts may open a toolsListChanged stream; an -32601 there is legal but unfriendly. Library consumers: additive (new optional TMCPSubscriptionsManager + IMCPNotificationSink); TMCPIdHTTPServer/TMCPStdioTransport public surface unchanged. Each open HTTP listen stream occupies one Indy worker thread (mind MaxConnections).
gaps.suggestedChange:
Phase A (recommended minimum): new Managers/MCPServer.SubscriptionsManager.pas implementing IMCPCapabilityManagerV2 for 'subscriptions/listen' (modern era only; legacy → -32601): validate params.notifications; compute agreed subset (currently {} because nothing is advertised — but include resourceSubscriptions entries only for URIs that exist AND only if resources.subscribe is advertised); register a TMCPSubscription {Id: RequestId; Filter; Sink: IMCPNotificationSink} in a thread-safe TMCPSubscriptionRegistry; immediately push notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged (with _meta.subscriptionId) through the sink; return a sentinel TValue telling the transport 'stream stays open'. HTTP: in TMCPIdHTTPServer add HandlePostRequestStream: set ContentType text/event-stream + X-Accel-Buffering: no, call ResponseInfo.WriteHeader, then loop: write queued messages as 'event: message
data: <json>

' via AContext.Connection.IOHandler.Write, write ':
' every 15-30 s as keep-alive, exit on EIdSocketError/EIdConnClosedGracefully (client cancellation; mark subscription cancelled, write nothing more) or on server Stop. On Stop (before FHTTPServer.Active := False): for every open subscription write notifications/cancelled {requestId: listenId} then the completion result {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":listenId,"result":{"resultType":"complete","_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId":listenId}}} and close. Stdio: introduce TMCPStdioWriter (TCriticalSection around Writeln/Flush) shared by the request loop and subscription sinks; keep subscriptions in the registry; handle client 'notifications/cancelled' (currently dropped at JsonRpcProcessor.pas:174-181) by removing the subscription; on EOF emit notifications/cancelled + completion result for each active subscription before exiting. Phase B (only if dynamic registration is ever added): publish notifications/tools/list_changed etc. through the registry and flip listChanged flags to true (GAP-SUB-02).

gaps.title: listChanged/subscribe stay false — correct today, but must remain in sync with any future dynamic registration and must be reported through server/discover for modern clients
gaps.current: CoreManager advertises resources {subscribe:false, listChanged:false} and tools {supportsProgress:false, supportsCancellation:false} (non-standard keys; CoreManager.pas:106-124). Tool/resource sets are built once from TMCPRegistry at manager construction (ToolsManager.pas:240-250; ResourcesManager.pas:497-505), so the advertised 'false' is truthful and no list_changed notification is ever owed.
gaps.required: "servers that declared the listChanged capability SHOULD send a notification" (legacy: at any time; modern: on listen streams with the matching filter). Servers may advertise neither feature.
gaps.compatImpact: Keep false unless GAP-SUB-01 Phase B ships. Removing the non-standard supportsProgress/supportsCancellation keys is harmless for legacy clients (unknown keys are ignored by all SDKs) but is another area's concern.
gaps.suggestedChange: Centralize capability construction in one function (e.g. TMCPCapabilityBuilder.Build(Era): TJSONObject) used by both TMCPCoreManager.Initialize (legacy) and the new server/discover handler (modern) so that tools.listChanged / resources.subscribe / resources.listChanged / prompts.listChanged and (modern only) extensions are declared from a single source of truth; add TMCPRegistry.OnChanged event so that, if runtime registration is added later, the SubscriptionsManager can fan out list_changed and the builder can flip listChanged to true.

gaps.title: Legacy HTTP GET SSE stream returns 200 text/event-stream and immediately closes; modern GET should be 405
gaps.current: HandleGetRequest (IdHTTPServer.pas:271-314): with Accept: text/event-stream it answers 200, Content-Type text/event-stream, empty body, closes; otherwise a JSON info blob. The comment at :296-298 acknowledges 'closes stream immediately'.
gaps.required: Legacy: server "MUST either return Content-Type: text/event-stream in response to this HTTP GET, or else return HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed, indicating that the server does not offer an SSE stream". Modern-only: "HTTP GET or DELETE to the MCP endpoint: respond with 405" (SHOULD). GET is removed in 2026-07-28 (replaced by subscriptions/listen).
gaps.compatImpact: Returning 405 is explicitly allowed by legacy clients (Claude Code/Inspector treat 405 as 'no standalone stream' and continue); an immediately-closed 200 stream can trigger reconnect loops in some clients. Overlaps the transport area.
gaps.suggestedChange: HandleGetRequest: return 405 Method Not Allowed (with Allow: POST, OPTIONS) for every GET to the MCP endpoint regardless of Accept, unless GAP-SUB-01 later implements a legacy standalone stream. Keep the non-SSE JSON info response only if the project wants it for browsers, but on a different path.

gaps.title: No `extensions` capability map and no place to advertise it; extension resultType values must be reserved
gaps.current: Capabilities are hand-built in CoreManager.Initialize (CoreManager.pas:103-124); TMCPCapabilities in Types.pas:278-287 (with an unused FLogging TJSONObject) is dead code. No server/discover exists (other area), so there is no modern capability surface at all.
gaps.required: Servers advertise extensions in server/discover capabilities.extensions (map id → settings object, ids with mandatory reverse-DNS prefix); a party that supports an extension the other does not MUST fall back to core behaviour or reject; resultType values beyond complete/input_required only when the extension is advertised. `extensions` is not part of the 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 schemas.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive: `Extensions` map empty by default (field omitted). Do not emit `extensions` in the legacy initialize result (not in those schemas; harmless but pointless). Library consumers can register extension ids via a new TMCPCapabilityBuilder.RegisterExtension(id, settings) without touching existing types.
gaps.suggestedChange: In the capability builder (GAP-SUB-02): TDictionary<string, TJSONObject> FExtensions; RegisterExtension validates the id against the _meta key rules (prefix = reverse-DNS labels, '/' separator, name [A-Za-z0-9._-]); emit 'extensions' in the modern DiscoverResult only when non-empty. Read client extensions from _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities.extensions into IMCPRequestContext.ClientExtensions: TArray<string> so managers can gate extension behaviour per request (EXT-02). Never emit a resultType other than complete/input_required unless the corresponding extension id is both registered server-side and present in the request's client extensions.

gaps.title: Tasks extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks) not implemented — rate as optional/later
gaps.current: No tasks/* methods (→ -32601), no task store, no background execution: tools run synchronously on the Indy worker thread / stdio loop (ToolsManager.pas:276-284). No legacy tasks.* capability is advertised and the legacy `task` param is ignored (ToolsManager.pas:252-274) — which already satisfies the 'MUST ignore' rule.
gaps.required: If offered: advertise capabilities.extensions['io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks'] = {} in server/discover; only return CreateTaskResult (resultType 'task', taskId, status, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt, ttlMs, pollIntervalMs) to requests whose _meta clientCapabilities.extensions contains the id, after the task is durably created; serve tasks/get (status-specific DetailedTask; -32602 unknown id; -32021 for non-declaring clients), tasks/update (inputResponses keyed to outstanding inputRequests; empty ack; ignore non-outstanding keys), tasks/cancel (empty ack, cooperative); optional notifications/tasks via subscriptions/listen taskIds; unguessable ids; per-request authz; never advertise legacy tasks.* under a version that includes the extension; tasks/result → -32601; on HTTP clients send Mcp-Name = taskId (header validation is the transport area).
gaps.compatImpact: Purely additive and opt-in (extensions are disabled by default per extensions/overview.mdx). Would introduce a new IMCPCapabilityManager (TMCPTasksManager) and a new tool-side API (e.g. TMCPToolBase.RunAsTask or a TMCPTaskContext) — existing tools untouched. Stdio single-process and HTTP multi-thread both need an in-memory TMCPTaskStore with TTL purge; a multi-instance deployment needs sticky routing on Mcp-Name (spec) or a shared store.
gaps.suggestedChange: Later phase: Managers/MCPServer.TasksManager.pas (IMCPCapabilityManagerV2) + Core/MCPServer.TaskStore.pas (TDictionary<string, TMCPTask> under TMonitor; TMCPTask {Id (TGuid + 16 random bytes, base64url), Status enum working/input_required/completed/failed/cancelled, StatusMessage, CreatedAt/LastUpdatedAt ISO-8601 UTC, TtlMs, PollIntervalMs, Result/Error TJSONObject, OutstandingInputRequests TJSONObject}); TMCPToolsManager.CallTool checks a new IMCPTaskCapableTool interface + Context.ClientExtensions contains 'io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks' → create task, start TTask.Run(execute tool; on EMCPInputRequired move to input_required with its inputRequests; on completion store result), return CreateTaskResult; if the tool REQUIRES task mode and the client did not declare it → EMCPMissingClientCapability with data.requiredCapabilities.extensions. Add the extension id to the capability builder only when a TasksManager is registered.

gaps.title: Roots/sampling: do not add server-side use; if ever exposed, only through MRTR builders with capability gating and a deprecation warning
gaps.current: No roots/list or sampling/createMessage usage anywhere; no legacy server-initiated requests exist (GET stream closes at IdHTTPServer.pas:294; POST SSE emits only the response at :488-509). Conformant with the SHOULD NOTs.
gaps.required: New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt roots/sampling (earliest removal: first revision on/after 2027-07-28); if used they MUST only travel as inputRequests (modern), MUST respect sampling.tools / sampling.context gating, and implementations SHOULD warn when deprecated capabilities are negotiated.
gaps.compatImpact: No change recommended. If the TMCPInputRequests builder (GAP-MRTR-01) exposes AddSampling/AddRoots for completeness, mark them `deprecated 'SEP-2577'` in Delphi so consumers get a compiler hint, and keep them behind the same capability check as elicitation.
gaps.suggestedChange: Document in README: 'Roots and sampling are deprecated in MCP 2026-07-28; this library does not implement them server-side. Pass directories via tool parameters/resource URIs/settings.ini; call LLM provider APIs directly (e.g. via System.Net.HttpClient) instead of sampling.' Optionally provide the deprecated builders as described.

alreadyConformant: MRTR-01 / patterns MUST NOT initiate requests: the server never sends JSON-RPC requests to the client — the legacy GET SSE stream closes immediately (src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:293-299) and the POST SSE path emits exactly one event, the response (IdHTTPServer.pas:488-509); stdio only ever writes responses (src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas:621-628). MRTR-14 (InputRequiredResult must be the last SSE message) is satisfied by construction for the same reason.

LG-01/LG-02/LG-03/LG-04 (modern) and LG-05: no `logging` capability is advertised (src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas:103-124), no notifications/message is ever emitted, and diagnostics go to stderr in stdio mode (src/MCPServer.dpr:543-544 sets TLogger.UseStdErr; src/Core/MCPServer.Logger.pas) — exactly the SEP-2577 migration path and the stdio rule that stdout carries only MCP messages.
RS-01/RS-02 (SHOULD NOT adopt roots/sampling): no roots/list or sampling/createMessage code exists anywhere under src/.
EL-09: no code emits -32042, elicitationId or notifications/elicitation/complete, so the 2026-07-28 'MUST NOT emit -32042' holds.

SUB-08/SUB-10 vacuously satisfied and truthfully advertised: resources.subscribe=false and resources.listChanged=false (CoreManager.pas:116-124), no tools.listChanged; tool and resource sets are fixed at manager construction (src/Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas:240-250; src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas:497-505), so no list_changed/updated notification is ever owed in either era.

SUB-09 / MethodNotFoundError semantics: unknown or unadvertised methods (subscriptions/listen, resources/subscribe, logging/setLevel, tasks/*, tasks/result) yield JSON-RPC -32601 via GetManagerForMethod → nil (src/Core/MCPServer.ManagerRegistry.pas:171-184; src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:121-123, 214-215) — the correct code; only the modern HTTP 404 mapping is missing (transport area).

Notifications from the client never receive a JSON-RPC response (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:174-181) and HTTP answers 202 Accepted for notification-only bodies (IdHTTPServer.pas:343-352), matching basic/index.mdx 'The receiver MUST NOT send a response' and streamable-http.mdx item 5.

TSK-04 'servers MUST ignore the legacy task parameter on CallToolRequest' and 'MUST NOT advertise legacy tasks.* capabilities': ExtractToolNameAndArguments reads only name/arguments (ToolsManager.pas:252-274) and no tasks capability is advertised (CoreManager.pas:103-124).
MRTR-11 (ignore unrecognized inputResponses data): unknown params such as inputResponses/requestState are ignored rather than rejected (ToolsManager.pas:252-274; ResourcesManager.pas:548-552).
SUB-07 partial: X-Accel-Buffering: no and Cache-Control: no-cache are already set on every SSE response (IdHTTPServer.pas:285-287, 481-483).

Tool-level failures are reported inside the result with isError:true rather than as protocol errors (ToolsManager.pas:276-284, 307-322), matching the CallToolResult guidance in schema.ts and MRTR's 'protocol errors → JSON-RPC error' split.
MRTR-15 (legacy clients never see InputRequiredResult) currently holds trivially because no InputRequiredResult can be produced; the gap only opens once GAP-MRTR-01 ships, hence GAP-MRTR-04.
notes: Client adoption of 2026-07-28 (as of 2026-09-03, from the cloned repo): docs/extensions/client-matrix.mdx only tracks EXTENSION support (MCP Apps for Claude web/Desktop, VS Code Copilot, M365 Copilot, Goose, Postman, MCPJam, ChatGPT, Cursor, Archestra, PostHog Code; Enterprise Auth for Archestra) and says nothing about protocol revisions. blog/content/posts/2026-07-28-spec-ga/index.md: 'All four Tier 1 SDKs speak 2026-07-28 as of today' (TypeScript, Python, Go, C#), Rust SDK in beta; ecosystem quotes are server/infra side (Cloudflare Agents SDK 'day zero', Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, FastMCP 4.0, Supabase, Honeycomb, Stacklok, Manufact/mcp-use). blog 2026-06-29-sdk-betas: 'clients that speak 2026-07-28 fall back to the initialize handshake when they reach a server on 2025-11-25 or earlier'; TS/Go servers must opt in to serve 2026-07-28, Python v2 serves both eras from one endpoint, C# preview defaults to stateless. blog 2026-07-27-ruby-sdk-1-0: Ruby implements 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 only. No blog post or spec doc states that Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop or VS Code speak 2026-07-28. The MCP Inspector (docs/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/protocol-eras.mdx) supports both eras but its DEFAULT protocolEra is `legacy` (plain initialize, no probing); `auto` probes server/discover and falls back; `modern` pins 2026-07-28. Conclusion: the legacy path (initialize; 2025-03-26/2025-06-18/2025-11-25) remains the primary path for Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, VS Code and default Inspector; the modern path matters today for SDK-built clients, Inspector in auto/modern, and hosted platforms.

Inspector modern-era behaviour that the server will actually meet: (1) stamps _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel'] = 'debug' on every request by default — the server must tolerate it and 'silence is correct behavior' (GAP-LG-01); (2) 'Subscribe' sends subscriptions/listen with resourceSubscriptions + resourcesListChanged and waits for notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged, reconnecting by re-sending listen if the stream drops (GAP-SUB-01); (3) drives MRTR manually with an MRTR_MAX_ROUNDS limit; (4) notes that the legacy server.elicitInput pattern ERRORS on a 2026-07-28 connection — MRTR is the only modern elicitation path; (5) Tasks tab is gated on the negotiated io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension in modern era.

Spec tension to decide on: subscriptions.mdx 'Graceful Closure' says the server SHOULD answer the listen request with a completion result on teardown, while cancellation.mdx (and schema CancelledNotification, 'On stdio') says the server MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing the listen id when tearing down the stream. Recommended ordering: stdio → notifications/cancelled then the completion result; HTTP → completion result then close the SSE stream (a notifications/cancelled on HTTP is harmless but the transport page says no client-side cancelled is expected there).

SEP-2322 still lists GetTaskPayloadRequest (tasks/result) as an MRTR-capable request; SEP-2663 removed tasks/result. Follow mrtr.mdx's three-method table (tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get) — the normative page.

The RC blog post (2026-05-21) shows an InputRequiredResult example with {"type":"elicitation","schema":...}; that shape is non-normative and wrong — use schema.ts ({method:'elicitation/create', params:{mode,message,requestedSchema}}) and the schema/2026-07-28/examples/InputRequiredResult/*.json files.

MRTR retry semantics for implementers: the retry is a brand-new request (new id) carrying the ORIGINAL name/arguments plus inputResponses (+ echoed requestState). The server must reconstruct everything from that one request; SEP-2322's ADO example shows accumulating earlier answers inside requestState across rounds. Load shedding (requestState without inputRequests) is also legal.

Delphi implementation hints: HMAC-SHA256 via System.Hash.THashSHA2.GetHMACAsBytes(Data, Key, THashSHA2.TSHA2Version.SHA256); base64url via System.NetEncoding (TBase64URLEncoding / TNetEncoding.Base64URL); random keys via System.Hash/THashSHA2 over TGuid.NewGuid + Random or Winapi BCryptGenRandom; ISO-8601 via System.DateUtils.DateToISO8601(Now, False) (Tasks). Tools are singletons shared by Indy worker threads (ToolsManager.pas:245-248) — never store per-request context in tool fields; pass IMCPRequestContext as a parameter.

Indy long-lived SSE (needed only for subscriptions/listen): TIdHTTPServer transmits ResponseInfo after OnCommand returns, so a listen handler must call ResponseInfo.WriteHeader and then write directly to AContext.Connection.IOHandler in a loop until disconnect/shutdown; each stream pins one worker thread (set TIdHTTPServer.MaxConnections accordingly); TMCPIdHTTPServer.Stop must close streams gracefully before FHTTPServer.Active := False.

Because capability flags are truthful (no listChanged/subscribe) the cheapest fully-compliant option for subscriptions/listen is to keep -32601 (with HTTP 404 in the modern era, transport area). The friendlier option (acknowledge with the agreed subset, possibly {}, keep the stream open with ':' keep-alives, close gracefully) costs the streaming plumbing in GAP-SUB-01 but makes Inspector/host 'Subscribe' flows succeed.

Legacy in-stream elicitation (server sends elicitation/create on the SSE stream and waits for the client's response POST) is NOT recommended: it requires per-session request/response correlation across HTTP requests (Mcp-Session-Id), blocks an Indy thread while waiting, and is exactly what SEP-2322 replaced. Fallback for legacy clients: isError text asking for the missing argument (GAP-MRTR-04).

Deprecated features timeline: roots, sampling, logging are Deprecated in 2026-07-28 with earliest removal 'first revision released on or after 2027-07-28' (deprecated.mdx); wire behaviour unchanged meanwhile. Not adding them keeps the library aligned with 'New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt'.

Type hygiene: TMCPCapabilities/TMCPToolsCapability/TMCPInitializeResponse/TMCPPingResponse/TMCPTool/TMCPToolsResponse in src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:278-337 are unused by the server; leave them for source compatibility but do not build new capability code on them (TMCPCapabilities.Logging would otherwise tempt someone to advertise the deprecated logging capability).

Related gaps owned by other areas but prerequisites here: server/discover + supportedVersions (extensions are advertised there); resultType on every modern result; HTTP status mapping (-32021/-32022/-32020 → 400, -32601 → 404); modern per-request _meta parsing; Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name validation (tasks/* must carry Mcp-Name = taskId); removal of SSE event ids/Last-Event-ID; unknown tool/resource → -32602 in modern era (today they are isError text results / contents text).

Open question for the orchestrator: whether the project wants a PromptsManager at all — prompts/get is one of the three MRTR-capable methods, and the tools/prompts/resources capability builder should be shared.

Ping is removed in 2026-07-28 (changelog 5: 'Remove ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed'); the CoreManager's ping handler (CoreManager.pas:52,142-155) must remain for legacy clients but is not part of the modern surface.

gapReports.area: Authorization (OAuth 2.1 resource-server role), transport security best practices (Origin/DNS rebinding, localhost binding, token passthrough, state/requestState integrity, x-mcp-header injection, logging hygiene), SDK/client ecosystem status for 2026-07-28, and conformance/acceptance tooling (conformance CLI, MCP Inspector)

requirements.source: /home/user/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx # Protocol Requirements (identical wording in 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26 basic/authorization.mdx)
requirements.text: "Authorization is **OPTIONAL** for MCP implementations. When supported: Implementations using an HTTP-based transport **SHOULD** conform to this specification." Consequence: a server may ship without OAuth, but every auth feature it does ship must follow the MUSTs below.

"Implementations using an STDIO transport **SHOULD NOT** follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment." The stdio transport must not require/validate bearer tokens or emit OAuth challenges.

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx # Overview (item 4) and authorization-server-discovery.mdx # Authorization Server Location; same MUST in 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 basic/authorization.mdx
requirements.text: "MCP servers **MUST** implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC9728)." and "The Protected Resource Metadata document returned by the MCP server **MUST** include the `authorization_servers` field containing at least one authorization server." (Applies only when the server implements authorization, per AUTH-01.)

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/authorization-server-discovery.mdx # Protected Resource Metadata Discovery Requirements; legacy stricter form in docs/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization.mdx line 87
requirements.text: Modern: "MCP servers **MUST** implement one of the following discovery mechanisms ... 1. **WWW-Authenticate Header**: Include the resource metadata URL in the `WWW-Authenticate` HTTP header under `resource_metadata` when returning `401 Unauthorized` responses ... 2. **Well-Known URI**: Serve metadata at a well-known URI ... `https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/public/mcp` ... or at the root: `https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`". Legacy 2025-06-18: "MCP servers **MUST** use the HTTP header `WWW-Authenticate` when returning a _401 Unauthorized_ to indicate the location of the resource server metadata URL" (header is mandatory, not optional). A dual-era server should therefore always emit the WWW-Authenticate header AND serve the well-known URI.

"MCP servers **SHOULD** include a `scope` parameter in the `WWW-Authenticate` header as defined in RFC 6750 Section 3 to indicate the scopes required for accessing the resource." Example: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", scope="files:read"`. Also: "Servers **SHOULD** strive for consistency in how they construct scope sets".

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx # Access Token Usage > Token Handling (identical in 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 # Token Handling)
requirements.text: "MCP servers, acting in their role as an OAuth 2.1 resource server, **MUST** validate access tokens as described in OAuth 2.1 Section 5.2. MCP servers **MUST** validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to RFC 8707 Section 2. If validation fails, servers **MUST** respond according to OAuth 2.1 Section 5.3 error handling requirements. Invalid or expired tokens **MUST** receive a HTTP 401 response." ... "MCP servers **MUST** only accept tokens that are valid for use with their own resources. MCP servers **MUST NOT** accept or transit any other tokens."

Client-side rule with a server-side consequence: "MCP client **MUST** use the Authorization request header field ... `Authorization: Bearer <access-token>` ... authorization **MUST** be included in every HTTP request from client to server. 2. Access tokens **MUST NOT** be included in the URI query string." A server must read bearer tokens only from the `Authorization` header (never from query parameters) and must re-validate on every request (no per-session caching of the auth decision).

"Servers **MUST** return appropriate HTTP status codes for authorization errors: 401 Unauthorized - Authorization required or token invalid; 403 Forbidden - Invalid scopes or insufficient permissions; 400 Bad Request - Malformed authorization request".

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx # Scope Challenge Handling > Runtime Insufficient Scope Errors
requirements.text: "When a client makes a request with an access token with insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server **SHOULD** respond with: `HTTP 403 Forbidden` ... `WWW-Authenticate` header with the `Bearer` scheme and additional parameters: `error="insufficient_scope"` ... `scope="required_scope1 required_scope2"` ... `resource_metadata` ... `error_description` (optional)". Also: "servers **SHOULD** include all scopes required for the current operation in a single challenge" and "Servers **SHOULD** be consistent in their scope inclusion strategy".

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx # Step-Up Authorization Flow (SEP-2350 scope accumulation, listed in the 2026-06-29 SDK-betas post as a 2026-07-28 hardening change)
requirements.text: "Servers **MUST** account for scope hierarchies, where a broader scope implies narrower ones, when deciding whether a token is sufficient for an operation."

"**MCP Servers** (Protected Resources) **SHOULD NOT** include `offline_access` in `WWW-Authenticate` scope or Protected Resource Metadata `scopes_supported`, as refresh tokens are not a resource requirement."

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx # Token Audience Binding and Validation; # Access Token Privilege Restriction
requirements.text: "MCP servers **MUST** validate that tokens presented to them were specifically issued for their use" ... "MCP servers **MUST** validate access tokens before processing the request, ensuring the access token is issued specifically for the MCP server, and take all necessary steps to ensure no data is returned to unauthorized parties. A MCP server **MUST** follow the guidelines in OAuth 2.1 - Section 5.2 to validate inbound tokens. MCP servers **MUST** only accept tokens specifically intended for themselves and **MUST** reject tokens that do not include them in the audience claim or otherwise verify that they are the intended recipient of the token." ... "If the MCP server makes requests to upstream APIs, it may act as an OAuth client to them. The access token used at the upstream API is a separate token, issued by the upstream authorization server. The MCP server **MUST NOT** pass through the token it received from the MCP client."

"Attackers who obtain tokens stored by the client, or tokens cached or logged on the server can access protected resources ... Clients and servers **MUST** implement secure token storage and follow OAuth best practices, as outlined in OAuth 2.1, Section 7.1." Plus: "implementors **MUST** follow OAuth 2.1 security best practices as outlined in OAuth 2.1 Section 7". Server-side consequence: never log or persist bearer tokens; never expose them via resources.

"Implementations **MUST** follow OAuth 2.1 Section 1.5 'Communication Security'. Specifically: 1. All authorization server endpoints **MUST** be served over HTTPS. 1. All redirect URIs **MUST** be either `localhost` or use HTTPS." Server-side consequence: `authorization_servers` entries in the PRM document and the `resource_metadata` URL must be https (or loopback for development); TLS on the MCP endpoint itself is expected for any non-loopback deployment.

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx # Confused Deputy Problem; docs/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices.mdx # Confused Deputy Problem > Mitigation
requirements.text: "MCP proxy servers using static client IDs **MUST** obtain user consent for each dynamically registered client before forwarding to third-party authorization servers" and (tutorial) "To prevent confused deputy attacks, MCP proxy servers **MUST** implement ..." a consent flow with signed/session-stored `state`. Applies only to servers that proxy to a third-party API using a static OAuth client id (not the case for this repo's core; relevant to library consumers who build such proxies).

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx # MCP Authorization Extensions; docs/extensions/overview.mdx # Negotiation; docs/extensions/client-matrix.mdx
requirements.text: Authorization extensions (`io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/enterprise-managed-authorization`) are "**Optional** ... **Additive** ... **Composable** ... **Versioned independently**"; servers advertise them in the `extensions` field of the `server/discover` response. Not required for conformance (SEP-2133: "Extension support is not required for 100% protocol conformance").

2025-03-26 only (pre-RFC 9728 model where the MCP server itself hosts the authorization server): "MCP servers **SHOULD** and MCP clients **MUST** implement OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata ... MCP servers that do not support Authorization Server Metadata **MUST** follow the default URI schema" (`/authorize`, `/token`, `/register` relative to the MCP server origin), and "When authorization is required and not yet proven by the client, servers **MUST** respond with HTTP 401". A dual-era server that enables auth cannot satisfy 2025-03-26 clients without becoming an authorization server; the plan should declare 2025-03-26 authorization out of scope (2025-03-26 clients supported unauthenticated only).

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx # Security & Endpoint; docs/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports.mdx # Security Warning; docs/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports.mdx # Security Warning
requirements.text: "Servers **MUST** validate the `Origin` header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks. - If the `Origin` header is present and invalid, servers **MUST** respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden. The HTTP response body **MAY** comprise a JSON-RPC _error response_ that has no `id`." (2025-06-18 has the first sentence only; 403 clause added in 2025-11-25.) Must hold regardless of whether CORS response headers are enabled. Scored by conformance scenario `dns-rebinding-protection` in both the 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 required server sets.
"When running locally, servers **SHOULD** bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1) rather than all network interfaces (0.0.0.0)."
"Servers **SHOULD** implement proper authentication for all connections. Without these protections, attackers could use DNS rebinding to interact with local MCP servers from remote websites."
"MCP servers **MUST NOT** accept any tokens that were not explicitly issued for the MCP server." ("Token passthrough is explicitly forbidden in the authorization specification".)

"MCP servers that implement authorization **MUST** verify all inbound requests. MCP servers **MUST NOT** treat possession of a state handle as authentication. MCP servers **SHOULD** use secure, non-deterministic handles generated with secure random number generators ... MCP servers **SHOULD** bind handles server-side to the authenticated user, for example by keying stored state as `<user_id>:<handle>` where the user ID is derived from the verified token rather than supplied by the client, and reject a handle presented by any other principal." (Modern era replaces protocol sessions with server-minted handles passed as tool arguments.)

"MCP servers that implement authorization **MUST** verify all inbound requests. MCP Servers **MUST NOT** use sessions for authentication. MCP servers **MUST** use secure, non-deterministic session IDs. Generated session IDs (e.g., UUIDs) **SHOULD** use secure random number generators ... MCP servers **SHOULD** bind session IDs to user-specific information." Transport: "The session ID **SHOULD** be globally unique and cryptographically secure (e.g., a securely generated UUID, a JWT, or a cryptographic hash) ... The session ID **MUST** only contain visible ASCII characters (ranging from 0x21 to 0x7E)". Applies while the server serves legacy (`initialize`-based) clients with `Mcp-Session-Id`.

requirements.source: docs/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices.mdx # Local MCP Server Compromise > Mitigation (final list)
requirements.text: "MCP servers intending for their servers to be run locally **SHOULD** implement measures to prevent unauthorized usage from malicious processes: - Use the `stdio` transport to limit access to just the MCP client - Restrict access if using an HTTP transport, such as: - Require an authorization token - Use unix domain sockets or other Interprocess Communication (IPC) mechanisms with restricted access". Attack listed: "An attacker accesses an insecure local server that's left running on localhost via DNS rebinding".

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr.mdx # Server Requirements (Basic Workflow) items on requestState; # Security Considerations
requirements.text: "If a client request contains a `requestState` field, servers **MUST** treat `requestState` as an attacker-controlled input. If `requestState` influences authorization, resource access, or business logic, servers **MUST** protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and **MUST** reject state that fails verification. Integrity protection **MAY** be omitted only when tampering can cause nothing worse than request failure." "To prevent replay, servers **SHOULD** include the following inside the integrity-protected `requestState` payload and verify each on receipt: the authenticated principal ...; a short expiry (TTL) ...; an identifier for the originating request". "Servers for which a given `requestState` must be consumed at most once ... **MUST** enforce that invariant server-side." "Servers **MUST** validate request state as described". Scored by required 2026-07-28 server scenario `input-required-result-tampered-state`.

requirements.source: docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http.mdx # Server Behavior for Custom Headers; # Server Validation; # Value Encoding; # Case Sensitivity (overlaps the transport area; listed here because the spec frames it as an injection/source-of-truth defence)
requirements.text: "Servers **MUST** reject requests with a recognized `Mcp-Param-{Name}` header that contains invalid characters". "Any server that processes the message body **MUST** validate that encoded header values, after decoding if Base64-encoded, match the corresponding values in the request body. Servers **MUST** reject requests with a `400 Bad Request` HTTP status and JSON-RPC error code `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) if any validation fails." "Servers that process the request body **MUST** reject requests where the values specified in the headers do not match the corresponding values in the request body. This prevents potential security vulnerabilities when different components in the network rely on different sources of truth". Table: value `null` or absent -> "Server MUST NOT expect the header"; header omitted but value in body -> "Server MUST reject". "servers **MUST** decode an encoded `Mcp-Name` or `Mcp-Param-{Name}` value before comparing". "Clients and servers **MUST** use case-insensitive comparisons for header names. Header _values_ ... are case-sensitive." Failure conditions include a missing required standard header (`MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name`).

"Server developers **SHOULD NOT** mark sensitive parameters (passwords, API keys, tokens, PII) with `x-mcp-header`, as header values are visible to network intermediaries." Plus the constraint list for `x-mcp-header` values (MUST NOT be empty; MUST match RFC 9110 token syntax; MUST NOT contain CR/LF; MUST be case-insensitively unique; MUST only be on integer/string/boolean; MUST be statically reachable via `properties` only) which a server must enforce at tool-registration time because "An `x-mcp-header` annotation anywhere else makes the annotation — and thus the tool definition — invalid".

"New codes **MUST NOT** be allocated in this sub-range [-32000..-32019], and new implementations **SHOULD NOT** use codes from this sub-range at all" ... "[-32020 to -32099] Implementations **MUST NOT** emit any code from this sub-range that is not defined by this specification and **MUST** use defined codes only with their specified meanings" (`-32020` HeaderMismatch, `-32021` MissingRequiredClientCapability, `-32022` UnsupportedProtocolVersion). "Implementations of this protocol version **MUST NOT** emit these codes: `-32002` ... `-32042`". Relevant when adding auth/header/state error paths.

"The server **MUST NOT** write anything to its `stdout` that is not a valid MCP message." and "The server **MAY** write UTF-8 strings to `stderr` for any logging purposes". Security-relevant because credential/diagnostic logging must never reach stdout in stdio mode.

"The HTTP response body **MAY** comprise a JSON-RPC _error response_ that has no `id`." Optional: return `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Origin not allowed"}}` with the 403 so clients can surface a diagnostic.

gaps.title: No authorization hook at all: bearer tokens are never read or validated; no extension point for library consumers
gaps.current: /home/user/Delphi-MCP-Server/src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas HandleHTTPRequest (lines 172-208) goes CORS check -> endpoint match -> OPTIONS/GET/POST dispatch; the `Authorization` header is never read anywhere in src (only `Origin`, `Accept`, `Mcp-Session-Id` are read: lines 224, 277, 289, 333, 337).
