MCPServer.dpr (74-112) wires only Settings/ManagerRegistry/CoreManager. README.md lines 350-353 advertise `claude mcp add ... --header "Authorization: Bearer your-token"` "(if configured)" but nothing can be configured. IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod (Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:43) and IMCPTool.Execute (Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:18) receive no principal/context.
gaps.required: AUTH-01/SEC-03: HTTP servers SHOULD implement proper authentication; once implemented, tokens MUST be validated per OAuth 2.1 §5.2 with audience binding, invalid/expired -> 401, insufficient scope -> 403, malformed -> 400 (AUTH-06/08/12). SEC-07: locally-run HTTP servers SHOULD require an authorization token.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients: none (hook is opt-in; default remains an open server). Library consumers: purely additive — new `MCPServer.Authorization` unit and a new `Authorizer` property on TMCPIdHTTPServer defaulting to nil; existing TMCPToolBase<T>, TMCPResourceBase<T>, IMCPCapabilityManager and TMCPRegistry code compiles unchanged. TMCPStdioTransport MUST NOT get the hook (AUTH-02).
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit src/Core/MCPServer.Authorization.pas: `TMCPAuthDecision = (adAllow, adUnauthorized, adForbidden, adBadRequest)`; `TMCPPrincipal` (Subject, Scopes: TArray<string>, Claims: TJSONObject, Raw token never stored); `TMCPAuthChallenge` record (Scheme='Bearer', ResourceMetadataUrl, Scope, Error, ErrorDescription); `IMCPAuthorizer = interface ['{...}'] function Authorize(const ABearerToken: string; const AHttpMethod, APath: string; out APrincipal: TMCPPrincipal; out AChallenge: TMCPAuthChallenge): TMCPAuthDecision; end;`. Ship `TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer` (list of tokens from settings, constant-time comparison loop, no RTL helper exists) and an abstract `TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer` with `ExpectedAudience: string` (required; raise EMCPConfiguration if empty), `ResourceMetadataUrl`, `RequiredScopes`, and a virtual `ValidateToken(const AToken: string; out AClaims: TJSONObject): Boolean` for consumers (introspection RFC 7662 via System.Net.HttpClient can be provided in-core; JWT signature verification left to a sample unit because the RTL has no JOSE). In TMCPIdHTTPServer add `property Authorizer: IMCPAuthorizer` and call it in HandleHTTPRequest after Origin validation and endpoint match, for GET/POST/DELETE but NOT for OPTIONS (preflight must stay unauthenticated) and NOT for the `.well-known` metadata path (GAP-AUTH-03). Read the token only from `RequestInfo.RawHeaders.Values['Authorization']` with case-insensitive `Bearer ` prefix; never from `RequestInfo.Params`. Re-run the authorizer on every request (no caching by session id).

gaps.title: No 401/403 challenge with WWW-Authenticate (resource_metadata, scope, error=insufficient_scope)
gaps.current: No code path sets `WWW-Authenticate`; the only non-2xx responses are 404 (IdHTTPServer.pas 189-190), 405 (202-203), 403 for Origin (247-248) and JSON-RPC errors carried in HTTP 200 (509, 553). HTTP status constants at lines 82-89 lack 400 and 401.
gaps.required: AUTH-04 (legacy MUST / modern one-of MUST): 401 responses carry `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<url>"`; AUTH-05: SHOULD add `scope="..."`; AUTH-09: 403 with `error="insufficient_scope", scope="...", resource_metadata="..."`; AUTH-11: never advertise `offline_access`.
gaps.compatImpact: Only affects deployments that enable an Authorizer. Legacy (2025-06-18/2025-11-25) clients such as the Inspector parse the same header, so one implementation serves both eras. No API change for library consumers.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add `HTTP_BAD_REQUEST = 400`, `HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED = 401` constants. Add `procedure TMCPIdHTTPServer.WriteAuthChallenge(ResponseInfo: TIdHTTPResponseInfo; const AChallenge: TMCPAuthChallenge; AStatus: Integer)` that builds `Bearer resource_metadata="..."[, scope="..."][, error="..."][, error_description="..."]` (quote/escape per RFC 9110; reject CR/LF) and assigns `ResponseInfo.WWWAuthenticate.Text` (Indy emits it as the WWW-Authenticate header) or `CustomHeaders.Values['WWW-Authenticate']`; set `ResponseNo`, `ContentType := 'application/json'` with an optional id-less JSON-RPC error body. Filter `offline_access` out of any scope list at configuration time and log a warning. Expose `WWW-Authenticate` via `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` (see GAP-SEC-02).

gaps.title: No RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/<endpoint>]
gaps.current: IdHTTPServer.pas lines 184-192: any path other than `FSettings.Endpoint` returns 404, so both `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` are 404. Settings (Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas 83-95, 143-155) have no authorization-server or resource-URI fields.
gaps.required: AUTH-03: when auth is supported the server MUST serve a PRM document whose `authorization_servers` has at least one entry; AUTH-04: modern clients fall back to probing the path-form then the root well-known URI when no header is present; the `resource` value must equal the canonical server URI (RFC 8707 §2 form, no trailing slash) that the AS binds into the token audience.
gaps.compatImpact: Endpoint only exists when auth is enabled; unauthenticated GET, served with CORS headers. No impact on legacy clients or library consumers; new optional settings only.
gaps.suggestedChange: In HandleHTTPRequest, before the endpoint-404 check: `if Assigned(FAuthorizer) and (RequestInfo.CommandType = hcGET) and ((RequestPath = WELL_KNOWN_PRM) or (RequestPath = WELL_KNOWN_PRM + FSettings.Endpoint)) then HandleProtectedResourceMetadata(...)`. Build with TJSONObject: `resource` (Settings.ResourceUri, default `Protocol://Host[:Port]Endpoint` lower-cased scheme/host, no trailing slash), `authorization_servers` (TJSONArray from new `[Auth] AuthorizationServers=` comma list; raise at Start if empty when auth enabled; require https unless loopback), `scopes_supported` (optional, from `[Auth] ScopesSupported=`), `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]`, `resource_name` (Settings.ServerName). `Content-Type: application/json`, `Cache-Control: max-age=3600`. Add `ResourceMetadataUrl` helper used by GAP-AUTH-02 so the header and the document agree.

gaps.title: No audience-binding contract and no token-passthrough guard for consumers who forward calls upstream
gaps.current: Nothing validates `aud`/resource binding (no auth code exists). src/Http/MCPServer.Http.Executor.pas provides a generic HTTP client (Get/Post with `TArray<TNetHeader>`) that a custom tool could use to forward the inbound `Authorization` header to an upstream API; nothing prevents or documents against it. README has no security guidance section.
gaps.required: AUTH-06/AUTH-12: servers MUST validate the token was issued for them (audience), MUST reject others, MUST NOT pass the inbound token to upstream APIs; SEC-04: MUST NOT accept tokens not explicitly issued for the server.
gaps.compatImpact: Design-level: makes audience validation mandatory in the shipped OAuth authorizer base class (consumers overriding `ValidateToken` cannot skip it). No change to tool/resource APIs; documentation for consumers.
gaps.suggestedChange: In `TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer.Authorize`: after `ValidateToken` returns claims, require `aud` (string or array) to contain `ExpectedAudience` (compare after lower-casing scheme/host, no trailing-slash normalisation beyond that) and `exp` > now, else adUnauthorized with `error="invalid_token"`. Never expose the raw token on `TMCPPrincipal` (store only claims). Add a README 'Security' section: 'the inbound bearer token is bound to this server; tools calling upstream APIs must obtain their own credentials (client_credentials or a stored user grant) and must never forward `Authorization`'. Do not ship any 'passthrough' authorizer.

gaps.title: settings.ini has no [Auth] section; auth cannot be turned on without code
gaps.current: Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas: only [Server], [CORS], [SSL] keys (LoadDefaults 83-95, CreateDefaultSettingsFile 106-132, LoadFromFile 134-171, SaveToFile 173-195). settings.ini.example mirrors this.
gaps.required: Operational prerequisite for AUTH-03/04/05 and SEC-07 (require an authorization token for locally-run HTTP servers).
gaps.compatImpact: Additive properties with safe defaults (`Enabled=0`); existing ini files keep working; consumers that construct TMCPSettings programmatically are unaffected.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add to TMCPSettings: `AuthEnabled: Boolean` (default False), `AuthMode: string` ('bearer'|'oauth'), `AuthBearerTokens: string` (comma list; document that a file/env var is preferable), `AuthResourceUri`, `AuthAuthorizationServers`, `AuthScopesSupported`, `AuthRequiredScopes`, `AuthResourceMetadataUrl` (optional override). Read/write in the three ini methods under `[Auth]`. In MCPServer.dpr RunHTTPServer, build `TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer` or `TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer` from settings and assign `Server.Authorizer`. Update settings.ini.example and README Configuration.

gaps.title: Tools, resources and managers cannot see the authenticated principal or request context (needed for per-user state handles, requestState binding, per-operation scope checks)
gaps.current: IMCPTool.Execute(const Arguments: TJSONObject) (Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas:18) and TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithParams(const Params: T) (line 49) get only arguments; IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod(const Method; const Params) (Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:43) gets only params; TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest(const RequestBody, SessionID) (Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:146) has no context object. Indy handles each connection on its own thread (TIdContext), stdio is single-threaded.
gaps.required: SEC-05: state handles SHOULD be bound server-side to the authenticated user derived from the verified token; SEC-08: requestState SHOULD embed the authenticated principal; AUTH-09: per-operation scope decisions need the token's scopes at tool level.
gaps.compatImpact: Zero source change for existing custom tools/resources/managers if the context is ambient (thread-local) and the new interface is opt-in. Signatures of IMCPTool/IMCPCapabilityManager/ProcessRequest stay intact.
gaps.suggestedChange: Add `TMCPRequestContext` (Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas or new MCPServer.RequestContext.pas) with Principal: TMCPPrincipal, Era: (mcpEraLegacy, mcpEraModern), ProtocolVersion, TransportKind, Headers: TStrings (read-only copy), plus `class threadvar`/`threadvar FCurrent` and `class property Current`. Set it in TMCPIdHTTPServer.HandleHTTPRequest (try/finally around dispatch) and TMCPStdioTransport.Run (principal = environment identity or nil). Add optional `IMCPContextAwareTool = interface function ExecuteWithContext(const Arguments: TJSONObject; const Context: TMCPRequestContext): TValue; end;` and in TMCPToolsManager.ExecuteTool prefer it via `Supports(Tool, IMCPContextAwareTool, CtxTool)`. Document `TMCPRequestContext.Current.Principal.Subject` as the key for state handles.

gaps.title: No per-operation scope enforcement, no scope hierarchy, and no way for manager/tool code to produce an HTTP 401/403/400 (JSON-RPC layer swallows everything into HTTP 200)
gaps.current: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest catches all exceptions (JsonRpcProcessor.pas 204-218) and maps them to -32603/-32601/-32700 inside an HTTP 200 (IdHTTPServer.pas 509, 553); TMCPToolsManager.ExecuteTool (ToolsManager.pas 120-128) converts tool exceptions to an `isError` text result. There is no scope concept in TMCPToolBase or the schema attributes (Types.pas 14-35).
gaps.required: AUTH-08: 403 for insufficient permissions; AUTH-09: SHOULD emit `error="insufficient_scope"` with all required scopes in one challenge; AUTH-10: MUST honour scope hierarchies when deciding sufficiency.
gaps.compatImpact: Additive: new attribute and exception types; ProcessRequest keeps its string-returning signature (add an overload returning a record). Existing tools without `[RequiresScope]` behave as before. Enables the Inspector's mid-session step-up (`403 insufficient_scope`) flow.
gaps.suggestedChange: Types.pas: `RequiresScopeAttribute = class(TCustomAttribute) constructor Create(const AScopes: string)`; `EMCPHttpError = class(Exception) StatusCode: Integer; Challenge: TMCPAuthChallenge; JsonRpcCode: Integer` and `EMCPInsufficientScope = class(EMCPHttpError)`. TMCPToolsManager.CallTool: read `[RequiresScope]` on the tool class via TRttiContext and call `IMCPAuthorizer.HasScopes(Principal, Required)` where `TMCPScopeHierarchy` (dictionary broader -> narrower, configured from `[Auth] ScopeHierarchy=files:admin>files:write>files:read`) resolves implication; on failure raise EMCPInsufficientScope with the full required set. JsonRpcProcessor: let EMCPHttpError propagate (re-raise before the catch-all) or return `TMCPProcessResult` (HttpStatus, Body, Headers) from a new overload; IdHTTPServer maps it to 403 + WWW-Authenticate via GAP-AUTH-02.

gaps.title: Origin validation is coupled to CORS settings and is skipped entirely when CORS is disabled or AllowedOrigins='*'; exact-match list rejects legitimate loopback origins with ports
gaps.current: IdHTTPServer.pas VerifyAndSetCORSHeaders 210-263: line 221-222 `if not Assigned(FSettings) or not FSettings.CorsEnabled then Exit;` — with `[CORS] Enabled=0` no Origin check happens; line 227 `if (FSettings.CorsAllowedOrigins <> '*') and (Origin <> '')` — `*` accepts every Origin and line 257 emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; line 236 `SameText(Trim(CurrentOrigin), Origin)` is exact-string only, so with the code default `http://localhost,http://127.0.0.1,https://localhost,https://127.0.0.1` (Settings.pas:91) an origin such as `http://localhost:6274` or `http://[::1]:5173` is rejected with 403 (settings.ini.example adds only `:3000`). No `Vary: Origin`. 403 body is empty text (line 248).
gaps.required: SEC-01: Origin MUST be validated on all incoming connections regardless of CORS configuration; invalid Origin MUST get 403 (body MAY be an id-less JSON-RPC error). SEC-13 optional body.
gaps.compatImpact: Default config already returns 403 for foreign origins (conformant); the gap is that two documented settings (`Enabled=0`, `AllowedOrigins=*`) silently violate a MUST. Fix must keep `*` meaning 'allow any' but log a warning, and must keep the ini keys. Library consumers: behaviour change only for CorsEnabled=False deployments that receive browser traffic — document in CHANGELOG.
gaps.suggestedChange: Split into `function ValidateOrigin(RequestInfo, ResponseInfo): Boolean` (always runs; new `[Security] AllowedOrigins=` defaulting to the CORS list for compatibility; match scheme+host with optional `:*` port wildcard; built-in loopback set `http(s)://localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` any port; absent Origin -> allow; `null` -> deny; mismatch -> 403 with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Origin not allowed"}}` and `Content-Type: application/json`) and `procedure ApplyCorsHeaders` (reflect the validated Origin instead of `*` when an Authorization header is present, add `Vary: Origin`). Keep TLogger.Info on block. Acceptance: conformance scenario `dns-rebinding-protection` under both `--requirements 2025-11-25` and `--requirements 2026-07-28`.

gaps.title: CORS allow/expose lists only cover legacy headers; browser-based modern clients cannot preflight Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name/Mcp-Param-*/Authorization or read WWW-Authenticate
gaps.current: IdHTTPServer.pas 258-261: `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, GET, OPTIONS`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Accept, Content-Type, Last-Event-ID, Mcp-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id`, `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Mcp-Session-Id`. HandleOptionsRequest (265-269) ignores `Access-Control-Request-Headers`.
gaps.required: Modern requests MUST carry `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name` and optionally dynamic `Mcp-Param-*` headers (SEC-09); authenticated requests carry `Authorization`; 401 challenges are read from `WWW-Authenticate` (AUTH-04), which is not a CORS-safelisted response header.
gaps.compatImpact: Purely additive header lists; legacy names retained. No library API change. (The MCP Inspector web UI proxies through its Node backend, so it is not affected; pure-browser clients are.)
gaps.suggestedChange: In HandleOptionsRequest reflect `RequestInfo.RawHeaders.Values['Access-Control-Request-Headers']` into `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` (covers dynamic `Mcp-Param-*`), otherwise use a static list `Accept, Content-Type, Authorization, Last-Event-ID, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name`. Set `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Mcp-Session-Id, WWW-Authenticate`. Keep `DELETE` out unless legacy session termination is implemented (transport area). Add `Vary: Origin, Access-Control-Request-Headers`.

gaps.title: HTTP server binds to all interfaces; Settings.Host is only used for logging
gaps.current: IdHTTPServer.pas Start (136-160) sets `FHTTPServer.DefaultPort := FPort` (155) and `Active := True` without adding a `Bindings` entry, so Indy creates a default binding on 0.0.0.0 (and :: when IPv6 is default). `FSettings.Host` ('localhost' by default, Settings.pas:86) is used only in the log line (159) and in the GET info JSON (309-310). README line 104 says the server 'will listen on http://localhost:3000/mcp', which is misleading.
gaps.required: SEC-02: when running locally servers SHOULD bind only to 127.0.0.1; SEC-07: restrict access for locally-run HTTP servers.
gaps.compatImpact: Behaviour change: deployments that reach the server remotely while `Host=localhost` would stop working. Mitigate with explicit `[Server] BindAddress=` (default = Host; `0.0.0.0`/`*` = all interfaces with a logged warning) and a CHANGELOG note. Library consumers using TMCPIdHTTPServer programmatically get a new `BindAddress` property (default '127.0.0.1').
gaps.suggestedChange: Add `property BindAddress: string` to TMCPIdHTTPServer and `[Server] BindAddress` to TMCPSettings. In Start: `FHTTPServer.Bindings.Clear; with FHTTPServer.Bindings.Add do begin IP := ResolvedIP; Port := FPort; IPVersion := Id_IPv4; end;` mapping 'localhost' -> '127.0.0.1' and adding a second binding `::1` (Id_IPv6) when available; `0.0.0.0`/`*` -> `IP := ''` (all) plus TLogger.Warning('binding to all interfaces; enable [Auth]'). Update README Transport Modes and settings.ini.example.

gaps.title: Full request/response bodies and session ids are logged at Info level and re-exposed through the logs://recent resource; once Authorization, requestState and elicitation inputResponses exist they will leak
gaps.current: IdHTTPServer.pas 331 `TLogger.Info('Request: ' + RequestBody)`, 335 `'Session ID from header: ' + SessionID`, 555 `'Response: ' + ResponseBody`; StdioTransport.pas 62 `'Received: ' + InputLine`, 70 `'Sent: ' + Response`; MCPServer.dpr 167 sets MinLogLevel := Info; Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Logs.pas serves recent log entries to any client (README 451 `logs://recent`). Headers are not logged today, but bodies will contain `_meta` (client identity), `requestState`, `inputResponses` (user answers / PII) and, for consumers who put tokens in tool args, secrets.
gaps.required: AUTH-13: servers MUST implement secure token handling; tokens 'cached or logged on the server' are an explicit threat. SEC-08 requestState is attacker-facing state that should not be disclosed. SEC-12: nothing but MCP messages on stdout (already true; keep it so).
gaps.compatImpact: Logging verbosity change only; `TLogger` API unchanged (add a `Redact` hook). Consumers who registered `logs://recent` keep it, but the default registration should require an authenticated principal or be removed from the default tool set.
gaps.suggestedChange: Log bodies only at TLogLevel.Debug through a new `TLogger.RedactJson(const Body: string)` that blanks `params._meta`, `params.requestState`, `params.inputResponses`, any key matching (?i)token|secret|password|authorization; never log header values (add `TLogger.Warning` guard in code review checklist). Keep TLogger.UseStdErr for stdio. Make TServerStatusResource/TLogsResource registration opt-in (`[Server] ExposeLogsResource=0`) or check `TMCPRequestContext.Current.Principal` before returning entries.

gaps.title: Legacy session id is generated with CreateGUID (RNG quality unverified on Linux), placed inside the initialize result body as non-standard `sessionId`, and any client-supplied Mcp-Session-Id is echoed back unvalidated
gaps.current: Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas 97 `FSessionID := TGuid.NewGuid.ToString` and 126 `ResultJSON.AddPair('sessionId', FSessionID)` (not a spec field); IdHTTPServer.pas 533-543 scrapes `result.sessionId` from the body to set the `Mcp-Session-Id` header; 348-349, 485-486, 548-549 echo whatever `Mcp-Session-Id` the client sent without charset validation; no server-side session table exists (FSessionID overwritten per initialize, never checked).
gaps.required: SEC-06 (legacy era): session IDs MUST be secure/non-deterministic (SHOULD use a CSPRNG), MUST only contain 0x21-0x7E, MUST NOT be used for authentication (already true), SHOULD be bound to user info if state is stored.
gaps.compatImpact: Legacy clients ignore the extra `sessionId` body field today; removing it is safe (Mcp-Session-Id header is the contract). Consumers reading TMCPCoreManager.SessionID keep working. Overlaps with the lifecycle/transport work that decides whether to keep sessions at all.
gaps.suggestedChange: Generate the id with an explicit CSPRNG helper (`MCPServer.Crypto.pas`: BCryptGenRandom on Windows, /dev/urandom on POSIX, or OpenSSL RAND_bytes when TaurusTLS is loaded) encoded base64url (visible ASCII, no braces); stop emitting `sessionId` in the JSON result and have the transport set the header directly from the core manager; validate inbound `Mcp-Session-Id` against `[\x21-\x7E]+` and respond 400 otherwise; never key any authorization decision on it. If per-session state is ever stored, key it as `<principal.subject>:<sessionId>`.

gaps.title: No integrity-protected requestState codec for the MRTR pattern (required once InputRequiredResult is implemented)
gaps.current: MRTR/InputRequiredResult does not exist yet (another area), but no HMAC/AEAD helper, key management or replay checks exist anywhere in src; System.Hash (THashSHA2.GetHMAC) is available in the RTL and unused.
gaps.required: SEC-08: requestState MUST be treated as attacker-controlled; MUST be integrity-protected when it influences authorization/resource access/business logic; MUST be rejected on verification failure; SHOULD embed principal, TTL and originating-request identifier; single-use MUST be enforced server-side where required. Scored by required 2026-07-28 server scenario `input-required-result-tampered-state` (and `input-required-result-request-state`).
gaps.compatImpact: Modern era only; new unit, no change to existing APIs. Consumers implementing multi-round tools get `TMCPRequestState.Pack/Unpack` instead of rolling their own.
gaps.suggestedChange: New unit src/Core/MCPServer.RequestState.pas: `TMCPRequestStateCodec` with `Key: TBytes` (from `[Security] StateKey=` base64 or generated per process; document that generated keys do not survive restarts/load-balancing), `function Pack(const APayload: TJSONObject; const AContext: TMCPRequestContext; ATtlSeconds: Integer): string` producing base64url(`json`) + '.' + base64url(HMAC-SHA256) where json includes `sub` (principal subject or ''), `exp` (Unix time), `m` (method), `h` (SHA-256 of canonical tool name + arguments), `d` (opaque data); `function Unpack(const AState: string; const AContext: TMCPRequestContext; out APayload: TJSONObject): Boolean` with constant-time MAC compare, expiry, principal and request-digest checks; on failure the tools manager returns JSON-RPC error -32602 (Invalid params), never -32000..-32019 (SEC-11). Provide `IMCPRequestStateStore` hook for single-use enforcement.

gaps.title: Mirrored HTTP headers (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param-*) are neither validated against the body nor rejected on invalid characters; no x-mcp-header support/validation in the schema generator (overlaps transport area, listed for the injection aspect)
gaps.current: IdHTTPServer.pas reads no `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name`/`MCP-Protocol-Version`/`Mcp-Param-*` header (only lines 224, 277, 289, 333, 337 read headers); JsonRpcProcessor dispatches purely on the body `method` (168-171). Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas has no `x-mcp-header` emission and no constraint validation; ToolsManager.CreateToolJSON (185-211) serialises whatever schema the tool returns.
gaps.required: SEC-09: servers that process the body MUST reject header/body mismatches and invalid `Mcp-Param-*` characters with 400 + `-32020`, MUST decode `=?base64?...?=` sentinels first, MUST NOT expect a header for null/absent values, MUST compare header names case-insensitively; SEC-10: invalid `x-mcp-header` annotations make the tool definition invalid (clients drop the tool), so the server must validate at registration.
gaps.compatImpact: Modern-era only: validation is applied solely when the request carries modern `_meta`/`MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28`; legacy requests (no header or 2025-xx versions) are not subject to header validation, so legacy clients are unaffected. Library consumers: new optional `[HeaderParam('Region')]` attribute; tools without it unchanged; registration now raises a clear exception for invalid annotations (previously silently accepted).
gaps.suggestedChange: New src/Server/MCPServer.HeaderValidation.pas: `TMCPMirroredHeaders.Validate(RequestInfo.RawHeaders, JSONRequest, ToolSchemaLookup): TMCPHeaderValidationResult` — case-insensitive header lookup (Indy `RawHeaders.Values` is already case-insensitive), decode sentinel (reject bad base64 with 400/-32020), compare `Mcp-Method` = body.method (case-sensitive), `Mcp-Name` = params.name|params.uri, each declared `Mcp-Param-<name>` = arguments at the property path (numeric compare for integers, `true`/`false` for booleans), reject `Mcp-Param-*` values with chars outside 0x20-0x7E/0x09; return HTTP 400 + `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<id>,"error":{"code":-32020,"message":"Header mismatch: ..."}}`. Schema generator: `HeaderParamAttribute` -> `"x-mcp-header": "<name>"`; validate token syntax (RFC 9110 tchar), no CR/LF, case-insensitive uniqueness, primitive type (string/integer/boolean; reject Double), top-level `properties` chain only; raise EMCPSchema at TMCPRegistry.RegisterTool time. README warning: never annotate secrets/PII (SEC-10).

gaps.title: Non-TaurusTLS TLS path enables TLS 1.0/1.1; TLS implementation choice is a hard-coded $DEFINE inside the library unit
gaps.current: IdHTTPServer.pas 395-396: `SSLOptions.Method := sslvTLSv1_2; SSLOptions.SSLVersions := [sslvTLSv1, sslvTLSv1_1, sslvTLSv1_2]` (legacy Indy/OpenSSL 1.0.2 path). Line 7 `{$DEFINE USE_TAURUS_TLS}` must be edited in the library source to switch (README 482-492 instructs consumers to edit `src\Server\MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas`). TaurusTLS path (380-384) sets no minimum protocol version explicitly.
gaps.required: AUTH-14 / OAuth 2.1 §1.5 communication security (TLS per current BCP: TLS 1.2+ only); README itself recommends TaurusTLS for modern ciphers.
gaps.compatImpact: Dropping TLS 1.0/1.1 could break only obsolete clients; all MCP clients are modern. Moving the define to an include file (`MCPServer.inc`) keeps the default (TaurusTLS on) and lets consumers override from their project without editing library sources.
gaps.suggestedChange: `SSLVersions := [sslvTLSv1_2]` (+ `sslvTLSv1_3` where the installed Indy supports it) in the OpenSSL-1.0.2 branch; for TaurusTLS set the minimum TLS version option to 1.2. Add `src/MCPServer.inc` containing the `USE_TAURUS_TLS` define and `{$I MCPServer.inc}` in the unit; document `-DMCP_NO_TAURUS` override. Keep `generate-ssl-cert.bat` but note self-signed certs are development-only (already in README).

gaps.title: No channel from protocol/manager code to an HTTP status + headers; every failure is HTTP 200 with -32603, which also mislabels errors under the new error-code policy
gaps.current: JsonRpcProcessor.pas 204-218 maps any exception to -32603 unless the message contains 'not found' (-32601) or parsing failed (-32700); IdHTTPServer always answers 200 for JSON (553) and SSE (509). HTTP status constants (82-89) lack 400/401.
gaps.required: AUTH-08 needs 401/403/400 at HTTP level; SEC-09 needs 400 + -32020; SEC-01 needs 403; SEC-11 forbids inventing codes in -32000..-32019 and requires defined codes with their meanings.
gaps.compatImpact: Keep `ProcessRequest(const RequestBody, SessionID): string` for library consumers who call the processor directly (TMCPStdioTransport does); add a new overload. Custom managers can raise the new exception types but are not required to.
gaps.suggestedChange: Types.pas: `EMCPJsonRpcError = class(Exception) Code: Integer; Data: TJSONValue` and `EMCPHttpError = class(EMCPJsonRpcError) StatusCode: Integer; Headers: TStrings`. JsonRpcProcessor: new `function ProcessRequestEx(const RequestBody: string; const Context: TMCPRequestContext): TMCPProcessResult` (record: HttpStatus, ContentType, Headers, Body); map EMCPJsonRpcError to its code, EMCPHttpError to its status; keep the string overload delegating to it. IdHTTPServer copies HttpStatus/Headers to ResponseInfo. Stdio ignores HttpStatus. Use only spec-defined codes (-32020/-32021/-32022, -32600..-32603, -32700).

gaps.current: Repository root contains only LICENSE, README.md, build.bat, generate-ssl-cert.bat, settings.ini.example, src/ (no tests/ or .github/; `find . -iname '*test*'` returns nothing). build.bat line 17 pins `DELPHI_PATH=C:\Program Files (x86)\Embarcadero\Studio\37.0`; Linux64 is built from Windows via MSBuild/PAServer (78-94). README 560-563 says 'Test with npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector or Claude Code'.
gaps.required: Not a spec MUST, but SEP-2484/SEP-1730 make the conformance suite the yardstick ('Tier 1 requires 100% pass rate'; requirement sets are frozen per revision), and the security MUSTs above (Origin 403, tampered requestState, header mismatch) are directly exercised by scored scenarios `dns-rebinding-protection`, `input-required-result-tampered-state`, `input-required-result-request-state`.

CI on GitHub-hosted runners needs a licensed Delphi compiler (not available), so plan for a self-hosted Windows runner or a documented manual release checklist.
gaps.suggestedChange: (1) tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX) covering OriginValidator, WWW-Authenticate builder, PRM document, static bearer authorizer (constant-time), header validator (SEP-2243 edge tables), RequestState codec (tamper/expiry/principal), schema x-mcp-header constraints. (2) scripts/run-conformance.ps1: start `Win64\Release\MCPServer.exe`, wait for `http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp`, then `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url http://localhost:3000/mcp --requirements 2026-07-28 --expected-failures ./conformance-baseline.yml` and again with `--requirements 2025-11-25` (both wires against the same endpoint — the README states a non-listed implementation's single endpoint 'must serve every claimed revision at its own wire'); optionally `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance tier-check --repo GDKsoftware/delphi-mcp-server --conformance-server-url http://localhost:3000/mcp --requirements 2025-11-25,2026-07-28`. (4) Pin tool versions in package.json devDependencies (`@modelcontextprotocol/conformance`, `@modelcontextprotocol/inspector`, Node >= 22.19.0). (5) build.bat: read DELPHI_PATH from env/rsvars, add `build.sh` stub calling MSBuild via PAServer docs.

gaps.title: README security/auth/Inspector documentation is stale or misleading
gaps.current: README.md line 6 badge `MCP-2025--06--18`, line 30 'Implements MCP specification 2025-06-18'; lines 350-353 imply an Authorization header can be 'configured'; line 104 claims listening on localhost (actually all interfaces, GAP-SEC-03); 'Security: Built-in security features including CORS configuration' (line 35) is the only security statement; Inspector section (408-436) predates the web/CLI/TUI split and the per-server `protocolEra` setting (default `legacy`), and does not mention Node 22.19+.
gaps.required: Documentation prerequisite for AUTH-01 (how to enable auth), SEC-02/SEC-07 (loopback binding, tokens for local HTTP), and for testing modern era with the Inspector.
gaps.compatImpact: None.
gaps.suggestedChange: Update badge/feature list to 2026-07-28 dual-era; add 'Security' section (Origin validation, BindAddress, [Auth] modes, no token passthrough, requestState integrity, x-mcp-header PII warning); rewrite 'Testing with MCP Inspector' to show `protocolEra: modern|legacy|auto`, `--cli --method tools/list`, exit code 3 for auth, and add a 'Conformance testing' section with the exact `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url ... --requirements <rev>` commands; state explicitly that 2025-03-26 clients are served unauthenticated only (AUTH-17).

gaps.title: Optional hardening: no Host-header allow-list (defence in depth against DNS rebinding when Origin is absent)
gaps.current: Only Origin is inspected (IdHTTPServer.pas 224); `RequestInfo.Host` is never compared with the configured host.
gaps.required: Not required by the spec (Origin validation is the MUST); the security tutorial lists 'attacker accesses an insecure local server that's left running on localhost via DNS rebinding' as the threat.
gaps.compatImpact: Opt-in setting; default off to avoid breaking reverse-proxy deployments.
gaps.suggestedChange: `[Security] AllowedHosts=localhost,127.0.0.1,[::1]` (empty = disabled); when set, reject requests whose `Host` (minus port) is not listed with 421 Misdirected Request or 403.

alreadyConformant: AUTH-02 (stdio SHOULD NOT do OAuth): Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas (whole unit, 43-99) performs no credential handling; MCPServer.dpr RunStdioServer (114-141) passes no settings-derived credentials. Keep it that way: do not wire the new IMCPAuthorizer into TMCPStdioTransport.

SEC-12 (stdout hygiene in stdio mode): MCPServer.dpr 161-163 sets TLogger.UseStdErr := True before any logging when --stdio is present; StdioTransport.pas 68-69 and 89-93 write only JSON-RPC messages to Output.

SEC-01 in the default configuration: Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas 227-251 rejects a present Origin that is not in the allow-list with HTTP 403 'Forbidden - Origin not allowed' and Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas 90-91 defaults CORS to enabled with a loopback-only list — i.e. the shipped defaults satisfy the Origin MUST (the gap is only for Enabled=0 / AllowedOrigins=*).

SEC-06 'MUST NOT use sessions for authentication' (legacy): no server-side session table exists; Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas 97/126 only mints an id and Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas 333-349 merely echoes the header — no authorization decision is ever keyed on Mcp-Session-Id.
AUTH-07 (no tokens from query string): nothing in src reads `RequestInfo.Params`/`QueryParams` for credentials; the future authorizer reads only the Authorization header.

SEC-04 / AUTH-12 (no token passthrough today): the core server makes no upstream HTTP calls; src/Http/MCPServer.Http.Executor.pas is a standalone helper not referenced by MCPServer.dpr (uses list 14-35) and takes explicit headers, so no inbound token is forwarded anywhere.

AUTH-14 transport security available: Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas ConfigureSSL (364-408) supports HTTPS with TaurusTLS/OpenSSL 3.x-4.x by default (line 7, 380-384) and validates certificate/key file presence (367-377); README 383-406 and 458-539 document CA-issued certs for production.
Unknown paths are 404 (IdHTTPServer.pas 187-192) and unknown methods 405 (202-203), limiting the attack surface to the single MCP endpoint (plus the well-known path to be added).
SEC-13 flexibility: the CORS 403 path already sets `ResponseNo`/`ResponseText` (247-248), so adding the optional id-less JSON-RPC error body is a one-line change.
Locality defaults: Settings.pas 85-86 default `Port=3000`, `Host=localhost` and settings.ini.example advertise loopback; only the binding (GAP-SEC-03) does not honour it.

Exception hygiene for tools: Managers/MCPServer.ToolsManager.pas 120-128 converts tool exceptions into `isError` results instead of leaking stack details as protocol errors (JsonRpcProcessor.pas 204-218 still returns E.Message in error.message — acceptable, but redact once auth errors exist).
notes: Ecosystem (server SDKs), from blog/content/posts/2026-07-28-spec-ga/index.md # SDKs: 'All four Tier 1 SDKs speak 2026-07-28 as of today: TypeScript, Python, Go, C#'; 'the Rust SDK supports the new spec in beta'. blog/content/posts/2026-07-27-ruby-sdk-1-0.md: Ruby SDK 1.0 implements 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 with 100% conformance (Tier 2); 2026-07-28 work under way.

Ecosystem (dual-era behaviour of official SDKs), from blog/content/posts/2026-06-29-sdk-betas-for-2026-07-28.md: 'clients that speak 2026-07-28 fall back to the initialize handshake when they reach a server on 2025-11-25 or earlier'; Python v2 'answers the legacy initialize handshake alongside server/discover' from one endpoint; TypeScript `createMcpHandler` 'serves 2026-07-28 per request and handles 2025-11-25 traffic from the same endpoint'; Go serves 2026-07-28 only when `StreamableHTTPOptions.Stateless = true` (otherwise negotiates down to 2025-11-25); C# preview defaults its HTTP transport to stateless (conformance known-sdks note: C# serves it at `/stateless`). 'for existing clients and servers nothing breaks today, and nothing breaks on July 28 either'. The Delphi plan's 'one endpoint, both eras' design matches Python/TypeScript behaviour and is what the conformance README expects for non-listed implementations ('the one endpoint you give must serve every claimed revision at its own wire').

Ecosystem (end-user clients): the spec repo contains NO statement of which end-user clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex, ChatGPT) ship 2026-07-28 support; docs/extensions/client-matrix.mdx only tracks extensions (MCP Apps, OAuth Client Credentials, EMA). Assume legacy-era clients dominate for the 12-month deprecation window; the README's stated targets (Claude Code over HTTP, Codex over stdio) must keep working via the legacy path. Verify current client behaviour empirically with the Inspector in `legacy`, `auto` and `modern` eras.

Dual-era normative guidance (docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning.mdx # Backward Compatibility with Initialization-Based Versions): a server 'MAY implement both behaviors'; 'A dual-era server selects its behavior from how the client opens: A request carrying modern per-request _meta is served statelessly ... An initialize request selects legacy semantics, scoped to ... the session (HTTP)'; 'A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently on the same endpoint'. Modern-only servers 'SHOULD name the protocol versions it supports in any error it returns to an initialize request'. HTTP: a request without MCP-Protocol-Version 'MAY' be treated as 2025-03-26 if the server supports pre-2025-06-18 clients. Legacy transport behaviours (GET stream, Mcp-Session-Id, DELETE, Last-Event-ID) 'are not part of this revision' but dual-era servers 'implement the behavior described in the corresponding revision'.

Authorization in the legacy eras: 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 already use the RFC 9728 resource-server model (same MUSTs as 2026-07-28; 2025-06-18 makes the WWW-Authenticate header mandatory on 401), so a single auth implementation serves 2025-06-18+ clients. 2025-03-26 used the MCP-server-as-authorization-server model (AUTH-17); recommend documenting it as unsupported for authenticated deployments.

Authorization changes in 2026-07-28 (changelog.mdx Minor 7-9, Deprecated 4) are all client/AS-side: RFC 9207 `iss` validation (client), `application_type` in DCR (client), issuer-bound credentials (client), DCR deprecated in favour of CIMD (AS/client). Server-side additions: scope hierarchy MUST (AUTH-10), single-challenge scope SHOULD (AUTH-09), offline_access SHOULD NOT (AUTH-11). Nothing in the server role requires CIMD support.

Official conformance tooling: repository https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance (owned by the Conformance Testing project; docs/community/sdk-tiers.mdx # Conformance Testing). Commands (from its README, fetched 2026-09-03): `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url http://localhost:3000/mcp` (all active scenarios), `--scenario <name>`, `--suite active|all|pending|draft`, `--requirements 2026-07-28` (frozen per-revision set; also `2025-11-25`), `--expected-failures ./conformance-baseline.yml` (YAML with `server:` list; supports `scenario:check-id` granularity; exit 1 on regression or stale baseline), `--verbose`; `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance list [--server] [--requirements 2026-07-28]`; `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance tier-check --repo <owner/repo> --conformance-server-url <url> --requirements 2025-11-25,2026-07-28`; scaffolding `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance new-scenario --sep <n>` (seps/2484). GitHub Action: `uses: modelcontextprotocol/conformance@v0.1.11` with `mode: server`, `url:`, `expected-failures:`. Anchor release at 2026-07-28 ship: `@modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.10`. Results land in `results/server-<scenario>-<timestamp>/checks.json`; every scenario also runs `wire-schema-valid` against the JSON schema of the negotiated version.

Frozen required SERVER scenarios for 2026-07-28 (conformance requirements/2026-07-28.yaml): server-stateless, completion-complete, tools-list, tools-call-simple-text, tools-call-image, tools-call-audio, tools-call-embedded-resource, tools-call-mixed-content, tools-call-error, tools-call-with-progress, server-sse-multiple-streams, resources-list, resources-read-text, resources-read-binary, resources-templates-read, sep-2164-resource-not-found, prompts-list, prompts-get-simple, prompts-get-with-args, prompts-get-embedded-resource, prompts-get-with-image, dns-rebinding-protection, caching, input-required-result-{basic-elicitation, basic-sampling, basic-list-roots, request-state, multiple-input-requests, multi-round, missing-input-response, non-tool-request, result-type, unsupported-methods, tampered-state, capability-check, ignore-extra-params, validate-input}. Not scored: tasks-* (extension). For 2025-11-25 (requirements/2025-11-25.yaml): server-initialize, logging-set-level, ping, completion-complete, tools-list, tools-call-* (simple-text, image, audio, embedded-resource, mixed-content, with-logging, error, with-progress, sampling, elicitation), elicitation-sep1034-defaults, elicitation-sep1330-enums, server-sse-multiple-streams, resources-* (list, read-text, read-binary, templates-read, subscribe, unsubscribe), prompts-* (list, get-simple, get-with-args, get-embedded-resource, get-with-image), dns-rebinding-protection. Note this repo has no prompts or completion support today, so 100% on either set implies implementing those (other areas).

Conformance coverage of the SERVER auth role: the requirements file says it covers 'an MCP server acting as an OAuth resource server', but neither revision's `server:` list contains any auth/* scenario — all `auth/*` scenarios are client-leg (metadata discovery, CIMD, scope handling, iss validation, etc.). Therefore server-side OAuth behaviour (401 challenge, PRM document, audience validation) is NOT machine-scored today; acceptance for GAP-AUTH-01..07 must rely on DUnitX tests plus a manual/Inspector OAuth run against a test authorization server (e.g. the Inspector CLI: exit code 3 = 'Server requires authentication (401/403, WWW-Authenticate, OAuth)').

MCP Inspector status (docs/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector.mdx, inspector/protocol-eras.mdx, inspector/cli.mdx, inspector/authorization.mdx, inspector/configuration.mdx): single package `@modelcontextprotocol/inspector` with web (`npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector`), CLI (`--cli`) and TUI (`--tui`); requires Node 22.19.0+; per-server `protocolEra` = `legacy` (default; plain initialize), `auto` (probe server/discover then fall back), `modern` (pin 2026-07-28, no fallback). Modern-era features it exercises: server/discover, per-request `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel`, `subscriptions/listen`, MRTR (`input_required`, `requestState` round-trips, `MRTR_MAX_ROUNDS`), x-mcp-header mirroring (CLI/TUI only — the browser SDK skips `Mcp-Param-*`, so a strict server returns -32020 from the web client), the modern error taxonomy (-32020/-32021/-32022, 404/-32601). Full OAuth flow in all three clients (DCR, static client `--client-id/--client-secret`, CIMD `--client-metadata-url`, EMA); handles mid-session 401 re-auth and 403 `insufficient_scope` step-up (scope union); CI flags `--stored-auth-only`, `--use-stored-auth`, `--wait-for-auth`; callback `http://127.0.0.1:6276/oauth/callback` for CLI/TUI. Config file format: `{"mcpServers":{"name":{"type":"http","url":"...","protocolEra":"modern","headers":{...}}}}`. The web backend proxies connections from Node, so the Delphi server sees no browser Origin from the Inspector.

Delphi implementation facts for the auth work: Indy exposes headers via `TIdHTTPRequestInfo.RawHeaders.Values[...]` (case-insensitive) and the response challenge via `TIdHTTPResponseInfo.WWWAuthenticate` (TStrings) or `CustomHeaders`; Indy parses only Basic credentials into AuthUsername/AuthPassword, so Bearer must be read raw. Each connection runs on its own Indy thread, so a `threadvar` request context is viable; TMCPJsonRpcProcessor is created per server (IdHTTPServer.pas 144) and shared across threads — keep it stateless. RTL provides HMAC-SHA256 (System.Hash.THashSHA2.GetHMAC) and an HTTP client (System.Net.HttpClient) for RFC 7662 introspection; there is no JOSE/JWT in the RTL (JWT signature verification needs a third-party unit or OpenSSL via TaurusTLS) — recommend keeping JWT verification out of the core and shipping it as a sample authorizer. There is no RTL constant-time compare; write one. Verify the RNG behind `CreateGUID`/`TGuid.NewGuid` on Linux before relying on it for session ids; prefer an explicit CSPRNG helper.

Scope of 'realistically in core' vs 'out of scope' for a Delphi library: IN — pluggable IMCPAuthorizer, static bearer authorizer, WWW-Authenticate challenge builder, RFC 9728 PRM endpoint, audience/expiry checks in an abstract OAuth resource-server base, per-tool `[RequiresScope]` + hierarchy, Origin/Host/bind hardening, requestState HMAC codec, header/body validation, log redaction. OUT — acting as an authorization server (spec: 'implementation details of the authorization server are beyond the scope'), DCR/CIMD (AS/client side), consent pages for confused-deputy proxies (document only), auth extensions (client-credentials/EMA are client+AS features; the server just advertises `extensions` if it adopts them), DPoP.

Both `dns-rebinding-protection` and the requestState scenarios are scored, so GAP-SEC-01 and GAP-SEC-06 are the two security items with hard conformance acceptance criteria; GAP-SEC-07 (header validation) is tested from the client leg (`http-standard-headers`, `http-custom-headers`, `http-invalid-tool-headers`) and SEP-2243 # Conformance Test Cases lists the server-side edge tables (case-insensitive names, mismatch -> 400, whitespace trimming, base64 sentinel decoding, invalid padding -> 400) to turn into DUnitX cases. Note SEP-2243's tables still cite `-32001`; the published spec renumbered HeaderMismatch to `-32020` (changelog Minor 12) — implement -32020.

Open questions for the orchestrator: (1) whether to keep `[CORS] AllowedOrigins=*` semantics or deprecate it; (2) whether the default binary should bind 127.0.0.1 only (spec SHOULD) given Linux/container users who expect 0.0.0.0 — proposal: default loopback + explicit `BindAddress=0.0.0.0` opt-in; (3) whether `logs://recent` and `server://status` example resources stay registered by default; (4) StateKey persistence strategy for load-balanced deployments (config-provided key vs per-process); (5) CI strategy given no Delphi on GitHub-hosted runners (self-hosted Windows runner running build.bat + tests + conformance vs. manual release checklist).

Repository facts relevant to planning: last spec-repo commit 2026-09-02 (1dc2c72); Delphi repo has no tests, no .github, Windows-only build.bat pinned to Studio 37.0 with TaurusTLS auto-discovery; src/Http/* client helpers exist but are not part of the dpr; README badge still says 2025-06-18.

plans.lens: COMPATIBILITY-FIRST INCREMENTAL: smallest safe steps that ship value early; dual-era from the very first release; every phase independently releasable; the legacy wire (initialize handshake, 2025-03-26/2025-06-18/2025-11-25) stays byte-identical and is proven so by golden tests captured from the current binary; library consumers (TMCPToolBase<T>, TMCPToolBase<T,R>, TMCPResourceBase<T>, IMCPCapabilityManager, IMCPManagerRegistry, TMCPRegistry, TMCPIdHTTPServer, TMCPStdioTransport, TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest) keep compiling and behaving because every extension is a new GUID'd interface discovered with Supports(), a new overload, a new unit, a new protected field with a safe default, or a new ini key with a compatible default.
plans.summary: Eight releasable phases (0-7, ~42 senior-Delphi days) turn the single-version 2025-06-18 server into a dual-era server. Phase 0 builds the safety net (DUnitX harness around the transport-independent TMCPJsonRpcProcessor, golden files captured from the CURRENT binary for every legacy method, constants consolidation, atomic counters). Phase 1 delivers the protocol core in one place (Protocol/): typed EMCPError with code/data/HttpStatus, TMCPRequestContext + per-request era detection from params._meta (initialize always wins as legacy), server/discover, legacy initialize version negotiation, modern-only result envelope injection (resultType, _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo, cacheable-result safety net), -32022/-32602/-32021 plumbing, id/jsonrpc validation, legacy-method gate in the modern era, and ProcessRequestEx returning body + HTTP status + era while the old ProcessRequest(string,string) keeps working -> after Phase 1 a 2026-07-28 client already works on stdio and on the HTTP happy path, and every legacy client is served exactly as before. Phase 2 makes the HTTP transport dual-era and secure: Origin validated on every connection (403 even with CORS disabled), MCP-Protocol-Version/Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name validation with Base64 sentinel decoding (-32020/400), era-gated status mapping (400/404 modern only, 200 legacy), 202 with no body, GET/DELETE -> 405 + Allow, no session minting, loopback binding, CORS header lists, TLS >= 1.2. Phase 3 fixes tools/resources modern correctness (ttlMs/cacheScope, -32602 unknown tool / resource not found by era (-32002 legacy), nil arguments crash, integer schema type, content array next to structuredContent, TMCPToolResult content builders, deterministic ordering, cursor -32602, capabilities derived from registered managers, annotations/icons). Phase 4 hardens stdio (UTF-8 byte I/O, LF-only, EOF/SIGTERM shutdown, reader/writer split with locked stdout, notifications/cancelled + progress, MaxConcurrentRequests default 1). Phase 5 adds prompts, completion, resource templates and pagination (needed for 100% conformance). Phase 6 adds incremental SSE streaming in Indy, MRTR/elicitation for tool/resource/prompt authors with an HMAC requestState codec, and a minimal subscriptions/listen. Phase 7 adds opt-in authorization hooks (static bearer, abstract OAuth resource-server base with audience binding, RFC 9728 metadata, WWW-Authenticate), log redaction, conformance baseline and documentation. Every phase lists the gap ids it closes; no phase requires a later one to be shippable.
plans.compatStrategy: ERA MODEL. The era is a property of each request, decided in exactly one function, TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.BuildRequestContext (Phase 1), for both transports: (1) method = 'initialize' -> legacy, always, even if _meta is present (versioning.mdx 'An initialize request selects legacy semantics'); (2) params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] is a JSON string -> modern (versioning.mdx 'A request carrying modern per-request _meta is served statelessly'); (3) otherwise legacy. HTTP adds a header layer via TMCPTransportHints (HasHeaderLayer, HeaderProtocolVersion, HeaderMethod, HeaderName): a modern body with a missing or non-matching MCP-Protocol-Version header -> -32020/400; a header naming a modern version with a body lacking _meta -> -32602/400 (basic/index.mdx 'A request missing any required field is malformed ... -32602 ... 400'); a header naming a version in neither set -> 400 with -32600 body (2025-11-25 transports.mdx 'invalid or unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version ... MUST respond with 400'); an absent header with no _meta -> legacy (streamable-http.mdx 'MAY treat a request that omits the header as protocol version 2025-03-26'). stdio has no header layer (stdio.mdx 'There is no header layer'); steps 1-3 apply verbatim. LEGACY ERA IS FROZEN: the legacy path keeps today's dispatch, today's result JSON (no resultType/_meta/ttlMs/cacheScope injection), today's HTTP 200 for JSON-RPC errors (404 is never used for a legacy request because 2025-11-25 transports.mdx defines 404 as 'session terminated'), today's 'not found' -> -32601 heuristic for non-EMCPError exceptions (kept for legacy-era requests only), today's Mcp-Session-Id echo of an incoming header (harmless, MAY), and answers 2025-06-18 to 2025-03-26 clients as today (allowed by lifecycle.mdx 'Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports'); the only legacy-visible changes are spec-driven error-path fixes (resource not found -> -32002 error, unknown tool -> -32602, -32600 for arrays/null ids) and 405 on GET (allowed by 2025-11-25 transports.mdx item 3). Golden tests captured from the v1.0 binary in Phase 0 guard this byte-for-byte. MODERN ERA is layered on top: envelope injection, status mapping, header validation and the legacy-method gate (ping/initialize/notifications/initialized/logging/setLevel/resources/subscribe|unsubscribe -> -32601, HTTP 404) run only when Ctx.Era = peModern. server/discover is answered identically in both eras and at any time (it never consults process state), so the stdio probe (stdio.mdx 'Backward Compatibility') and HTTP first-request detection work; a stdio process may serve an initialize after modern messages and vice versa (versioning.mdx 'MAY serve both eras concurrently'). PER-TRANSPORT COEXISTENCE: HTTP is stateless in both eras (no session minting; incoming Mcp-Session-Id ignored for modern, echoed for legacy); stdio keeps one side-slot, TMCPTransportSession.NegotiatedLegacyVersion, written only by initialize and read only by legacy-era requests. LIBRARY CONSUMERS: IMCPCapabilityManager, IMCPManagerRegistry, IMCPTool, IMCPResource keep their GUIDs and members; new behaviour is reached through IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPContextAwareTool, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPPrompt, IMCPCompletable (all probed with Supports()) and through the thread-local TMCPRequestContext.Current so unchanged tools still see era/capabilities/progress/cancellation; TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.Create(Registry) and ProcessRequest(Body, SessionID): string remain (ProcessRequestEx is an addition); TMCPCoreManager.Create(Settings), .SessionID, TMCPStdioTransport.Create(Registry, CoreManager)/Run, TMCPIdHTTPServer.Start/Stop/ManagerRegistry/CoreManager/Settings/Port, TMCPRegistry.* and the JSONRPC_* / MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constants remain (constants re-exported as aliases); TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithParams(const Params: T): string stays the documented override and new virtuals get distinct names (ExecuteWithContext) so no overload/hiding errors appear in existing subclasses; every new ini key has a default that reproduces current behaviour except the three documented security defaults (Origin always validated, loopback bind, TLS 1.2+), each with a one-line opt-out.

architecture.change: Extend src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas: keep MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-06-18' (documented as the legacy default; Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Project.pas:101 and consumers reference it); add MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2026-07-28'; MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS: array[0..0] of string = ('2026-07-28'); MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ('2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26') (accepted on initialize/header); MCP_SERVED_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ('2025-11-25','2025-06-18') (echoed on initialize; 2025-03-26 negotiates up unless the batch option is enabled); MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-11-25'; MCP_META_PROTOCOL_VERSION/MCP_META_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES/MCP_META_CLIENT_INFO/MCP_META_LOG_LEVEL/MCP_META_SERVER_INFO/MCP_META_SUBSCRIPTION_ID/MCP_META_PROGRESS_TOKEN string constants; MCP_LOG_LEVELS = ('debug','info','notice','warning','error','critical','alert','emergency'); MCP_LEGACY_ONLY_METHODS = ('ping','initialize','notifications/initialized','logging/setLevel','resources/subscribe','resources/unsubscribe','roots/list'); MCP_CACHEABLE_METHODS = ('server/discover','tools/list','prompts/list','resources/list','resources/templates/list','resources/read'); move JSONRPC_PARSE_ERROR..JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR here and add MCP_ERROR_HEADER_MISMATCH = -32020, MCP_ERROR_MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY = -32021, MCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION = -32022, MCP_ERROR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_LEGACY = -32002 (legacy era only). Keep the JSONRPC_* declarations in MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas as aliases (= MCPServer.Types.JSONRPC_...) and delete the duplicate block at src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99.
architecture.rationale: Single authoritative home for versions and codes (basic/index.mdx 'Error Codes': only spec-defined codes in -32020..-32099, never -32002 in the modern era); constants are duplicated today (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:27-32 and IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99) and consumer code referencing them must keep compiling.

architecture.change: New unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.Errors.pas: EMCPError = class(Exception) with Code: Integer, Data: TJSONValue (owned, cloned into error.data), HttpStatus: Integer (0 = let the status policy decide); factories MethodNotFound(Method), InvalidParams(Msg, Data = nil), InvalidRequest(Msg), UnsupportedProtocolVersion(Requested, Supported: TArray<string>) -> data {supported, requested} + HttpStatus 400, MissingRequiredClientCapability(Required: TJSONObject) -> data {requiredCapabilities} + 400, HeaderMismatch(Msg) -> 400, MetaInvalid(Msg) -> -32602 + 400, ResourceNotFound(Uri, Era) -> -32602 (modern) / -32002 (legacy) with data {uri}. EMCPToolError = class(Exception) (tool execution failure -> isError:true without the 'Error executing tool:' prefix). EMCPInputRequired (Phase 6) carrying an owned TMCPInputRequiredResult. TMCPJsonRpcProcessor catches EMCPError first and emits code/message/data verbatim; other exceptions -> -32603 (legacy era additionally keeps the Pos('not found') -> -32601 heuristic of JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215 so existing consumer behaviour is unchanged there).
architecture.rationale: CreateErrorResponse has no data parameter (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:128-144) and the code is inferred from message text (:214-215), which cannot express -32022 data.supported/requested, -32021 data.requiredCapabilities, -32020, or -32602 for unknown tool / resource not found; in the modern era the heuristic would turn any 'Resource not found' text into -32601 -> HTTP 404, which dual-era clients read as 'legacy server'.

architecture.change: New unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.RequestContext.pas: TMCPProtocolEra = (peLegacy, peModern); TMCPTransportHints = record HasHeaderLayer: Boolean; HeaderProtocolVersion, HeaderMethod, HeaderName: string; RemoteAddress: string; Session: TMCPTransportSession end; TMCPTransportSession = class (NegotiatedLegacyVersion: string; Lock: TCriticalSection) owned by TMCPStdioTransport (one per process) and by TMCPIdHTTPServer (one shared, only NegotiatedLegacyVersion unused there); IMCPRequestContext = interface ['{new GUID}'] with Era, ProtocolVersion, Method, RequestId: TValue, ClientCapabilities: TJSONObject (borrowed; nil for legacy), ClientInfo: TJSONObject, LogLevel: string, ProgressToken: TJSONValue (cloned, type preserved), InputResponses: TJSONObject, RequestState: string, Principal (Phase 7), IsCancelled: Boolean, procedure CheckCancelled (raises EMCPRequestCancelled), procedure ReportProgress(Progress: Double; Total: Double = -1; const Msg: string = ''), function HasClientCapability(const Path: string): Boolean (e.g. 'elicitation.form'; empty elicitation object implies form), procedure RequireClientCapability(const Path: string) (raises EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability), Sink: IMCPMessageSink (WriteNotification(JSON); nil when the transport cannot stream). TMCPRequestContext implements it; class property Current: IMCPRequestContext backed by a threadvar set/cleared by the processor around dispatch (safe: Indy runs one connection per thread, stdio dispatches on worker threads or the reader thread).
architecture.rationale: Managers and tools receive only (Method, Params) today (Types.pas:39-44; Tool.Base.pas:18) and cannot know the era, the declared client capabilities (basic/index.mdx 'A server MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared'), the logLevel, or a cancellation signal; a thread-local carrier keeps every existing signature intact.

architecture.change: Add to src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas (interfaces only): IMCPCapabilityManagerEx = interface(IMCPCapabilityManager) ['{new GUID}'] function ExecuteMethodEx(const Context: IMCPRequestContext; const Method: string; const Params: TJSONObject): TValue; end; IMCPCapabilityProvider = interface ['{new GUID}'] function GetCapabilityJSON(Era: TMCPProtocolEra): TJSONObject; end (returns the value object, e.g. {listChanged:false}); IMCPManagerEnumerator = interface ['{new GUID}'] function GetManagers: TArray<IMCPCapabilityManager>; end implemented by TMCPManagerRegistry (IMCPManagerRegistry itself is not changed because consumers may implement it). The processor does: if Supports(Manager, IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, Ex) then Ex.ExecuteMethodEx(Ctx, Method, Params) else Manager.ExecuteMethod(Method, Params). Built-in managers implement both.
architecture.rationale: Delphi interfaces cannot be extended without breaking implementers; probing new GUIDs with Supports() lets third-party managers written against IMCPCapabilityManager keep working while built-ins get the context and can advertise capabilities (server/tools.mdx 'Servers that support tools MUST declare the tools capability', same for resources/prompts/completions).

architecture.component: JSON-RPC processor (era detection, validation, envelope, status policy)
architecture.change: src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas: add TMCPProcessResult = record Body: string; HttpStatus: Integer; Era: TMCPProtocolEra; ErrorCode: Integer; IsNotification: Boolean; Deferred: Boolean (Phase 6, stream stays open) end and function ProcessRequestEx(const RequestBody: string; const Hints: TMCPTransportHints): TMCPProcessResult; the existing ProcessRequest(RequestBody, SessionID): string becomes a wrapper (legacy hints, returns Body). New constructor overload Create(ManagerRegistry; Settings: TMCPSettings) (existing one kept; without settings serverInfo is not injected). Pipeline: parse (invalid -> -32700, id null) -> message shape (TJSONArray -> -32600 unless the 2025-03-26 batch option is on; missing/non-'2.0' jsonrpc or missing/empty method -> -32600; id present but null/bool/object/array/fraction -> -32600 with id null; params present but not an object -> -32602) -> notification? (no id: dispatch via ProcessNotification to the owning manager inside try/except, log, no body) -> BuildRequestContext (era algorithm from compatStrategy; modern: MCP-Protocol-Version presence/equality (-32020) -> version in MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (-32022, data.supported = modern list, data.requested) -> Mcp-Method equals method and Mcp-Name equals params.name/params.uri after sentinel decoding for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get (-32020) -> clientCapabilities is an object (-32602 HttpStatus 400) -> logLevel in MCP_LOG_LEVELS (-32602) -> method in MCP_LEGACY_ONLY_METHODS (-32601, unless Settings.LenientModernPing and method = 'ping')) -> set TMCPRequestContext.Current -> dispatch -> envelope (modern only): coerce non-object results (TValue.Empty -> {}, string that parses as an object -> that object, else {"value": ...} + warning), AddPair('resultType','complete') if absent, get-or-create _meta and add io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo {name, version, title?, description?, websiteUrl?} if absent and Settings.EmitServerInfo, and for MCP_CACHEABLE_METHODS with resultType 'complete' add ttlMs 0 / cacheScope 'private' if absent -> status policy: modern: ErrorCode in [-32020,-32021,-32022,-32700,-32600] -> 400; EMCPError.HttpStatus = 400 -> 400; -32601 -> 404; else 200. legacy: always 200. Legacy header rule (transport-level, applied before era detection when HasHeaderLayer): header value not in legacy or modern sets -> 400 with -32600 body.
architecture.rationale: ProcessRequest reads only id/method/params (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:166-188), never _meta, never sets a status (IdHTTPServer.pas:509,553 always 200); the modern spec requires resultType on every result (basic/index.mdx 'The result MUST include a resultType field'), -32602/400 for missing _meta, -32022/400 for unsupported versions, -32020/400 for header failures, -32601/404 for unknown methods (streamable-http.mdx 'Protocol Version Header'), and the same object must keep serving legacy clients with HTTP 200.

architecture.component: Core manager: server/discover, initialize negotiation, capability builder
architecture.change: src/Managers/MCPServer.CoreManager.pas: implement IMCPCapabilityManagerEx; HandlesMethod adds 'server/discover'; Discover(Ctx) returns {resultType:'complete', supportedVersions: MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (+ served legacy versions only if Settings.DiscoverListsLegacyVersions), capabilities: TMCPCapabilityBuilder.Build(peModern), instructions (omit when ''), ttlMs: Settings.DiscoverTtlMs (default 3600000), cacheScope:'public', _meta:{io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo}} and never touches process state; Initialize(Ctx, Params): Requested := Params.protocolVersion; Negotiated := Requested if in MCP_SERVED_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS else MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION... with the compatibility rule that MCP_SERVED_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ('2025-11-25','2025-06-18') and anything else (2025-03-26, 2026-07-28, garbage) answers '2025-06-18' exactly as today unless the batch option promotes 2025-03-26; store Negotiated in Hints.Session.NegotiatedLegacyVersion (stdio); remove the FSessionID write (CoreManager.pas:97) and the non-schema 'sessionId' pair (:126) - SessionID property stays and returns ''; capabilities come from TMCPCapabilityBuilder; log a Warning when params.capabilities contains roots or sampling (SEP-2577 'SHOULD emit a warning'). New unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.Capabilities.pas: TMCPCapabilityBuilder.Build(Registry: IMCPManagerRegistry; Era): TJSONObject - for each manager from IMCPManagerEnumerator: Supports(IMCPCapabilityProvider) -> use its object; else map GetCapabilityName in ['tools','resources','prompts','completions'] -> {} ; 'core' -> nothing; if the registry is nil fall back to today's static {tools:{listChanged:false}, resources:{subscribe:false, listChanged:false}}; RegisterExtension(Id, Settings) emits 'extensions' only when non-empty and only for peModern; never emits 'logging'. TMCPCoreManager gets property ManagerRegistry: IMCPManagerRegistry set by TMCPIdHTTPServer.Start / TMCPStdioTransport.Create (they already hold FCoreManager, IdHTTPServer.pas:41,67; StdioTransport.pas:17,33) or by the consumer.
architecture.rationale: server/discover is a MUST (server/discover.mdx 'Servers MUST implement it') and is answered with -32601 today (CoreManager.pas:48-53); initialize ignores params.protocolVersion (CoreManager.pas:101) although lifecycle.mdx requires echoing a supported requested version; capabilities are hard-coded with non-schema keys supportsProgress/supportsCancellation (CoreManager.pas:106-114) and cannot reflect a prompts manager; FSessionID is a shared unsynchronised field written from Indy worker threads (:97).

architecture.change: src/Core/MCPServer.Settings.pas additive keys with compatible defaults: [Server] Instructions='', Title='', Description='', WebsiteUrl='', DiscoverTtlMs=3600000, EmitServerInfo=1, BindAddress='' (empty = derive from Host: localhost -> 127.0.0.1 and ::1; '0.0.0.0'/'*' = all interfaces with a startup warning), ExposeLogsResource=1; [Protocol] LenientModernPing=0, LegacyBatch2025_03_26=0, DiscoverListsLegacyVersions=0, ToolsListTtlMs=0, ToolsListCacheScope=public, ResourcesListTtlMs=0, ResourcesListCacheScope=private, LegacyGetStream=0; [Security] AllowedOrigins=(defaults to CorsAllowedOrigins plus loopback-any-port patterns http://localhost:*, http://127.0.0.1:*, http://[::1]:*), BearerToken='', RequestStateKey='' (Phase 6), AllowedHosts='' (optional); [Auth] Enabled=0, Mode=bearer|oauth, ResourceUri, AuthorizationServers, ScopesSupported, RequiredScopes (Phase 7). CorsEnabled/CorsAllowedOrigins keep their meaning (CORS response headers) but no longer gate Origin validation.
architecture.rationale: TIniFile.Read* with defaults (Settings.pas:143-155) makes new keys invisible to existing settings.ini files; instructions/title/websiteUrl feed DiscoverResult and serverInfo (schema Implementation), and the security defaults implement streamable-http.mdx 'SHOULD bind only to localhost' and 'MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections'.

architecture.change: src/Server/MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas HandleHTTPRequest order becomes: ValidateOrigin (always; absent Origin allowed, 'null' or unlisted -> 403 with Content-Type application/json body {jsonrpc:'2.0',error:{code:-32600,message:'Origin not allowed'}}, Vary: Origin) -> ApplyCorsHeaders (only when CorsEnabled; Allow-Headers 'Accept, Content-Type, Authorization, Last-Event-ID, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name' plus the reflected Access-Control-Request-Headers on preflight so Mcp-Param-* pass; Allow-Methods 'POST, GET, DELETE, OPTIONS'; Expose-Headers 'Mcp-Session-Id, WWW-Authenticate') -> optional Authorizer (Phase 7; never for OPTIONS or the .well-known path) -> endpoint match (404) -> OPTIONS 204 ContentLength 0 -> GET/DELETE/others -> 405 with Allow: POST, OPTIONS (Settings.LegacyGetStream restores today's immediately-closed SSE stream for legacy Accept: text/event-stream GETs) -> POST: read UTF-8 body; build TMCPTransportHints from RawHeaders (Indy name lookup is case-insensitive; values trimmed); notification-or-response body: modern header -> responses get 400/-32600 (id null), notifications are dispatched and answered 202 with ContentLength := 0, ContentText := '' (verify with curl -i that Indy emits no default HTML body; else call ResponseInfo.WriteHeader manually); requests: Res := FJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx(Body, Hints); ResponseInfo.ResponseNo := Res.HttpStatus; if Res.HttpStatus <> 200 or not AcceptsSSE (proper Accept parsing over all Accept lines, q=0 excluded) -> application/json (TStringStream UTF-8), else SSE event 'event: message'/'data: '+Body+#10#10 without 'id:' lines (FEventIDCounter/GetNextEventID removed); Mcp-Session-Id: never minted (drop the Pos('"sessionId"') block at IdHTTPServer.pas:533-547), echoed back only for Res.Era = peLegacy. Start: FHTTPServer.Bindings.Clear; Bindings.Add with IP := resolved BindAddress (127.0.0.1 [+ ::1 Id_IPv6]) and Port := FPort; keep DefaultPort for HandleQuerySSLPort. ConfigureSSL: SSLVersions := [sslvTLSv1_2 (+TLS1_3 where available)] on the OpenSSL-1.0.2 branch; move the USE_TAURUS_TLS define to src/MCPServer.inc. New pure-function unit src/Server/MCPServer.HttpHeaders.pas: DecodeMcpHeaderValue(Raw; out Value; out Err): Boolean (Trim; '=?base64?'...'?=' case-sensitive sentinel; strict alphabet [A-Za-z0-9+/], '=' only as trailing padding, Length mod 4 = 0 before calling TNetEncoding.Base64.DecodeStringToBytes + TEncoding.UTF8.GetString because TBase64Encoding silently skips invalid characters; plain values must be 0x20-0x7E/0x09) and ParseAccept(RawHeaders): TArray<TMediaRange>. Stop (Phase 6): signal FShutdownEvent, drain open SSE streams with a bounded wait, then Active := False.
architecture.rationale: Origin validation is skipped when CorsEnabled=0 or AllowedOrigins='*' (IdHTTPServer.pas:221-227) although streamable-http.mdx makes it a MUST with 403; MCP-Protocol-Version/Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name are never read (only CORS list :259-260); HTTP status is always 200 (:509,:553); 202 responses may carry Indy's default body (:343-352); GET returns 200 JSON info (:301-313) which violates the legacy 'text/event-stream or 405' MUST; the server listens on all interfaces because no Binding is added (:155-156); TLS 1.0/1.1 are enabled (:396); event ids use a non-atomic counter (:416-420) and are removed from 2026-07-28 (changelog major change 9).

architecture.change: src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas: replace Text I/O with byte streams (THandleStream over STD_INPUT_HANDLE/STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE on Windows, fd 0/1 on POSIX), manual line splitting on #10 with trailing #13 stripped, TEncoding.UTF8 decode, and writes of TEncoding.UTF8.GetBytes(Json + #10) followed by flush (no TStreamWriter preamble/BOM); set TLogger.UseStdErr := True in Create and add TLogger.StdoutReserved so console logging can never fall back to stdout; TMCPStdioWriter (TCriticalSection around write+flush, one line per call) implementing IMCPMessageSink; reader loop on the calling thread: notifications (notifications/cancelled -> InflightRegistry.Cancel(requestId) + log reason; others dispatched synchronously) and requests (enqueued to a bounded worker pool, property MaxConcurrentRequests default 1 = strictly sequential dispatch order as today, while the reader keeps draining stdin so cancel/ping are observed); after a worker finishes: if Ctx.IsCancelled then discard else Writer.WriteMessage(Res.Body); new src/Server/MCPServer.InflightRegistry.pas (TDictionary<string /*id JSON text*/, IMCPRequestContext> under a lock; Register/Complete/Cancel; also maps subscriptions/listen ids to streams in Phase 6); procedure Stop/RequestShutdown (sets FTerminated, closes the stdin handle so the blocked read returns) and property ShutdownEvent: TEvent; on EOF/Stop: stop accepting, drain in-flight work with a bounded wait (2 s), write graceful subscriptions/listen results (Phase 6), flush, return; the outer except block (StdioTransport.pas:73-95) no longer writes a null-id -32603 to stdout - it logs and, on a stdout write failure, terminates the loop. MCPServer.dpr: in stdio mode either skip installing the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers or have SignalHandler call StdioTransport.RequestShutdown; ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown only in DEBUG and never in stdio mode.
architecture.rationale: Readln/Writeln on the RTL Text records use the ANSI code page on Windows (StdioTransport.pas:57,68) although 'JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded'; the loop blocks in Readln while a tool runs (:54-71) so notifications/cancelled and legacy ping cannot be observed; SIGTERM only sets an event nobody waits on in stdio mode (dpr:65-72,114-141) so the client must escalate to SIGKILL (stdio.mdx 'Shutdown'); the outer handler writes an uncorrelated null-id error (:73-95) which violates 'MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message' in spirit.

architecture.component: Tools manager and tool base classes
