ttlMs/cacheScope on tools/list from ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope (defaults 0/'public'; emitted for modern era only); deterministic order (TMCPRegistry registration order via a TList<string>); params.cursor read, any cursor the server did not issue -> -32602 'Invalid cursor', optional ListPageSize (0 = single page); CreateToolJSON omits empty description and emits annotations/icons/_meta from IMCPToolMetadata when present; OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool hooks (Phase 7). src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas: TMCPToolBase, TMCPToolBase<T>, TMCPToolBase<T,R> additionally implement IMCPContextAwareTool ['{new GUID}'] function ExecuteWithContext(const Arguments: TJSONObject; const Context: IMCPRequestContext): TValue whose default calls Execute(Arguments); TMCPToolBase<T> gets a NEW virtual (distinct name, not an overload) function ExecuteWithContext(const Params: T; const Context: IMCPRequestContext): TMCPToolResult; virtual; whose default wraps ExecuteWithParams(Params) into a text block (keeping the 'Error:' prefix heuristic); protected FAnnotations: TMCPToolAnnotations (tri-state hints), FIcons, FMeta with helpers SetReadOnly/SetDestructive/AddIcon; IMCPToolMetadata ['{new GUID}'] exposes them. New unit src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Result.pas: TMCPToolResult with AddText(Text, Annotations = nil), AddImage(Bytes, MimeType), AddAudio(Bytes, MimeType), AddResourceLink(Uri, Name, Description, MimeType, Title), AddEmbeddedText(Uri, Text, MimeType), AddEmbeddedBlob(Uri, Bytes, MimeType), SetStructuredContent(Value: TJSONValue; AddTextFallback = True), IsError, Meta, ToJSON(Era) (legacy 2025-06-18/11-25: drop non-object structuredContent; 2025-03-26: drop structuredContent and downgrade resource_link to text); base64 via TBase64Encoding.Create(0) (no line breaks).
architecture.rationale: Unknown tool and malformed params are isError text results today (ToolsManager.pas:237-248) but server/tools.mdx 'Error Handling' makes them -32602 protocol errors; TMCPToolBase<T,R> results carry structuredContent without the required content array (ToolsManager.pas:168-181; CallToolResult.required includes content); a call without 'arguments' passes nil into TMCPSerializer.DeserializeObject which iterates the nil object (Serializer.pas:111) although 'arguments' is optional in every revision; the tools list iterates a TDictionary (ToolsManager.pas:223) although tools/list order SHOULD be deterministic; image/audio/embedded content is required by the conformance server scenarios and there is no typed builder.

architecture.change: src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Generator.pas: tkInteger/tkInt64 -> 'integer' (tkFloat stays 'number'; TDateTime/TDate/TTime -> string with format date-time); Boolean detected via RttiType.Handle = TypeInfo(Boolean) (and ByteBool/WordBool/LongBool) instead of the name compare at Schema.Generator.pas:119; recursive GenerateTypeSchema for nested classes (properties/required), dynamic arrays and TList<T>/TObjectList<T> (typed items), sets (array of enum names, uniqueItems), with a visited-set/depth cap; empty parameter classes emit {type:'object', additionalProperties:false} (server/tools.mdx recommended form); new optional attributes in MCPServer.Types.pas: SchemaTitle, SchemaFormat, SchemaMinimum/SchemaMaximum, SchemaMinLength/SchemaMaxLength, SchemaPattern, SchemaDefault, SchemaName(jsonName). src/Protocol/MCPServer.Serializer.pas: DeserializeObject nil-safe (treat nil as empty object); class var StrictRequired: Boolean (default False in 1.x; when True a missing property without [Optional] raises EArgumentException 'Missing required parameter' and type-kind mismatches raise instead of StrToIntDef/StrToFloatDef coercion); ConvertValueToJson handles tkDynArray, TList<T>, tkSet, non-Boolean enumerations (name string) and emits null for nil objects so structuredContent conforms to the generated outputSchema. Optional unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Validator.pas (Phase 5): TMCPSchemaValidator.Validate(Schema, Instance, out Errors) covering type, required, enum, properties, items, additionalProperties, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, pattern, const, nullable type arrays; same-document $ref only; depth cap; never network $ref.
architecture.rationale: Integers are advertised as 'number' (Schema.Generator.pas:115) which mis-describes inputs and forbids x-mcp-header later; nested objects/arrays emit no shape (:124-128, :68-69); the serializer omits array/nil/enum properties the generated outputSchema marks required, violating 'Servers MUST provide structured results that conform to this schema'; 'Servers MUST validate all tool inputs' (tools.mdx Security Considerations) while missing required parameters are silently defaulted (Serializer.pas:130-131). basic/index.mdx: 'Implementations MUST NOT automatically dereference $ref values that resolve to a network URI'.

architecture.component: Resources manager and resource base classes
architecture.change: src/Managers/MCPServer.ResourcesManager.pas: implement IMCPCapabilityManagerEx + IMCPCapabilityProvider ({subscribe:false, listChanged:false}); ReadResource: nil params / non-string or empty uri -> EMCPError.InvalidParams; unknown uri -> EMCPError.ResourceNotFound(Uri, Ctx.Era) (-32602 + data.uri modern, -32002 legacy); exceptions from Read propagate as -32603 (remove the text-swallowing try/except at ResourcesManager.pas:155-163); ttlMs/cacheScope (modern era only) on resources/list, resources/templates/list (ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope, default 0/private) and resources/read (from IMCPCacheableResource or 0/private); optional mimeType/description omitted when ''; deterministic order (registration order); cursor handling via the shared pagination helper; blob contents via IMCPResourceReader; templates via IMCPResourceTemplate (exact match first, then first matching template); never handles resources/subscribe|unsubscribe. src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas: TMCPResourceBase<T> keeps IMCPResource and gains protected FTtlMs (0), FCacheScope (csPrivate), FTitle, FSize (-1), FAnnotations, FIcons, FMeta exposed through IMCPCacheableResource ['{new GUID}'] and IMCPResourceMetadata ['{new GUID}']; TMCPResourceContents record (URI, MimeType, Text, Blob: TBytes, IsBlob) + IMCPResourceReader ['{new GUID}'] function ReadContents: TArray<TMCPResourceContents>; TMCPBinaryResourceBase; IMCPResourceTemplate ['{new GUID}'] (GetUriTemplate/Name/Title/Description/MimeType, Matches(URI, Vars), CreateResource) with TMCPResourceTemplateBase compiling RFC 6570 level 1/2 templates to TRegEx. New src/Protocol/MCPServer.Uri.pas (IsValidUri: RFC 3986 scheme check) and src/Protocol/MCPServer.Pagination.pas (opaque cursor = base64url('v1:' + offset); Parse -> -32602 on anything the server did not issue; Slice; nextCursor omitted at end, never ''). Built-ins: project://info and project://readme -> ttlMs 3600000/public; logs://recent and server://status -> 0/private; project://info reports the supported version list instead of 'MCP 2025-06-18'.
architecture.rationale: A missing resource is returned as a successful text result (ResourcesManager.pas:165-170) although 2026-07-28 resources.mdx says 'servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602' and 2025-11-25 says 'Resource not found: -32002'; Params is dereferenced without a nil check (:134); ListResourcesResult/ReadResourceResult require ttlMs/cacheScope (caching.mdx 'Servers MUST include caching hints'); IMCPResource.Read returns one string so blobs and multi-part contents are impossible (Resource.Base.pas:17); templates are hard-coded empty (:186-193).

architecture.change: New src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.Base.pas: TMCPPromptArgument record (Name, Title, Description, Required); TMCPPromptMessages builder (AddText(Role, Text), AddImage(Role, Bytes, MimeType), AddAudio, AddResourceLink(Role, Resource), AddEmbeddedResource(Role, Contents)); IMCPPrompt ['{new GUID}'] (GetName/GetTitle/GetDescription/GetArguments, function Get(const Arguments: TJSONObject; Messages: TMCPPromptMessages; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): string /* description */); TMCPPromptBase and generic TMCPPromptBase<T: class, constructor> deriving arguments from T's writable string properties via RTTI reusing [SchemaDescription]/[Optional] (required = not Optional) and validating presence of required arguments (-32602 'Missing required argument'). New src/Managers/MCPServer.PromptsManager.pas: IMCPCapabilityManagerEx + IMCPCapabilityProvider ({listChanged:false}); prompts/list (deterministic, paginated, modern ttlMs/cacheScope), prompts/get (unknown name -> -32602 with data {name}; arguments must be an object of strings; result {description?, messages}, NO ttlMs/cacheScope, resultType via processor; EMCPInputRequired handled in Phase 6). New src/Managers/MCPServer.CompletionManager.pas (completion/complete; ref/prompt by name, ref/resource by uriTemplate then exact uri; IMCPCompletable ['{new GUID}'] on prompts/templates; values capped at 100 with hasMore; capability {}). src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas: RegisterPrompt/CreatePrompt/GetPromptNames/HasPrompt, RegisterResourceTemplate/..., registration-order lists, name validation warnings (^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$; class var StrictNames raises), class constructor for eager dictionary creation. Sample src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.SummarizeLogs.pas. Register the two managers in MCPServer.dpr (both RunHTTPServer and RunStdioServer) and add src\Prompts to build.bat -U paths and the dproj DCC_UnitSearchPath/DCCReference list.
architecture.rationale: No prompts/completion exist (Registration.pas:13-36 knows only tools/resources); both are MAY features but the required server scenario sets for 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 include prompts-* and completion-complete, so 100% conformance requires them; adding them is purely additive and reuses the pagination/caching/error plumbing built in Phases 1-3.

architecture.change: New src/Protocol/MCPServer.Mrtr.pas: TMCPInputRequests (TDictionary-backed, key uniqueness enforced; AddElicitationForm(Key, Message, RequestedSchema), AddElicitationUrl(Key, Message, Url), AddSampling(Key, Params) and AddRoots(Key) marked deprecated 'SEP-2577'); TMCPInputRequiredResult (InputRequests, RequestState; ToJSON raises if both are empty); EMCPInputRequired = class(Exception) owning a TMCPInputRequiredResult; TMCPInputResponses wrapper (TryGetElicit(Key, out TMCPElicitResult{Action: accept|decline|cancel; Content}), TryGetSampling, TryGetRoots; malformed -> -32602; unknown keys ignored). New src/Protocol/MCPServer.Elicitation.pas: TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder (AddString/AddInteger/AddNumber/AddBoolean/AddEnum/AddMultiSelect -> flat object schema), TMCPElicitation.Form/Url builders (url must be absolute; https unless Settings allow), TMCPElicitSchema.Validate(Content, RequestedSchema). New src/Core/MCPServer.RequestState.pas: TMCPRequestStateCodec.Pack(Payload, Ctx, Method, ArgsDigest, TtlSeconds): string = base64url(json{p,m,d,u,exp}) + '.' + base64url(HMAC-SHA256 via System.Hash.THashSHA2.GetHMACAsBytes) and Open(...) with constant-time compare, expiry, method/digest/principal checks; key from [Security] RequestStateKey or random per process (warning logged). Manager integration: only TMCPToolsManager.CallTool, TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource and TMCPPromptsManager.GetPrompt catch EMCPInputRequired; before serialising they check every inputRequests value against Ctx.ClientCapabilities (elicitation/create needs elicitation (+ .url for mode url; empty object = form only), sampling/createMessage needs sampling (+ sampling.tools when tools present), roots/list needs roots) and raise EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability (-32021/400) otherwise; Ctx.Era = peModern -> result {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests?, requestState?} (no ttlMs/cacheScope); Ctx.Era = peLegacy -> tools: {content:[text explaining that the tool needs interactive input which requires MCP 2026-07-28; supply the value as an argument], isError:true}, resources/prompts: -32603. The processor treats an EMCPInputRequired reaching it from any other method as -32603. Tool authors: override ExecuteWithContext(Params, Ctx): read Ctx.InputResponses/Ctx.RequestState (Open), and when input is missing raise EMCPInputRequired.Create(TMCPInputRequests.Create.AddElicitationForm('confirm', 'Delete 12 files?', TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder.Create.AddBoolean('ok', True).Build), Codec.Pack(...)).
architecture.rationale: mrtr.mdx: servers MAY answer tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get with an InputRequiredResult, MUST include at least one of inputRequests/requestState, MUST NOT send inputRequests the client has not declared, MUST treat requestState as attacker-controlled and protect its integrity (HMAC), MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult on any other request; legacy clients only understand server-initiated requests (lifecycle 'Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated'), so the era gate is mandatory. This is the only sanctioned elicitation path for modern clients (streamable-http.mdx 'The server MUST NOT send independent JSON-RPC requests on this stream').

architecture.change: New src/Server/MCPServer.SseWriter.pas: TMCPSseWriter(Context: TIdContext; ResponseInfo) implementing IMCPMessageSink: Open sets ContentType text/event-stream, CharSet utf-8, Cache-Control no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering: no, ContentLength := -1, CloseConnection := True (Indy does not chunk-encode IOHandler writes; Connection: close delimits the body) then ResponseInfo.WriteHeader; WriteEvent writes 'event: message'#10'data: ' + JSON + #10#10 via Context.Connection.IOHandler.Write(IndyTextEncoding_UTF8); WriteComment writes ': keep-alive'#10#10 (doubles as the disconnect probe); IsConnected checks IOHandler.Connected/ClosedGracefully; EIdConnClosedGracefully/EIdSocketError on write -> mark Ctx cancelled (modern era only; legacy: 'Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling'). HandlePostRequest execution model: run the processor with a buffering sink; if a tool calls ReportProgress (or a logLevel-scoped message is emitted) before completion and the client accepts text/event-stream, switch to SSE lazily (headers not yet written), flush buffered notifications, then the final response; otherwise answer application/json. Pass Context: TIdContext into HandlePostRequest*. New src/Managers/MCPServer.SubscriptionsManager.pas: IMCPCapabilityManagerEx for 'subscriptions/listen' (modern era only; legacy -> -32601): validate params.notifications; agreed subset = requested types the server actually supports (today: none for list_changed unless TMCPRegistry.OnChanged is wired; resourceSubscriptions only for existing URIs when resources.subscribe is advertised) -> immediately write notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged with _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId = listen id and the agreed subset; register in TMCPSubscriptionRegistry (thread-safe); return a deferred marker (TMCPProcessResult.Deferred) so the transport keeps the stream open: HTTP loops WaitFor(ShutdownEvent or queue, 15 s) -> keep-alive comment / flush notifications / exit on disconnect; stdio keeps the subscription in the inflight registry and honours notifications/cancelled for the listen id. Every notification on the stream carries _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId. Teardown on Stop/EOF: stdio writes notifications/cancelled {requestId: listenId} then the completion result {jsonrpc:'2.0', id: listenId, result:{resultType:'complete', _meta:{io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId: listenId}}}; HTTP writes the completion result then closes. TMCPIdHTTPServer keeps a TThreadList of open writers and Stop drains them before Active := False.
architecture.rationale: HandlePostRequestSSE assigns one string to ResponseInfo.ContentText (IdHTTPServer.pas:488-501) so nothing can be written while a tool runs and no stream can stay open; progress (progress.mdx MAY) and the subscriptions pattern (subscriptions.mdx 'MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message', cancellation.mdx 'MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing a subscriptions/listen request ID when it tears down that subscription stream') need incremental writes; the MCP Inspector's modern Subscribe button sends subscriptions/listen and expects an acknowledgment.

architecture.change: New src/Core/MCPServer.Authorization.pas: TMCPAuthDecision = (adAllow, adUnauthorized, adForbidden, adBadRequest); TMCPPrincipal (Subject, Scopes, Claims; never the raw token); TMCPAuthChallenge (ResourceMetadataUrl, Scope, Error, ErrorDescription); IMCPAuthorizer ['{new GUID}'] function Authorize(const BearerToken, HttpMethod, Path: string; out Principal; out Challenge): TMCPAuthDecision; TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer (tokens from [Security] BearerToken, constant-time compare); abstract TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer (ExpectedAudience required, RequiredScopes, TMCPScopeHierarchy 'a>b>c' so broader scopes imply narrower ones, virtual ValidateToken(Token, out Claims) - RFC 7662 introspection via System.Net.HttpClient shipped; JWT verification left to a sample since the RTL has no JOSE) that always enforces aud contains ExpectedAudience and exp > now. TMCPIdHTTPServer: property Authorizer: IMCPAuthorizer (nil = open, as today); token read only from the Authorization header ('Bearer ' prefix, case-insensitive scheme), never from query params; run after Origin validation, skipped for OPTIONS and for GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[<Endpoint>] which serves {resource, authorization_servers[], scopes_supported?, bearer_methods_supported:['header'], resource_name} (401/403 responses carry WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."[, scope="..."][, error="insufficient_scope"] with an id-less JSON-RPC error body; offline_access filtered out of advertised scopes). RequiresScopeAttribute on tool classes checked in TMCPToolsManager.CallTool -> EMCPHttpError 403. Principal exposed via IMCPRequestContext.Principal. TMCPStdioTransport never gets an authorizer. TLogger.RedactJson blanks params._meta, params.requestState, params.inputResponses and keys matching (?i)token|secret|password|authorization; request/response bodies logged at Debug only; header values never logged.
architecture.rationale: authorization/index.mdx: authorization is OPTIONAL but, when present, tokens MUST be validated with audience binding (401/403/400), 'MCP servers MUST implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC9728)', 'Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification'; streamable-http.mdx 'Servers SHOULD implement proper authentication for all connections'; the README advertises an Authorization header (README.md:352-353) that nothing reads; full bodies are logged at Info (IdHTTPServer.pas:331,555; StdioTransport.pas:62,70) and re-exposed through logs://recent.

architecture.change: src/Core/MCPServer.Registration.pas: class constructor creates the dictionaries eagerly (no lazy EnsureInitialized race); registration-order lists; document that all Register* calls must complete before Start/Run. src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Server.pas: AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement for FRequestCount/FActiveConnections (rename the JSON field to activeRequests or keep the name and document); src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Logs.pas: drop the access-log side effect of GetResourceData (Resource.Logs.pas:209) or keep it but declare the resource ttlMs 0/private.
architecture.rationale: Plain Inc/Dec on class vars (Resource.Server.pas:95-109) are called from every Indy worker thread (IdHTTPServer.pas:177-179,206); a dual-era server 'MAY serve both eras concurrently' and Phase 4 adds stdio concurrency.

architecture.change: New tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX, Win32/Win64) with units tests/Processor.Tests.pas (era detection, envelope, error mapping, status policy), tests/HttpHeaders.Tests.pas (sentinel decoding, Accept parsing), tests/Golden.Tests.pas (legacy and modern golden files under tests/golden/legacy/*.json and tests/golden/modern/*.json: request + expected response + expected status, volatile fields normalised), tests/Http.Tests.pas (in-process TMCPIdHTTPServer on an ephemeral port driven by TIdHTTP: Origin 403, 202 empty body, 405 + Allow, 400/404 mapping, bind address), tests/Stdio.Tests.pas (spawn MCPServer.exe --stdio via TProcess/CreateProcess; UTF-8 round trip 'é'/emoji; EOF exit; SIGTERM/TerminateProcess timing), tests/Tools.Tests.pas, tests/Resources.Tests.pas, tests/Prompts.Tests.pas, tests/Mrtr.Tests.pas (tampered/expired/foreign-principal requestState), tests/Auth.Tests.pas; scripts/run-conformance.ps1 and scripts/run-inspector-smoke.ps1 with ci-servers.json (protocolEra legacy/auto/modern entries); conformance-baseline.yml; CHANGELOG.md; README sections.
architecture.rationale: The repository has no tests, no CI and a Windows-only build.bat pinned to Studio 37.0; the compatibility promise ('legacy byte-identical') is only credible if goldens are captured from the current binary before any change and re-run on every phase.

phases.name: Phase 0 - Safety net and hygiene (release 1.0.1)
phases.goal: Capture today's legacy wire behaviour as executable goldens, create the DUnitX harness around the transport-independent processor, and land zero-risk hygiene so that every later phase can prove 'no legacy regression'.
steps: Create tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX) referencing src/ units; add a TProcessorHarness that instantiates TMCPManagerRegistry + TMCPCoreManager(TMCPSettings.Create('', False)) + TMCPToolsManager + TMCPResourcesManager exactly like MCPServer.dpr:74-91 and calls TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest.

Capture golden files from the CURRENT code for the legacy wire: initialize (params.protocolVersion 2025-03-26 / 2025-06-18 / 2025-11-25 / garbage), notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list, tools/call echo|get_time|calculate|list_files (valid, missing arguments, unknown tool, invalid params), resources/list, resources/read (each built-in, unknown uri, missing params), resources/templates/list, unknown method, unparseable body, id null, batch array; normalise timestamps/uptime/memory before comparing; store as tests/golden/legacy/<name>.json {request, response, httpStatus}.

Move the JSONRPC_* constants to MCPServer.Types.pas, keep aliases in MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas, delete the duplicates in MCPServer.IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99; add MCP_ERROR_* (-32020/-32021/-32022) and the version/meta constants (no behaviour change).

Replace Inc/Dec on TServerStatusResource class vars (Resource.Server.pas:95-109) with AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement; replace Inc(FEventIDCounter) (IdHTTPServer.pas:416-420) with TInterlocked.Increment until it is removed in Phase 2; make TMCPRegistry create its dictionaries in a class constructor.
Set TLogger.UseStdErr := True inside TMCPStdioTransport.Create and add TLogger.StdoutReserved so embedders cannot corrupt stdout; keep TLogger.LogToConsole default False.

Add scripts/run-conformance.ps1 (starts the built exe, waits on the endpoint, runs the official conformance CLI with --requirements 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28, records results) and scripts/run-inspector-smoke.ps1 (Inspector CLI --method tools/list in legacy era); record the current failing scenarios in conformance-baseline.yml so regressions become visible from the start.
Add CHANGELOG.md and a 'Compatibility promise' README paragraph describing the golden-test policy.

gapIdsClosed: GAP-ECO-01 (harness and scripts; baseline finalised in Phase 7)
risks: No Delphi compiler on Linux/GitHub-hosted runners: goldens must be captured on a Windows dev box and committed; document the procedure.
Golden normalisation must not hide real regressions: only whitelist known-volatile fields (timestamps, uptime, memory, log entries).

phases.name: Phase 1 - Protocol core: typed errors, request context, era detection, server/discover, result envelope (release 1.1.0)
phases.goal: Make the server dual-era on both transports at the JSON-RPC layer: modern clients get server/discover, per-request _meta handling, resultType/_meta.serverInfo, correct modern error codes; legacy clients get correct initialize negotiation and byte-identical results.
steps: Add src/Protocol/MCPServer.Errors.pas (EMCPError with Code/Data/HttpStatus and the factories) and src/Protocol/MCPServer.RequestContext.pas (TMCPProtocolEra, TMCPTransportHints, TMCPTransportSession, IMCPRequestContext/TMCPRequestContext with thread-local Current, HasClientCapability/RequireClientCapability); add IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator to MCPServer.Types.pas and implement IMCPManagerEnumerator in TMCPManagerRegistry.

In TMCPJsonRpcProcessor add ProcessRequestEx(Body, Hints): TMCPProcessResult and the Create(Registry, Settings) overload; implement message-shape validation (-32700 / -32600 for arrays, bad jsonrpc, bad method, id null/bool/object/fraction, non-object params -> -32602) and ProcessNotification (dispatch to the owning manager, swallow errors, log; notifications/cancelled logged with reason).

Implement BuildRequestContext: method = 'initialize' -> peLegacy; _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion string -> peModern with checks in this order: (HTTP only) header missing -> HeaderMismatch; header <> _meta value -> HeaderMismatch; version not in MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS -> UnsupportedProtocolVersion(data.supported = modern list, data.requested); (HTTP only) Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name checks with sentinel decoding -> HeaderMismatch; clientCapabilities missing or not an object -> MetaInvalid (-32602, HttpStatus 400); logLevel present but not in MCP_LOG_LEVELS -> MetaInvalid; method in MCP_LEGACY_ONLY_METHODS -> MethodNotFound (LenientModernPing exempts ping); else (HTTP) header naming a modern version without _meta -> MetaInvalid; header value in neither set -> InvalidRequest with HttpStatus 400; else peLegacy with ProtocolVersion = header value or Session.NegotiatedLegacyVersion or '2025-06-18'.

Dispatch through IMCPCapabilityManagerEx when supported, else ExecuteMethod; set/clear TMCPRequestContext.Current around the call; catch EMCPError (code/message/data), EMCPInputRequired reaching the processor -> -32603 (Phase 6), any other Exception -> -32603, except in the legacy era where the existing Pos('not found') -> -32601 heuristic is preserved.

Modern-only envelope: coerce result to a TJSONObject, add resultType 'complete' if absent, add _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo {name, version [+ title, description, websiteUrl]} if absent and Settings.EmitServerInfo, and for MCP_CACHEABLE_METHODS add ttlMs 0 / cacheScope 'private' if absent (safety net for third-party managers; built-ins set their own in Phase 3). Legacy results are untouched (goldens prove it).

Status policy inside the processor (single source of truth): modern: -32020/-32021/-32022/-32700/-32600 -> 400, EMCPError.HttpStatus = 400 -> 400, -32601 -> 404, else 200; legacy: 200, except the transport-level invalid MCP-Protocol-Version header -> 400 with a -32600 body. Phase 2 makes the HTTP transport honour it; stdio ignores it.

TMCPCoreManager: add 'server/discover' (Discover returns supportedVersions ['2026-07-28'], capabilities from TMCPCapabilityBuilder, instructions, ttlMs Settings.DiscoverTtlMs, cacheScope 'public', _meta.serverInfo; params may be nil or contain only _meta); Initialize negotiates the requested legacy version (2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 echoed; everything else answers 2025-06-18 as today), stores it in Hints.Session, drops the FSessionID write and the 'sessionId' body pair, warns on deprecated roots/sampling client capabilities; add property ManagerRegistry and the settings-driven serverInfo builder (Instructions/Title/Description/WebsiteUrl/DiscoverTtlMs/EmitServerInfo added to TMCPSettings).

New src/Protocol/MCPServer.Capabilities.pas: TMCPCapabilityBuilder.Build(Registry, Era) using IMCPCapabilityProvider/GetCapabilityName mapping, static fallback when no registry; emit tools:{listChanged:false} and resources:{subscribe:false, listChanged:false} (the undefined supportsProgress/supportsCancellation keys are dropped; TMCPToolsCapability keeps its properties, marked deprecated, and gains ListChanged).

Wire both transports to the new overloads with legacy-equivalent hints (HTTP hints get HasHeaderLayer=True and the raw header values but Phase 1 still answers HTTP 200 for everything - the status comes with Phase 2), TMCPStdioTransport owns one TMCPTransportSession, TMCPIdHTTPServer passes Settings to the processor.

Tests: legacy goldens unchanged; new modern goldens: server/discover (with and without initialize before), tools/list + tools/call with _meta (resultType + serverInfo + ttlMs/cacheScope safety net), missing clientCapabilities -> -32602/400, unknown version '1900-01-01' -> -32022 with data.supported/requested, invalid logLevel -> -32602, modern ping -> -32601 (and lenient flag), id null -> -32600, missing jsonrpc -> -32600, initialize with modern _meta -> legacy handshake, concurrent initialize from 50 threads (no shared field left).

Update README badge to 'MCP 2026-07-28 (dual-era)' and add a 'Protocol versions and dual-era behaviour' section (era detection rules, what legacy clients see, extension points IMCPCapabilityManagerEx/IMCPCapabilityProvider/EMCPError/TMCPRequestContext.Current).
deliverables: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx with era detection, envelope injection and status policy
server/discover and correct legacy initialize negotiation in TMCPCoreManager
Modern golden suite; legacy goldens byte-identical
gapIdsClosed: GAP-BP-08 (static + provider hook; registry-derived completion in Phase 3)
risks: Era misdetection would silently degrade a client; mitigated by the ordered algorithm living in one function with table-driven unit tests for every branch.
The legacy 'not found' heuristic is kept only for legacy requests; a modern request whose consumer manager raises a plain Exception now yields -32603 instead of -32601 (documented, correct).

Dropping 'sessionId' from the initialize body and supportsProgress/supportsCancellation from capabilities is a wire change on the legacy path; no known client reads them (schema.json leaves these objects open) - the goldens are updated deliberately for exactly these two keys and nothing else.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Dual-era Streamable HTTP transport and security hardening (release 1.2.0)
phases.goal: Make TMCPIdHTTPServer conformant for both eras: header validation, era-gated HTTP status codes, Origin validation on every connection, clean 202/405 responses, no session minting, loopback binding, modern TLS.
steps: Split VerifyAndSetCORSHeaders into ValidateOrigin (always runs; [Security] AllowedOrigins with scheme+host match and ':*' port wildcard; loopback origins on any port allowed by default; '*' keeps allow-all with a startup warning; 403 + id-less JSON-RPC error body + Vary: Origin) and ApplyCorsHeaders (only when CorsEnabled; updated Allow-Headers/Allow-Methods/Expose-Headers; OPTIONS reflects Access-Control-Request-Headers and answers 204 with ContentLength 0).

Populate TMCPTransportHints from RawHeaders (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, case-insensitive lookup, trimmed) and add src/Server/MCPServer.HttpHeaders.pas with the strict Base64 sentinel decoder and an RFC-compliant Accept parser; unit-test the SEP-2243 edge table (lowercase header names accepted, 'TOOLS/CALL' rejected, padded Mcp-Name trimmed, bad Base64 padding -> -32020, UTF-8 Mcp-Name for non-ASCII names).

HandlePostRequest: set ResponseInfo.ResponseNo := Res.HttpStatus; JSON body for any non-200 status; SSE only when the client accepts text/event-stream AND streaming is needed (Phase 6) - default to application/json now; remove SSE 'id:' lines, FEventIDCounter and GetNextEventID; Mcp-Session-Id echoed only when Res.Era = peLegacy, never minted; delete the sessionId scraping block (IdHTTPServer.pas:533-547).

Notification/response bodies: dispatch notifications through ProcessNotification then 202 with ContentLength := 0 and empty ContentText (verify with curl -i on Windows that no Indy default body is emitted; otherwise WriteHeader manually); a JSON-RPC response body with a modern MCP-Protocol-Version header -> 400 with -32600 (id null); legacy -> 202 as today; array bodies -> 400/-32600 (modern) or 200/-32600 (legacy) unless the 2025-03-26 batch option (Phase 4) is enabled.

GET and DELETE (and any other method) -> 405 with Allow: POST, OPTIONS; [Protocol] LegacyGetStream=1 restores today's immediately-closed SSE stream for legacy Accept: text/event-stream GETs; the endpoint-info JSON is removed from the MCP endpoint (optionally served at '/').

Start: Bindings.Clear + Bindings.Add(IP := resolved BindAddress, Port := FPort) (+ ::1 when IPv6 requested); '0.0.0.0'/'*' logs a warning recommending [Auth]; README 'Remote connections' paragraph updated with BindAddress=0.0.0.0.

ConfigureSSL: TLS 1.2+ only on the OpenSSL-1.0.2 branch, explicit minimum on TaurusTLS where the API allows; move the USE_TAURUS_TLS define to src/MCPServer.inc with {$I} so consumers override without editing library sources.

Log request/response bodies at Debug through TLogger.RedactJson (blank params._meta, requestState, inputResponses, token/secret/password keys); never log header values; make logs://recent registration switchable ([Server] ExposeLogsResource, default 1).

Tests: in-process HTTP suite (Origin 403 with CORS disabled, loopback origin with port accepted, 202 Content-Length 0, GET/DELETE 405 + Allow, modern -32601 -> 404 vs legacy 200, header mismatch -> 400/-32020, no header + _meta -> 400/-32020, modern header + no _meta -> 400/-32602, unknown header version -> 400, bind to 127.0.0.1 only); rerun conformance dns-rebinding-protection under both requirement sets.
deliverables: Dual-era TMCPIdHTTPServer with era-gated status mapping and header validation
Security defaults: Origin always validated, loopback bind, TLS 1.2+, redacted logs
settings.ini.example and README transport/security sections updated
gapIdsClosed: GAP-HTTP-13 (error-code part; batch option in Phase 4)
risks: Indy internals (default body on empty 202/204, Bindings default, header case-insensitivity) cannot be verified in this Linux container; each is a one-line check on the Windows build (curl -i, netstat) and is called out in the step text.
Loopback binding and always-on Origin validation are deliberate runtime behaviour changes; both have one-line ini opt-outs and CHANGELOG entries.
Removing the GET endpoint-info JSON could surprise someone who curl'ed it; it is undocumented in the README.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Tools and resources modern correctness, capability derivation (release 1.3.0)
phases.goal: Make tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list schema-valid in the modern era and error-correct in both eras, without changing legacy success paths.
steps: TMCPToolsManager: ExtractToolNameAndArguments raises EMCPError.InvalidParams for malformed params; absent 'arguments' -> empty object (fixes the nil dereference in Serializer.pas:111); unknown tool -> -32602 'Unknown tool: x'; EMCPToolError -> isError text; other exceptions keep the 'Error executing tool:' prefix; final else branch guarantees 'content'; TJSONObject results also get a text block with the compact JSON; ttlMs/cacheScope on tools/list (modern only; ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope from settings, defaults 0/'public'); registration-order listing; cursor -> -32602 when unrecognised, optional ListPageSize; IMCPCapabilityProvider {listChanged:false}.

Schema generator: 'integer' for tkInteger/tkInt64, Boolean via TypeInfo, TDateTime as string/date-time, recursive nested objects/arrays/TList<T>/sets, additionalProperties:false for empty parameter classes; serializer: nil-safe, arrays/lists/sets/enums serialised, nil objects -> null, StrictRequired flag (default False, documented as the 2.0 default).

New src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Result.pas (TMCPToolResult content builders, SetStructuredContent with text fallback, ToJSON(Era) shaping) and IMCPToolMetadata/IMCPContextAwareTool on the three base classes; new virtual TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithContext(Params, Ctx): TMCPToolResult with a default that wraps ExecuteWithParams; ship one built-in tool that returns an image block (e.g. a generated 1x1 PNG) and one with readOnlyHint to exercise annotations.

TMCPResourcesManager: EMCPError for missing/invalid uri and for unknown uri (-32602 + data.uri modern, -32002 legacy), -32603 for read failures, omit empty mimeType/description, registration-order listing, cursor -> -32602, ttlMs/cacheScope (modern only) from IMCPCacheableResource / list settings, IMCPResourceReader blob path (TBase64Encoding.Create(0)), IMCPResourceMetadata optional fields (title/size/icons/annotations/_meta), IMCPCapabilityProvider {subscribe:false, listChanged:false}; TMCPRegistry.RegisterResource validates the URI scheme (MCPServer.Uri.pas); built-in resources declare their ttlMs/cacheScope; project://info reports the supported version list.

Complete TMCPCapabilityBuilder: derive capabilities from IMCPManagerEnumerator + IMCPCapabilityProvider (a consumer registering only TMCPToolsManager no longer advertises resources); add RegisterExtension for future extensions (omitted when empty; modern only); TMCPRegistry warns on invalid or duplicate tool names (StrictNames raises).

Tests: tools/call without arguments for get_time succeeds; unknown tool -> -32602 in both eras; resource not found -> -32602 (modern, data.uri) / -32002 (legacy); read exception -> -32603; modern tools/list has resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope and legacy tools/list does not; deterministic order across 100 calls; blob resource base64 single line; capability object reflects registered managers; conformance scenarios tools-call-image/audio/embedded-resource/mixed-content/error, resources-read-binary, sep-2164-resource-not-found, caching.
deliverables: Updated goldens (error paths only) and conformance baseline
gapIdsClosed: GAP-TL-07 (strict flag + nil safety; validator in Phase 5)
GAP-TL-24 (empty-class form; remaining attributes in Phase 5)
risks: Unknown tool / resource not found become JSON-RPC errors on the legacy path too (spec-endorsed); any consumer test expecting the old isError text must be updated - called out in CHANGELOG with before/after JSON.

Schema text changes ('integer', nested shapes, additionalProperties:false) alter tools/list bytes for existing consumers; harmless for clients but snapshot tests in consumer repos may need refreshing.

phases.name: Phase 4 - stdio robustness: UTF-8 framing, shutdown, cancellation, progress, optional 2025-03-26 batches (release 1.4.0)
phases.goal: Make the stdio transport spec-correct on Windows and Linux, responsive to cancellation and legacy ping during long tool calls, and able to emit request-scoped notifications, without changing dispatch order by default.
steps: Replace Text I/O with UTF-8 byte streams and LF-only framing (no BOM); keep blank-line tolerance; test with an echo of 'é' and an emoji on Windows.

Reader/writer split: TMCPStdioWriter (locked, implements IMCPMessageSink) and a reader loop that dispatches notifications synchronously and requests through a bounded worker pool with MaxConcurrentRequests (default 1 keeps today's sequential order; documented opt-in for higher values); src/Server/MCPServer.InflightRegistry.pas registers contexts before dispatch and drops them after the response is written.

notifications/cancelled: parse requestId (string or number, keyed by JSON text) and reason, log at Info, InflightRegistry.Cancel marks the context; a cancelled request's response is discarded and ReportProgress becomes a no-op; unknown/finished ids and malformed params are ignored silently (never answered).

Progress: read params._meta.progressToken into the context (JSON type preserved); ReportProgress enqueues notifications/progress {progressToken, progress, total?, message?} to the sink with monotonic enforcement and a MinProgressIntervalMs throttle; stdio writes them before the response (HTTP streaming arrives in Phase 6; until then HTTP contexts get a nil sink and ReportProgress is a no-op there).

Shutdown: TMCPStdioTransport.RequestShutdown/ShutdownEvent; MCPServer.dpr installs no SIGTERM/SIGINT override in stdio mode (or routes it to RequestShutdown and closes the stdin handle so Eof returns); on EOF drain in-flight work with a 2 s bound, flush, exit; ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown only in DEBUG and never in stdio mode; the outer except block no longer writes to stdout and terminates on a broken stdout.

Optional (decision-gated, default off): [Protocol] LegacyBatch2025_03_26=1 makes initialize echo '2025-03-26' when requested and lets ProcessRequestEx process a legacy-era TJSONArray element-by-element returning a JSON array (or nothing when all were notifications); modern-era arrays stay -32600/400.

Tests: spawn the exe with --stdio and drive it over pipes: legacy handshake, UTF-8 round trip, cancel during a deliberately slow test tool (response suppressed), ping answered while the slow tool runs, progress notifications precede the response, EOF exits within 2 s, SIGTERM exits without SIGKILL on Linux.
deliverables: UTF-8/LF-correct, cancellable, progress-capable stdio transport with graceful shutdown
Optional 2025-03-26 batch support behind a setting
risks: Worker-thread execution of tools on stdio is new; MaxConcurrentRequests=1 preserves ordering, and tools already run on Indy worker threads over HTTP, so the thread-safety contract is unchanged.
RTL Text I/O code-page behaviour must be confirmed on Windows before/after (documented in the gap analysis as unverified in this container).
Closing the stdin handle from a signal handler is platform-sensitive; fall back to a polling read with a short timeout if it misbehaves.

phases.name: Phase 5 - Prompts, completion, resource templates, schema validation (release 1.5.0)
phases.goal: Add the optional server features that the required conformance scenario sets exercise (prompts-*, completion-complete, resources-templates-read) as purely additive units, sharing the pagination/caching/error plumbing.
steps: Add src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.Base.pas (IMCPPrompt, TMCPPromptBase, TMCPPromptBase<T>, TMCPPromptMessages builders) and src/Managers/MCPServer.PromptsManager.pas (prompts/list with pagination and modern ttlMs/cacheScope, prompts/get with -32602 for unknown name / missing required argument / non-string argument values, no caching fields on GetPromptResult); register in MCPServer.dpr; add src\Prompts to build.bat and the dproj; sample prompt embedding logs://recent.

Add IMCPResourceTemplate/TMCPResourceTemplateBase (RFC 6570 level 1/2 matching via TRegEx with percent-decoding), TMCPRegistry.RegisterResourceTemplate, templates in resources/templates/list (uriTemplate, name, optional title/description/mimeType) and template resolution in resources/read; sample logs://{level}.

Add src/Managers/MCPServer.CompletionManager.pas (completion/complete; ref/prompt, ref/resource; IMCPCompletable; values capped at 100 with hasMore/total; -32602 for unknown ref; capability {} only when registered; optional per-client token bucket hook).

Add src/Protocol/MCPServer.Schema.Validator.pas (2020-12 subset, same-document $ref only, depth cap) and the remaining schema attributes; TMCPToolsManager validates arguments against inputSchema for tools not derived from the generic bases (isError with joined messages) and, in DEBUG, self-checks structuredContent against outputSchema.

Tests: prompts/list/get goldens both eras (resource_link and title/icons gated for 2025-03-26), completion for a template argument, template match/miss, validator table tests; conformance prompts-*, completion-complete, resources-templates-read under both requirement sets.
deliverables: Schema validator and extra schema attributes
README sections 'Creating Custom Prompts', 'Resource templates', 'Input validation'
risks: RFC 6570 matching is easy to get subtly wrong (reserved expansion, percent-decoding); restrict to levels 1-2 and document.
Prompts/completion increase the surface consumers must register in their own .dpr to stay dual-era conformant; document the recommended manager set.

phases.name: Phase 6 - Incremental SSE streaming, MRTR/elicitation, requestState integrity, minimal subscriptions/listen (release 1.6.0)
phases.goal: Expose the headline 2026-07-28 features to tool/resource/prompt authors (progress over HTTP, elicitation via InputRequiredResult, integrity-protected requestState) and make long-lived streams possible in Indy, with a safe legacy fallback.
steps: Add src/Server/MCPServer.SseWriter.pas and pass TIdContext into the POST handlers; implement the lazy JSON-or-SSE decision (buffer until the first notification, then WriteHeader + stream); disconnect during a modern request marks the context cancelled and suppresses further writes; keep-alive comments every 15-30 s on long streams; TMCPIdHTTPServer.Stop drains open streams before deactivating.

Add src/Protocol/MCPServer.Mrtr.pas, src/Protocol/MCPServer.Elicitation.pas and src/Core/MCPServer.RequestState.pas; integrate EMCPInputRequired handling into TMCPToolsManager.CallTool, TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource and TMCPPromptsManager.GetPrompt with the capability check (-32021 when a required client capability is absent), modern InputRequiredResult (no caching fields, last SSE message) and the legacy fallback (isError text / -32603); expose InputResponses/RequestState on IMCPRequestContext; processor converts an EMCPInputRequired from any other method into -32603.

Ship a sample tool (e.g. 'delete_files' with a form elicitation confirming the action, and a URL-mode example behind a setting) plus README 'Elicitation (MCP 2026-07-28)' with the security rules (no secrets via form mode, bind URL flows to the user, never pre-authenticated URLs).

Add src/Managers/MCPServer.SubscriptionsManager.pas: subscriptions/listen (modern only) acknowledges the agreed subset (currently empty unless resource subscriptions are enabled), keeps the stream open with keep-alives, honours client cancellation (HTTP disconnect / stdio notifications/cancelled), and closes gracefully on Stop/EOF with the completion result (stdio additionally sends notifications/cancelled first); TMCPRegistry.OnChanged hook so that if dynamic registration is ever added, listChanged can be flipped and fan-out wired.

Tests: MRTR round-trip (input_required -> retry with inputResponses -> complete), tampered/expired/foreign-principal requestState -> -32602, missing capability -> -32021/400, legacy client -> isError text, progress notifications on an HTTP SSE response, client disconnect -> cancelled, subscriptions/listen ack-first and graceful close on both transports; conformance input-required-result-* scenarios, tools-call-with-progress, server-sse-multiple-streams.
deliverables: MRTR/elicitation API for authors + requestState HMAC codec
risks: Indy long-lived streams pin one worker thread each and require Connection: close (no chunked encoding) - set MaxConnections accordingly and verify proxies (nginx X-Accel-Buffering already set).
Per-process random RequestStateKey breaks MRTR across restarts/load-balanced instances; the config key is documented as required for those deployments.
If the schedule slips, subscriptions/listen may stay at -32601/404, which is still conformant because no listChanged/subscribe capability is advertised.

phases.name: Phase 7 - Authorization hooks, hardening, docs and conformance baseline (release 1.7.0)
phases.goal: Provide opt-in, spec-shaped authentication for HTTP deployments and finish the ecosystem deliverables (README, settings, conformance baseline, Inspector recipes, manual client matrix).
steps: Add src/Core/MCPServer.Authorization.pas (IMCPAuthorizer, TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer, abstract TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer with mandatory audience/expiry checks and RFC 7662 introspection helper, scope hierarchy), TMCPIdHTTPServer.Authorizer, 401/403 challenge writer (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata, scope, error=insufficient_scope), the RFC 9728 well-known document, [Auth] settings and wiring in MCPServer.dpr; RequiresScopeAttribute + OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool hooks in TMCPToolsManager; a simple token bucket (RateLimitPerMinute, default 0 = off) returning 429 with a JSON-RPC -32603 body; never wire any of it into TMCPStdioTransport.
Optional [Security] AllowedHosts host-header allow-list (default off).

Finish GAP-ECO-01: conformance-baseline.yml reflecting the final expected state (target: no failures for both requirement sets; tasks-* not scored), scripts kept in sync, ci-servers.json entries for protocolEra legacy/auto/modern and an auth entry expecting Inspector exit code 3 without a token; document the self-hosted Windows runner option.

README overhaul: badge 2026-07-28 dual-era; Features; Transport modes (405 on GET/DELETE, no sessions, BindAddress); 'Protocol versions and dual-era behaviour' (era table, HTTP status table, curl examples for both eras); 'Using as a Library' checklist (register managers, UseStdErr, thread safety, new interfaces); tool/prompt/resource authoring (naming rules, schema dialect subset, TMCPToolResult, EMCPToolError vs EMCPError, annotations/icons, elicitation); Security (Origin, bind, auth modes, no token passthrough, requestState, x-mcp-header PII warning); Testing (DUnitX, conformance CLI commands, Inspector eras and CLI, Claude Code/Codex matrix); state explicitly that 2025-03-26 clients are served unauthenticated only.

Manual acceptance matrix executed and recorded in docs/acceptance-<version>.md: Claude Code over HTTP (legacy), Codex over stdio (legacy), Inspector web/CLI in legacy/auto/modern, an official 2026-07-28 SDK client (TypeScript or Python) against HTTP and stdio, curl error matrix.
deliverables: Final conformance baseline and CI scripts
risks: Server-side OAuth behaviour is not machine-scored by the conformance suite (all auth/* scenarios are client-leg), so acceptance depends on DUnitX tests plus a manual Inspector OAuth run.
JWT verification is intentionally not in core (no JOSE in the RTL); consumers needing it must implement ValidateToken or use introspection.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx(const RequestBody: string; const Hints: TMCPTransportHints): TMCPProcessResult and constructor Create(ManagerRegistry; Settings: TMCPSettings) overload
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Existing Create(ManagerRegistry) and ProcessRequest(RequestBody, SessionID): string remain and delegate with legacy-equivalent hints; consumers using the old call simply get no serverInfo injection.

publicApiChanges.item: New units src/Protocol/MCPServer.Errors.pas (EMCPError, EMCPToolError, EMCPInputRequired) and src/Protocol/MCPServer.RequestContext.pas (IMCPRequestContext, TMCPRequestContext.Current, TMCPTransportHints, TMCPTransportSession)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Opt-in; plain Exception from custom managers/tools still maps to -32603 (legacy era additionally keeps the 'not found' -> -32601 heuristic).

publicApiChanges.item: IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPContextAwareTool, IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPPrompt, IMCPCompletable, IMCPAuthorizer, IMCPMessageSink (all new GUIDs)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: IMCPCapabilityManager, IMCPManagerRegistry, IMCPTool and IMCPResource keep their GUIDs and members; new interfaces are probed with Supports() and implemented by the shipped base classes, so consumer subclasses inherit them and direct interface implementers are untouched.

publicApiChanges.item: MCPServer.Types constants: MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION kept ('2025-06-18', documented as legacy default); new MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION, MCP_MODERN/LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, MCP_META_*, MCP_ERROR_*; JSONRPC_* moved to Types with aliases left in MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor

plans.testing: 1) Unit tests (DUnitX, tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj, Win32/Win64, run from the IDE or a rsvars-driven script; Linux64 via PAServer optional). The processor is transport-independent, so most tests feed JSON strings plus TMCPTransportHints into TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx and assert Body/HttpStatus/Era/ErrorCode: table-driven era-detection matrix (initialize with/without _meta; _meta present with header present/absent/mismatched; modern header without _meta; unknown header version; no header no _meta), envelope injection (resultType only when modern; serverInfo toggle; cacheable safety net only for the six methods), status policy table, id/jsonrpc/params validation, legacy-only method gate incl. LenientModernPing, notification dispatch and cancel parsing, capability builder with 0/1/2/custom managers, pagination cursor codec, sentinel Base64 decoder edge table from SEP-2243 (case-insensitive names, 'TOOLS/CALL' rejected, whitespace trimmed, bad padding -> -32020, UTF-8 round trip), Accept parser (q=0, multiple Accept lines), schema generator snapshots, serializer round trips (arrays/enums/nil/TDateTime), TMCPToolResult ToJSON per era, requestState codec (tamper, expiry, wrong principal, wrong method/digest), elicitation schema builder/validator, authorizer decisions and challenge header formatting, PRM document, scope hierarchy. 2) Golden protocol tests for both eras: tests/golden/legacy/*.json captured from the v1.0 binary in Phase 0 (byte-identical after normalising volatile fields; deliberate updates only for the documented error-path and sessionId/capability-key changes), tests/golden/modern/*.json added per phase (server/discover, tools/list, tools/call incl. image/audio/embedded, resources/*, prompts/*, completion, MRTR round trips, all modern errors with their HTTP status). Every phase re-runs the whole golden suite. 3) In-process HTTP tests: start TMCPIdHTTPServer on an ephemeral port with an in-memory TMCPSettings and drive it with TIdHTTP: Origin 403 with CORS disabled, loopback origin with any port accepted, preflight headers, 202 with Content-Length: 0, GET/DELETE 405 + Allow, modern 404/-32601 vs legacy 200/-32601, 400 bodies for -32020/-32022/-32602, no Mcp-Session-Id minted, bind to 127.0.0.1 only (connect to a LAN address fails), SSE streaming with progress then response, disconnect -> cancelled, subscriptions/listen ack-first, 401/403 challenges when an authorizer is set, well-known metadata reachable without a token. 4) Stdio process tests: spawn MCPServer.exe --stdio over pipes: legacy initialize/tools/list, modern server/discover first, initialize after modern messages, UTF-8 'é'/emoji echo on Windows, cancel during a slow test tool suppresses the response, ping answered during a slow tool, progress lines precede the response, EOF exits < 2 s, SIGTERM (Linux) exits without SIGKILL, nothing but JSON lines on stdout while logging is on. 5) Official tooling: scripts/run-conformance.ps1 runs the official conformance CLI (repository github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance, referenced by docs/community/sdk-tiers.mdx and SEP-2484) against http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp with the frozen requirement sets for 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 and an expected-failures baseline (exact flag names verified against the conformance README at implementation time; the anchor release for 2026-07-28 is 0.2.0-alpha.10 per the gap analysis); target after Phase 6: no failures in either set (tasks-* are unscored). scripts/run-inspector-smoke.ps1 uses the MCP Inspector CLI (docs/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/cli.mdx: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli --config ./ci-servers.json --server <name> --method tools/list --format json`) with ci-servers.json entries for protocolEra legacy, auto and modern (docs/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector/protocol-eras.mdx) plus a stdio entry, and an auth entry asserting the auth-required exit code when no token is supplied. 6) Manual matrix recorded per release: Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http delphi-mcp-server http://localhost:3000/mcp`; legacy handshake, tools/list, tool call, resource read), Codex (stdio config from README; legacy), Claude Desktop (stdio, optional), MCP Inspector web in all three eras (Subscribe button in modern era, per-request logLevel=debug tolerated, MRTR elicitation flow with the sample tool), one official 2026-07-28 SDK client (TypeScript or Python) over HTTP and stdio, and a curl error matrix (all modern 400/404 cases, legacy invalid header -> 400, Origin 403). 7) Thread-safety checks: 50 concurrent initialize/tools/call over HTTP with FastMM full debug mode, no leaks (ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown in DEBUG builds only). 8) Windows-specific verifications flagged from the gap analysis before finalising Phase 2/4: Indy empty-body behaviour on 202/204, Bindings default, RawHeaders case-insensitivity, RTL Text code page, TStreamWriter BOM.
risks: No Delphi toolchain on Linux or hosted CI: all compile/run verification happens on a Windows developer machine or a self-hosted runner; mitigate with the scripted checklist, committed goldens and a release gate that requires the DUnitX + conformance + Inspector scripts to pass.

Era misdetection is the single highest-impact failure mode (a modern request served as legacy or vice versa); the algorithm lives in one function with exhaustive table tests, and server/discover never depends on state.

HTTP 404 has opposite meanings across eras (modern 'method not found' vs legacy 'session terminated'); the status policy is era-gated and tested so a legacy client can never receive 404 for a JSON-RPC error.

Every 4xx returned to a modern request must carry the JSON-RPC error body, otherwise dual-era clients fall back to initialize (streamable-http.mdx 'Backward Compatibility'); enforced by the processor always producing a body and by HTTP tests.

Indy behaviour assumptions (default HTML body on empty responses, no chunked encoding for IOHandler writes, one thread per connection, Bindings default) are documented as 'verify on Windows' and each has a fallback in the step text.
Long-lived SSE streams pin Indy worker threads; MaxConnections and Stop() draining must be tuned before advertising subscriptions.

Security defaults (Origin always validated, loopback bind, TLS 1.2+) change runtime behaviour for a minority of deployments; each has a one-line opt-out and a CHANGELOG entry, and the alternative (violating a spec MUST) is worse.

Error-path wire changes on the legacy side (-32602 unknown tool, -32002 resource not found) are spec-required but could break consumer integration tests that assert the old text results; called out with before/after JSON.
Thread-safety of consumer tools/resources becomes visible on stdio once MaxConcurrentRequests > 1; default 1 and documentation limit the blast radius.

Client ecosystem for 2026-07-28 is still forming (Tier 1 SDKs speak it; end-user clients such as Claude Code/Codex are not documented as doing so), so most production traffic will stay legacy for the deprecation window - the legacy path is therefore treated as the primary product and guarded first.
requestState HMAC keys generated per process break MRTR across restarts or load-balanced instances; a configured key is documented as mandatory for those deployments.

Scope creep: prompts/completion/templates/subscriptions/auth are MAY features; phases 5-7 are independently droppable without harming conformance of the earlier phases (a server that does not advertise a capability is conformant).
openDecisions: 2025-03-26 support level. Default: keep answering '2025-06-18' to 2025-03-26 initialize requests (status quo, allowed by lifecycle.mdx 'MUST respond with another protocol version it supports'), reject array bodies with -32600, and ship full 2025-03-26 (echo + batch receive) only behind [Protocol] LegacyBatch2025_03_26=1 (Phase 4). Revisit if a real 2025-03-26 batching client appears.

supportedVersions / error.data.supported content. Default: modern versions only (['2026-07-28']); legacy revisions are reachable only through initialize, and listing them could make a modern client retry with a legacy version in _meta and loop on -32022. Offer [Protocol] DiscoverListsLegacyVersions=1 for operators who prefer the versioning.mdx example shape.

Legacy HTTP sessions. Default: stateless in both eras (never mint Mcp-Session-Id; echo an incoming one only for legacy requests); this removes the FSessionID race and all 400/404 session obligations. Alternative (per-session store in the transport) only if per-session legacy state is ever needed.

Default bind address. Default: derive from [Server] Host (localhost -> 127.0.0.1 and ::1), explicit BindAddress=0.0.0.0 for remote/container deployments with a startup warning. Alternative: keep 0.0.0.0 to avoid any behaviour change, accepting a spec SHOULD violation.

[CORS] AllowedOrigins=* semantics. Default: '*' remains an explicit allow-all opt-out (with a warning) so existing configs keep working; [Security] AllowedOrigins becomes the canonical key and defaults to the CORS list plus loopback-any-port patterns.

Strict required-parameter validation (TMCPSerializer.StrictRequired). Default: off in 1.x (no behaviour change for consumer tools), announced as on in 2.0; the schema already advertises 'required', so flipping early is defensible if the owner prefers correctness over compatibility.
Modern ping. Default: LenientModernPing=0 (ping is removed in 2026-07-28 -> -32601/404); set to 1 for transitional clients.
Stdio concurrency. Default: MaxConcurrentRequests=1 (sequential dispatch order preserved; reader thread still observes cancel/ping); raise per deployment once tools are known to be thread-safe.

Scope of optional features. Default: implement prompts, completion, resource templates (Phase 5) and a minimal subscriptions/listen (Phase 6) because the required conformance scenario sets exercise them; each can be dropped without breaking earlier phases.

subscriptions/listen depth. Default: minimal conformant implementation (ack agreed subset, keep-alives, graceful close, cancel); listChanged/subscribe stay false until dynamic registration exists. Alternative: leave -32601/404 (also conformant) if Phase 6 is trimmed.

Authorization in core. Default: pluggable IMCPAuthorizer + static bearer + abstract OAuth resource-server base with introspection; JWT verification as a sample only; no authorization-server role. Alternative: ship only the hook and documentation.

Built-in logs://recent and server://status resources. Default: keep registered (compat) but declare them ttlMs 0/private, add [Server] ExposeLogsResource to disable, and remove the access-log side effect from logs://recent.

Era-only emission of resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope/_meta.serverInfo. Default: modern-era only (keeps legacy responses byte-identical and goldens simple). Alternative: always emit (schema-tolerated in legacy revisions) for a simpler code path.
requestState key persistence. Default: [Security] RequestStateKey (base64) with a per-process random fallback that logs a warning; document as required for multi-instance or restart-resilient MRTR.

CI strategy. Default: manual release checklist executed via the committed PowerShell scripts on a Windows machine; add a self-hosted Windows runner (build.bat + DUnitX + conformance + Inspector smoke) when available. Decide whether Linux64 builds via PAServer are part of the release gate.

Naming of the new virtual for tool authors (ExecuteWithContext) and whether TMCPToolBase<T,R> also gets a context-aware variant returning R. Default: add ExecuteWithContext to all three bases returning TMCPToolResult/TValue, leave ExecuteWithParams untouched.
outOfScope: Acting as an OAuth authorization server (authorize/token/register endpoints), Dynamic Client Registration, CIMD, DPoP, consent pages for confused-deputy proxies: authorization/index.mdx scopes the MCP server to the resource-server role and 2025-03-26's server-hosted AS model is superseded; documented as unsupported (2025-03-26 clients served unauthenticated only).

Tasks extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks: tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel, durable task store, background execution): extensions are 'always disabled by default', tasks-* scenarios are not scored, and a server that never returns CreateTaskResult is fully compliant (SEP-2663 'Backward Compatibility'); GAP-TSK-01 deferred to a later major.

Deprecated features: logging capability / logging/setLevel / notifications/message emission, roots/list and sampling/createMessage usage (server side), HTTP+SSE 2024-11-05 transport: all 'SHOULD NOT adopt' under the feature lifecycle (server/utilities/logging.mdx warning, client/roots.mdx, client/sampling.mdx, streamable-http.mdx HTTP+SSE warning); only the logLevel validation, a deprecation warning on negotiated roots/sampling, and deprecated-marked MRTR builders are provided. GAP-RS-01 (roots/sampling, MRTR area) is documentation only.

x-mcp-header schema attribute and Mcp-Param-* header validation (GAP-HTTP-12, GAP-TL-18): a MAY feature that only becomes a MUST once a tool declares it; no built-in tool needs it; unrecognised Mcp-Param-* headers are already ignored as the spec requires. Can be added later on top of the 'integer' schema fix and MCPServer.HttpHeaders without breaking anything.

SSE resumability / Last-Event-ID / SSE event ids: removed in 2026-07-28 (changelog major change 9) and optional in legacy; never implemented (no replay buffer), so they are deleted rather than completed.

Legacy server-initiated requests over SSE (legacy in-stream elicitation/sampling/roots): would require per-session request/response correlation across HTTP requests and blocks Indy threads; SEP-2322 replaced it. Legacy clients get an isError explanation when a tool needs elicitation.

A full JSON Schema 2020-12 validator (composition/conditional keywords, external $ref, format registry): only the subset the RTTI generator can emit is validated; the spec forbids network $ref dereferencing anyway.
OpenTelemetry trace-context propagation (traceparent/tracestate/baggage in _meta): reserved keys are passed through untouched; no exporter is added.

Per-session legacy state (initialized flag, session-scoped log level, session expiry/404 handling): the dual-era design is stateless in both eras; nothing in the current server relies on session state.
Windows service/daemon packaging, Docker images, code signing and installer work: unrelated to protocol conformance.

plans.lens: ARCHITECTURE-FIRST: introduce one transport-agnostic request pipeline (parse → validate envelope → build per-request protocol context/era → header validation → dispatch → result decoration → error/status mapping → transport framing) and a per-request context object (era, protocolVersion, clientCapabilities, clientInfo, logLevel, progressToken, inputResponses/requestState, cancellation, notification sink) BEFORE adding any 2026-07-28 feature, so every feature (discover, resultType, caching hints, MRTR, streaming, prompts) is written once and served correctly to both eras on both transports (Indy HTTP and stdio), while IMCPCapabilityManager / IMCPTool / IMCPResource / TMCPRegistry / TMCPIdHTTPServer / TMCPStdioTransport keep their existing signatures for library consumers.
plans.summary: Today TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest (src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas:146-224) extracts only id/method/params, never reads params._meta, dispatches by name, wraps whatever the manager returns, and maps every exception by substring ('not found' → -32601 else -32603) inside an HTTP 200 (IdHTTPServer.pas:509,553); the legacy initialize always answers '2025-06-18' (CoreManager.pas:101) with non-schema capability keys and a body 'sessionId' scraped by the transport (IdHTTPServer.pas:533-547). The plan makes the processor the single spec-enforcing spine: (1) a request context with per-request era detection (initialize ⇒ legacy; params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] ⇒ modern; otherwise legacy, with MCP-Protocol-Version header disambiguation on HTTP), (2) a typed EMCPError model carrying JSON-RPC code, optional data and HTTP status so -32020/-32021/-32022/-32602(_meta)→400 and -32601→404 apply only in the modern era while legacy keeps 200, (3) central result decoration (resultType, _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo, safety-net ttlMs/cacheScope on the six cacheable methods) gated on Era=modern so legacy responses stay byte-identical, (4) server/discover + a capability builder derived from registered managers, shared with initialize. Then, in order of value/risk: HTTP transport conformance (standard headers with Base64 sentinel decoding, Origin-always, 127.0.0.1 binding, GET/DELETE 405, no sessions), tools/resources data-model fixes for both eras (content required, -32602 unknown tool, ttlMs/cacheScope, integer schemas, strict validation, deterministic order, cursors, blobs), prompts/templates/completion (needed for the conformance suites), a streaming layer (Indy IOHandler SSE writer + stdio reader/worker/serialized-writer + in-flight registry) that enables cancellation and progress, MRTR/elicitation with an HMAC requestState codec, optional subscriptions/listen, and finally an authorization hook, RFC 9728 metadata, conformance/Inspector tooling and docs. All public APIs stay source-compatible; the few behaviour changes (unknown tool → JSON-RPC error, resource not found → JSON-RPC error, required params enforced, loopback binding, GET → 405) are spec-required and get explicit mitigations. Total ≈ 42 senior-Delphi days over 8 phases; the first two phases (≈10 days) make the server a conformant dual-era server for the core methods.
plans.compatStrategy: ERA DETECTION (one function, TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.BuildContext, used by both transports): (1) method = 'initialize' ⇒ Era=peLegacy regardless of _meta (versioning.mdx §Compatibility Matrix: 'An initialize request selects legacy semantics'); negotiate params.protocolVersion: if it is in MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS echo it, else answer MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2025-11-25' (2025-11-25 lifecycle.mdx §Version Negotiation: 'If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports'). (2) else if params._meta is an object with a string 'io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion' ⇒ Era=peModern: on HTTP first check hints — missing MCP-Protocol-Version header or header ≠ _meta value ⇒ EMCPError.HeaderMismatch (-32020, HTTP 400; streamable-http.mdx §Protocol Version Header); then value ∉ MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS ⇒ EMCPError.UnsupportedProtocolVersion (-32022, data {supported, requested}, HTTP 400; versioning.mdx §Protocol Version Negotiation, schema.ts UnsupportedProtocolVersionError); 'io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities' absent/not object ⇒ EMCPError.InvalidParams (-32602, HTTP 400; basic/index.mdx §_meta 'A request missing any required field is malformed'); logLevel present but ∉ MCP_LOG_LEVELS ⇒ -32602 (logging.mdx §Error Handling); method ∈ MCP_LEGACY_ONLY_METHODS (ping, logging/setLevel, resources/subscribe, resources/unsubscribe, roots/list) ⇒ EMCPError.MethodNotFound (-32601, HTTP 404; changelog 2026-07-28 major change 5, streamable-http.mdx 'If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with 404'). (3) else ⇒ Era=peLegacy: on HTTP, if the MCP-Protocol-Version header names a modern version the body lacks required _meta ⇒ -32602/400; if the header is non-empty and in neither list ⇒ -32600/400 (2025-06-18 transports.mdx §Protocol Version Header: 'invalid or unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version … MUST respond with 400'); LegacyVersion := header value if legacy, else TMCPTransportSession.NegotiatedLegacyVersion (stdio process scope, set by initialize), else '2025-03-26' (2025-06-18 transports.mdx: absent header ⇒ 'SHOULD assume protocol version 2025-03-26'). stdio uses the same function with empty header hints (stdio.mdx §Request Metadata: 'There is no header layer'). COEXISTENCE: both eras are served concurrently on the same endpoint/process ('A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently'); era is a per-request property, never a process latch, so server/discover keeps returning DiscoverResult after an initialize (clients cache the era per process, versioning.mdx). Legacy stays byte-identical to today except spec-required fixes: negotiated version echo, removal of the non-schema 'sessionId'/'supportsProgress'/'supportsCancellation' members (legacy schemas leave capability objects open), JSON-RPC errors for unknown tool/resource. Modern-only behaviour (resultType, _meta.serverInfo, ttlMs/cacheScope, HTTP 400/404 mapping, header validation, MRTR) is gated on Era=peModern. Legacy sessions: stateless by default (Mcp-Session-Id is a MAY in 2025-06-18/11-25; never minted, echoed only for legacy requests, ignored for modern per streamable-http.mdx §Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions). 2025-03-26 clients: initialize echoes 2025-03-26 and JSON-RPC batch arrays are accepted for legacy requests whose LegacyVersion='2025-03-26' (2025-03-26 basic/index.mdx §Batching MUST receive); arrays are -32600 otherwise (400 in modern era). LIBRARY CONSUMERS: no existing interface gains members (Delphi interfaces cannot be extended without breaking implementers); new capabilities are exposed through new GUID'd interfaces discovered with Supports() (IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPResourceTemplate), new protected virtuals with default implementations on TMCPToolBase<T>/<T,R>/TMCPResourceBase<T>, additive class methods on TMCPRegistry, constructor overloads (TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.Create(Registry, Settings)), and an ambient threadvar-backed TMCPRequestContext.Current for code that cannot change signatures. The old ProcessRequest(Body, SessionID): string remains and delegates to ProcessRequestEx with stdio-style hints, so custom transports written against it keep compiling and now get dual-era behaviour for free (minus HTTP status mapping). Custom managers that return TJSONObject automatically receive resultType/_meta.serverInfo/ttlMs/cacheScope injection in the modern era; managers that set those keys themselves are left untouched.

architecture.change: Extend MCPServer.Types (additive): MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2026-07-28'; MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS=['2026-07-28']; MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS=['2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26']; MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2025-11-25'; MCP_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (modern first); MCP_META_PROTOCOL_VERSION/CLIENT_CAPABILITIES/CLIENT_INFO/LOG_LEVEL/SERVER_INFO/SUBSCRIPTION_ID/PROGRESS_TOKEN key constants; MCP_LOG_LEVELS (debug…emergency per schema.ts LoggingLevel); MCP_CACHEABLE_METHODS (server/discover, tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read per caching.mdx §Cacheable Results); MCP_LEGACY_ONLY_METHODS; TMCPProtocolEra=(peLegacy, peModern); TMCPTransportKind=(tkStdio, tkHttp); all JSON-RPC codes moved here (JSONRPC_PARSE_ERROR…JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR) plus MCP_ERROR_HEADER_MISMATCH=-32020, MCP_ERROR_MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY=-32021, MCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION=-32022, MCP_ERROR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_LEGACY=-32002 (legacy era only); new interfaces IMCPCapabilityManagerEx (ExecuteMethodEx(Method, Params, Context)), IMCPCapabilityProvider (GetCapabilityJSON: TJSONObject), IMCPManagerEnumerator (GetManagers). MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays ('2025-06-18', marked deprecated in a comment). The duplicate JSONRPC_* blocks in JsonRpcProcessor.pas:27-32 and IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99 become aliases/are deleted.
architecture.rationale: One authoritative home for versions, reserved _meta keys and error codes; BP-07 forbids emitting undefined codes in -32020..-32099 and -32002 in the modern era, so codes must be typed constants, not strings matched by Pos().

architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.Errors: EMCPError = class(Exception) with Code: Integer, Data: TJSONValue (owned, cloned into error.data), HttpStatus: Integer (0 = let the era policy decide) and factories MethodNotFound(Method), InvalidRequest(Msg), InvalidParams(Msg, Data=nil, HttpStatus=0), Internal(Msg), UnsupportedProtocolVersion(Requested, Supported: TArray<string>) → data {supported:[…], requested} HttpStatus 400, MissingRequiredClientCapability(Required: TJSONObject) → data {requiredCapabilities} HttpStatus 400, HeaderMismatch(Msg) HttpStatus 400, ResourceNotFound(Uri, Era) → code -32602 (modern) or -32002 (legacy) with data {uri}. EMCPToolError = class(Exception) (tool-level failure ⇒ isError result). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor catches EMCPError first (code/data/status verbatim), then EMCPToolError only inside tools manager, then generic Exception ⇒ -32603 (the 'not found' substring heuristic is removed; ExecuteMethodCall raises EMCPError.MethodNotFound).
architecture.rationale: Closes the string-based mapping at JsonRpcProcessor.pas:211-215 that turns 'Tool not found'/'SSL Certificate file not found' into -32601 (which becomes HTTP 404 in the modern era and would flip probing clients into legacy mode) and provides the only way to emit error.data for -32021/-32022 and resource-not-found.

architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.RequestContext: TMCPRequestId record (Kind: ridAbsent|ridNull|ridString|ridNumber|ridInvalid; AsJSON) replacing the TValue-based ExtractRequestID; TMCPTransportHints record (Transport: TMCPTransportKind; HasHeaders; HeaderProtocolVersion, HeaderMethod, HeaderName: string; ParamHeaders: TStrings (Mcp-Param-*); Session: TMCPTransportSession); TMCPTransportSession = class (NegotiatedLegacyVersion: string guarded by TMonitor; one per stdio process, nil for HTTP); IMCPMessageSink (SendNotification(const Json: TJSONObject) taking ownership; IsCancelled; Streaming) implemented per transport; IMCPRequestContext/TMCPRequestContext (Era, ProtocolVersion, LegacyVersion, Method, RequestId, ClientCapabilities/ClientInfo: TJSONObject (owned clones, nil for legacy pre-initialize), LogLevel, ProgressToken: TJSONValue clone, InputResponses: TJSONObject, RequestState: string, Transport, Sink; HasClientCapability(const Path: string) e.g. 'elicitation.form'; RequireClientCapability(const Path; RequiredJson) raising EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability; ReportProgress(Progress, Total=-1, Msg='') honouring monotonicity and a MinProgressIntervalMs throttle; IsCancelled/CheckCancelled raising EMCPRequestCancelled); class property TMCPRequestContext.Current backed by a threadvar that the processor sets around dispatch and nils in finally (threadvar interface refs are not finalised automatically). TMCPInflightRegistry (TDictionary<string,IMCPRequestContext> keyed by RequestId JSON text, TMonitor-guarded) for notifications/cancelled.
architecture.rationale: BP-10/BP-11/BP-13/BP-17 require every request to carry and be judged by its own metadata; managers and tools need Era/ClientCapabilities/logLevel without changing IMCPCapabilityManager.ExecuteMethod(Method, Params) (Types.pas:39-44) or IMCPTool.Execute(Arguments) (Tool.Base.pas:18). Indy runs one thread per connection and the new stdio worker pool runs one request per task, so a threadvar is a safe ambient carrier.

architecture.change: Keep class name and Create(ManagerRegistry); add Create(ManagerRegistry; Settings: TMCPSettings) overload and properties ServerIdentity, EmitServerInfo. New function ProcessRequestEx(const Body: string; const Hints: TMCPTransportHints; const Sink: IMCPMessageSink = nil): TMCPProcessResult (record: Kind = prkNone|prkResponse|prkBatch; Body: string; HttpStatus: Integer; ErrorCode: Integer; Era: TMCPProtocolEra; RequestId: TMCPRequestId; StreamHandle: TObject for phase 7).
