Old ProcessRequest(Body, SessionID): string delegates with stdio-style hints and returns .Body. Stages: (1) Parse (-32700; TJSONArray ⇒ batch only when Era/LegacyVersion='2025-03-26', else -32600); (2) ValidateEnvelope: jsonrpc must be '2.0', method a non-empty string, id absent (notification) | string | integer, else -32600 with id null; params present but not object ⇒ -32602; a body with result/error and no method is a client-sent response ⇒ ignore (legacy: no output ⇒ 202; modern: -32600); (3) BuildContext = era detection described in compatStrategy; (4) HeaderValidation (HTTP hints, modern era only; delegated to MCPServer.HttpHeaders); (5) Dispatch: notifications ⇒ manager.ExecuteMethod inside try/except (log, never respond), 'notifications/cancelled' ⇒ TMCPInflightRegistry.Cancel(params.requestId) with reason logged (cancellation.mdx §Implementation Notes); requests ⇒ Supports(Manager, IMCPCapabilityManagerEx) ? ExecuteMethodEx(Method, Params, Ctx) : ExecuteMethod(Method, Params), with TMCPRequestContext.Current set; (6) Decorate: TValue.Empty ⇒ {} ; string ⇒ parsed object or {value} with a warning; modern era only: AddPair('resultType','complete') if absent, _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'] if absent and EmitServerInfo, and for Method ∈ MCP_CACHEABLE_METHODS with resultType='complete' default ttlMs:0 / cacheScope:'private' when absent; legacy era: untouched; (7) MapErrors/Status: EMCPError.HttpStatus if set, else policy: modern {-32601→404, -32020/-32021/-32022/-32700/-32600→400, rest→200}; legacy {all 200 except the header rules}; stdio ignores HttpStatus; (8) Frame: compact TJSONObject.ToJSON (single line, no embedded newlines for stdio.mdx).
architecture.rationale: Every feature is added once at the stage where it belongs; both transports call the same function; the status policy lives next to the era decision so legacy clients never receive a 404 (which 2025-11-25 transports.mdx §Session Management defines as 'session terminated').

architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.Capabilities: TMCPServerIdentity (Name, Version, Title, Description, WebsiteUrl, Instructions from TMCPSettings) with ToJSON; TMCPCapabilityBuilder.Build(Managers: TArray<IMCPCapabilityManager>; Era): TJSONObject — for each manager: Supports(IMCPCapabilityProvider) ? its JSON : name-based default ('tools'→{listChanged:false}, 'resources'→{subscribe:false,listChanged:false}, 'prompts'→{listChanged:false}, 'completions'→{}, 'core'→skip); 'extensions' map emitted only when non-empty and Era=modern; never 'logging'. TMCPManagerRegistry implements IMCPManagerEnumerator. TMCPCoreManager: add 'server/discover' (modern-only; returns {supportedVersions: MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, capabilities, instructions?, ttlMs: Settings.DiscoverTtlMs (default 3600000), cacheScope:'public'} — resultType/_meta.serverInfo come from decoration), implements IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, gets a ManagerRegistry property (assigned by TMCPIdHTTPServer.Start / TMCPStdioTransport.Create from their existing FCoreManager/FManagerRegistry fields, or by the consumer), Initialize negotiates protocolVersion, emits schema-valid capabilities, drops sessionId/FSessionID write (SessionID property kept, returns ''), logs a SEP-2577 warning when client capabilities contain roots/sampling; when Settings.LegacyEnabled=False initialize answers -32601 whose message lists supported versions (versioning.mdx 'SHOULD name the protocol versions it supports in any error it returns to an initialize request').
architecture.rationale: discover.mdx 'Servers MUST implement it'; tools.mdx/resources.mdx/prompts.mdx 'Servers that support X MUST declare the X capability' — deriving capabilities from registered managers keeps a consumer who registers only TMCPToolsManager honest and lets a PromptsManager advertise itself without editing CoreManager.

architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.HttpHeaders (pure functions, unit-testable): DecodeMcpHeaderValue(Raw; out Value; out Err): Trim; if it starts with '=?base64?' and ends with '?=' (case-sensitive) strictly validate alphabet/padding/length mod 4 before TNetEncoding.Base64.DecodeStringToBytes + TEncoding.UTF8.GetString (System.NetEncoding is lenient, SEP-2243 requires 400 on bad padding); else require chars 0x20-0x7E/0x09. ValidateStandardHeaders(Hints, Method, Params, Bindings): Mcp-Method missing or ≠ method (case-sensitive value, case-insensitive name via Indy RawHeaders.Values) ⇒ HeaderMismatch; for tools/call & prompts/get compare decoded Mcp-Name with params.name, for resources/read with params.uri; for each IMCPHeaderBindingSource binding (tool inputSchema properties carrying x-mcp-header): body value present & non-null ⇒ header required and must match (numeric compare for integers, 'true'/'false' for booleans), body value absent/null ⇒ header ignored, invalid characters ⇒ reject. Applied only when Era=peModern and the message is a request (streamable-http.mdx Note: header requirements for notification POSTs are undefined). TMCPToolsManager implements IMCPHeaderBindingSource with a TMonitor-guarded cache per tool name.
architecture.rationale: streamable-http.mdx §Standard Request Headers ('REQUIRED for compliance'), §Server Validation ('MUST return HTTP status 400 Bad Request and MUST include a JSON-RPC error response using … -32020'), §Value Encoding ('servers MUST decode an encoded Mcp-Name or Mcp-Param-{Name} value before comparing').

architecture.change: TMCPIdHTTPServer request order: ValidateOrigin (always, independent of CorsEnabled; scheme+host match with optional ':*' port wildcard, loopback defaults, absent Origin allowed, 403 + id-less JSON-RPC -32600 body, Vary: Origin) → Authorizer (phase 8) → path (404) → OPTIONS (reflect Access-Control-Request-Headers, static list adds Authorization, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name; Expose-Headers Mcp-Session-Id, WWW-Authenticate; ContentLength 0) → GET/DELETE ⇒ 405 with Allow: POST, OPTIONS (permitted by 2025-11-25 transports.mdx §Listening item 3 and required for modern-only traffic) → POST: read UTF-8 body, fill TMCPTransportHints from RawHeaders, create TMCPHttpMessageSink(Context, ResponseInfo), call ProcessRequestEx; Kind=prkNone ⇒ 202 with ContentLength 0 and an empty TMemoryStream as ContentStream (avoids Indy's default HTML body); otherwise ResponseNo := HttpStatus and either application/json body or, if the sink already switched to SSE, the final response as the last 'event: message / data:' event. Mcp-Session-Id: never minted; echoed only for Era=legacy; ignored for modern. Bindings: explicit Bindings.Add with IP := Settings.BindAddress (default '127.0.0.1', '::1' added when IPv6 wanted, '0.0.0.0'/'*' = all with a logged warning). SSE event ids and FEventIDCounter removed. TLS: OpenSSL-1.0.2 branch limited to TLS 1.2+, USE_TAURUS_TLS define moved to src/MCPServer.inc. New unit MCPServer.SseWriter (TMCPHttpMessageSink): on first SendNotification sets ContentType text/event-stream, CharSet utf-8, Cache-Control no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering no, ContentLength -1, CloseConnection True, calls ResponseInfo.WriteHeader and writes events through Context.Connection.IOHandler.Write(..., IndyTextEncoding_UTF8); WriteComment(':keep-alive') doubles as a disconnect probe (IOHandler.CheckForDisconnect(False) + Connected), EIdConnClosedGracefully/EIdSocketError mark the context cancelled (modern era only; legacy: 'Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling'). FOpenStreams: TThreadList for Stop() to drain/close before FHTTPServer.Active := False.
architecture.rationale: Closes Origin (streamable-http.mdx §Security & Endpoint MUST 403), binding (SHOULD 127.0.0.1), session (changelog major change 1), 202-no-body (§Sending Messages item 5), streaming (§Receiving Messages) and cancellation (§Cancellation MUST treat disconnect as cancellation) requirements while keeping TMCPIdHTTPServer's public surface (Port, Active, ManagerRegistry, CoreManager, Settings, Start, Stop) intact.

architecture.change: TMCPStdioTransport keeps Create(ManagerRegistry, CoreManager)/Run and adds Stop, MaxConcurrentRequests (default 4; 1 = sequential worker; 0 = execute inline on the reader thread, today's behaviour), InputStream/OutputStream properties (default stdin/stdout handles) for tests. Run: byte-level UTF-8 I/O over THandleStream (manual line split on #10, strip trailing #13; write TEncoding.UTF8.GetBytes(Json+#10) — no TStreamWriter BOM) replacing Text I/O whose code page is the ANSI ACP on Windows; sets TLogger.UseStdErr := True and TLogger.StdoutReserved := True; reader loop parses each line, notifications are processed synchronously (fast path so notifications/cancelled reaches TMCPInflightRegistry while a tool runs), requests are queued to a bounded TThreadPool/TTask worker whose completion writes through TMCPStdioMessageSink (one TCriticalSection around write+flush, exactly one message per call); a TMCPTransportSession holds NegotiatedLegacyVersion; on EOF/Stop: stop accepting, drain in-flight work with a bounded wait (2 s), send graceful completion for open subscriptions (phase 7), close stdout, return. The outer except block no longer writes id:null errors to stdout (stdio.mdx 'MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message'); a write failure on stdout terminates the loop. MCPServer.dpr: in stdio mode do not install SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers (or close fd 0 from the handler so Eof returns True) and set ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown only for DEBUG non-stdio builds.
architecture.rationale: stdio.mdx: 'JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded', 'Servers SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed', modern cancellation needs the reader to keep reading while work runs, and the 'process is not a session' rule (basic/index.mdx §Statelessness) means interleaved requests must be servable.

architecture.change: TMCPToolsManager implements IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPHeaderBindingSource; unknown tool ⇒ EMCPError.InvalidParams('Unknown tool: X') (tools.mdx §Error Handling example -32602); malformed name/arguments ⇒ -32602; absent arguments ⇒ empty TJSONObject (CallToolRequestParams.arguments is optional; today nil reaches TMCPSerializer.DeserializeObject 'for Pair in Json' at Serializer.pas:111); properties ListTtlMs (default 0), ListCacheScope (default 'private'; sample dpr sets public/300000), PageSize (0 = single page; cursor = base64url('v1:'+offset), invalid ⇒ -32602); tools kept in a TList in registration order (TMCPRegistry gains ordered name lists) for deterministic tools/list; BuildToolCallResponse handles TMCPToolResult first, then TJSONArray/string/TJSONObject (adds the required 'content' text fallback with compact JSON when only structuredContent exists), any other TValue ⇒ text; EMCPToolError ⇒ isError; 'Error:' prefix heuristic retained behind LegacyErrorPrefixDetection=True. New unit MCPServer.Tool.Result: TMCPToolResult (AddText/AddImage/AddAudio/AddResourceLink/AddEmbeddedText/AddEmbeddedBlob/SetStructuredContent(Value, AddTextFallback=True)/IsError/Meta; base64 via TBase64Encoding.Create(0) so no line breaks; ToJSON(Era) drops non-object structuredContent for legacy). TMCPToolBase<T> gains 'function ExecuteWithContext(const Params: T; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TMCPToolResult; virtual' whose default wraps ExecuteWithParams; TMCPToolBase<T,R> likewise; all three bases implement IMCPToolMetadata (annotations record with tri-state hints, icons, _meta) via protected fields. Schema generator: Integer/Int64 ⇒ 'integer', Boolean detected by TypeInfo, nested classes/arrays/sets/records recursed with cycle guard, TDateTime ⇒ string/date-time, new attributes SchemaTitle/SchemaFormat/SchemaMinimum/SchemaMaximum/SchemaMinLength/SchemaMaxLength/SchemaPattern/SchemaDefault/SchemaName/SchemaHeader (emits x-mcp-header, validated: non-empty tchar, no CR/LF, case-insensitive unique, string/integer/boolean only, root properties chain only, raises at registration), empty param class ⇒ {type:object, additionalProperties:false}. Serializer: required (non-[Optional]) properties enforced and type mismatches rejected with actionable EArgumentException (TMCPSerializer.StrictMode=True escape hatch), dynamic arrays/TList/enums/sets/nil objects serialised consistently with the generated outputSchema. New MCPServer.Schema.Validator (2020-12 subset: type, required, enum, properties, items, additionalProperties, min/max, minLength/maxLength, pattern, const; local $ref only, depth cap) used for hand-built TMCPToolBase schemas and elicitation responses.
architecture.rationale: schema.json 2026-07-28 requires ListToolsResult [cacheScope, resultType, tools, ttlMs] and CallToolResult [content, resultType]; tools.mdx 'Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs'; x-mcp-header forbids type 'number'; the current 'Error: Tool not found' isError result violates the protocol-error rule in both eras.

architecture.change: TMCPResourcesManager implements IMCPCapabilityManagerEx/IMCPCapabilityProvider; ReadResource: nil params / non-string uri ⇒ -32602; unknown uri ⇒ EMCPError.ResourceNotFound(uri, Era) (-32602 modern with data.uri per resources.mdx §Error Handling; -32002 legacy per 2025-11-25 resources.mdx §Error Handling); read exception ⇒ -32603 (no more 'Error reading resource' text); contents from IMCPResourceReader (TArray<TMCPResourceContents> with Text or Blob) when supported, else Resource.Read as one text item; ttlMs/cacheScope from IMCPCacheableResource (defaults 0/'private'; built-ins: project://info & project://readme 3600000/'public', logs://recent & server://status 0/'private'); lists ordered by registration, ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope/PageSize as for tools; optional descriptor fields (title, size, icons, annotations, _meta) via IMCPResourceMetadata emitted only when set, empty description/mimeType omitted. Resource templates: IMCPResourceTemplate (GetUriTemplate/Matches/CreateResource; RFC 6570 level-1/2 matcher compiled to TRegEx) + TMCPRegistry.RegisterResourceTemplate; ReadResource falls back to the first matching template. IMCPResource is not modified; TMCPResourceBase<T> gains protected FTtlMs/FCacheScope/FTitle/FSize/FIcons/FAnnotations/FMeta and implements the new interfaces. MCPServer.Uri helper validates RFC3986 scheme syntax at registration and read.
architecture.rationale: resources.mdx: 'If the requested resource does not exist, servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602', 'MUST NOT return an empty contents array', 'Binary data MUST be properly encoded', 'Servers MUST validate all resource URIs'; caching.mdx MUST on resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read.

architecture.change: New src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.Base.pas: TMCPPromptArgument record; TMCPPromptMessages builder (AddText/AddImage/AddAudio/AddResourceLink/AddEmbeddedResource with role user|assistant, content shapes from schema.ts ContentBlock); IMCPPrompt; TMCPPromptBase and generic TMCPPromptBase<T: class, constructor> mirroring TMCPToolBase<T> (arguments from T's string properties, [Optional]/[SchemaDescription] reused, missing required ⇒ -32602, unknown argument ⇒ -32602). TMCPRegistry.RegisterPrompt/CreatePrompt/GetPromptNames/HasPrompt. New src/Managers/MCPServer.PromptsManager.pas ('prompts/list' with ttlMs/cacheScope/pagination; 'prompts/get' → {description?, messages} — no ttlMs/cacheScope because GetPromptResult is not CacheableResult; unknown prompt ⇒ -32602 with data {name}; EMCPInputRequired handled as for tools). New src/Managers/MCPServer.CompletionManager.pas ('completion/complete': ref/prompt by name, ref/resource by template uriTemplate or exact uri; argument {name,value}; optional context.arguments; IMCPCompletable on prompts/templates; ≤100 values, hasMore/total; capability {completions:{}} via IMCPCapabilityProvider). Sample prompt src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.SummarizeLogs.pas; dpr/dproj/build.bat get src\Prompts; README gains 'Creating Custom Prompts'.
architecture.rationale: prompts.mdx 'Servers that support prompts MUST declare the prompts capability'; prompts/get is one of the three MRTR-capable methods; both frozen conformance requirement sets (2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28) contain prompts-* and completion-complete scenarios, so 100% needs them.

architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.Mrtr: TMCPInputRequests (AddElicitationForm(Key, Message, RequestedSchema)/AddElicitationUrl(Key, Message, Url)/AddSampling/AddRoots (the last two marked deprecated 'SEP-2577'), key uniqueness enforced); TMCPInputRequiredResult (InputRequests, RequestState; ToJSON raises if both empty per mrtr.mdx server requirement 6); EMCPInputRequired = class(Exception) carrying it; TMCPInputResponses accessor over params.inputResponses (TryGetElicit(Key, out Action, Content), TryGetSampling, TryGetRoots; malformed ⇒ -32602; unknown keys ignored); TMCPElicitation.Form/Url builders and TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder (flat primitive properties only: string/number/integer/boolean/enum/multi-select). New unit MCPServer.RequestState: TMCPRequestStateCodec.Seal(Payload, Ctx, Method, ArgsDigest, TtlSeconds): string = base64url(json{p,m,d,u,exp}) + '.' + base64url(HMAC-SHA256 via System.Hash.THashSHA2.GetHMACAsBytes) and Open(...) with constant-time compare, expiry, principal and request-digest checks; key from Settings.RequestStateKey (base64) else random per process with a logged warning. Managers (tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get only) catch EMCPInputRequired: Era=modern ⇒ for every inputRequests method check Ctx.HasClientCapability ('elicitation.form' or empty elicitation object for form, 'elicitation.url' for url, 'sampling', 'roots') else raise EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability(data.requiredCapabilities), then return {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests?, requestState?} (no ttlMs/cacheScope; decoration skips input_required); Era=legacy ⇒ tools: isError text asking for the input as arguments; resources/prompts: -32603. EMCPInputRequired reaching the processor from any other method ⇒ -32603 (mrtr.mdx 'MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult responses on any other client requests'). Tool authors: ExecuteWithContext(Params, Ctx) — read Ctx.InputResponses / Ctx.RequestState, raise EMCPInputRequired.
architecture.rationale: mrtr.mdx: servers MUST use MRTR for server-to-client requests, MUST treat requestState as attacker-controlled and protect its integrity, MUST NOT send inputRequests the client has not declared; legacy sessions must never see resultType 'input_required' (2025-06-18 lifecycle.mdx §Operation 'Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated').

architecture.change: New src/Managers/MCPServer.SubscriptionsManager.pas implementing 'subscriptions/listen' (modern only): validate params.notifications, compute the honoured subset (only types advertised by the capability builder; resourceSubscriptions only for existing URIs when resources.subscribe is true), register TMCPSubscription {Id: RequestId, Filter, Sink} in a TMonitor-guarded registry, push notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged with _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId'] as the first message, return a deferred marker so the transport keeps the stream open; transports loop (HTTP: keep-alive comments every 15-30 s, exit on disconnect; stdio: registry entry, notifications/cancelled referencing the listen id stops it); on Stop/EOF: HTTP writes the completion result {resultType:'complete', _meta:{subscriptionId}} then closes; stdio writes notifications/cancelled {requestId: listenId} then the completion result. TMCPRegistry.OnChanged event lets listChanged flip to true only when runtime registration exists.
architecture.rationale: subscriptions.mdx §Acknowledgment MUST-first ordering, §Graceful Closure, cancellation.mdx (server-sent notifications/cancelled only for listen teardown). Not advertising listChanged/subscribe keeps -32601 compliant, so this is a UX/optional phase.

architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.Authorization: TMCPAuthDecision, TMCPPrincipal (Subject, Scopes, Claims; raw token never stored), TMCPAuthChallenge, IMCPAuthorizer.Authorize(BearerToken, HttpMethod, Path, out Principal, out Challenge): TMCPAuthDecision; TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer (constant-time compare); abstract TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer (ExpectedAudience required, exp/aud checks enforced in the base, virtual ValidateToken for introspection/JWT supplied by the consumer). TMCPIdHTTPServer.Authorizer property (nil = open); applied after Origin, not to OPTIONS or the well-known path; token read only from the Authorization header; 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…"[, scope="…"], 403 with error="insufficient_scope"; GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/<endpoint>] serves RFC 9728 metadata {resource, authorization_servers (required non-empty), scopes_supported, bearer_methods_supported:['header'], resource_name}. [RequiresScope] attribute checked in TMCPToolsManager with a configured scope hierarchy. Principal exposed on IMCPRequestContext. Never wired into TMCPStdioTransport (basic/index.mdx §Auth: stdio 'SHOULD NOT follow this specification'). Settings [Auth] and [Security] sections; log redaction (bodies at Debug through TLogger.RedactJson blanking params._meta, requestState, inputResponses and token-like keys).
architecture.rationale: authorization/index.mdx: HTTP servers SHOULD implement auth; if they do, tokens MUST be validated for audience, 401/403/400 status rules and RFC 9728 metadata are MUST; SEC-07 recommends a token for locally-run HTTP servers. Kept pluggable so the core has no OAuth dependency.

architecture.change: TMCPSettings additive keys with defaults: [Server] BindAddress=127.0.0.1, Instructions, Title, Description, WebsiteUrl, DiscoverTtlMs=3600000, EmitServerInfo=1, ExposeLogsResource=1; [Protocol] LegacyEnabled=1, LenientModernPing=0, ToolsListTtlMs, ResourcesListTtlMs; [Security] AllowedOrigins (CORS list stays as alias), AllowedHosts, RequestStateKey, BearerTokens; [Auth] Enabled, Mode, ResourceUri, AuthorizationServers, ScopesSupported, RequiredScopes, ScopeHierarchy; [Stdio] MaxConcurrentRequests=4. build.bat reads DELPHI_PATH from env/rsvars and adds src\Prompts; MCPServer.dproj DCCReference list updated; tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX) + tests/golden/{legacy-2025-03-26,legacy-2025-06-18,legacy-2025-11-25,modern-2026-07-28}/*.json; scripts/run-conformance.ps1 and conformance-baseline.yml; README: badge 2026-07-28 dual-era, 'Protocol versions & dual-era behaviour', 'Security', 'Testing with MCP Inspector (protocolEra legacy|auto|modern)', 'Conformance testing', library extension points, stdio checklist (UseStdErr, UTF-8, LF framing), CHANGELOG with behaviour changes.
architecture.rationale: Operators need to switch eras/bindings/auth without code; the repo has no tests today, and the conformance CLI is the ecosystem's yardstick (docs/community/sdk-tiers.mdx §Conformance Testing).

phases.name: Phase 1 — Protocol spine: context, pipeline, errors, era detection, discover, decoration, status mapping
phases.goal: Make TMCPJsonRpcProcessor the single place where both eras are recognised and served correctly for the existing methods, with byte-identical legacy output and schema-valid modern output, on both transports, with a DUnitX harness in place.
steps: Add constants/types/interfaces to MCPServer.Types (versions, meta keys, log levels, cacheable/legacy-only method sets, TMCPProtocolEra, IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator, all error-code constants incl. -32020/-32021/-32022 and legacy -32002); keep MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION and JSONRPC_* aliases.

Create MCPServer.Errors (EMCPError with Code/Data/HttpStatus + factories, EMCPToolError) and MCPServer.RequestContext (TMCPRequestId, TMCPTransportHints, TMCPTransportSession, IMCPMessageSink, IMCPRequestContext/TMCPRequestContext with threadvar Current, TMCPInflightRegistry).

Rewrite TMCPJsonRpcProcessor internals into the eight pipeline stages; add ProcessRequestEx + TMCPProcessResult; old ProcessRequest delegates; envelope validation (-32600 for id:null/bool/object, missing jsonrpc/method; params not object ⇒ -32602; client-sent responses ignored/-32600 by era); batch arrays accepted only for LegacyVersion='2025-03-26' (per-element processing, array response, no body when all notifications), -32600 otherwise (400 in modern era).

Implement BuildContext exactly as in compatStrategy (initialize ⇒ legacy+negotiation; _meta ⇒ modern with header/version/clientCapabilities/logLevel checks and legacy-only method gating incl. optional LenientModernPing; else legacy with header disambiguation); store negotiated legacy version in TMCPTransportSession for stdio.

Dispatch stage: prefer IMCPCapabilityManagerEx via Supports(); set/clear TMCPRequestContext.Current; route notifications to HandlesMethod managers with exceptions swallowed (never respond); 'notifications/cancelled' ⇒ registry cancel + reason logged.

Decoration stage (modern era only): resultType:'complete' if absent; _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'] = {name, version[, title, description, websiteUrl]} if absent and EmitServerInfo; safety-net ttlMs:0/cacheScope:'private' for MCP_CACHEABLE_METHODS when absent and resultType='complete'; wrap TValue.Empty/string/other into an object (log warning for non-object manager results).

Error/status stage: EMCPError → code/message/data; HttpStatus override or era policy (modern: -32601→404; -32020/-32021/-32022/-32700/-32600→400; -32602 only when HttpStatus=400 was set by _meta validation; else 200; legacy: 200 except header-rule 400s).

MCPServer.Capabilities (TMCPServerIdentity, TMCPCapabilityBuilder); TMCPManagerRegistry implements IMCPManagerEnumerator; TMCPToolsManager/TMCPResourcesManager implement IMCPCapabilityProvider ({listChanged:false} / {subscribe:false,listChanged:false}) and IMCPCapabilityManagerEx (initially forwarding to ExecuteMethod).

TMCPCoreManager: server/discover (modern only, {supportedVersions:['2026-07-28'], capabilities, instructions?, ttlMs, cacheScope:'public'}); initialize negotiation per BP-21; schema-valid capabilities from the builder; remove sessionId member and FSessionID write (property keeps compiling, returns ''); LegacyEnabled=False ⇒ initialize -32601 naming supported versions; SEP-2577 warning for roots/sampling client capabilities; ManagerRegistry property wired from TMCPIdHTTPServer.Start and TMCPStdioTransport.Create.

Transports (minimal): TMCPIdHTTPServer builds TMCPTransportHints from RawHeaders (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param-*), passes them to ProcessRequestEx, sets ResponseNo := HttpStatus, stops scraping sessionId; TMCPStdioTransport passes its TMCPTransportSession; both keep JSON/SSE framing as today.

Thread-safety hygiene: AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement in TServerStatusResource; TMCPRegistry dictionaries created in a class constructor; delete GetNextEventID/FEventIDCounter (SSE ids removed in 2026-07-28 changelog major change 9, optional in legacy).

Settings: Instructions, ServerTitle/Description/WebsiteUrl, DiscoverTtlMs, EmitServerInfo, LegacyEnabled, LenientModernPing; Resource.Project reports the supported-versions list instead of 'MCP 2025-06-18'.
tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX): pipeline tests with a fake IMCPManagerRegistry and golden JSON fixtures per era (see testing).
deliverables: Passing headless matrix: legacy initialize for 2025-03-26/06-18/11-25/garbage/2026-07-28, legacy ping, modern discover, modern tools/list with resultType+serverInfo, -32602/400 missing clientCapabilities, -32022/400 unknown version, -32020/400 header mismatch, -32601 404 vs 200 by era, id:null ⇒ -32600, batch 2025-03-26
risks: Threadvar interface reference must be nil-ed in finally or it leaks per Indy thread.
Order of modern checks (header mismatch before unsupported version before missing clientCapabilities) must match the spec text or dual-era clients misdetect; lock it in with golden tests.
Legacy output must be diffed against a captured baseline of today's responses to prove byte-identity except the intended removals (sessionId, supportsProgress/Cancellation, negotiated version).

phases.name: Phase 2 — Streamable HTTP conformance (both eras) on Indy
phases.goal: Make the HTTP transport satisfy the MUSTs of streamable-http.mdx for modern requests and the 2025-11-25/2025-06-18 transport pages for legacy requests, without sessions and with hardened defaults.
steps: MCPServer.HttpHeaders: strict Base64 sentinel decoder, ValidateStandardHeaders (Mcp-Method for all requests, Mcp-Name for tools/call|prompts/get|resources/read), Mcp-Param-* validation against IMCPHeaderBindingSource; wired into pipeline stage 4 for Era=modern requests only; SEP-2243 edge tables as unit tests (lowercase header names accepted, 'TOOLS/CALL' rejected, surrounding whitespace trimmed, bad padding ⇒ 400/-32020).

Split VerifyAndSetCORSHeaders into ValidateOrigin (always; port-wildcard patterns; loopback defaults; 'null' denied; absent allowed; 403 + id-less JSON-RPC error body; Vary: Origin) and ApplyCorsHeaders (only when CorsEnabled; reflect Access-Control-Request-Headers on preflight; Allow-Methods 'POST, GET, DELETE, OPTIONS'; Expose-Headers 'Mcp-Session-Id, WWW-Authenticate'; ContentLength 0 on OPTIONS). AllowedOrigins='*' remains an explicit opt-out with a startup warning.
GET and DELETE ⇒ 405 with Allow: POST, OPTIONS (remove the 'endpoint info' JSON and the immediately-closed SSE stream).
202 (notifications) and 204 removal: set ContentLength 0 and an empty ContentStream; verify with curl -i that no HTML body is emitted; requests with invalid id now get -32600 instead of 204.
Session handling: never mint; echo Mcp-Session-Id only for legacy-era requests; ignore for modern; delete the Pos('"sessionId"') block.

Accept parsing over all Accept header lines with q-values; default to application/json; SSE only when the sink streamed (phase 5) — until then SSE framing kept for clients that offer it, but as a single event without id lines.
Client-sent JSON-RPC responses: modern (header modern) ⇒ 400/-32600 id null; legacy ⇒ 202.
BindAddress setting with explicit Bindings (127.0.0.1 default, ::1 optional, 0.0.0.0 warns); keep DefaultPort for HandleQuerySSLPort.
TLS: OpenSSL-1.0.2 branch SSLVersions := [sslvTLSv1_2(+1_3)]; move USE_TAURUS_TLS to src/MCPServer.inc; document -D override.
Logging: request/response bodies at Debug via TLogger.RedactJson; never log Authorization; session id not logged at Info.
HTTP integration tests with TIdHTTP against an in-process TMCPIdHTTPServer on a random port.
deliverables: tests: header validation table, Origin 403 with CORS disabled, GET/DELETE 405, 202 empty body, status mapping per era over real HTTP
risks: Indy behaviours asserted from memory (default HTML body on empty responses, RawHeaders.Values case-insensitivity, Bindings default 0.0.0.0) must be verified on the Windows build before finalising; no Indy sources in this container.
Loopback binding and Origin-always are visible changes for existing deployments — CHANGELOG + settings keys mitigate.
Browser-based modern clients need the exact CORS header names; the Inspector web UI proxies via Node so it will not surface CORS mistakes.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Tools & resources data model for both eras
phases.goal: Emit schema-valid tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list results in the modern era and spec-correct errors in both eras; give tool/resource authors typed result and metadata APIs without breaking existing subclasses.
steps: Tools manager: -32602 for unknown tool/malformed params; empty arguments object when absent; ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope/PageSize with cursor validation; registration-order list; content text fallback for structuredContent-only results; non-string/JSON TValue ⇒ text; EMCPToolError; LegacyErrorPrefixDetection.

MCPServer.Tool.Result (TMCPToolResult) and TMCPToolBase<T>/<T,R>.ExecuteWithContext virtual; IMCPToolMetadata (annotations/icons/_meta) on all bases; CreateToolJSON emits annotations/icons/_meta only when set and omits empty description; icon src restricted to https:// or data:.

Schema generator: integer type, Boolean by TypeInfo, recursive nested/array/set/record schemas with cycle guard, TDateTime date-time, additionalProperties:false for empty param classes, new Schema* attributes incl. [SchemaHeader] (x-mcp-header with the constraints validated at registration); TMCPToolsManager implements IMCPHeaderBindingSource from the emitted schema.

Serializer: enforce required properties and type kinds (StrictMode=True escape hatch); serialise dynamic arrays/TList/enums/sets/nil consistently with outputSchema; MCPServer.Schema.Validator for hand-built schemas and a DEBUG self-check of structuredContent vs outputSchema.
Tool naming validation (^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$) with warning (StrictToolNames raises); duplicate registration warning; Tool.Name vs registry key consistency.

Resources manager: -32602/-32002 by era with data.uri; -32603 on read failure; nil-params/-32602; IMCPCacheableResource/IMCPResourceReader/IMCPResourceMetadata on TMCPResourceBase<T>; blob contents with TBase64Encoding.Create(0); registration-order lists, pagination, ttlMs/cacheScope; RFC3986 URI validation via MCPServer.Uri; built-in cache values; TMCPBinaryResourceBase sample.
Resource templates: IMCPResourceTemplate + RFC 6570 level 1/2 matcher, TMCPRegistry.RegisterResourceTemplate, templates/list emission, read fallback; sample logs://{level}.
Golden fixtures for every list/read/call shape in both eras; legacy fixtures assert absence of resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope/_meta.serverInfo.
risks: Strict deserialisation changes behaviour for consumers whose callers omit non-[Optional] parameters — the schema already promised 'required'; StrictMode and CHANGELOG mitigate.
Schema text changes ('integer', additionalProperties:false) break consumers' snapshot tests.
TValue.AsBoolean on non-Boolean enums may raise EInvalidCast depending on RTL version — confirm on Windows.

phases.name: Phase 4 — Prompts, completion (and templates polish)
phases.goal: Add the prompts and completions capabilities as additive, registry-driven managers so the server can reach 100% on both frozen conformance requirement sets and expose the third MRTR-capable method.
steps: MCPServer.Prompt.Base: TMCPPromptArgument, TMCPPromptMessages builder (text/image/audio/resource_link/embedded resource), IMCPPrompt, TMCPPromptBase, generic TMCPPromptBase<T>; TMCPRegistry prompt factories.

MCPServer.PromptsManager: prompts/list (ttlMs/cacheScope/pagination/deterministic order) and prompts/get (-32602 for unknown prompt/missing required argument/non-string argument values; description + messages; no caching fields); IMCPCapabilityProvider {listChanged:false}; IMCPCapabilityManagerEx.

MCPServer.CompletionManager: completion/complete with ref/prompt and ref/resource (template or exact), argument validation, optional context.arguments, IMCPCompletable, ≤100 values; capability {completions:{}} only when registered.
Register both managers in MCPServer.dpr (HTTP and stdio) and document registration for library consumers; sample prompt; README 'Creating Custom Prompts'.
Golden fixtures: prompts-list/get (both eras, including 2025-03-26 without resource_link), completion-complete.
risks: Content-block gating for 2025-03-26 (no resource_link) is polish; legacy schemas are open, so a wrong gate is harmless but a missing text fallback is not.
Completion rate limiting is left as a hook (documented).

phases.name: Phase 5 — Streaming layer: Indy SSE writer, stdio concurrency, cancellation, progress, shutdown
phases.goal: Provide the IMCPMessageSink implementations that let request-scoped notifications precede the final response on both transports, honour cancellation (HTTP disconnect in modern era, notifications/cancelled on stdio), and shut down cleanly.
steps: MCPServer.SseWriter (TMCPHttpMessageSink): lazy switch to SSE on first notification (WriteHeader + IOHandler writes, CloseConnection True or manual chunked framing), keep-alive comment writer, disconnect probe ⇒ Ctx.Cancelled (modern only), final response written as last event; pass TIdContext into HandlePostRequest*; FOpenStreams TThreadList; Stop() signals FShutdownEvent, drains, force-disconnects, then Active := False.

Stdio: THandleStream/byte UTF-8 I/O with LF framing; reader loop + notification fast path + bounded worker pool (MaxConcurrentRequests 4/1/0 semantics) + TMCPStdioMessageSink with one critical section; TMCPInflightRegistry registration around dispatch; suppress the response when the context was cancelled; Stop()/EOF drain with bounded wait; dpr signal handling fixed (no swallowed SIGTERM; no leak dialog in stdio).

IMCPRequestContext.ReportProgress: only when params._meta.progressToken exists (string|number preserved), monotonic, throttled, silent after completion/cancellation; notifications/progress {progressToken, progress, total?, message?} through the sink.
CheckCancelled/IsCancelled available to tools via ExecuteWithContext or TMCPRequestContext.Current; TMCPToolsManager catches EMCPRequestCancelled and returns nothing.

Tests: stdio transport over in-memory streams (interleaved ping during a slow tool with MaxConcurrentRequests=2; cancelled request produces no response; progress lines precede the response; non-ASCII round trip); HTTP: SSE stream contains progress events then the response; client disconnect mid-tool marks cancelled.
deliverables: src/Server/MCPServer.StdioTransport.pas (rewritten internals, same public API + Stop/MaxConcurrentRequests/streams)
risks: Indy has no automatic chunked encoding for IOHandler writes; CloseConnection True loses keep-alive on streamed responses — acceptable, document.
Tools now run on worker threads on stdio; consumers relying on main-thread execution must set MaxConcurrentRequests=0.
Windows Text I/O code page and TStreamWriter BOM behaviour are asserted from RTL semantics — verify with a non-ASCII echo over --stdio.

phases.name: Phase 6 — MRTR, elicitation and requestState
phases.goal: Expose the only modern-era mechanism for user input (InputRequiredResult with elicitation/create) to tool, resource and prompt authors, with capability gating and integrity-protected state, and a defined legacy fallback.
steps: MCPServer.Mrtr: TMCPInputRequests builder (form/url elicitation, deprecated sampling/roots), TMCPInputRequiredResult, EMCPInputRequired, TMCPInputResponses accessor, TMCPElicitation + TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder, ElicitResult validation against requestedSchema via MCPServer.Schema.Validator.

MCPServer.RequestState HMAC-SHA256 codec (Seal/Open with principal, exp, method, args digest; constant-time compare; key from settings or random per process); document single-use enforcement as author responsibility.

Managers: catch EMCPInputRequired only in tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get; modern: capability checks (elicitation.form/url, sampling(.tools), roots) ⇒ -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities on failure, else input_required result (no caching fields); legacy: isError text (tools) / -32603 (resources, prompts); processor treats EMCPInputRequired from other methods as -32603.
IMCPRequestContext exposes InputResponses/RequestState parsed from params; MRTR retry is stateless (new id, original params + inputResponses + requestState).

Sample tool (e.g. 'confirm_delete') demonstrating a two-round elicitation with sealed requestState; README 'Elicitation (MCP 2026-07-28)' with security rules (no secrets via form, no pre-authenticated URLs, https URLs).

Tests: input_required shape, missing-capability -32021/400, tampered/expired/cross-principal requestState ⇒ -32602, extra inputResponses ignored, missing response ⇒ new InputRequiredResult, legacy fallback shapes.
deliverables: manager MRTR handling in Tools/Resources/Prompts managers
risks: Per-process random StateKey breaks retries across restarts/load-balanced instances — configure a key in production.
Clients that never retry must not leave server state behind — design is stateless by construction, keep it so.

phases.name: Phase 7 — subscriptions/listen (optional)
phases.goal: Answer subscriptions/listen with an acknowledgment and a long-lived stream so Inspector/host 'Subscribe' flows succeed and listChanged can be advertised once dynamic registration exists.
steps: MCPServer.SubscriptionsManager with filter validation, honoured-subset computation, acknowledged-first ordering per subscription id, registry keyed by listen id.

HTTP long-lived stream loop in TMCPIdHTTPServer (keep-alive comments, disconnect ⇒ teardown without further messages, Stop ⇒ completion result then close); stdio stream objects with notifications/cancelled handling and EOF/Stop ⇒ notifications/cancelled + completion result.
TMCPRegistry.OnChanged fan-out for list_changed; capability builder flips listChanged/subscribe only when a source exists.
Tests: ack first, subscriptionId tagging, cancel stops notifications, graceful closure result on shutdown.
risks: Each open HTTP stream pins an Indy worker thread — set MaxConnections and document.
Spec tension between subscriptions.mdx (completion result) and cancellation.mdx (notifications/cancelled on teardown) — implement both in the stated order per transport.

phases.name: Phase 8 — Authorization hook, RFC 9728 metadata, conformance/Inspector tooling, documentation
phases.goal: Ship an opt-in authentication surface that follows the resource-server MUSTs, and give the repo repeatable acceptance tooling and accurate docs.
steps: MCPServer.Authorization (IMCPAuthorizer, TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer, abstract OAuth resource-server base with audience/expiry checks, TMCPAuthChallenge/WriteAuthChallenge, [RequiresScope] + scope hierarchy); TMCPIdHTTPServer.Authorizer; 401/403 with WWW-Authenticate; /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/endpoint] document; [Auth] settings; principal on the request context; never on stdio.
Optional Host allow-list and simple per-IP token bucket (RateLimitPerMinute, 429) and OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool hooks on TMCPToolsManager.

scripts/run-conformance.ps1: build, start server, run npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --requirements 2026-07-28 and --requirements 2025-11-25 with conformance-baseline.yml; Inspector CLI smoke in legacy/auto/modern eras; pin tool versions in package.json.

README/CHANGELOG/settings.ini.example: dual-era behaviour, HTTP status table, header requirements, security section, library extension points, stdio checklist, Inspector protocolEra, conformance commands; badge 2026-07-28.
Decide and document CI (self-hosted Windows runner vs release checklist).
risks: Server-side auth is not machine-scored by the conformance suite (only client-leg auth scenarios exist) — rely on DUnitX + Inspector OAuth run.
No Delphi compiler on GitHub-hosted runners.

publicApiChanges.item: IMCPCapabilityManager, IMCPManagerRegistry, IMCPTool, IMCPResource (GUIDs and members unchanged); new optional interfaces IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPHeaderBindingSource, IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPPrompt, IMCPCompletable discovered with Supports()
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Existing implementers compile and behave as before; processor/managers fall back to the old members when the new interface is absent.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor: Create(ManagerRegistry) kept; new Create(ManagerRegistry, Settings) overload; ProcessRequest(Body, SessionID): string kept (SessionID ignored) and now era-aware; new ProcessRequestEx(Body, Hints, Sink): TMCPProcessResult; CreateErrorResponse becomes public class function with Data parameter
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Custom transports keep compiling; document that without hints they get stdio semantics (no header validation, no HTTP status).

publicApiChanges.item: Error-code constants: JSONRPC_* move to MCPServer.Types with aliases left in MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor for one release; duplicates in MCPServer.IdHTTPServer removed (they were in the implementation section, not exported)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Aliases keep MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR resolving.

publicApiChanges.item: MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION remains '2025-06-18' but is deprecated; new MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION, MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, MCP_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Deprecation comment; Resource.Project switched to the new constants.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPCoreManager: Create(Settings) kept; SessionID property returns '' (sessions no longer minted); new ManagerRegistry property; initialize result loses 'sessionId', 'supportsProgress', 'supportsCancellation' and echoes the client's legacy protocolVersion; handles 'server/discover'
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Wire change only for non-schema members no conformant client reads; CHANGELOG entry; consumers with their own core manager must add server/discover (README).

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPToolsManager: unknown tool and malformed params become JSON-RPC -32602 errors instead of isError text results; absent arguments become an empty object; new properties ListTtlMs, ListCacheScope, PageSize, LegacyErrorPrefixDetection, OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Spec-required (tools.mdx §Error Handling); documented in CHANGELOG; consumer integration tests that asserted the text result need updating.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPResourcesManager: resource not found becomes JSON-RPC -32602 (modern) / -32002 (legacy) with data.uri; read exceptions become -32603; new ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope/PageSize; templates supported
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Spec-required in both eras; CHANGELOG; clients see failures as errors instead of text blobs.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPToolBase<T>/<T,R>: ExecuteWithParams stays the abstract override point; new virtual ExecuteWithContext(Params, Ctx): TMCPToolResult with a default that wraps ExecuteWithParams; new protected fields for annotations/icons/_meta
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Existing subclasses compile unchanged; new features are opt-in overrides.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPSerializer.Deserialize enforces required (non-[Optional]) properties and rejects type-kind mismatches (previously silent defaults/coercion)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Behaviour change matching the advertised schema; TMCPSerializer.StrictMode := False restores leniency; CHANGELOG.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPSchemaGenerator emits 'integer' for Integer/Int64, recursive nested schemas, additionalProperties:false for empty param classes; new Schema* attributes
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Schema text changes only; consumers snapshotting schemas update fixtures.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPRegistry: RegisterTool/RegisterResource validate names/URIs with warnings (StrictToolNames raises); ordered name lists; new RegisterPrompt/RegisterResourceTemplate/CreatePrompt/GetPromptNames/HasPrompt/OnChanged
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Warnings only by default; duplicate registration keeps last-wins semantics.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPIdHTTPServer: same properties/methods; GET and DELETE now answer 405 (the JSON 'endpoint info' and empty SSE stream are removed); Origin is validated even when CorsEnabled=False; default bind address 127.0.0.1 instead of all interfaces; no Mcp-Session-Id minting; new BindAddress and Authorizer properties
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Remote deployments must set [Server] BindAddress=0.0.0.0 (warned at startup); [Security] AllowedOrigins=* keeps the old permissive behaviour explicitly; CHANGELOG and README call-outs; 405 on GET is allowed by every legacy revision and handled by all SDK clients.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPStdioTransport: Create(Registry, CoreManager)/Run kept; new Stop, MaxConcurrentRequests, InputStream/OutputStream; tools execute on worker threads by default (MaxConcurrentRequests=4); stdout is UTF-8 with LF framing; TLogger.UseStdErr forced on
publicApiChanges.mitigation: MaxConcurrentRequests=0 restores inline execution on the reader thread; tools were already executed on Indy threads over HTTP so thread-safety was already the contract.

publicApiChanges.item: TLogger: request/response bodies logged at Debug with redaction instead of Info; new RedactJson, StdoutReserved; MCPServer.dpr no longer sets ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown in stdio mode
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Set MinLogLevel := Debug to see bodies; documented.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPSettings: new properties/ini keys (BindAddress, Instructions, Title, Description, WebsiteUrl, DiscoverTtlMs, EmitServerInfo, LegacyEnabled, LenientModernPing, AllowedOrigins, AllowedHosts, RequestStateKey, Auth*, MaxConcurrentRequests, list TTLs); existing keys unchanged
publicApiChanges.mitigation: All defaults preserve current semantics except BindAddress/Origin (see above); TIniFile reads with defaults so old files load.

publicApiChanges.item: MCPServer.dpr sample registers TMCPPromptsManager and TMCPCompletionManager; library consumers must register them themselves to get prompts/completions
publicApiChanges.mitigation: README 'Using as a Library' updated; capabilities are derived from what is registered, so nothing is advertised that is not served.

plans.testing: 1) Unit tests (DUnitX, tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj, built by build.bat and run on Windows; Linux via PAServer when available): (a) pipeline tests calling TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx with a fake IMCPManagerRegistry and explicit TMCPTransportHints for both transports — envelope validation (id:null/bool/object ⇒ -32600; missing jsonrpc/method; params not object), era detection matrix (initialize with each legacy version/garbage/2026-07-28 ⇒ echoed or 2025-11-25; _meta modern happy path; missing clientCapabilities ⇒ -32602/400; unknown version ⇒ -32022/400 with data.supported/requested; header missing/mismatch ⇒ -32020/400; modern-version header without _meta ⇒ -32602/400; garbage legacy header ⇒ 400; header-less ⇒ legacy 2025-03-26 incl. batch), legacy-only methods in modern era ⇒ -32601/404 vs legacy 200, decoration (resultType/_meta.serverInfo/ttlMs/cacheScope present only in modern results; managers' own values not overwritten), status policy table, notifications never answered (202/no output), client-sent responses; (b) MCPServer.HttpHeaders table tests from SEP-2243 (lowercase names accepted, value case mismatch rejected, whitespace trimmed, Base64 sentinel decode incl. UTF-8 and invalid padding ⇒ reject, Mcp-Param-* numeric/boolean compare, null/absent argument ⇒ header ignored); (c) schema generator snapshots, serializer strictness, schema validator, name/URI validation, pagination cursors, base64 blob single-line; (d) requestState codec (tamper/expiry/principal/digest/constant-time); (e) stdio transport over in-memory streams (UTF-8 non-ASCII round trip, LF framing, interleaved ping during a slow tool, cancelled request suppressed, progress before response, EOF drain). 2) Protocol-level golden tests: tests/golden/<era-version>/<case>.json holding request + expected response (with volatile fields masked); one runner iterates all cases through the processor; legacy goldens are captured from the current binary before Phase 1 so byte-identity (minus intended removals) is provable; modern goldens are validated against schema/2026-07-28/schema.json with a Node script in scripts/ (ajv) where a Node toolchain is available. 3) HTTP integration tests: in-process TMCPIdHTTPServer on a random port driven by TIdHTTP — Origin 403 with CORS disabled, GET/DELETE 405 with Allow, 202 with Content-Length 0, 400/404 mapping per era, SSE framing with progress events, disconnect-as-cancellation, no Mcp-Session-Id on modern responses, concurrency smoke (50 parallel initialize/tools/call without AV). 4) Official tooling: scripts/run-conformance.ps1 runs npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --requirements 2026-07-28 and again with --requirements 2025-11-25 against the same endpoint (dual-era), with --expected-failures conformance-baseline.yml (tasks-* and other extension scenarios excluded); optionally tier-check. MCP Inspector (Node ≥ 22.19): config with three server entries for the same URL using protocolEra legacy, auto and modern, plus a stdio entry; CLI smoke `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli --config ci-servers.json --server delphi-modern --method tools/list --format json` and interactive checks of discover, logLevel stamping, MRTR round trips, header mirroring (CLI/TUI), and exit code 3 when auth is enabled without a token. 5) Manual client matrix (release checklist): Claude Code over HTTP (legacy initialize path; tools/resources/prompts; concurrent sessions), Codex over stdio (legacy path; non-ASCII arguments on Windows; Ctrl-free shutdown via stdin close), Claude Desktop/VS Code over HTTP if available, curl scripts for both eras (headers, batch, id:null), Cloudflare Tunnel with BindAddress=0.0.0.0 + bearer token. 6) CI: self-hosted Windows runner executing build.bat Release Win64, the DUnitX suite, the conformance script and the Inspector CLI smoke; until that exists, the checklist is part of the PR template.
risks: Indy internals (default HTML body on empty responses, WriteHeader + IOHandler streaming, chunked encoding absence, RawHeaders case-insensitivity, Bindings default) cannot be verified in this container; Phase 2/5 estimates assume they behave as described and must be re-checked on the Windows build first.

Delphi cannot be compiled here: RTL claims about Text I/O code pages, TStreamWriter BOM, TValue.AsBoolean on enums and threadvar finalisation are from documented semantics and need a smoke test before relying on them.

Legacy-path regressions matter more than modern features because Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop and the Inspector default (protocolEra=legacy) all use initialize today; every phase must keep the legacy golden fixtures green.

Behaviour changes for library consumers (JSON-RPC errors for unknown tool/resource, strict parameter validation, loopback binding, GET 405, Origin-always, worker-thread execution on stdio) are spec-driven but visible; each has an explicit knob or CHANGELOG entry — do not add knobs that would let operators violate a MUST.

Dual-era clients decide era from the body of every 400/404; any code path that returns a 4xx to a modern request without a JSON-RPC error body (e.g. Indy defaults, auth 401 with empty body) would push them into legacy mode — the status/body mapping must be centralised and tested.
The 'not found' substring heuristic must be removed before server/discover ships, otherwise a tool raising 'File not found' becomes -32601/404 for modern clients.
Stdio concurrency introduces shared mutable state risks in consumer tools; the MaxConcurrentRequests=0 escape hatch and documentation are the mitigation, plus atomics on the built-in counters.
requestState key management for multi-instance deployments and the absence of single-use enforcement are documented author responsibilities.

Scope creep: prompts/templates/completion/subscriptions/auth are MAY features; the plan orders them after the MUST-level phases so the release can stop after Phase 3 and still be a conformant dual-era server for tools/resources.
No Delphi on GitHub-hosted CI runners; without a self-hosted runner the conformance gate is manual.
openDecisions: Legacy sessions: stay stateless (never mint Mcp-Session-Id, echo only for legacy requests) [recommended default] vs. mint per-initialize sessions in an HTTP-only store with 404-after-termination semantics (only needed if per-session legacy state such as logging/setLevel is wanted).

2025-03-26 support: keep it in MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS with JSON-RPC batch receive for legacy requests whose version is 2025-03-26/assumed [recommended default, ≈0.5 day inside Phase 1] vs. drop it and answer such initialize requests with 2025-11-25 (permitted by BP-21).

Contents of DiscoverResult.supportedVersions and UnsupportedProtocolVersionError.data.supported: modern-only ['2026-07-28'] [recommended default; legacy versions are only reachable through initialize and a modern client retrying with '2025-11-25' in _meta would be rejected again] vs. listing legacy versions too as the versioning.mdx example does.
Modern-era ping: strict -32601/404 [recommended default] vs. LenientModernPing=1 answering {resultType:'complete'} for transitional clients.
Default HTTP bind address: 127.0.0.1 [recommended default, spec SHOULD] with explicit BindAddress=0.0.0.0 opt-in vs. keeping 0.0.0.0 for container users.
[CORS] AllowedOrigins=* semantics: keep as an explicit, warned opt-out of Origin validation [recommended default] vs. deprecating it.

HTTP status for application-level -32602 (unknown tool, resource not found, invalid cursor, bad prompt argument): 200 [recommended default; only _meta/header failures mandate 400 and a 400 without a recognised modern code triggers client fallback] vs. 400 everywhere.
Stdio execution model default: MaxConcurrentRequests=4 [recommended default] vs. 1 (sequential worker) vs. 0 (inline, today's behaviour).

Scope of this release: Phases 1-3 mandatory; Phase 4 (prompts/completion) recommended because both frozen conformance requirement sets score prompts-* and completion-complete; Phases 5-6 recommended for modern-era value (cancellation/progress/MRTR); Phase 7 (subscriptions/listen) optional — recommended only after a conformance run shows a scored need or Inspector UX is a priority; Phase 8 auth recommended as opt-in.

Authorization depth in core: pluggable IMCPAuthorizer + static bearer + RFC 9728 metadata + abstract OAuth base without JWT verification [recommended default] vs. shipping a JWT/JWKS verifier (needs a third-party JOSE unit or OpenSSL via TaurusTLS).

Default cache hints: tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list and templates/list in the sample server 'public'/300000; library defaults 0/'private'; project://info and project://readme 3600000/'public'; logs://recent and server://status 0/'private' [recommended defaults]; keep logs://recent registered by default [recommended] or gate it behind ExposeLogsResource.
RequestState key: [Security] RequestStateKey in settings.ini for production with random per-process fallback and warning [recommended default].
CI: self-hosted Windows runner running build + DUnitX + conformance + Inspector smoke [recommended] vs. manual release checklist only.
outOfScope: Acting as an OAuth authorization server (2025-03-26 authorization model, DCR, CIMD hosting, consent pages for confused-deputy proxies): the spec places AS implementation outside the MCP server; 2025-03-26 clients are served unauthenticated only (documented).
JWT signature/JWKS verification inside the core library: no JOSE in the Delphi RTL; provided as an abstract hook and a sample, not core.

Tasks extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks): optional extension, disabled by default per docs/extensions/overview.mdx; requires a durable task store and background execution — separate project after Phase 5.

Deprecated features (SEP-2577): no 'logging' capability, no logging/setLevel or notifications/message emission (TLogger stays on stderr/file), no server-side roots/list or sampling/createMessage use; builders for sampling/roots inputRequests are provided only as deprecated helpers.
Legacy server-initiated requests over the HTTP GET stream or stdio (2025-xx elicitation/sampling/roots): replaced by MRTR; legacy clients get an isError/-32603 fallback instead.
HTTP+SSE transport (2024-11-05) and SSE resumability/Last-Event-ID/event ids: deprecated/removed; 405 on GET is permitted by all supported revisions.

Full JSON Schema 2020-12 validator with remote $ref, composition keywords beyond a bounded subset, and dialect switching: only the subset the generator emits plus elicitation schemas is validated; documented per basic/index.mdx 'SHOULD document which schema dialects they support'.
OpenTelemetry trace-context propagation and MCP Apps/other extensions: extensions map is emitted only when a consumer registers one; no built-in extension.
Windows service / installer packaging, Linux CI on GitHub-hosted runners, DPoP and mutual-TLS authentication.

plans.lens: LIBRARY-CONSUMER-FIRST: zero breaking changes for embedders (custom TMCPToolBase<T>/TMCPToolBase<T,R> tools, TMCPResourceBase<T> resources, IMCPCapabilityManager managers, TMCPRegistry, TMCPIdHTTPServer, TMCPStdioTransport, TMCPSettings); every new protocol feature is reached through new optional interfaces discovered with Supports(), new virtuals with default bodies, new attributes, and settings whose defaults reproduce today's wire behaviour for legacy clients.
plans.summary: Turn the current single-version 2025-06-18 server (src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas:11) into a dual-era server by adding one central per-request context in TMCPJsonRpcProcessor that (a) detects the era from the message itself (initialize => legacy; params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] => modern; otherwise legacy), (b) validates modern _meta/headers with typed EMCPError exceptions that carry JSON-RPC code, data and an HTTP status, and (c) post-processes every result once (resultType, _meta.serverInfo, ttlMs/cacheScope safety net) so custom managers written against the unchanged IMCPCapabilityManager interface become 2026-07-28-valid without recompiling their logic. Transports keep their public surface (TMCPIdHTTPServer.Start/Stop/ManagerRegistry/CoreManager/Settings; TMCPStdioTransport.Create(Registry, CoreManager)/Run; TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.Create(Registry)/ProcessRequest(Body, SessionID)) and gain additive members: ProcessRequestEx returning body+HTTP status, header validation for Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name/MCP-Protocol-Version (-32020/400), 404 for unknown methods in the modern era only, stateless sessions in both eras, Origin validation independent of CORS, an Indy SSE writer for request-scoped notifications and subscriptions/listen, and a concurrent stdio reader/worker/writer loop for cancellation and progress. Tool authors opt into annotations, icons, output schema, progress and elicitation through protected fields, a new ExecuteWithParamsEx virtual, IMCPRequestContext and EMCPInputRequired, while every existing ExecuteWithParams-based tool keeps compiling and producing byte-identical legacy responses. Nine phases, roughly 64 senior-Delphi days, ordered so that the blocker gaps (era detection, server/discover, resultType, HTTP status mapping, header validation, tools/list envelope, content array for <T,R> tools, resource-not-found error) land first behind a DUnitX golden-test harness that pins today's legacy output.
plans.compatStrategy: ERA DETECTION (single place, transport-independent: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.BuildRequestContext in src/Protocol/MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.pas). Input: the parsed message plus TMCPTransportHints {HasHeaders, HeaderProtocolVersion, HeaderMethod, HeaderName, McpParamHeaders: TStrings, SessionVersion (stdio process / HTTP-negotiated legacy version if any)}. Rules, in order: (1) method = 'initialize' => peLegacy, always (versioning.mdx 'An initialize request selects legacy semantics'); any _meta on it is ignored. (2) params._meta is a TJSONObject whose 'io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion' is a TJSONString => peModern: value must be in MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS ('2026-07-28') else EMCPError.UnsupportedProtocolVersion (-32022, data {supported, requested}, HTTP 400); 'io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities' must be a TJSONObject else EMCPError.InvalidParams (-32602, HttpStatus 400; basic/index.mdx 'A request missing any required field is malformed ... MUST reject it with -32602 ... On HTTP ... 400'); optional logLevel must be one of debug/info/notice/warning/error/critical/alert/emergency else -32602; clientInfo/progressToken copied into the context. (3) HTTP only: Hints.HeaderProtocolVersion is a modern version but the body has no modern _meta => peModern malformed => -32602/400 (required _meta field missing). (4) otherwise peLegacy with ProtocolVersion = Hints.SessionVersion if known, else Hints.HeaderProtocolVersion if it names a legacy version, else '2025-03-26' (streamable-http.mdx 'MAY treat a request that omits the header as protocol version 2025-03-26'; 2025-11-25 transports 'SHOULD assume protocol version 2025-03-26'). On stdio there is no header layer (stdio.mdx 'There is no header layer'), so only rules 1, 2 and 4 apply; the per-process negotiated legacy version is stored in a TMCPTransportSession owned by TMCPStdioTransport and passed as Hints.SessionVersion. Both eras are served concurrently on the same endpoint/process (versioning.mdx 'A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently'); the era is never a process-wide latch, so server/discover keeps answering DiscoverResult after a legacy initialize (stdio clients cache the era per process, versioning.mdx 'The era determination is a property of the server'). MODERN-ONLY METHOD GATE: after detection, peModern requests for 'ping', 'initialize', 'notifications/initialized', 'logging/setLevel', 'resources/subscribe', 'resources/unsubscribe' raise EMCPError.MethodNotFound (-32601; HTTP 404) unless TMCPSettings.LenientModernPing is set (changelog.mdx major change 5 removes ping/logging/setLevel; major change 2 removes initialize). LEGACY PATH: byte-identical to today except for spec-required fixes (correct version echo per lifecycle.mdx 'If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version', 'sessionId' body field dropped, capability sub-keys corrected, resource-not-found/unknown-tool become JSON-RPC errors). resultType and _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo are injected only when Ctx.Era = peModern, so legacy responses do not change shape. RESULT POST-PROCESSING (processor, once, for every manager including consumer-provided ones): if the result is not a TJSONObject it is wrapped ({} for TValue.Empty; parsed object for a JSON string; {'value': ...} otherwise, with a warning) so 'result' is always an object (basic/index.mdx 'Result responses MUST include a result field'); modern: AddPair('resultType','complete') if absent (managers that return input_required set it themselves and are left alone); modern: get-or-create '_meta' and add 'io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo' {name, version [, title, description, websiteUrl, icons]} unless TMCPSettings.EmitServerInfo = False (basic/index.mdx 'Servers SHOULD include ... unless specifically configured not to do so'); modern safety net for the six cacheable methods (server/discover, tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read; caching.mdx 'Servers MUST include caching hints'): add 'ttlMs': 0 and 'cacheScope': 'private' when absent so a consumer's old manager still yields a schema-valid result (built-in managers set better values themselves). ERROR MODEL: EMCPError(Code, Message, Data: TJSONValue owned, HttpStatus: Integer = 0) in new unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.Errors.pas with factories MethodNotFound, InvalidParams, InvalidRequest, InternalError, UnsupportedProtocolVersion, MissingRequiredClientCapability, HeaderMismatch, ResourceNotFound(Era, Uri) (-32602 modern with data.uri; -32002 legacy per 2025-11-25 resources.mdx 'Resource not found: -32002'; 2026-07-28 basic/index.mdx 'MUST NOT emit -32002'). Processor catch order: EMCPError => its code/data; EMCPInputRequired escaping a non-MRTR method => -32603 with log; any other Exception => -32603 (the current Pos('not found') heuristic at JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214 is kept ONLY for legacy-era requests behind TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.LegacyNotFoundHeuristic (default True) so consumers' existing managers behave as before, and is never applied to modern requests where -32601 maps to HTTP 404 and would mislead dual-era clients). HTTP STATUS POLICY (returned in TMCPProcessResult.HttpStatus; stdio ignores it): peModern: -32020/-32021/-32022 => 400; -32602 with HttpStatus=400 (only the _meta validator sets it) => 400; -32700 and -32600 => 400; -32601 => 404 (streamable-http.mdx 'MUST respond with 404 Not Found and a JSON-RPC error with code -32601'); every other error incl. application-level -32602 (unknown tool, resource not found, invalid cursor) and all successes => 200. peLegacy: always 200 from the processor (a 404 would be read by legacy clients as 'session terminated', 2025-11-25 transports Session Management item 4); the transport adds 400 for an MCP-Protocol-Version header that is neither a legacy nor a modern version (2025-11-25 transports 'invalid or unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version ... MUST respond with 400'), 403 for a disallowed Origin, 405 for GET/DELETE. Every 4xx to a modern request carries the JSON-RPC error body so dual-era clients do not fall back to initialize (streamable-http.mdx Backward Compatibility). LIBRARY CONSUMERS: no member is added to IMCPTool, IMCPResource, IMCPCapabilityManager or IMCPManagerRegistry (Delphi interfaces cannot be extended without breaking implementers); all new behaviour is reached via new GUID'd interfaces (IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPToolContextAware, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPPrompt, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPCompletable, IMCPAuthorizer) probed with Supports(), new protected fields/virtuals with default implementations on the base classes, additive TMCPRegistry class methods, additive TMCPSettings properties (ini keys with defaults), and an ambient TMCPRequestContext.Current (threadvar, explicitly assigned/cleared by the processor because Delphi does not finalize managed threadvars) so unchanged tools can read Era/ClientCapabilities/ReportProgress without any signature change. Existing constants (MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION, JSONRPC_* in MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor) keep their names and values (re-exported aliases). Behaviour changes that are spec-mandated but visible (resource-not-found as JSON-RPC error, GET => 405, Origin validated even with CORS disabled, sessions not minted) are listed in the migration guide with a settings escape hatch where the spec allows one.

architecture.change: Add to src/Protocol/MCPServer.Types.pas: MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2026-07-28'; MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS: array of string=('2026-07-28'); MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS=('2025-11-25','2025-06-18') plus MCP_ACCEPTED_LEGACY_INITIALIZE_VERSIONS=('2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26'); MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2025-11-25'; keep MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2025-06-18' with a 'deprecated' comment; MCP_META_* key constants (io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, clientCapabilities, clientInfo, logLevel, serverInfo, subscriptionId; progressToken); MCP_RESULT_TYPE_COMPLETE/INPUT_REQUIRED; MCP_LOG_LEVELS; JSONRPC_PARSE_ERROR..JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR moved here plus MCP_ERROR_HEADER_MISMATCH=-32020, MCP_ERROR_MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY=-32021, MCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION=-32022, MCP_ERROR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_LEGACY=-32002 (legacy era only); TMCPProtocolEra=(peLegacy, peModern). New unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.Errors.pas: EMCPError = class(Exception) with Code, Data (TJSONValue, owned, cloned into error.data), HttpStatus (0 = policy default) and class factories MethodNotFound(Method), InvalidRequest(Msg), InvalidParams(Msg; Data=nil; HttpStatus=0), InternalError(Msg), UnsupportedProtocolVersion(Requested; Supported) => data {supported:[...], requested}, MissingRequiredClientCapability(Required: TJSONObject) => data {requiredCapabilities}, HeaderMismatch(Detail) => message 'Header mismatch: ...', ResourceNotFound(Era, Uri) => -32602 + data {uri} modern, -32002 legacy; EMCPToolError (isError result, message verbatim); EMCPInputRequired (Phase 6). JsonRpcProcessor.pas and IdHTTPServer.pas keep their JSONRPC_* identifiers as aliases (= MCPServer.Types.JSONRPC_...) for one release so consumer code referencing them compiles.
architecture.rationale: basic/index.mdx Error Codes: 'Implementations MUST NOT emit any code from this sub-range that is not defined by this specification and MUST use defined codes only with their specified meanings'; schema.ts defines HEADER_MISMATCH=-32020, MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY=-32021, UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION=-32022 with required data members. Today CreateErrorResponse has no data parameter (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:128-144) and the code is chosen by Pos('not found', E.Message) (:214), which misclassifies TMCPRegistry 'Tool not found: %s' (Registration.pas:76) and any consumer exception as -32601. Duplicated constants at JsonRpcProcessor.pas:27-32 and IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99 get one home.

architecture.change: New unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.RequestContext.pas: IMCPRequestContext = interface ['{new GUID}'] with GetEra: TMCPProtocolEra; GetProtocolVersion: string; GetIsModern: Boolean; GetRequestId: TJSONValue (borrowed clone); GetMethod: string; GetClientCapabilities: TJSONObject (borrowed; nil for legacy pre-initialize; for legacy it is the object recorded at initialize by the transport session); GetClientInfo: TJSONObject; GetLogLevel: string; GetProgressToken: TJSONValue; GetInputResponses: TJSONObject; GetRequestState: string; GetPrincipal: TMCPPrincipal (Phase 8, nil-safe); IsCancelled: Boolean; procedure CheckCancelled (raises EMCPRequestCancelled); procedure ReportProgress(Progress: Double; Total: Double = -1; const Msg: string = ''); function HasClientCapability(const Path: string): Boolean (dotted path, e.g. 'elicitation.form'; empty elicitation object counts as form per elicitation.mdx 'an empty capabilities object is equivalent to declaring support for form mode only'); procedure RequireClientCapability(const Required: TJSONObject) (raises EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability); Sink: IMCPMessageWriter (nil when the transport cannot stream). TMCPRequestContext = class(TInterfacedObject, IMCPRequestContext) with a cancel flag driven by TInterlocked, monotonic progress guard, throttle (MinProgressIntervalMs default 100) and 'sealed' flag set by the processor before the response is written so late ReportProgress calls are no-ops (progress.mdx 'Progress notifications MUST stop after completion'). class property Current: IMCPRequestContext backed by threadvar CurrentContextRef: Pointer, assigned by the processor around dispatch and set to nil in a finally block (Delphi does not finalize managed threadvars). Additive interface in MCPServer.Types: IMCPCapabilityManagerEx = interface(IMCPCapabilityManager) ['{new GUID}'] function ExecuteMethodEx(const Method: string; const Params: TJSONObject; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TValue; end; the processor prefers it via Supports() and otherwise calls the unchanged ExecuteMethod. TMCPToolsManager, TMCPResourcesManager, TMCPCoreManager and the new managers implement both.
architecture.rationale: basic/index.mdx: 'A server MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared'; schema.ts RequestMetaObject: 'Servers MUST NOT infer capabilities from prior requests'. Managers and tools currently receive only (Method, Params) / (Arguments) (Types.pas:43; Tool.Base.pas:18) and cannot know the era or capabilities; tool instances are singletons shared by Indy worker threads (ToolsManager.pas:84-94), so per-request state must travel as a parameter or ambient threadvar, never in tool fields.

architecture.change: Keep constructor Create(ManagerRegistry) and function ProcessRequest(const RequestBody, SessionID: string): string (delegates with legacy hints). Add: constructor Create(ManagerRegistry; Settings: TMCPSettings) overload; properties Settings, EmitServerInfo (default True), LegacyNotFoundHeuristic (default True), LenientModernPing (from settings). Add TMCPTransportHints record (HasHeaders, HeaderProtocolVersion, HeaderMethod, HeaderName, McpParamHeaders: TStrings, SessionVersion, Session: TMCPTransportSession) and TMCPProcessResult record (Body, HttpStatus, IsNotification, Era, ErrorCode, ResponseKind: (rkNone, rkJson, rkDeferredStream)). function ProcessRequestEx(const RequestBody: string; const Hints: TMCPTransportHints; const Sink: IMCPMessageWriter = nil): TMCPProcessResult implements: parse (-32700; TJSONArray body => -32600 'Batching is not supported' because 2025-03-26 is not in the servable legacy set — see open decision 1); message validation (jsonrpc must be '2.0', method non-empty TJSONString else -32600; id present but null/bool/object/array/non-integer number => -32600 with id null; id absent => notification path; message with result/error and no method => ignored, logged at Debug); notification path: dispatch to the manager (ProcessNotification, exceptions logged, never answered) and return IsNotification; BuildRequestContext (era detection as in compatStrategy); modern-only method gate; HTTP header validation when Hints.HasHeaders (delegated to MCPServer.HttpHeaders, raises EMCPError.HeaderMismatch); set TMCPRequestContext.Current; dispatch via IMCPCapabilityManagerEx or IMCPCapabilityManager; result post-processing (object wrapping, resultType, serverInfo, cacheable safety net); status policy. Also class function ValidateMeta and BuildRequestContext are public class functions so DUnitX can test them without a registry.
architecture.rationale: The processor is the only chokepoint every response passes through (IdHTTPServer.pas:488,522; StdioTransport.pas:64), so injecting resultType/_meta there covers consumer managers automatically (basic/index.mdx 'The result MUST include a resultType field'; schema.ts Result: 'Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field'). Today ExtractRequestID turns id:null into a notification (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:82-87,174-181) although 'Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be null' (basic/index.mdx Requests), and TValue.Empty results produce a response without 'result' (:192-200).

architecture.component: TMCPCoreManager (legacy initialize + modern server/discover + capability aggregation)
architecture.change: Keep Create(ASettings) and the SessionID property (now returns ''; marked deprecated in a comment). Add optional property ManagerRegistry: IMCPManagerRegistry (assigned by TMCPIdHTTPServer.Start / TMCPStdioTransport.Create from the CoreManager fields that already exist but are unused, IdHTTPServer.pas:41,67 and StdioTransport.pas:17,33, or by the consumer). HandlesMethod adds 'server/discover'. Initialize: read params.protocolVersion; if in MCP_ACCEPTED_LEGACY_INITIALIZE_VERSIONS and servable (2025-06-18/2025-11-25) echo it, else answer MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION ('2025-11-25'); store the negotiated version and a clone of params.capabilities in Hints.Session (transport-owned TMCPTransportSession, never in a manager field — FSessionID at CoreManager.pas:17/97 is removed as a written field); emit capabilities via TMCPCapabilityBuilder; drop 'sessionId' from the body (CoreManager.pas:126); log a TLogger.Warning when clientCapabilities declare roots or sampling (SEP-2577 'Implementations SHOULD emit a warning'). Discover(Ctx): {resultType:'complete', supportedVersions: MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, capabilities: builder(peModern), instructions (if Settings.Instructions <> ''), ttlMs: Settings.DiscoverTtlMs (default 3600000), cacheScope:'public', _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo: BuildServerInfo}.
