TMCPCapabilityBuilder (new src/Managers/MCPServer.Capabilities.pas): iterate managers via IMCPManagerEnumerator (implemented by TMCPManagerRegistry; consumers with their own IMCPManagerRegistry fall back to the static tools+resources object as today); for each manager Supports(IMCPCapabilityProvider) => GetCapabilityJSON, else map GetCapabilityName in ['tools','resources','prompts','completions'] => {} and skip 'core'; modern only: add 'extensions' when RegisterExtension was called (empty by default). Built-ins emit tools:{listChanged:false}, resources:{subscribe:false, listChanged:false}, prompts:{listChanged:false}, completions:{}. Never emit 'logging' or the undefined supportsProgress/supportsCancellation keys (CoreManager.pas:106-114).
architecture.rationale: discover.mdx: 'Servers MUST implement it'; DiscoverResult required fields resultType, supportedVersions, capabilities, ttlMs, cacheScope (schema.ts DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult). 2025-11-25 lifecycle.mdx: 'If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version' while Initialize always writes '2025-06-18' (CoreManager.pas:101). tools.mdx/resources.mdx/prompts.mdx: 'Servers that support X MUST declare the X capability' — capabilities must follow what is registered, not a hard-coded object (CoreManager.pas:103-124). Removing FSessionID also removes the cross-thread data race on a Delphi string.

architecture.change: Public surface unchanged (Create(Owner), Start, Stop, Port, Active, ManagerRegistry, CoreManager, Settings); additive properties BindAddress, Authorizer (Phase 8), OnAuthenticate. HandleHTTPRequest pipeline: ValidateOrigin (always, independent of CorsEnabled; absent Origin allowed; 'null' or unlisted => 403 with body {jsonrpc:'2.0', error:{code:-32600, message:'Origin not allowed'}}; matching by scheme+host case-insensitive with optional ':*' port wildcard; built-in loopback set http(s)://localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1] any port) => ApplyCorsHeaders when CorsEnabled (Allow-Headers 'Accept, Content-Type, Authorization, Last-Event-ID, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name' or the preflight's Access-Control-Request-Headers reflected; Allow-Methods 'POST, GET, DELETE, OPTIONS'; Expose-Headers 'Mcp-Session-Id, WWW-Authenticate'; Vary: Origin) => optional well-known PRM path (Phase 8) => endpoint check (404 for other paths, unchanged) => OPTIONS 204 empty => GET/DELETE 405 with Allow: POST, OPTIONS (legacy 2025-11-25 transports permit 405 for GET and DELETE; the current endpoint-info JSON at IdHTTPServer.pas:303-313 moves behind Settings.EndpointInfoPath, default '' = disabled) => POST: read UTF-8 body; build TMCPTransportHints from RawHeaders (Values[] lookup is case-insensitive; trim values; collect Mcp-Param-* into McpParamHeaders); legacy header sanity: MCP-Protocol-Version present but in neither version list => 400 with -32600 body; call FJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx(Body, Hints, Sink); IsNotification => 202 with ContentStream := empty TMemoryStream (FreeContentStream True) and ContentLength 0 so Indy emits no default HTML body (verify with curl -i); ResponseKind rkJson => ResponseNo := HttpStatus, application/json; Mcp-Session-Id is neither minted nor echoed in any era (option A, see open decision 3) and Last-Event-ID is ignored; SSE only when the request streamed (see SSE writer). Remove FEventIDCounter/GetNextEventID and 'id:' lines (changelog major change 9; legacy ids are MAY). Start: FHTTPServer.Bindings.Clear; Bindings.Add with IP := resolved BindAddress (default = Settings.Host resolved: 'localhost' => '127.0.0.1'; '0.0.0.0'/'*' => all with a logged warning), Port := FPort. TLS: OpenSSL branch SSLVersions := [sslvTLSv1_2] (+1_3 when available); move {$DEFINE USE_TAURUS_TLS} into src/MCPServer.inc. Counters: TServerStatusResource uses AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement.
architecture.rationale: streamable-http.mdx Security & Endpoint: 'Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections ... If the Origin header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403' — today VerifyAndSetCORSHeaders exits when CorsEnabled=False or AllowedOrigins='*' (IdHTTPServer.pas:221-227). 'When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost' — Start binds via DefaultPort only (:155-156). Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions: 'HTTP GET or DELETE ... 405', 'Mcp-Session-Id ... do not mint or echo', 'Last-Event-ID: ignore it'. Legacy 2025-11-25 transports: 'The server MUST either return Content-Type: text/event-stream in response to this HTTP GET, or else return HTTP 405' — the current 200 JSON info body (IdHTTPServer.pas:301-313) satisfies neither. Sending Messages item 5: notifications => '202 Accepted with no body'.

architecture.change: New pure unit src/Server/MCPServer.HttpHeaders.pas (no Indy dependency; takes TStrings/JSON so DUnitX can drive it): function DecodeMcpHeaderValue(const Raw: string; out Value, Err: string): Boolean — trims; if it starts with '=?base64?' and ends with '?=' (case-sensitive) strictly validate the alphabet [A-Za-z0-9+/], '=' only as trailing padding, Length mod 4 = 0 BEFORE calling TNetEncoding.Base64.DecodeStringToBytes (System.NetEncoding silently skips invalid characters) then TEncoding.UTF8.GetString; otherwise every char must be 0x20-0x7E or #9. procedure ValidateStandardHeaders(const Hints; const Method: string; Params: TJSONObject; const Era) — only for peModern requests with an id: (a) MCP-Protocol-Version missing => HeaderMismatch('missing MCP-Protocol-Version'); (b) header <> _meta protocolVersion => HeaderMismatch (checked before -32022 so a disagreement is reported as mismatch); (c) Mcp-Method missing or <> method (case-sensitive) => HeaderMismatch; (d) method in ('tools/call','prompts/get') => decoded Mcp-Name must equal params.name; 'resources/read' => params.uri; missing/undecodable/different => HeaderMismatch; (e) Mcp-Param-{Name}: for each binding advertised by the target tool's inputSchema x-mcp-header (Phase 8; cached per tool name) compare decoded header with the argument at the property path (numeric compare for integers, 'true'/'false' for booleans, exact for strings); body value null/absent => header must not be expected (ignored if present); body value present but header missing => HeaderMismatch; recognised header with invalid characters => HeaderMismatch; unknown Mcp-Param-* ignored. Notifications: validate Mcp-Method only if present (streamable-http.mdx 'header requirements for notification POSTs are not defined'). Legacy-era requests skip all of this.
architecture.rationale: streamable-http.mdx Server Validation: 'When rejecting a request due to header validation failure, servers MUST return HTTP status 400 Bad Request and MUST include a JSON-RPC error response using ... -32020'; failure conditions 'A required standard header (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name) is missing', mismatch after Base64 decoding, invalid characters; Value Encoding: markers 'are case-sensitive and MUST appear exactly as shown (lowercase)'; Case Sensitivity: header names case-insensitive, values case-sensitive. Currently no Mcp-* header other than Mcp-Session-Id is read (IdHTTPServer.pas:333-337).

architecture.change: New unit src/Server/MCPServer.SseWriter.pas: IMCPMessageWriter = interface ['{new GUID}'] procedure WriteMessage(const Json: string); function IsConnected: Boolean; end (shared abstraction with stdio). TMCPSseWriter wraps TIdContext + TIdHTTPResponseInfo: Open sets ContentType 'text/event-stream', CharSet utf-8, Cache-Control no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering no, ContentLength := -1, CloseConnection := True (Indy does not chunk IOHandler writes; close-delimited body keeps HTTP/1.1 clients correct — verify on Windows with curl -N), calls ResponseInfo.WriteHeader; WriteMessage writes 'event: message'#10'data: '+Json+#10#10 via Context.Connection.IOHandler.Write(..., IndyTextEncoding_UTF8) under a per-writer TCriticalSection; WriteComment writes ': keep-alive'#10#10; IsConnected := IOHandler.Connected after CheckForDisconnect(False); EIdConnClosedGracefully/EIdSocketError on write mark the context cancelled (streamable-http.mdx Cancellation) only when Era = peModern (legacy: 'Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling'). HandlePostRequest execution model: pass Context into the handler; create a TMCPBufferingSink that records notifications; run ProcessRequestEx; if no notification was produced answer application/json (JSON is the cheaper default; streamable-http.mdx item 6 allows either); if notifications were produced and the client offered text/event-stream (proper Accept parsing over all Accept lines, q=0 honoured) open the SSE writer, flush buffered notifications, write the final response, close; if the client did not offer SSE, drop the notifications and answer JSON. Long-running tools that call ReportProgress before finishing switch the sink to live mode: the first ReportProgress opens the SSE stream immediately so progress is delivered while the tool runs (the sink upgrade happens on the Indy worker thread that owns the connection). subscriptions/listen (modern only; legacy => -32601): TMCPSubscriptionsManager (src/Managers/MCPServer.SubscriptionsManager.pas, IMCPCapabilityManagerEx) validates params.notifications, computes the agreed subset (currently {} plus resourceSubscriptions only for existing URIs when resources.subscribe is advertised), registers TMCPSubscription {Id, Filter, Writer} in a locked registry, writes notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged with _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId = request id as the first message, returns rkDeferredStream; the transport loops WaitFor(shutdown or queue event, 15000 ms) writing queued notifications (each tagged with subscriptionId) or a keep-alive comment (doubles as disconnect probe); on client disconnect it exits silently; on Stop it writes the completion result {jsonrpc, id, result:{resultType:'complete', _meta:{io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId: id}}} then closes; Stop keeps a TThreadList of open writers, signals FShutdownEvent, waits up to N seconds, force-disconnects, then sets FHTTPServer.Active := False. TMCPRegistry gains an OnChanged event so a future dynamic registry can fan out list_changed and flip listChanged to true.
architecture.rationale: streamable-http.mdx Receiving Messages: 'The server MAY send JSON-RPC notifications ... before the final response. These notifications MUST relate to the originating client request'; 'The final JSON-RPC response SHOULD terminate the stream'; 'servers SHOULD include the X-Accel-Buffering: no header'; keep-alive comment lines are 'encouraged'. Cancellation: 'Closing the SSE response stream MUST be treated by the server as cancellation'. subscriptions.mdx: 'The server MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message ... and MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before it'; Graceful Closure result shape. Today HandlePostRequestSSE assigns one string to ContentText after ProcessRequest returns (IdHTTPServer.pas:488-501), so nothing can be streamed and Stop cannot close streams (:162-170).

architecture.component: stdio transport (concurrent reader/worker/writer, UTF-8, cancellation, shutdown)
architecture.change: TMCPStdioTransport keeps Create(ManagerRegistry, CoreManager) and Run; adds MaxConcurrentRequests (default 4; 1 = strictly sequential dispatch while still reading stdin), MinProgressIntervalMs, procedure Stop, property ShutdownEvent: TEvent, and owns a TMCPTransportSession (negotiated legacy version + client capabilities recorded at initialize) passed as Hints.Session. I/O: replace Text I/O with THandleStream over fd 0/1 (GetStdHandle on Windows); read bytes, split on #10, strip trailing #13, decode TEncoding.UTF8 (never TStreamWriter with UTF8 encoding, which can emit a BOM); write with TEncoding.UTF8.GetBytes(Json + #10) and flush through TMCPStdioWriter (IMCPMessageWriter, TCriticalSection around write+flush, one message per call). Run: reader loop on the calling thread; notifications are processed synchronously (notifications/cancelled => parse params.requestId (string or number, keyed by JSON text), log reason at Info, TMCPInflightRegistry.Cancel(id); unknown/finished ids ignored silently); requests are enqueued to a bounded TThreadPool/TTask worker whose completion writes the response through the writer unless Ctx.IsCancelled (then nothing is written, per stdio.mdx 'MUST NOT send any further messages for it'); TMCPInflightRegistry (TDictionary<string, IMCPRequestContext> + lock) registered before dispatch and removed after the response or cancel. Run returns on EOF or Stop: stop accepting, drain in-flight work with a bounded wait (2 s), write notifications/cancelled + completion result for open subscriptions, flush, close stdout. Create sets TLogger.UseStdErr := True and TLogger.StdoutReserved := True (DoWriteLog never falls back to Output while a stdio transport exists). Outer exception handler no longer writes an id:null -32603 line to stdout (StdioTransport.pas:73-95); write failures (EPIPE/EInOutError on stdout) terminate the loop. MCPServer.dpr: in stdio mode do not install the SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers (leave default terminate action) or make SignalHandler close fd 0 so Eof unblocks; ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown only in DEBUG and never in stdio mode (a leak dialog would hold the process open after EOF).
architecture.rationale: stdio.mdx: 'JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded' (transports/index.mdx) — Readln/Writeln on Input/Output use the ANSI code page on Windows (StdioTransport.pas:57,68); 'The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message'; 'Servers SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed'; Cancellation: 'Servers SHOULD stop work on a cancelled request as soon as practical and MUST NOT send any further messages for it'; Statelessness: 'clients may interleave unrelated requests on the same transport'. The current loop is strictly synchronous (StdioTransport.pas:54-96) so a cancel or legacy ping is unread until the running tool returns.

architecture.component: Tools: definitions, results, validation, era shaping
architecture.change: src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Base.pas additive: TMCPOptionalBool = (obUnset, obFalse, obTrue); TMCPToolAnnotations record (Title; ReadOnlyHint, DestructiveHint, IdempotentHint, OpenWorldHint: TMCPOptionalBool); TMCPIcon record (Src, MimeType, Theme; Sizes: TArray<string>); IMCPToolMetadata = interface ['{new GUID}'] GetAnnotations, GetIcons, GetMeta; IMCPToolContextAware = interface ['{new GUID}'] function ExecuteWithContext(const Arguments: TJSONObject; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TValue; all three base classes implement both (protected fields FAnnotations, FIcons, FMeta; helpers AddIcon(Src, MimeType, Sizes, Theme) rejecting non-https:///data: sources with a warning; SetReadOnly/SetDestructive/SetIdempotent/SetOpenWorld). New virtuals with default bodies: TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithParamsEx(const Params: T; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TMCPToolResult (default: TMCPToolResult.FromText(ExecuteWithParams(Params)) preserving the 'Error:' prefix heuristic behind TMCPToolsManager.LegacyErrorPrefixDetection default True); TMCPToolBase<T,R>.ExecuteWithParamsEx(const Params: T; const Ctx): R (default calls ExecuteWithParams). Class attributes [ToolAnnotations(...)] and [ToolIcon(...)] optional. New unit src/Tools/MCPServer.Tool.Result.pas: TMCPToolResult with AddText(Text; Annotations=nil), AddImage(Bytes, MimeType), AddAudio, AddResourceLink(Uri, Name, Description, MimeType, Title), AddEmbeddedText(Uri, Text, MimeType), AddEmbeddedBlob(Uri, Bytes, MimeType), SetStructuredContent(Value: TJSONValue owned; AddTextFallback=True), IsError, Meta, ToJSON(Era) (legacy 2025-06-18/2025-11-25: non-object structuredContent dropped, text kept; 2025-03-26: structuredContent dropped and resource_link downgraded to text); base64 via TBase64Encoding.Create(0) (no line breaks). TMCPToolsManager: keeps Create/ListTools/CallTool; adds ListTools(Params) overload with cursor pagination (PageSize 0 = single page; invalid cursor => -32602), ListTtlMs (default 0), ListCacheScope (default csPrivate; MCPServer.dpr sets csPublic/300000), deterministic order (TMCPRegistry keeps a registration-order TList<string>), FindTool(Name), OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool hooks, ValidateRequiredArguments (default False in 1.x, see open decision 5). CallTool: nil/malformed params or non-string name => EMCPError.InvalidParams (-32602); unknown tool => EMCPError.InvalidParams('Unknown tool: X') (-32602; today an isError text, ToolsManager.pas:245-248); absent 'arguments' => empty TJSONObject passed (today nil reaches TMCPSerializer.DeserializeObject 'for Pair in Json', Serializer.pas:111); dispatch via IMCPToolContextAware then IMCPTool; BuildToolCallResponse handles TMCPToolResult first, then the existing TJSONArray/string/TJSONObject forms — the TJSONObject branch now also emits content:[{type:'text', text: compact JSON}] (CallToolResult.content is required in every revision; tools.mdx 'a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block'); other TValue kinds become a text block. CreateToolJSON emits annotations (set hints only), icons, _meta from IMCPToolMetadata, omits empty description, gates title/outputSchema/icons/_meta for 2025-03-26 and non-object outputSchema for <2026-07-28. Schema generator: tkInteger/tkInt64 => 'integer'; Boolean by TypeInfo; TDateTime => string/date-time; recursive nested objects, typed items for dynamic arrays/TList<T>, sets => enum arrays; empty classes => {type:object, additionalProperties:false}; new attributes SchemaTitle, SchemaFormat, SchemaMinimum/Maximum, SchemaMinLength/MaxLength, SchemaPattern, SchemaDefault, SchemaName, SchemaHeader (x-mcp-header, Phase 8). Serializer: tkDynArray/TList/tkSet/non-Boolean enum serialization so structuredContent conforms to the generated outputSchema; nil object => omitted and generator does not list class-typed properties as required. Tool naming validated (^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$) with a warning (strict mode raises); duplicate registration warns instead of EListError.
architecture.rationale: schema.ts ListToolsResult extends PaginatedResult, CacheableResult (ttlMs, cacheScope required); tools.mdx Error Handling: 'Unknown tool' and 'Malformed requests' are protocol errors '-32602'; Tool.inputSchema may carry annotations/icons; 'Servers SHOULD return tools in a deterministic order' (today TDictionary order, ToolsManager.pas:223); x-mcp-header 'MUST only be applied to parameters with primitive types (integer, string, boolean). Parameters with type number are not permitted' — the generator currently maps Integer to 'number' (Schema.Generator.pas:115). Tool result content shapes per tools.mdx Tool Result.

architecture.component: Resources: errors, metadata, blobs, caching, templates
architecture.change: src/Resources/MCPServer.Resource.Base.pas additive: TMCPCacheScope = (csPublic, csPrivate); IMCPCacheableResource (GetTtlMs, GetCacheScope); IMCPResourceMetadata (GetTitle, GetSize, GetAnnotations, GetIcons, GetMeta); TMCPResourceContents record (URI, MimeType, Text, Blob: TBytes, IsBlob, Meta) with FromText/FromBytes; IMCPResourceReader (ReadContents: TArray<TMCPResourceContents>); IMCPResourceTemplate (GetUriTemplate/Name/Title/Description/MimeType, Matches(URI, Vars), CreateResource(URI, Vars)) with TMCPResourceTemplateBase implementing RFC 6570 level-1/2 matching via TRegEx named groups and percent-decoding; TMCPBinaryResourceBase. TMCPResourceBase<T> gains protected FTtlMs (default 0), FCacheScope (default csPrivate), FTitle, FSize (-1), FAnnotations, FIcons, FMeta and implements the new interfaces; IMCPResource itself is untouched. TMCPResourcesManager: keeps Create/ListResources/ReadResource/ListResourceTemplates; adds Params overloads with cursor pagination, ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope, FTemplates list fed by TMCPRegistry.RegisterResourceTemplate(UriTemplate, Factory)/GetResourceTemplateURIs/CreateResourceTemplate; ReadResource: Params=nil or uri not a TJSONString/empty => -32602 'Missing required parameter: uri'; URI syntax check (scheme ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:) at RegisterResource and ReadResource; exact lookup, then first matching template, else EMCPError.ResourceNotFound(Era, Uri) (never an empty contents array nor a text 'Error: Resource not found', ResourcesManager.pas:165-170); exceptions from Read propagate as -32603 instead of being written into 'text' (:155-163); Supports(IMCPResourceReader) for blob/multi contents else one text item; modern: ttlMs/cacheScope from IMCPCacheableResource (fallback 0/private) on read and from ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope on lists (same cacheScope on every page). Optional fields emitted only when set; title/_meta gated to >=2025-06-18, icons to >=2025-11-25. Built-ins: project://info and project://readme => 3600000/public; logs://recent and server://status => 0/private; Resource.Project reports the supported version list instead of MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION; drop the access-log side effect in TLogsRecentResource.GetResourceData or keep it documented. Shared pagination helper src/Protocol/MCPServer.Pagination.pas (cursor = Base64Url('v1:'+offset); unparsable/out-of-range/empty => -32602 'Invalid cursor'; nextCursor omitted at end, never '').
architecture.rationale: resources.mdx Error Handling: 'If the requested resource does not exist, servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 ... Servers MUST NOT return an empty contents array'; changelog minor 6 (-32002 => -32602) and basic/index.mdx 'MUST NOT emit -32002' (modern) versus 2025-11-25 'Resource not found: -32002' (legacy). caching.mdx: 'Servers MUST include caching hints on results ... resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read'; 'MUST apply the same cacheScope to all response pages'. pagination.mdx: 'Invalid cursors SHOULD result in an error with code -32602'; 'an empty string is a valid cursor'. IMCPResource.Read returns a single string (Resource.Base.pas:17) so binary contents are impossible today; System.NetEncoding's default Base64 inserts line breaks every 76 chars, hence TBase64Encoding.Create(0).

architecture.change: New src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.Base.pas: TMCPPromptArgument record (Name, Title, Description, Required); TMCPPromptMessages builder (AddText(Role, Text), AddImage(Role, Bytes, MimeType), AddAudio, AddResourceLink(Role, Resource), AddEmbeddedResource(Role, Contents)); IMCPPrompt = interface ['{new GUID}'] GetName/GetTitle/GetDescription/GetArguments/GetIcons/GetMeta; function Get(const Arguments: TJSONObject; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext; Messages: TMCPPromptMessages): string (returns description); TMCPPromptBase and generic TMCPPromptBase<T: class, constructor> mirroring TMCPToolBase<T>: arguments derived from T's writable string properties via RTTI reusing [SchemaDescription]/[Optional] (name = LowerCase(prop), required = not Optional), Get deserializes with TMCPSerializer and raises -32602 'Missing required argument: x' / 'Unknown argument'; abstract ExecuteWithParams(const Params: T; Messages: TMCPPromptMessages): string plus ExecuteWithParamsEx(Params, Ctx, Messages) virtual. TMCPRegistry adds RegisterPrompt(Name, Factory)/CreatePrompt/GetPromptNames/HasPrompt. New src/Managers/MCPServer.PromptsManager.pas (IMCPCapabilityManager + IMCPCapabilityManagerEx + IMCPCapabilityProvider {listChanged:false}): prompts/list (deterministic order, pagination, modern ttlMs/cacheScope), prompts/get (unknown name => -32602 with data {name}; arguments must be an object of strings; result {description?, messages[]} with NO ttlMs/cacheScope because GetPromptResult is not a CacheableResult; EMCPInputRequired => input_required in modern era, -32603 'Interactive input not supported by client' in legacy). New src/Managers/MCPServer.CompletionManager.pas: completion/complete over IMCPCompletable (Complete(ArgumentName, Value, Context): TMCPCompletion {Values <=100, Total, HasMore}) implemented optionally by prompts and resource templates; ref/prompt by name, ref/resource by uriTemplate then exact URI; missing argument.name/value => -32602; capability {completions:{}} only when registered. Sample prompt src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.SummarizeLogs.pas embedding logs://recent. MCPServer.dpr, MCPServer.dproj DCCReference list and build.bat -U paths gain src\Prompts.
architecture.rationale: prompts.mdx: 'Servers that support prompts MUST declare the prompts capability'; prompts/get result shape {description, messages[{role, content}]} + resultType; 'Invalid prompt name: -32602; Missing required arguments: -32602'. completion.mdx: 'Servers that support completions MUST declare the completions capability'; values 'Must not exceed 100 items'. Prompts/completion are MAY features but the frozen 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25 required server scenario sets include prompts-* and completion-complete, so 100% conformance needs them; they are additive units and can ship after the core phases.

architecture.component: MRTR / elicitation for tool, resource and prompt authors
architecture.change: New unit src/Protocol/MCPServer.Mrtr.pas: TMCPInputRequests builder (AddElicitationForm(Key, Message, Schema: TJSONObject owned), AddElicitationUrl(Key, Message, Url), AddSampling(Key, Params) and AddRoots(Key) marked 'deprecated 'SEP-2577'', keys unique via TDictionary); TMCPInputRequiredResult (InputRequests, RequestState; ToJSON raises if both empty); EMCPInputRequired = class(Exception) owning a TMCPInputRequiredResult, with class helpers Elicit(Key, Message, Schema; RequestState='') and WithState(RequestState); TMCPInputResponses wrapper over params.inputResponses with TryGetElicit(Key; out R: TMCPElicitResult {Action: eaAccept/eaDecline/eaCancel; Content: TJSONObject}) (malformed => -32602; unknown keys ignored), TryGetSampling, TryGetRoots; TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder (AddString/AddInteger/AddNumber/AddBoolean/AddEnum/AddMultiSelect producing the flat requestedSchema) and TMCPElicitSchema.Validate(Content, Schema): TArray<string>. New unit src/Core/MCPServer.RequestState.pas: TMCPRequestStateCodec with Key: TBytes (from [Security] RequestStateKey base64, else random per process with a logged warning), Pack(Payload: TJSONObject; Ctx; TtlSeconds): string = base64url(json{p, m: method, d: SHA-256 of canonical name+arguments/uri, u: principal or '', exp}) + '.' + base64url(HMAC-SHA256 via System.Hash.THashSHA2.GetHMACAsBytes), Unpack(State; Ctx; out Payload): Boolean with constant-time compare (hand-written), expiry, method, digest and principal checks; IMCPRequestStateStore hook for single-use enforcement. IMCPRequestContext gains SealState(Payload; Ttl) and TryOpenState(out Payload). Manager handling (only in TMCPToolsManager.CallTool, TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource, TMCPPromptsManager.GetPrompt; mrtr.mdx 'MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult responses on any other client requests'): catch EMCPInputRequired; modern era: verify every inputRequests entry against Ctx.ClientCapabilities (elicitation/create needs elicitation; mode url needs elicitation.url; form/absent needs elicitation.form or empty elicitation object; sampling/createMessage needs sampling (+sampling.tools when tools present); roots/list needs roots) and raise EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability with data {requiredCapabilities:{elicitation:{form:{}}}} (-32021, HTTP 400) otherwise; return {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests?, requestState?} with no ttlMs/cacheScope (the processor's safety net skips input_required); legacy era: tools => {content:[{type:'text', text:'This tool needs additional input (<message>) which requires MCP 2026-07-28; supply it as tool arguments'}], isError:true}; resources/prompts => -32603. The processor turns an EMCPInputRequired that reaches it from any other method into -32603 and logs it. Tampered or expired requestState => -32602 'Invalid request state' (SEC: mrtr.mdx 'MUST reject state that fails verification'). Elicitation rules enforced by the builders: url must be absolute (https unless Settings.AllowInsecureElicitationUrls); README documents 'MUST NOT use form mode for secrets'.
architecture.rationale: mrtr.mdx: 'Servers MUST send server-to-client requests ... using the MRTR pattern'; 'Servers MUST include at least one of inputRequests or requestState'; 'Servers MUST NOT send an inputRequests that the client has not declared support for'; 'servers MUST treat requestState as an attacker-controlled input ... MUST protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and MUST reject state that fails verification'; SHOULD embed principal, TTL and originating-request identifier. elicitation.mdx: form requests need requestedSchema (flat primitives), url requests need mode 'url' + url; 'Servers MUST NOT send elicitation requests with modes that are not supported by the client'. Legacy clients never understand input_required (2025-06-18 lifecycle 'Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated'), hence the era gate; legacy in-stream elicitation is out of scope.

architecture.component: Tool authoring example (shows the additive API in use; existing tools untouched)
architecture.change: unit YourProject.Tool.Deploy; type TDeployParams = class public [SchemaDescription('Target environment')] [SchemaEnum('staging','production')] property Environment: string read FEnv write FEnv; [Optional] [SchemaHeader('Region')] [SchemaDescription('Region')] property Region: string read FRegion write FRegion; end; TDeployResult = class public property DeploymentId: string ...; property Status: string ...; property Warnings: TArray<string> ...; end; TDeployTool = class(TMCPToolBase<TDeployParams, TDeployResult>) protected function ExecuteWithParamsEx(const Params: TDeployParams; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TDeployResult; override; public constructor Create; override; end; constructor TDeployTool.Create; begin inherited; FName := 'deploy'; FTitle := 'Deploy build'; FDescription := 'Deploys the current build'; SetReadOnly(False); SetDestructive(True); SetIdempotent(False); SetOpenWorld(True); AddIcon('https://example.com/icons/deploy.png', 'image/png', ['48x48']); end; function TDeployTool.ExecuteWithParamsEx(const Params: TDeployParams; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TDeployResult; var Confirm: TMCPElicitResult; begin if Params.Environment = 'production' then begin if not Ctx.InputResponses.TryGetElicit('confirm', Confirm) then raise EMCPInputRequired.Elicit('confirm', 'Deploy to PRODUCTION?', TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder.Create.AddBoolean('ok', 'I understand', False).Build, Ctx.SealState(TJSONObject.Create.AddPair('env', Params.Environment), 300)); if (Confirm.Action <> eaAccept) or not Confirm.Content.GetValue<Boolean>('ok', False) then raise EMCPToolError.Create('Deployment cancelled by user'); end; Ctx.ReportProgress(0.2, 1, 'Packaging'); Ctx.CheckCancelled; ... Ctx.ReportProgress(1, 1, 'Done'); Result := TDeployResult.Create; Result.DeploymentId := ...; end; initialization TMCPRegistry.RegisterTool('deploy', function: IMCPTool begin Result := TDeployTool.Create; end); Wire effect: tools/list shows annotations {readOnlyHint:false, destructiveHint:true, idempotentHint:false, openWorldHint:true}, icons, inputSchema with 'x-mcp-header':'Region' and outputSchema generated from TDeployResult (integer/array types correct); modern tools/call without inputResponses returns resultType input_required (+ -32021 if the client did not declare elicitation); the retry carries inputResponses.confirm and the sealed requestState; progress rides the SSE/stdio channel when the client sent _meta.progressToken; a legacy client gets an isError text asking for confirmation via arguments. Existing TEchoTool/TCalculateTool etc. keep overriding ExecuteWithParams and are unchanged.
architecture.rationale: Demonstrates that annotations, output schema, icons, progress and elicitation are all reachable through protected fields, one new virtual and the context, without touching TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithParams or IMCPTool (Tool.Base.pas:11-25, 44-60), which is the compatibility contract of the library.

architecture.change: New unit src/Core/MCPServer.Authorization.pas: TMCPAuthDecision = (adAllow, adUnauthorized, adForbidden, adBadRequest); TMCPPrincipal (Subject, Scopes, Claims; never the raw token); TMCPAuthChallenge (ResourceMetadataUrl, Scope, Error, ErrorDescription); IMCPAuthorizer = interface ['{new GUID}'] function Authorize(const BearerToken, HttpMethod, Path: string; out Principal: TMCPPrincipal; out Challenge: TMCPAuthChallenge): TMCPAuthDecision; TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer (constant-time compare); abstract TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer (ExpectedAudience required; virtual ValidateToken(Token; out Claims) with an RFC 7662 introspection implementation via System.Net.HttpClient; aud/exp enforced in the base so overrides cannot skip audience binding; JWT signature verification left to a sample unit); TMCPScopeHierarchy ([Auth] ScopeHierarchy=files:admin>files:write>files:read) and [RequiresScope('...')] attribute on tool classes checked in TMCPToolsManager.CallTool (EMCPInsufficientScope => 403 + WWW-Authenticate error='insufficient_scope', scope='all required'). TMCPIdHTTPServer: property Authorizer (nil = open, as today), invoked after Origin validation for GET/POST/DELETE (never OPTIONS, never the PRM path), token read only from the Authorization header ('Bearer ' case-insensitive), re-validated on every request; WriteAuthChallenge builds 'Bearer resource_metadata="..."[, scope="..."][, error="..."][, error_description="..."]' (offline_access filtered out) with 401/403/400 and an id-less JSON-RPC error body; GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[<Endpoint>] serves {resource, authorization_servers[], scopes_supported?, bearer_methods_supported:['header'], resource_name} when auth is enabled (authorization_servers must be https or loopback). TMCPStdioTransport never uses the authorizer. Settings [Auth]: Enabled=0, Mode=bearer|oauth, BearerTokens, ResourceUri, AuthorizationServers, ScopesSupported, RequiredScopes, ScopeHierarchy; [Security]: AllowedOrigins, AllowedHosts (optional 421), BearerToken, RequestStateKey, RateLimitPerMinute (token bucket per remote IP, 429 with -32603 body; 0 = off), RedactBodies (default True: log bodies only at Debug through TLogger.RedactJson blanking _meta, requestState, inputResponses and keys matching token|secret|password|authorization). logs://recent and server://status stay registered but private (or gated on Principal when auth is enabled).
architecture.rationale: authorization/index.mdx: 'Authorization is OPTIONAL' but when supported 'MCP servers MUST implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC9728)', 'MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience', 'Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive a HTTP 401', 'Servers MUST account for scope hierarchies'; 'Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification'. streamable-http.mdx: 'Servers SHOULD implement proper authentication'. security-considerations.mdx: 'The MCP server MUST NOT pass through the token it received from the MCP client'; tokens 'logged on the server' are an explicit threat — bodies are logged at Info today (IdHTTPServer.pas:331,555; StdioTransport.pas:62,70). README already advertises an Authorization header that nothing reads (README.md Integration with Claude Code).

architecture.change: TMCPSettings additive properties with ini defaults: [Server] BindAddress (default = Host), Instructions, Title, Description, WebsiteUrl, DiscoverTtlMs=3600000, EmitServerInfo=1, EndpointInfoPath=''; [Protocol] LenientModernPing=0, StrictRequiredArguments=0, MaxConcurrentStdioRequests=4; [Security]/[Auth] as above; [Tools] ListTtlMs, ListCacheScope; [Resources] ListTtlMs, ListCacheScope; new keys read with defaults so existing settings.ini files load unchanged (Settings.pas:143-155 pattern). build.bat/dproj: add src\Prompts and src\Tests paths, read DELPHI_PATH from env. New tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX) plus tests/golden/ and scripts/run-conformance.ps1. README: badge 2026-07-28 dual-era, 'Protocol versions and dual-era behaviour', 'Security', rewritten Inspector section (protocolEra legacy|auto|modern, --cli --method), 'Conformance testing', 'Migration guide for library consumers' (list of behaviour changes and escape hatches), expanded 'Creating Custom Tools/Resources/Prompts'.
architecture.rationale: Operators need switches for every spec MAY/SHOULD that changes visible behaviour; consumers need a migration guide; the repo has no tests (find returned nothing) so a harness is the precondition for refactoring the processor safely.

phases.name: Phase 0 - Test harness and legacy golden baseline
phases.goal: Pin today's legacy wire behaviour before touching the processor so every later phase can prove zero regression for legacy clients and library consumers.
steps: Create tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX, console runner, Win32/Win64) with a TestRegistry helper that builds TMCPManagerRegistry + TMCPCoreManager + TMCPToolsManager + TMCPResourcesManager exactly as MCPServer.dpr does (dpr:84-91).

Record golden responses for the current build through TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest: initialize (2025-03-26/2025-06-18/2025-11-25 requested), notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list, tools/call for echo/get_time/calculate/list_files (valid, invalid enum, unknown parameter, unknown tool, no arguments), resources/list, resources/read (each built-in + unknown URI), resources/templates/list, unknown method, parse error, id:null. Store as tests/golden/legacy-baseline/*.json with a normaliser for volatile fields (timestamps, sessionId, uptime).

Add an in-process Indy integration fixture that starts TMCPIdHTTPServer on an ephemeral port and drives it with TIdHTTP (record status codes, headers, bodies for POST JSON, POST with Accept: text/event-stream, GET, DELETE, OPTIONS, foreign Origin).
Add a stdio fixture that spawns MCPServer.exe --stdio (Windows) and round-trips lines, including a non-ASCII echo argument to document the current code-page defect (GAP-ST-02) as an expected-failure.
Document in tests/README.md which golden files are contractual for the legacy era (must stay byte-identical except for the spec-mandated fixes enumerated in the migration guide).
risks: Delphi cannot be compiled in the analysis sandbox; the harness must be built on a Windows box with Delphi 12+ and DUnitX from GetIt.
Golden files can over-constrain incidental ordering (TDictionary order) — normalise arrays where the spec does not mandate order.

phases.name: Phase 1 - Protocol core: errors, request context, era detection, server/discover, result envelope
phases.goal: Make the transport-independent processor dual-era: modern requests are recognised, validated and answered with resultType/_meta/serverInfo; legacy requests are answered exactly as before except for spec-required fixes; server/discover exists.
steps: Add constants/TMCPProtocolEra to MCPServer.Types.pas and the EMCPError family in new MCPServer.Errors.pas; alias the old JSONRPC_* identifiers in JsonRpcProcessor.pas and IdHTTPServer.pas.
Add MCPServer.RequestContext.pas (IMCPRequestContext, TMCPRequestContext, threadvar-backed Current, IMCPCapabilityManagerEx in Types.pas).

Rewrite TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx: parse + message validation (-32700/-32600), notification dispatch (ProcessNotification), BuildRequestContext (era rules 1/2/3/4), _meta validation (-32602 with HttpStatus 400, -32022 with data.supported/requested, logLevel check), modern-only method gate (-32601, LenientModernPing), dispatch preferring IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, result wrapping, resultType injection, _meta.serverInfo injection (EmitServerInfo, Settings overload), cacheable safety net (ttlMs 0 / cacheScope private) for the six cacheable methods, HTTP status policy; keep ProcessRequest(Body, SessionID) as a wrapper; keep LegacyNotFoundHeuristic for legacy era only.

TMCPCoreManager: server/discover (Discover), version negotiation in Initialize (echo 2025-06-18/2025-11-25, 2025-03-26 and anything else => 2025-11-25), record negotiated version + client capabilities in the transport session object (Hints.Session), remove FSessionID writes and the 'sessionId' body field, deprecated-capability warning for roots/sampling.

MCPServer.Capabilities.pas: TMCPCapabilityBuilder over IMCPManagerEnumerator (new interface implemented by TMCPManagerRegistry) and IMCPCapabilityProvider (implemented by TMCPToolsManager {listChanged:false} and TMCPResourcesManager {subscribe:false, listChanged:false}); RegisterExtension for a future 'extensions' map (modern only); static fallback when the registry does not enumerate.
Settings: Instructions, Title, Description, WebsiteUrl, DiscoverTtlMs, EmitServerInfo, LenientModernPing; BuildServerInfo shared by initialize, discover and _meta injection.

Tests: unit tests for BuildRequestContext (each rule), ValidateMeta, every EMCPError factory JSON, golden tests for modern discover/tools/list/tools/call/resources/* (resultType + serverInfo present) and re-run the legacy baseline (byte-identical except protocolVersion echo and removed sessionId/undefined capability keys).
risks: Managed threadvar for the ambient context must be nil'ed in a finally block or it leaks per Indy thread.
Consumers that raised Exception('... not found') from custom managers to obtain -32601 keep that only in the legacy era; documented.
Choice of supportedVersions content (modern-only) must be consistent with -32022 data.supported.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Streamable HTTP dual-era transport
phases.goal: Map the processor's status policy and header validation onto Indy, harden Origin/binding, make sessions stateless, and answer GET/DELETE with 405, without changing what a conformant legacy client sees.
steps: Add MCPServer.HttpHeaders.pas (DecodeMcpHeaderValue strict Base64 sentinel, ValidateStandardHeaders) and call it from ProcessRequestEx when Hints.HasHeaders and Era = peModern (order: presence/mismatch -32020 before -32022).

HandlePostRequest: build TMCPTransportHints from RawHeaders (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, all Mcp-Param-*), legacy header sanity (unknown version => 400 + -32600 body), call ProcessRequestEx, set ResponseNo := Res.HttpStatus, application/json by default; 202/204 responses use an empty ContentStream with ContentLength 0 (verify no Indy default HTML body with curl -i); dispatch notifications to managers before 202; stop minting/echoing Mcp-Session-Id and remove the Pos('"sessionId"') scraping (IdHTTPServer.pas:533-547); ignore Last-Event-ID; remove FEventIDCounter/GetNextEventID and 'id:' SSE lines.

ValidateOrigin (always) + ApplyCorsHeaders (only when CorsEnabled) with the extended Allow/Expose lists, reflected Access-Control-Request-Headers on preflight, Vary: Origin, 403 body with id-less JSON-RPC error; [Security] AllowedOrigins defaults to the CORS list, '*' remains an explicit opt-out with a logged warning.
GET/DELETE => 405 + Allow: POST, OPTIONS; optional Settings.EndpointInfoPath restores the info JSON on a non-MCP path; OPTIONS => 204 with ContentLength 0.
Start: explicit Bindings entry for BindAddress (default Settings.Host resolved; 0.0.0.0/* opt-in with warning); TLS 1.2+ only in the OpenSSL branch; USE_TAURUS_TLS define moved to src/MCPServer.inc.
Proper Accept parsing (all Accept headers, q=0, */*); JSON is the default response format; SSE only when streaming happens (Phase 5).
Thread safety: AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement in TServerStatusResource; TMCPRegistry dictionaries created in a class constructor; document 'register before Start'.

Batch decision: TJSONArray bodies => 400 + -32600 (2025-03-26 not in the servable set); IsRequestOnlyNotificationsOrResponses kept for the 202 shortcut; a POSTed JSON-RPC response object => 202 in legacy era, 400 + -32600 (id null) in modern era.

Tests: Indy integration fixture cases — mcp-method lowercase accepted; Mcp-Method: TOOLS/CALL => 400/-32020; Mcp-Name with surrounding spaces accepted; missing Mcp-Method on modern request => 400/-32020; header/_meta version mismatch => 400/-32020; MCP-Protocol-Version: 1900-01-01 => 400/-32022 with data.supported; no header + no _meta => legacy 200; no header + _meta => 400/-32602; unknown method modern => 404/-32601, legacy => 200/-32601; notification => 202 with Content-Length: 0; GET/DELETE => 405 + Allow; Origin http://evil.example => 403 even with CORS disabled; =?base64?SGVsbG8?= (bad padding) => 400/-32020; Base64 UTF-8 Mcp-Name equal to a non-ASCII resource URI accepted; 50 concurrent initialize calls => no AV.
risks: Indy internals (default body for empty responses, case-insensitive RawHeaders lookup, Bindings default) are asserted from RTL knowledge and must be verified on Windows with curl; no Indy source in the sandbox.
Binding to loopback by default and 405 on GET are visible behaviour changes for operators — mitigated by BindAddress/EndpointInfoPath settings and the migration guide.
Origin validation with CORS disabled may surprise browser-based setups that relied on Enabled=0; '*' opt-out documented.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Tools and resources conformance (envelopes, errors, content, schema, caching, pagination)
phases.goal: Make every built-in and consumer tool/resource produce schema-valid 2026-07-28 results while keeping ExecuteWithParams/GetResourceData authoring unchanged, and expose annotations/icons/output schema/binary contents additively.
steps: ToolsManager: tools/list envelope (ttlMs, cacheScope, deterministic registration order, cursor pagination with -32602 on invalid cursor), unknown tool and malformed params => EMCPError.InvalidParams (-32602), absent arguments => empty object, content array added for TJSONObject results with compact JSON text fallback, non-standard TValue kinds => text block, EMCPToolError => isError with message verbatim, LegacyErrorPrefixDetection switch, FindTool, OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool hooks, ValidateRequiredArguments (default False) and TMCPSchemaValidator subset (type/required/enum/properties/items/additionalProperties/min/max/minLength/maxLength/pattern/const, same-document $ref only, depth cap).

Tool.Base: TMCPToolAnnotations/TMCPIcon/IMCPToolMetadata/IMCPToolContextAware, protected fields + helpers, ExecuteWithParamsEx virtuals with default bodies on TMCPToolBase<T> and <T,R>, optional class attributes; MCPServer.Tool.Result.pas (TMCPToolResult builders, base64 without line breaks, era-shaping ToJSON).

Schema generator: 'integer' for Integer/Int64, Boolean by TypeInfo, TDateTime => string/date-time (serializer ISO 8601 both ways), recursive nested objects/typed arrays/TList<T>/sets with cycle guard, additionalProperties:false for empty param classes, new Schema* attributes; serializer: tkDynArray/TList/tkSet/non-Boolean enum output so structuredContent conforms to outputSchema; class-typed properties not marked required unless non-nil.
Tool naming validation and duplicate-registration warning in TMCPRegistry/TMCPToolsManager.

ResourcesManager: -32602/-32002 by era with data.uri, -32603 for read failures, uri param validation, URI syntax check, IMCPCacheableResource/IMCPResourceReader/IMCPResourceMetadata support, ttlMs/cacheScope on list/read/templates (modern), pagination, optional fields only when set with legacy gating; MCPServer.Pagination.pas and MCPServer.Uri.pas; built-in resources get ttl/scope values; Resource.Project reports the version list.
CreateToolJSON era shaping: omit title/outputSchema/icons/_meta for 2025-03-26, non-object outputSchema for <2026-07-28.

Tests: schema snapshots for all built-in tools (integer type, additionalProperties:false for get_time), tools/call with no arguments, unknown tool => -32602, invalid cursor => -32602, resources/read unknown => -32602+data.uri modern / -32002 legacy, blob round-trip, structuredContent validates against outputSchema for a sample <T,R> tool with arrays/enums, legacy golden re-run.
deliverables: updated Tool.Base, Resource.Base, ToolsManager, ResourcesManager, Schema.Generator, Serializer, Registration, built-in resources
risks: Emitted schema text changes ('integer', additionalProperties:false, nested shapes) break consumer snapshot tests — documented in the migration guide.
Resource-not-found and unknown-tool become JSON-RPC errors in both eras (spec-required); clients that displayed the text result see an error instead.
Serializer changes for enums/arrays alter structuredContent for tools that previously emitted wrong or missing fields (bug fix).

phases.name: Phase 4 - stdio transport modernisation (UTF-8, concurrency, cancellation, shutdown)
phases.goal: Make stdio a correct dual-era channel: UTF-8 framing, interleaved requests, cancellation and progress delivery, prompt exit on EOF/SIGTERM, nothing but MCP messages on stdout.
steps: Replace Text I/O with THandleStream-based UTF-8 line reader/writer; TMCPStdioWriter implements IMCPMessageWriter with a lock; LF-only output.

Reader thread loop + bounded worker pool (MaxConcurrentRequests, default 4; 1 = sequential) + TMCPInflightRegistry; notifications processed inline; notifications/cancelled cancels the in-flight context (reason logged) and suppresses the response; TMCPTransportSession per process carries the negotiated legacy version and client capabilities.

Progress: ReportProgress writes notifications/progress {progressToken (cloned JSON type), progress, total?, message?} through the writer before the response, monotonic and throttled; sealed after completion.

Shutdown: Stop/ShutdownEvent; EOF drains in-flight work (bounded), writes cancellation + completion results for open subscriptions (Phase 5), closes stdout; dpr does not install POSIX signal handlers in stdio mode (or closes fd 0 from the handler); ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown only in DEBUG non-stdio.
Logger: StdoutReserved guard; Create sets UseStdErr; body logging moved to Debug.
Remove the stdout write from the outer exception handler; stdout write failure terminates Run.
Tests: Windows spawn test with 'é'/emoji echo; interleaved ping during a slow test tool; cancel then verify no response is written; EOF exits within 2 s; SIGTERM exits on Linux.
risks: Consumer tools that were only ever exercised on stdio may not be thread-safe; MaxConcurrentRequests=1 is the escape hatch and the README states that tools already run concurrently on HTTP.
RTL code-page behaviour must be confirmed on Windows; Linux defaults to UTF-8 so the defect is platform-specific.

phases.name: Phase 5 - HTTP streaming (Indy SSE writer) and subscriptions/listen
phases.goal: Deliver request-scoped progress notifications on the POST response stream, treat client disconnect as cancellation, and offer a minimal but conformant subscriptions/listen stream.
steps: MCPServer.SseWriter.pas (TMCPSseWriter over TIdContext/TIdHTTPResponseInfo: WriteHeader once, IOHandler writes, keep-alive comments, disconnect detection, per-writer lock); pass Context into HandlePostRequest.

Buffering sink with lazy upgrade to SSE on the first notification when the client offered text/event-stream; final response terminates the stream; JSON when nothing was streamed; disconnect marks the context cancelled only in the modern era.

TMCPSubscriptionsManager (modern only): validate filter, agreed subset, acknowledged-first, subscriptionId tagging, deferred response marker; transport loop with WaitFor/keep-alive; TThreadList of open streams; Stop writes completion results and closes before deactivating Indy; stdio counterpart writes notifications/cancelled + completion on EOF/Stop; client notifications/cancelled on stdio stops the stream.
TMCPRegistry.OnChanged event plumbed so listChanged can become true later; capabilities remain false until a dynamic registry exists.

Tests: progress events precede the result on SSE; JSON response when no progress; client abort marks Ctx.IsCancelled and no further writes; subscriptions/listen gets acknowledged first, keep-alive comment within 20 s, completion result on Stop; legacy subscriptions/listen => -32601/200.
risks: Indy streaming (WriteHeader + IOHandler writes, close-delimited body) is the least verifiable part in the sandbox; prototype first with curl -N.
Each open listen stream pins an Indy worker thread; set MaxConnections and document.
Spec tension on teardown ordering (completion result vs notifications/cancelled) resolved as: HTTP completion result then close; stdio notifications/cancelled then completion result.

phases.name: Phase 6 - MRTR and elicitation for tool, resource and prompt authors
phases.goal: Give library consumers a safe, additive way to request user input (elicitation form/url) with integrity-protected requestState, capability gating and a defined legacy fallback.
steps: MCPServer.Mrtr.pas: TMCPInputRequests, TMCPInputRequiredResult, EMCPInputRequired, TMCPInputResponses, TMCPElicitResult, TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder, TMCPElicitSchema.Validate.

MCPServer.RequestState.pas: HMAC-SHA256 codec with principal/TTL/method/args-digest, constant-time compare, key from [Security] RequestStateKey or per-process random with warning, IMCPRequestStateStore hook; IMCPRequestContext.SealState/TryOpenState/InputResponses/RequestState.

Managers: catch EMCPInputRequired only in tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get; capability verification against Ctx.ClientCapabilities (-32021 with data.requiredCapabilities, HTTP 400); modern input_required result without caching fields; legacy fallback (isError text / -32603); processor converts stray EMCPInputRequired to -32603; tampered/expired state => -32602.

README section 'Elicitation (MCP 2026-07-28)' with the deploy example, security rules (no secrets via form mode; bind URL flows to the authenticated user; never pre-authenticated URLs; https URLs) and the dual-era caveat; deprecated AddSampling/AddRoots builders flagged with Delphi 'deprecated'.

Tests: modern tools/call => input_required with inputRequests; retry with inputResponses + requestState => complete; tampered/expired/other-principal state => -32602; missing elicitation capability => -32021/400 with requiredCapabilities; unknown inputResponses keys ignored; decline/cancel path; legacy tools/call => isError text; input_required never emitted from tools/list.
risks: A per-process random key breaks requestState across restarts and load-balanced instances; operators must configure RequestStateKey for multi-instance deployments.
Only modern clients (SDK-built, Inspector in modern/auto era) exercise this path today; legacy hosts get the isError fallback.

phases.name: Phase 7 - Prompts, resource templates, completion
phases.goal: Add the remaining server primitives as additive managers so the server can reach 100% of the frozen 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 required server scenarios.
steps: MCPServer.Prompt.Base.pas (IMCPPrompt, TMCPPromptBase, TMCPPromptBase<T>, TMCPPromptMessages builders) and TMCPRegistry prompt methods.
MCPServer.PromptsManager.pas (prompts/list with caching/pagination, prompts/get with -32602 semantics, MRTR support, capability provider) and sample prompt embedding logs://recent.

Resource templates: TMCPResourceTemplateBase with RFC 6570 level-1/2 matching, registry methods, ListResourceTemplates emitting registered templates, ReadResource template fallback; sample logs://{level}.
MCPServer.CompletionManager.pas with IMCPCompletable on prompts/templates; register in both Run* procedures of MCPServer.dpr; update dproj/build.bat paths.

Tests: prompts/list envelope; prompts/get unknown => -32602 with data.name; missing required argument => -32602; GetPromptResult has no ttlMs; template match/percent-decoding; completion values capped at 100 with hasMore.
risks: All three are MAY features; if the owner defers them, the server remains conformant but cannot score 100% on the frozen scenario sets.
Consumers who build their own registry must register the new managers to expose these capabilities (documented).

phases.name: Phase 8 - Authorization hooks, x-mcp-header, rate limiting, log hygiene
phases.goal: Provide opt-in resource-server authentication that follows the OAuth 2.1 MUSTs when enabled, plus the remaining security SHOULDs, without changing the default open behaviour.
steps: MCPServer.Authorization.pas (IMCPAuthorizer, TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer, TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer with mandatory audience/exp checks and RFC 7662 introspection, TMCPScopeHierarchy, [RequiresScope] attribute); TMCPPrincipal on IMCPRequestContext.

TMCPIdHTTPServer: Authorizer property, challenge writer (401/403/400 + WWW-Authenticate with resource_metadata/scope/error), RFC 9728 well-known endpoint, per-IP token bucket (429), Authorization never logged; stdio untouched.

x-mcp-header: SchemaHeaderAttribute emitted by the generator with constraint validation at RegisterTool (non-empty, RFC 9110 tchar, no CR/LF, case-insensitive uniqueness, string/integer/boolean only, top-level properties chain); TMCPToolsManager caches header bindings per tool; HttpHeaders validation of Mcp-Param-* (numeric compare for integers, 'true'/'false' for booleans, null/absent => header not expected, present-but-missing header => -32020); README warning not to annotate secrets/PII.
Log redaction (TLogger.RedactJson, bodies at Debug), [Security]/[Auth] settings, logs://recent gated on principal when auth is enabled.

Tests: static bearer accept/reject (401 + WWW-Authenticate), insufficient scope => 403 with error=insufficient_scope and full scope list, PRM document fields, audience mismatch => 401, x-mcp-header constraint rejections at registration, Mcp-Param-Region mismatch => 400/-32020, Inspector CLI without token exits with code 3.
deliverables: updated TMCPIdHTTPServer, TMCPSettings, TLogger, Schema.Generator, HttpHeaders, ToolsManager
risks: Server-side OAuth behaviour is not machine-scored by the conformance suite (only client-leg auth scenarios exist), so acceptance is DUnitX + a manual Inspector OAuth run.
JWT signature verification needs OpenSSL/TaurusTLS or a third-party JOSE unit; kept out of core.

phases.name: Phase 9 - Documentation, migration guide, conformance and Inspector acceptance, CI
phases.goal: Ship the release with a consumer migration guide, updated README/config, and repeatable conformance/Inspector runs for both eras.
steps: README: badge and Features for 2026-07-28 dual-era; 'Protocol versions and dual-era behaviour' (era detection, HTTP status mapping, headers, stateless sessions, 405 on GET/DELETE, curl examples for both eras); 'Using as a Library' checklist (UseStdErr, register managers incl. prompts/completion, register before Start, thread-safety, MaxConcurrentRequests); 'Creating Custom Tools/Resources/Prompts' with the additive APIs; 'Security'; 'Testing with MCP Inspector' (protocolEra legacy|auto|modern, --cli --method, exit code 3); 'Conformance testing'.

CHANGELOG.md + MIGRATION.md listing every behaviour change with its escape hatch (LegacyNotFoundHeuristic, LenientModernPing, EndpointInfoPath, AllowedOrigins '*', BindAddress, StrictRequiredArguments, LegacyErrorPrefixDetection, MaxConcurrentRequests, EmitServerInfo).
settings.ini.example with all new sections/keys and comments; build.bat reads DELPHI_PATH from env and adds src\Prompts; dproj DCCReference list updated.

scripts/run-conformance.ps1: start Win64\Release\MCPServer.exe, wait for the endpoint, run the official conformance CLI for --requirements 2026-07-28 and --requirements 2025-11-25 against the same URL with an expected-failures baseline (conformance-baseline.yml), then Inspector --cli smoke in legacy and modern eras; pin tool versions in package.json.

Manual client matrix executed and recorded in tests/MANUAL-MATRIX.md (Claude Code over HTTP, Codex over stdio, Claude Desktop stdio, VS Code, Inspector legacy/auto/modern, TypeScript SDK modern client).
Decide CI strategy (self-hosted Windows runner running build.bat + DUnitX + conformance, or documented manual release checklist).
risks: Conformance CLI flags/scenario names come from the external conformance repository and may drift; pin the version and re-check before release.
No Delphi on GitHub-hosted runners; CI needs a self-hosted Windows machine.

publicApiChanges.item: MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant (MCPServer.Types) keeps value '2025-06-18'; new MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION, MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION, MCP_META_* keys, MCP_ERROR_* codes, TMCPProtocolEra
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Old constant retained (comment: deprecated, use MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION / negotiated version); Resource.Project switched to the new list.

publicApiChanges.item: JSONRPC_* constants moved to MCPServer.Types; MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor and MCPServer.IdHTTPServer keep same-named aliases
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Aliases kept for one release; consumer code referencing MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor.JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR still compiles.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor: Create(ManagerRegistry) and ProcessRequest(const RequestBody, SessionID: string): string unchanged; new Create(ManagerRegistry, Settings) overload, ProcessRequestEx(Body, Hints, Sink): TMCPProcessResult, ProcessNotification, properties Settings/EmitServerInfo/LegacyNotFoundHeuristic/LenientModernPing, public class functions BuildRequestContext/ValidateMeta
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Old overload delegates with legacy hints; return string unchanged (a TJSONArray batch is now answered with -32600 instead of -32700 — only affects 2025-03-26 batching clients).

publicApiChanges.mitigation: Legacy behaviour preserved by default; consumers wanting -32601/-32602 raise EMCPError.MethodNotFound/InvalidParams; documented in MIGRATION.md.

publicApiChanges.item: IMCPCapabilityManager, IMCPManagerRegistry, IMCPTool, IMCPResource: GUIDs and members unchanged
publicApiChanges.mitigation: All extensions are new interfaces (IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityProvider, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPToolContextAware, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPPrompt, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPCompletable, IMCPAuthorizer) discovered with Supports(); consumers implementing the old interfaces directly get sensible defaults (no annotations, ttlMs 0/private, static capability mapping by GetCapabilityName).

publicApiChanges.mitigation: Session id was a non-schema body field no known client reads; README documents that custom core managers must implement server/discover to be dual-era.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPToolBase, TMCPToolBase<T>, TMCPToolBase<T,R>: constructors/abstract members unchanged; new protected fields FAnnotations/FIcons/FMeta and helpers; new virtual ExecuteWithParamsEx with default implementation calling ExecuteWithParams; implement IMCPToolMetadata and IMCPToolContextAware
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Subclasses overriding ExecuteWithParams compile unchanged; a subclass that already declares its own ExecuteWithParamsEx gets a name-hiding warning only (documented).

publicApiChanges.item: Tool result forms: string, TJSONObject and TJSONArray TValue results keep working; TJSONObject results now also carry a 'content' text block; new TMCPToolResult accepted; 'Error:' prefix => isError heuristic kept behind LegacyErrorPrefixDetection (default True); new EMCPToolError
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Additive; content array is required by every revision so its addition fixes previously invalid results.

publicApiChanges.mitigation: Spec-required wire change for error cases only (tools.mdx Error Handling); tools that guarded nil arguments keep working with an empty object.

authorizer challenge strings and PRM document; log redaction. 2) Protocol golden tests for both eras: tests/golden/legacy-baseline (recorded in Phase 0 from the current build, contractual for 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 clients) and tests/golden/modern-2026-07-28 (discover, tools/list, tools/call incl. no-arguments and input_required round trips, resources/list/read/templates, prompts/list/get, completion/complete, subscriptions/listen ack/completion, every error path with status code) compared with a normaliser for timestamps/uptime; a 'legacy diff allow-list' file enumerates the only permitted legacy differences (protocolVersion echo, removed sessionId and supportsProgress/supportsCancellation keys, resource-not-found/unknown-tool errors, content array on structured results). 3) Transport integration tests: in-process TMCPIdHTTPServer on an ephemeral port driven by TIdHTTP/System.Net.HttpClient for status codes, headers, 202 empty body, 405 Allow, Origin 403, CORS preflight reflection, SSE framing and progress ordering (curl -N verification documented for Indy streaming), disconnect-as-cancellation, subscriptions/listen keep-alive and graceful close on Stop, concurrency (50 parallel initialize/tools/call without AV), rate limit 429; stdio spawn tests on Windows and Linux (UTF-8 'é'/emoji round trip, LF framing, interleaved ping during a slow tool, cancel suppresses the response, EOF exit < 2 s, SIGTERM exit on Linux, nothing but JSON on stdout while LogToConsole is on). 4) Official tooling: scripts/run-conformance.ps1 runs the official conformance CLI (npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --requirements 2026-07-28 and --requirements 2025-11-25, with --expected-failures conformance-baseline.yml; scenario names such as dns-rebinding-protection, input-required-result-tampered-state, tools-call-with-progress, resources-read-binary, prompts-get-with-args, caching, server-stateless are the acceptance list; pin the package version and re-verify flags before release since the tool lives outside the spec repo) and MCP Inspector CLI smoke (npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli --config ./ci-servers.json --server delphi-modern --method tools/list --format json with protocolEra modern, again with protocolEra legacy and auto, and an auth-enabled entry asserting exit code 3 without a token); Inspector web/TUI manual pass in all three eras for tools, resources, prompts, subscriptions (modern Subscribe => acknowledged), MRTR pending-request modal and x-mcp-header display (Mcp-Param-* mirroring is only exercised by CLI/TUI, not the browser). 5) Manual client matrix (tests/MANUAL-MATRIX.md): Claude Code over HTTP (legacy initialize, tools/list, tools/call, resources), Codex over stdio, Claude Desktop stdio, VS Code Copilot HTTP, a TypeScript SDK modern client (per-request _meta, headers, discover), and a dual-era SDK client against the same endpoint to confirm it stays modern; each entry records protocol version negotiated, headers seen, and any 4xx observed. 6) Regression gate: every phase re-runs the legacy golden suite and the Phase 0 Indy/stdio fixtures before merge.
risks: Nothing in this plan could be compiled or executed in the analysis sandbox (no Delphi, no Indy sources); RTL/Indy behaviours relied upon (Text I/O code page, TBase64Encoding line breaks, WriteHeader + IOHandler streaming with close-delimited bodies, default HTML body for empty responses, case-insensitive RawHeaders.Values, Bindings default) must be verified on Windows before the corresponding phase is signed off.

Legacy hosts (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Inspector default era) remain the dominant traffic; any accidental change to legacy output is the highest-impact regression, hence the Phase 0 golden baseline and the per-era gating of every injected field.

Spec-mandated behaviour changes that consumers may notice: resource-not-found and unknown-tool become JSON-RPC errors, GET on the MCP endpoint returns 405, Origin is validated even with CORS disabled, sessions are no longer minted, loopback binding by default, JSON instead of SSE for plain requests, integer schema type. Each is documented with an escape hatch where the spec allows one.

Concurrency: the stdio transport moves from single-threaded to worker threads; consumer tools that mutate shared state without locks may race (they already do on HTTP). MaxConcurrentRequests=1 mitigates; shared library state (TServerStatusResource counters, TLogBuffer, TMCPRegistry) is made atomic/locked.

Indy long-lived SSE streams pin worker threads and depend on close-delimited bodies; misconfigured reverse proxies may buffer; X-Accel-Buffering and keep-alive comments reduce but do not eliminate this.
HTTP 404 has opposite meanings across eras; a bug in era detection that returns 404 to a legacy client would trigger re-initialize loops — covered by explicit tests for -32601 status per era.

Dual-era clients decide era from the 400 body; any 4xx returned to a modern request without a recognised modern JSON-RPC error body would push such clients to legacy mode — every 4xx path in the transport carries the body.

Conformance and Inspector tooling versions drift (scenario names, flags, error code renumbering already happened once: -32001/-32003/-32004 => -32020/-32021/-32022); pin versions and re-check before release.
requestState HMAC keys generated per process break MRTR across restarts or load-balanced instances unless RequestStateKey is configured.

Delphi threadvars holding managed types are not finalised automatically; the ambient context must be released in a finally block on every path (including exceptions) to avoid leaks under Indy's thread pool.

Effort estimate (about 64 senior-Delphi days) assumes one developer with Delphi 12+, TaurusTLS and DUnitX already set up; prompts/templates/completion (Phase 7) and auth (Phase 8) can be deferred without affecting core conformance.
openDecisions: Legacy version set: keep 2025-03-26 servable (requires JSON-RPC batch receiving, GAP-BP-18/GAP-HTTP-13/GAP-ST-05) or answer a 2025-03-26 initialize with 2025-11-25 (permitted by 2025-11-25 lifecycle 'Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports'). Recommended default: servable legacy set = 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25; accept a 2025-03-26 initialize by answering 2025-11-25; reject array bodies with -32600 in both eras.

supportedVersions and -32022 data.supported content: only versions servable via per-request _meta (['2026-07-28']) or also legacy versions (the versioning.mdx example lists both). Recommended default: modern-only list, because a modern client would otherwise retry with a legacy version in _meta, which the server cannot serve statelessly; legacy availability is documented in README and discover instructions.

Legacy sessions: stateless in both eras (never mint or echo Mcp-Session-Id; no 400/404 session obligations) versus a per-session store in the HTTP transport. Recommended default: stateless (option A) — spec MAY, removes the FSessionID race and the body-scraping, and matches today's effective behaviour for SSE-accepting clients (the SSE path never set the header).

resultType and _meta.serverInfo injection: modern-only (recommended) or unconditional (legacy Result schemas are open and would tolerate it). Recommended default: modern-only, keeping legacy responses byte-identical and the golden baseline meaningful; a TMCPSettings switch is unnecessary.

Strict required-argument validation (StrictRequiredArguments/ValidateRequiredArguments): on by default (schema promises 'required') or off to preserve current lenient deserialisation. Recommended default: off in this release with a deprecation note, on in the next major version.

Default bind address: loopback (spec SHOULD; README currently claims localhost) versus all interfaces (current effective behaviour, used by remote/Cloudflare-tunnel setups). Recommended default: BindAddress = Settings.Host resolved (localhost => 127.0.0.1) with an explicit BindAddress=0.0.0.0 opt-in and a CHANGELOG callout.
GET endpoint-info JSON: remove, or keep on a separate path. Recommended default: remove from the MCP endpoint (405) and offer Settings.EndpointInfoPath (default disabled).

Cache hints for the sample server: tools/list and resources/list public with ttlMs 300000 (static sets, no auth) versus library defaults 0/private. Recommended default: library defaults 0/private (never wrong under CA-05); MCPServer.dpr sets public/300000 for the sample; project://info and project://readme 3600000/public; logs://recent and server://status 0/private.
Scope of Phase 7 (prompts, resource templates, completion): ship in this release or defer. Recommended default: ship (needed for 100% on both frozen conformance sets; purely additive units).
LenientModernPing: answer ping for modern _meta requests (tolerant, technically non-conformant) or -32601/404. Recommended default: False (strict), setting available.
Modern parse error HTTP status: 400 (recommended, matches 'MUST return an HTTP error status code' for unacceptable input) versus 200; legacy parse errors stay 200 to keep current behaviour.
Default stdio concurrency (MaxConcurrentRequests): 4 (recommended; cancellation and ping stay responsive) versus 1 (strictly sequential, zero surprise for non-thread-safe consumer tools).

Keep logs://recent and server://status registered by default in the sample server (they expose process telemetry and log lines to any client). Recommended default: keep, mark private, gate on principal when auth is enabled, and document how to unregister.

RequestStateKey persistence for multi-instance deployments: config-provided base64 key (recommended for anything behind a load balancer) versus per-process random key (development default with a warning).
CI strategy: self-hosted Windows runner executing build.bat, DUnitX and the conformance script (recommended) versus a documented manual release checklist, given no Delphi on GitHub-hosted runners.

Whether to validate the legacy MCP-Protocol-Version header strictly (2025-11-25 transports: invalid/unsupported => 400). Recommended default: reject only values that are in neither the legacy nor the modern list; absent header => legacy 2025-03-26 semantics/negotiated version.
outOfScope: Acting as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server (2025-03-26 authorization model, /authorize, /token, DCR endpoints): the spec places the AS outside the MCP server; only the resource-server role (PRM document, bearer validation, challenges) is in scope, and 2025-03-26 clients are served unauthenticated only.
JWT signature verification in the core library (no JOSE in the Delphi RTL); shipped as a sample authorizer using TaurusTLS/OpenSSL or a third-party unit.

Tasks extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks: tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel, CreateTaskResult, task store): optional extension disabled by default per extensions/overview.mdx; GAP-TSK-01 deferred to a later release after MRTR and subscriptions exist.

Server-side use of deprecated features: Roots (roots/list), Sampling (sampling/createMessage) and Logging (logging capability, logging/setLevel, notifications/message) — 2026-07-28 changelog 'New implementations should not adopt them'; the server keeps TLogger on stderr/file and only validates io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel. Builders for sampling/roots inputRequests exist only as deprecated helpers.

Legacy in-stream elicitation/sampling (server-initiated JSON-RPC requests on SSE streams for 2025-xx clients): requires per-session request/response correlation across HTTP requests and blocking Indy threads; MRTR is the only supported elicitation path, legacy clients get an isError fallback.
HTTP+SSE transport (2024-11-05) endpoints: deprecated since 2025-03-26 and 'New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it'.
SSE resumability (Last-Event-ID, event ids, redelivery): removed in 2026-07-28 and optional in legacy; the server implements no replay.

Extensions beyond the empty extensions map (MCP Apps/UI, OAuth client credentials, enterprise-managed authorization): extension ids can be registered by consumers but no extension behaviour is implemented.
A full JSON Schema 2020-12 validator with remote $ref resolution: only a same-document subset validator is provided; remote $ref is never dereferenced (basic/index.mdx MUST NOT).
OpenTelemetry trace propagation (traceparent/tracestate/baggage in _meta): reserved keys are passed through untouched but not consumed.
Dynamic (post-Start) tool/resource registration with listChanged notifications: registries stay immutable after Start; TMCPRegistry.OnChanged and the subscriptions manager leave the door open.
Unix domain socket / TCP variants of the stdio framing (custom transports).
Windows service/daemon packaging, installer changes, and non-Windows build scripts beyond documenting the Linux64 MSBuild/PAServer path.

plans.lens: OPERATIONS / STATELESS-FIRST: gateway- and load-balancer-friendly (routable headers validated but never trusted for dispatch, no server-minted sessions in either era, cacheable and deterministic list results, HMAC-protected requestState that works across instances), real SSE streaming in Indy (progress, subscriptions/listen with keep-alives, stream close = cancel), thread-safety under Indy's thread-per-connection model and a newly concurrent stdio loop, Linux + Windows parity, observability (W3C trace-context passthrough from _meta, structured/redacted stderr logging, health endpoint), and a pluggable HTTP authorization hook (bearer/OAuth resource-server) with a principal that flows into tools, cacheScope and requestState.
plans.summary: Turn the single-version 2025-06-18 server into a dual-era, stateless server in nine phases. The pivot is one transport-independent request pipeline in TMCPJsonRpcProcessor (new ProcessRequestEx) that (1) detects the era per message — 'initialize' => legacy; params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] => modern; otherwise legacy at the header-declared or process-negotiated legacy revision — (2) validates modern _meta and HTTP headers (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param-*) with the exact JSON-RPC codes (-32020/-32021/-32022/-32602) and HTTP statuses (400/404 modern only; never 404 for legacy), (3) builds a per-request TMCPRequestContext (era, version, client capabilities, logLevel, progressToken, trace context, principal, cancellation, notification sink) reachable by unchanged managers/tools through a threadvar and by new code through additive interfaces, and (4) injects the modern envelope centrally (resultType, _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo, default ttlMs/cacheScope on the six cacheable methods) so legacy responses stay byte-identical and third-party managers become schema-valid without code changes. Sessions are removed in both eras (spec MAY; the current FSessionID is a data race, CoreManager.pas:17/:97), which makes every HTTP request routable to any instance; legacy version continuity comes from the MCP-Protocol-Version header on HTTP and from a single per-process side-slot on stdio. Errors become typed (EMCPError with code/data/HTTP status), replacing the Pos('not found') heuristic that today mislabels 'Tool not found'/'Resource not found' as -32601 (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214) — a dual-era hazard because modern clients treat unknown-method/404 as 'legacy server'. Indy gains a real SSE writer (WriteHeader + IOHandler writes, ':' keep-alives doubling as disconnect probes, disconnect = cancellation in the modern era only) and a drain-aware Stop; stdio gains a reader thread + serialized writer + bounded worker pool so cancellation, legacy ping and interleaved modern requests are honoured. Later phases add prompts/completion/templates, MRTR + elicitation with an HMAC-SHA256 requestState codec whose key is shared across instances, x-mcp-header mirroring, and an IMCPAuthorizer hook with RFC 9728 metadata.
