Library consumers keep compiling: no member is added to IMCPTool, IMCPResource, IMCPCapabilityManager or IMCPManagerRegistry; everything new is an additive interface discovered with Supports(), a constructor overload, a virtual with a default, or a settings key with a safe default.
plans.compatStrategy:
ERA MODEL. Era is a property of each message, never of the connection (basic/index.mdx § Statelessness; versioning.mdx § Compatibility Matrix: 'A request carrying modern per-request _meta is served statelessly ... An initialize request selects legacy semantics ... A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently'). Detection lives in one function, TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.BuildRequestContext(Method, Params, Hints): (1) method = 'initialize' => peLegacy, negotiate params.protocolVersion per 2025-11-25 lifecycle.mdx § Version Negotiation ('If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise ... another protocol version it supports'); any _meta is ignored. (2) params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] is a TJSONString => peModern; HTTP header checks first (absent or ≠ _meta => -32020/400, streamable-http.mdx § Protocol Version Header + § Server Validation 'A required standard header ... is missing'), then version ∈ MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS else -32022/400 with data.supported/requested (versioning.mdx § Protocol Version Negotiation), then clientCapabilities must be a TJSONObject else -32602/400 (basic/index.mdx § _meta 'A request missing any required field is malformed ... -32602 ... On HTTP ... 400'), logLevel ∈ 8 levels else -32602 (logging.mdx § Error Handling), then Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name/Mcp-Param-* (-32020/400). (3) no modern _meta: HTTP: MCP-Protocol-Version header names a modern version => modern request lacking required _meta => -32602/400; names a legacy version => peLegacy at that version; absent => peLegacy assumed 2025-03-26 (2025-06-18 transports.mdx § Protocol Version Header SHOULD; 2026-07-28 streamable-http MAY); unknown value => 400 with -32600 body (legacy MUST 400, 2025-06-18 transports.mdx). stdio: peLegacy at the process side-slot NegotiatedLegacyVersion (set by initialize) or MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION when no initialize happened (permissive, matches today). Modern-era requests for legacy-only methods (initialize is caught by rule 1; ping, logging/setLevel, resources/subscribe, resources/unsubscribe, roots/list) => -32601 (+404 on HTTP; changelog.mdx major changes 4-5; streamable-http.mdx 'If the server does not implement the requested RPC method, it MUST respond with 404 Not Found and ... -32601'). Legacy-era requests never get 404 (2025-11-25 transports.mdx § Session Management item 3-4 makes 404 mean 'session terminated, re-initialize').

HTTP TRANSPORT COEXISTENCE. Single endpoint (Settings.Endpoint) serves both eras. Sessions: never minted, never echoed in either era (legacy: 'MAY assign a session ID' — we do not; modern: 'ignore it, and do not mint or echo session IDs', streamable-http.mdx § Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions). Consequence: no sticky routing required; any instance can answer any request. Legacy revision continuity across requests comes from the MCP-Protocol-Version header (2025-06-18+ clients MUST send it after initialize). GET and DELETE answer 405 + Allow: POST, OPTIONS in both eras (legacy MUST 'either return text/event-stream ... or else return HTTP 405', 2025-11-25 transports.mdx § Listening for Messages item 3; modern SHOULD 405). Last-Event-ID ignored, SSE ids dropped (changelog.mdx major change 9). Origin validated for every request independent of CORS (streamable-http.mdx § Security & Endpoint MUST). Status mapping is era-gated inside the processor (single source of truth, TMCPProcessResult.HttpStatus). SSE POST responses: default application/json; text/event-stream only when a request-scoped notification is emitted or for subscriptions/listen (modern only; legacy requests never get a long-lived stream). Disconnect = cancellation only in the modern era (streamable-http.mdx § Cancellation MUST; legacy 'Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling', 2025-06-18 transports.mdx § Sending Messages item 6). Every 4xx returned to a modern request carries the JSON-RPC error body so dual-era clients do not misdetect a legacy server (streamable-http.mdx § Backward Compatibility).

STDIO COEXISTENCE. One process serves both eras concurrently: server/discover always answers DiscoverResult regardless of whether initialize happened (versioning.mdx 'The era determination is a property of the server'; stdio.mdx § Backward Compatibility), and initialize keeps working after modern requests. The only process state is NegotiatedLegacyVersion (allowed: 'scoped to the stdio process'). No header layer: hints.HasHeaderLayer = False so header rules are skipped (stdio.mdx § Request Metadata).

LIBRARY CONSUMERS. Interfaces with GUIDs are frozen: IMCPCapabilityManager (Types.pas:39-44), IMCPManagerRegistry (:46-50), IMCPTool (Tool.Base.pas:11-25), IMCPResource (Resource.Base.pas:11-23). New behaviour is reached via new GUID'd interfaces probed with Supports() (IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityDeclaration, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPContextAwareTool, IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPPrompt, IMCPCompletable, IMCPAuthorizer), via the ambient threadvar TMCPRequestContext.Current (safe because Indy runs one connection per thread and the stdio pool sets it per work item), via constructor overloads (TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.Create(Registry, Settings); TMCPStdioTransport.Create(Registry, CoreManager, Settings)), via virtuals with defaults (TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithContext calls ExecuteWithParams), and via settings keys with safe defaults. TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest(Body, SessionID): string stays as a thin wrapper (SessionID ignored) so third-party transports compile. Old constants stay (MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-06-18' kept as deprecated alias; JSONRPC_* re-exported from MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor as aliases of MCPServer.Types). Wire-level behaviour changes that consumers must know (documented in CHANGELOG): unknown tool/resource become JSON-RPC errors instead of text results; initialize result loses sessionId/supportsProgress/supportsCancellation; GET returns 405; server binds loopback by default; stdio executes tools on worker threads unless MaxConcurrentRequests=1; required tool parameters are enforced unless TMCPSerializer.StrictMode=False.

architecture.change: Add to MCPServer.Types: MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2026-07-28'; MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS=['2026-07-28']; MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS=['2025-11-25','2025-06-18'] (2025-03-26 accepted on initialize but negotiated up, see open decisions); MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2025-11-25'; MCP_META_* key constants (io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, clientCapabilities, clientInfo, logLevel, serverInfo, subscriptionId, progressToken, traceparent/tracestate/baggage); MCP_LEGACY_ONLY_METHODS; MCP_LOG_LEVELS; JSONRPC_* moved here plus MCP_ERROR_HEADER_MISMATCH=-32020, MCP_ERROR_MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY=-32021, MCP_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION=-32022, MCP_ERROR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND_LEGACY=-32002 (legacy era only), MCP_RESULT_TYPE_COMPLETE/INPUT_REQUIRED; TMCPProtocolEra=(peLegacy, peModern). Keep MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION as 'deprecated' alias. New unit MCPServer.Errors: EMCPError(Code, Message, Data: TJSONValue owned, HttpStatus: Integer=0 meaning 'derive from era policy') with factories MethodNotFound, InvalidParams, InvalidRequest, InternalError, UnsupportedProtocolVersion(Requested, Supported) => data {supported[], requested}, MissingRequiredClientCapability(Required: TJSONObject) => data {requiredCapabilities}, HeaderMismatch(Detail), ResourceNotFound(Uri, Era) => -32602 modern / -32002 legacy with data {uri}; EMCPToolError (isError result); EMCPInputRequired (MRTR). Delete duplicate JSONRPC_* consts in IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99; keep aliases in JsonRpcProcessor.pas:27-32 for one release.
architecture.rationale: Codes must be emitted only with spec-defined meanings (basic/index.mdx § Error Codes: '-32020 to -32099 ... MUST use defined codes only with their specified meanings'; -32002 MUST NOT be emitted by 2026-07-28 implementations). Today the code is inferred from exception text: Pos('not found', E.Message) => -32601 (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215), so TMCPRegistry.CreateTool 'Tool not found: %s' (Registration.pas:76), 'Resource not found' (:88) and even 'SSL Certificate file not found' (IdHTTPServer.pas:370) become Method-not-found; once -32601 maps to HTTP 404 in the modern era this would flip probing clients into legacy mode. Error data is needed for -32021/-32022 and CreateErrorResponse has no data parameter (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:128-144).

architecture.component: Request context, transport hints, process result (transport-independent core)
architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.RequestContext: IMCPRequestContext {Era; ProtocolVersion; Method; RequestId: TJSONValue (clone); ClientCapabilities: TJSONObject (borrowed, nil for legacy pre-initialize); ClientInfo; LogLevel; ProgressToken: TJSONValue; TraceParent/TraceState/Baggage: string (from _meta, read-only); Principal: IMCPPrincipal (nil when no authorizer); Transport: (ttStdio, ttHttp); RemoteAddress; IsCancelled; CheckCancelled (raises EMCPRequestCancelled); ReportProgress(Progress, Total=-1, Msg=''); SendLog(Level, Logger, Data) (no-op unless LogLevel set; never used by core); RequireClientCapability(const Path: string) => raises EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability; HasClientCapability(Path); InputResponses; RequestState; Extensions: TArray<string>}. TMCPRequestContext implements it with an interlocked cancel flag, monotonic progress guard and min-interval throttle (MinProgressIntervalMs default 100). class property Current backed by a threadvar, set/cleared by the processor around dispatch. TMCPTransportHints record {HasHeaderLayer; ProtocolVersionHeader; McpMethodHeader; McpNameHeader; ParamHeaders: TArray<TPair<string,string>>; AcceptsSse; RemoteAddress; Principal; NegotiatedLegacyVersion (stdio side-slot, in/out); NotificationSink: IMCPNotificationSink; CancelToken}. IMCPNotificationSink {procedure Send(const Json: TJSONObject)} implemented by the SSE writer (HTTP) and the locked stdout writer (stdio). TMCPProcessResult record {Body: string; HttpStatus: Integer; IsNotification; Era; ProtocolVersion; ErrorCode; Deferred: Boolean; Stream: IMCPStreamHandle}.
architecture.rationale: Managers get only (Method, Params) today (Types.pas:43; JsonRpcProcessor.pas:125) and tools only Arguments (Tool.Base.pas:18); tool instances are singletons shared across Indy threads (ToolsManager.pas:84-94, :245), so per-request state must travel as a parameter or thread-local, never as a field. A single hints record lets DUnitX drive every HTTP rule without Indy. Trace-context fields are reserved _meta keys the server must not interpret (basic/index.mdx § _meta 'implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at these keys') — they are captured for logging/propagation only.

architecture.component: JSON-RPC processor pipeline (era detection, validation, envelope, status policy)
architecture.change: Add function ProcessRequestEx(const Body: string; const Hints: TMCPTransportHints): TMCPProcessResult (old ProcessRequest delegates with default hints). Pipeline: parse (-32700; JSON array => legacy 2025-03-26 batch only if enabled, else -32600) → structural validation (jsonrpc='2.0', method non-empty string, id absent|string|integer; id null/bool/object/array or fractional => -32600 with id null; params present but not object => -32602) → notification path (dispatch to InflightRegistry for notifications/cancelled; to manager via ExecuteMethod for others inside try/except; return IsNotification=True, no body) → BuildRequestContext (era detection and all -32020/-32021/-32022/-32602 checks described in compatStrategy) → legacy-only method gate for modern era (-32601) → dispatch: if Supports(Manager, IMCPCapabilityManagerEx) then ExecuteMethodEx(Ctx, Method, Params) else ExecuteMethod(Method, Params), with TMCPRequestContext.Current set in try/finally → result normalisation: TValue.Empty => {}; string that parses to an object => that object, else {"value": s} + warning; TJSONObject as-is → modern envelope injection: AddPair('resultType','complete') if absent (managers set 'input_required' themselves); if Settings.EmitServerInfo and _meta lacks io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo add {name, version, title?, description?, websiteUrl?}; for Method in [server/discover, tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read] add ttlMs:0 / cacheScope:'private' when absent → status policy: peModern: -32020/-32021/-32022 => 400; -32602 raised with HttpStatus=400 (meta/header validation) => 400; -32601 => 404; -32700/-32600 => 400; others 200. peLegacy: -32700/-32600 => 400; everything else 200 (never 404). EMCPError.HttpStatus overrides. Catch order: EMCPRequestCancelled => no body; EMCPInputRequired reaching the processor => -32603 'InputRequiredResult not permitted for method'; EMCPError => its code/data; Exception => -32603 (no substring heuristics).
architecture.rationale: Every response passes through ProcessRequest (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:146-224), so central injection makes custom managers schema-valid for 2026-07-28 (Result.resultType 'Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field'; caching.mdx 'Servers MUST include caching hints ... MUST provide a ttlMs value that is >= 0'; basic/index.mdx per-response serverInfo SHOULD) while legacy responses stay byte-identical. Today id:null is silently treated as a notification (:82-87, :174-181) although 'the ID MUST NOT be null' (basic/index.mdx § Requests), responses may omit result (:192-200), notifications never reach managers, and HTTP status is always 200 (IdHTTPServer.pas:509, :553). ttlMs 0 / private is the only default that can never be wrong for an authenticated deployment (caching.mdx § Security Considerations).

architecture.component: Core manager: server/discover, legacy initialize negotiation, capability builder, no sessions
architecture.change: TMCPCoreManager implements IMCPCapabilityManagerEx and IMCPCapabilityDeclaration; HandlesMethod adds 'server/discover'. Discover(Ctx): {resultType:'complete', supportedVersions: MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (see open decision), capabilities: TMCPCapabilityBuilder.Build(peModern), instructions (omit if ''), ttlMs: Settings.DiscoverTtlMs (default 3600000), cacheScope: 'public' unless an authorizer is configured (then 'private'), _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo}. Initialize: Requested := params.protocolVersion; Negotiated := Requested if in MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS else MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION; write Negotiated into Hints.NegotiatedLegacyVersion (stdio side-slot); capabilities from the builder with legacy shape tools:{listChanged:false}, resources:{subscribe:false, listChanged:false}, prompts:{listChanged:false} only when a prompts manager is registered; serverInfo {name, version, title?}; instructions?; drop sessionId and supportsProgress/supportsCancellation; log deprecated client capabilities (roots/sampling) at Warning (SEP-2577). Delete FSessionID write; SessionID property returns '' (deprecated). New unit MCPServer.Capabilities: TMCPCapabilityBuilder.Build(Era; Registry: IMCPManagerEnumerator): for each manager Supports(IMCPCapabilityDeclaration) ? GetCapabilityDeclaration : name-based fallback ('tools'/'resources'/'prompts'/'completions' => {}); adds 'extensions' map (modern only, only when non-empty; ids validated against _meta prefix rules). TMCPManagerRegistry implements new IMCPManagerEnumerator (GetManagers).
architecture.rationale: 'Servers MUST implement it [server/discover]' (discover.mdx; versioning.mdx § Protocol Version Negotiation) and DiscoverResult requires resultType, supportedVersions, capabilities, ttlMs, cacheScope (schema.ts DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult). Initialize today always answers MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION (CoreManager.pas:101) ignoring params.protocolVersion, violating 'If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version' (2025-11-25 lifecycle.mdx § Version Negotiation); it emits non-schema keys supportsProgress/supportsCancellation and a body sessionId (:106-114, :126) and overwrites a shared FSessionID from every Indy thread (:97). Capabilities are hard-coded so a consumer registering only TMCPToolsManager still advertises resources ('Servers that declare the resources capability MUST respond to resources/list', resources.mdx § Capabilities). Removing sessions is the stateless-first choice: legacy sessions are MAY (2025-11-25 transports.mdx § Session Management) and modern forbids minting.

architecture.component: HTTP header validation (routable headers validated, never trusted for dispatch)
architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.HttpHeaders with pure, unit-testable functions: DecodeMcpHeaderValue(Raw; out Value; out Err): Trim; if starts with '=?base64?' and ends with '?=' (case-sensitive) strictly validate alphabet [A-Za-z0-9+/], '=' only as trailing padding, Length mod 4 = 0 (System.NetEncoding is lenient and must not be relied on), decode with TNetEncoding.Base64.DecodeStringToBytes + TEncoding.UTF8.GetString; else require every char in 0x20-0x7E or #9. ValidateStandardHeaders(Hints, Method, Params; out Err): Mcp-Method missing or Trim(value) <> Method (case-sensitive) => Err; for Method in ['tools/call','prompts/get'] Expected := params.name, for 'resources/read' Expected := params.uri: header missing / undecodable / decoded <> Expected => Err. ValidateParamHeaders(Hints, ToolBindings, Arguments): for each x-mcp-header binding (name, path, kind): body value absent or null => header must be ignored; present => header required, decode, compare (string exact; integer numeric equality allowing 42 vs 42.0; boolean 'true'/'false'); invalid chars => Err. Unknown Mcp-Param-* headers ignored. All Err results map to EMCPError.HeaderMismatch(-32020, HttpStatus 400) with the request id. Header names are looked up case-insensitively (Indy TIdHeaderList; add a test with 'mcp-method'). Run only when Hints.HasHeaderLayer and Ctx.Era = peModern and the message is a request (notification POSTs: validate Mcp-Method only if present). TMCPIdHTTPServer fills Hints from RequestInfo.RawHeaders (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, every header starting with 'Mcp-Param-').
architecture.rationale: streamable-http.mdx § Standard Request Headers ('These headers are REQUIRED for compliance'), § Value Encoding ('servers MUST decode an encoded Mcp-Name or Mcp-Param-{Name} value before comparing'), § Server Validation ('MUST reject requests where the values specified in the headers do not match ... MUST return HTTP status 400 Bad Request and MUST include a JSON-RPC error ... -32020'; failure conditions: required header missing, mismatch, invalid characters), § Case Sensitivity ('MUST use case-insensitive comparisons for header names. Header values ... are case-sensitive'). SEP-2243 test tables: 'mcp-method: tools/call' accept, 'Mcp-Method: TOOLS/CALL' reject, 'Mcp-Name:  foo ' accept, invalid Base64 padding => 400. Today no header other than Accept/Origin/Mcp-Session-Id is read (IdHTTPServer.pas:224, :277, :333-337). Ops rule: gateways route on the header, the server executes on the body; validation keeps both sources of truth equal without ever dispatching on a header.

architecture.change: HandleHTTPRequest order: ValidateOrigin (always; independent of CorsEnabled; allow absent Origin; deny 'null'; scheme+host case-insensitive, port exact or ':*' wildcard; built-in loopback set localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1] any port; 403 with body {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Origin not allowed"}} and Content-Type application/json) → optional Host allow-list (421) → health path (GET Settings.HealthPath, default '/healthz', 200 {"status":"ok","versions":[...]} for load-balancer probes; off when empty) → PRM well-known path when an authorizer is set → endpoint match (404) → OPTIONS (reflect Access-Control-Request-Headers; static list adds Authorization, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name; Allow-Methods 'POST, OPTIONS'; Expose-Headers 'Mcp-Session-Id, WWW-Authenticate'; Vary: Origin, Access-Control-Request-Headers; ContentLength 0) → Authorizer (401/403 with WWW-Authenticate; skipped for OPTIONS) → GET/DELETE => 405 + Allow: POST, OPTIONS, ContentLength 0 → POST: read body UTF-8; parse; if array and not 2025-03-26 batch mode => 400/-32600; if response object => 202 legacy / 400 -32600 modern; build Hints (headers, RemoteAddress = Context.Binding.PeerIP, AcceptsSse from all Accept header lines with media-type parsing and q<>0, Principal, NotificationSink lazily bound to an SSE writer); call ProcessRequestEx; if IsNotification => 202 with ContentLength := 0 and ContentText := '' (verify Indy emits no default HTML body; otherwise WriteHeader manually); if Deferred => streaming path (see SSE component); else ResponseNo := Res.HttpStatus, application/json body via TStringStream UTF-8; never set Mcp-Session-Id. Start: Bindings.Clear; add binding IP := Settings.BindAddress (default 127.0.0.1; 'localhost' mapped; add ::1 IPv6 binding when Settings.BindIPv6), Port; '0.0.0.0' logs a warning when AllowedOrigins='*' or no authorizer; MaxConnections := Settings.MaxConnections; keep DefaultPort for HandleQuerySSLPort. Remove GetNextEventID/FEventIDCounter and the 'id:' SSE lines; remove the Pos('"sessionId"') scraping (IdHTTPServer.pas:533-547) and all Mcp-Session-Id echoes (:289-291, :348-349, :485-486, :548-549). TLS: non-Taurus branch SSLVersions := [sslvTLSv1_2] (+1_3 where available); move {$DEFINE USE_TAURUS_TLS} to src/MCPServer.inc so consumers override without editing library source. Request/response bodies logged at Debug only through TLogger.RedactJson.
architecture.rationale: Origin: 'Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections ... If the Origin header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403' (streamable-http.mdx § Security & Endpoint; same MUST in 2025-11-25) but VerifyAndSetCORSHeaders exits when CorsEnabled=False or AllowedOrigins='*' (IdHTTPServer.pas:221-227) and matches exact strings so http://localhost:6274 is rejected (:236). Bind: 'servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1)' but Start sets only DefaultPort (:155-156) so Indy listens on all interfaces while Settings.Host is used only in a log line (:159). GET today returns a 200 JSON info body or an immediately-closed 200 SSE stream (:271-314), neither of which legacy allows ('MUST either return Content-Type: text/event-stream ... or else return HTTP 405', 2025-11-25 transports.mdx). 202 'with no body' (streamable-http.mdx § Sending Messages item 5). A health path outside the MCP endpoint keeps LB probes off the 405 path. The non-atomic Inc(FEventIDCounter) (:416-420) would break the legacy 'MUST be globally unique' rule, and ids are removed in 2026-07-28.

architecture.component: Real SSE streaming in Indy (request-scoped notifications, subscriptions/listen, disconnect = cancel, drain on Stop)
architecture.change: New unit MCPServer.SseWriter: TMCPSseWriter(Context: TIdContext; ResponseInfo) implementing IMCPNotificationSink and IMCPStreamHandle. Open: ContentType 'text/event-stream', CharSet utf-8, Cache-Control no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering no, ContentLength := -1, CloseConnection := True (HTTP/1.1 close-delimited body; chunked framing is the alternative if keep-alive of streamed responses is wanted), then ResponseInfo.WriteHeader; WriteEvent(Json) => IOHandler.Write('event: message'#10'data: ' + Json + #10#10, IndyTextEncoding_UTF8) inside a per-writer TCriticalSection; WriteComment => ': keep-alive'#10#10; IsConnected => IOHandler.CheckForDisconnect(False) then Connected; write exceptions (EIdConnClosedGracefully, EIdSocketError) mark the request cancelled (modern) or are logged (legacy). Execution model for ordinary requests: run the manager on the Indy worker thread with a buffering sink; if the client offered text/event-stream and the first notification arrives before completion, open the SSE stream, flush the buffer, keep writing; final response as last event, then return (stream closes: 'The final JSON-RPC response SHOULD terminate the stream'). If the client did not offer SSE, notifications are dropped and the JSON response is sent. A keep-alive/disconnect probe thread is not needed for short requests; long tools call Ctx.CheckCancelled which probes IsConnected at most every SseKeepAliveSeconds. subscriptions/listen (modern only; legacy => -32601): TMCPSubscriptionsManager (IMCPCapabilityManagerEx) validates params.notifications, computes the agreed subset (only types the server can actually emit — currently none unless a source is registered — and resourceSubscriptions filtered to existing URIs when resources.subscribe is advertised), registers TMCPSubscription {Id (cloned RequestId), Filter, Sink} in a TMonitor-guarded TMCPSubscriptionRegistry, returns a Deferred result. Transport loop: open SSE, write notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged with _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId first, then WaitFor(FShutdownEvent or subscription queue event, SseKeepAliveSeconds*1000): timeout => WriteComment; queued => write; disconnect => unregister, write nothing more; shutdown => write completion result {"resultType":"complete","_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId":id}} then close. All stream notifications carry _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId. Server-side notifications/cancelled is emitted only by the stdio teardown path (HTTP just closes after the completion result). Stop(): FShutdownEvent.SetEvent; wait up to Settings.ShutdownDrainSeconds (default 5) for open writers (TThreadList<TMCPSseWriter>) to finish; force Context.Connection.Disconnect on the rest; then FHTTPServer.Active := False. dpr: SIGTERM/CTRL_C set ShutdownEvent (already) and RunHTTPServer calls Stop (already) — drain semantics now live in Stop.
architecture.rationale: HandlePostRequestSSE computes the whole response then assigns ContentText once (IdHTTPServer.pas:488-501); Indy transmits after the handler returns, so nothing can be streamed and no disconnect can be observed (Context is not even passed down, :53-55). Spec: SSE stream MAY carry notifications/progress before the final response (streamable-http.mdx § Receiving Messages); 'Closing the SSE response stream MUST be treated by the server as cancellation ... MUST NOT send any further messages for it' (§ Cancellation); 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' SHOULD; keep-alive comment lines encouraged for subscriptions/listen; ack-first and subscriptionId tagging are MUSTs (subscriptions.mdx § Acknowledgment, § Receiving Notifications); graceful closure result SHOULD (§ Graceful Closure). Stop() today just sets Active := False (:162-170), which would block on long-lived handlers. Each open listen stream pins one Indy thread, hence MaxConnections exposure.

architecture.component: stdio transport: concurrent reader/worker/writer, cancellation, UTF-8, shutdown, dual-era probe
architecture.change: TMCPStdioTransport.Run rewritten: (a) I/O via THandleStream on fd 0/1 (POSIX) or GetStdHandle (Windows) with a manual UTF-8 line splitter on #10 (strip trailing #13) and byte writes of TEncoding.UTF8.GetBytes(Json + #10) — no TStreamWriter (BOM risk) and no Text I/O (ANSI code page on Windows); minimal fallback SetTextCodePage(Input/Output, CP_UTF8). (b) TMCPStdioWriter implements IMCPMessageWriter/IMCPNotificationSink with a TCriticalSection: one line per call, flush each time; a write failure (EPIPE) sets FTerminated. (c) Reader loop on the calling thread: notifications processed inline (cheap; notifications/cancelled => InflightRegistry.Cancel(idKey), reason logged at Info; malformed/unknown ignored); requests enqueued to a bounded TThreadPool (Settings.StdioMaxConcurrentRequests, default 4; 1 = sequential compatibility mode that still keeps the reader responsive). (d) TMCPInflightRegistry (TDictionary<string /*id JSON text*/, IMCPRequestContext> + lock) registered before dispatch, removed after the response is written; cancelled requests write no response; ReportProgress becomes a no-op once cancelled. (e) Hints.HasHeaderLayer=False; Hints.NegotiatedLegacyVersion is the single per-process field (interlocked string swap under a critical section) written by initialize; server/discover always answers. (f) Shutdown: EOF or Stop => stop accepting, drain in-flight with bounded wait (ShutdownDrainSeconds), for each open subscription write notifications/cancelled {requestId} then the completion result, flush, close stdout, return. dpr: in stdio mode do not install SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers (leave default terminate) or make the handler close fd 0 so the reader sees EOF; ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown only in DEBUG and never in stdio mode. (g) Create sets TLogger.UseStdErr := True and TLogger.StdoutReserved := True so no consumer can route console logs to stdout while a stdio transport exists. Outer except no longer writes an id:null -32603 to stdout; it logs and, for stdout failures, terminates.
architecture.rationale: Run is a synchronous Readln→ProcessRequest→Writeln loop (StdioTransport.pas:54-71): a notifications/cancelled or legacy ping cannot be read while a tool executes, and nothing can write a notification before a response. stdio.mdx: 'Servers SHOULD stop work on a cancelled request as soon as practical and MUST NOT send any further messages for it'; ping 'MUST respond promptly' (2025-11-25 ping.mdx); 'Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection' and 'clients may interleave unrelated requests on the same transport' (basic/index.mdx § Statelessness). Delphi Text I/O encodes with the system code page unless SetTextCodePage is called (nothing in the repo does), so non-ASCII JSON is not UTF-8 on Windows ('JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded', transports/index.mdx). The POSIX SignalHandler only sets an event (dpr:66-71) that RunStdioServer never waits on (dpr:114-141), so SIGTERM no longer terminates the process and the except block emits an uncorrelated {"id":null,"error":{"code":-32603}} (StdioTransport.pas:73-94), violating 'MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message' in spirit and 'Error responses MUST include the same ID as the request'.

architecture.change: TServerStatusResource: AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement on FRequestCount/FActiveConnections (Int64/Integer), read via AtomicCmpExchange; JSON field renamed activeRequests (or keep name, document). TMCPRegistry: class constructor creates the dictionaries eagerly (drop EnsureInitialized lazy checks); add FToolOrder/FResourceOrder/FPromptOrder TList<string> for deterministic registration order; document that all Register* must complete before Start/Run (registry is read-only afterwards; optional TMultiReadExclusiveWriteSynchronizer if runtime registration is ever wanted). TMCPManagerRegistry FManagers: read-only after Start (documented). TLogger already lock-protected (Logger.pas:165-198). TMCPJsonRpcProcessor stays field-free except registry/settings.
architecture.rationale: IsMultiThread is set (dpr:170) and Indy runs HandleHTTPRequest per connection thread; ConnectionOpened/IncrementRequestCount/ConnectionClosed use plain Inc/Dec (Resource.Server.pas:95-109) and are called per request (IdHTTPServer.pas:177-179, :206); with the new stdio worker pool the same paths run concurrently on stdio. 'A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently' (versioning.mdx) and 'Servers SHOULD return tools in a deterministic order' (tools.mdx § Capabilities; changelog minor change 3) — TDictionary iteration order (ToolsManager.pas:223; ResourcesManager.pas:107; Registration.pas:91-96) is not registration order.

architecture.component: Tools manager, tool result API, schema generator/serializer/validator
architecture.change: TMCPToolsManager: implements IMCPCapabilityManagerEx and IMCPCapabilityDeclaration ({listChanged:false}); ordered TList<IMCPTool>; ListTools(Params, Ctx): cursor via TMCPPagination, ListPageSize (0 = one page), modern ttlMs := Settings.ToolsListTtlMs (default 300000), cacheScope := 'public' unless an authorizer/OnBeforeCallTool filter is configured (then 'private'); same cacheScope on every page. CallTool: params.name missing/not string or arguments not object => EMCPError.InvalidParams (-32602, HTTP 200); unknown tool => EMCPError.InvalidParams('Unknown tool: x'); absent arguments => owned empty TJSONObject; execute via IMCPContextAwareTool when supported else IMCPTool.Execute; EMCPToolError => isError text; EMCPInputRequired => modern input_required result / legacy isError text; EMCPError => re-raise; other Exception => isError 'Error executing tool: ' (EAccessViolation/EOutOfMemory => -32603); OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool hooks. BuildToolCallResponse: TMCPToolResult first; TJSONObject => content:[{type:text,text:compact JSON}] + structuredContent; string => text (+ legacy 'Error:' prefix heuristic behind LegacyErrorPrefixDetection=True); TJSONArray => content; anything else => text via ToString; content is always present. CreateToolJSON: omit empty description; annotations/icons/_meta via IMCPToolMetadata; era shaping (outputSchema omitted for legacy when root type <> object; title/icons omitted for 2025-03-26). New unit MCPServer.Tool.Result: TMCPToolResult (AddText/AddImage/AddAudio/AddResourceLink/AddEmbeddedText/AddEmbeddedBlob/SetStructuredContent(+text fallback)/IsError/Meta; ToJSON(Era)); base64 via TBase64Encoding.Create(0,'') (no line breaks). TMCPToolBase/<T>/<T,R>: implement IMCPContextAwareTool (default forwards), IMCPToolMetadata (protected FAnnotations/FIcons/FMeta + SetReadOnlyHint etc.), new virtual 'function ExecuteWithContext(const Params: T; const Ctx: IMCPRequestContext): TMCPToolResult' whose default wraps ExecuteWithParams; tool-name validation ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$ (warn; StrictToolNames raises). Schema generator: tkInteger/tkInt64 => 'integer'; Boolean by TypeInfo; TDateTime => string/format date-time; recursive nested objects/arrays/sets/records with cycle guard; empty params class => additionalProperties:false; new attributes SchemaTitle/SchemaFormat/SchemaMinimum/SchemaMaximum/SchemaMinLength/SchemaMaxLength/SchemaPattern/SchemaDefault/SchemaName/SchemaHeader (x-mcp-header with registration-time validation: non-empty, RFC 9110 tchar, no CR/LF, case-insensitive unique, string/integer/boolean only, root properties chain only, Int64 refused). Serializer: raise on missing required properties and on type-kind mismatch (class var StrictMode=True); nil-safe DeserializeObject; ConvertValueToJson handles tkDynArray/TList<T>/tkSet/non-Boolean enums/nil objects. New MCPServer.Schema.Validator: subset validator (type, required, enum, const, properties, items, additionalProperties, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, pattern, nullable type arrays, same-document $ref only, depth cap) used for hand-written TMCPToolBase tools and elicitation responses.
architecture.rationale: tools.mdx § Error Handling: 'Unknown tool' and 'Malformed requests' are protocol errors returned as -32602, but CallTool returns an isError text (ToolsManager.pas:237-248). CallToolResult requires content in every revision, yet TMCPToolBase<T,R> results carry only structuredContent (:168-181). arguments is optional in CallToolRequestParams but a nil TJSONObject reaches 'for Pair in Json' (Serializer.pas:111) — a crash surfacing as an isError text. Integer maps to 'number' (Schema.Generator.pas:115) which forbids x-mcp-header on any Integer ('Parameters with type number are not permitted', streamable-http.mdx § Schema Extension) and lets LLMs send 3.5. 'Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs' (tools.mdx § Security Considerations) but missing required params silently keep defaults (Serializer.pas:130-131). ListToolsResult.required = [cacheScope, resultType, tools, ttlMs] in schema.json 2026-07-28. Stable cursors with a list fingerprint are stateless and therefore LB-safe.

architecture.component: Resources manager, blob/multi-part contents, templates, metadata, caching
architecture.change: TMCPResourcesManager: IMCPCapabilityManagerEx + IMCPCapabilityDeclaration ({subscribe:false, listChanged:false}); ordered list; ListResources(Params, Ctx) with pagination and modern ttlMs/cacheScope (ListTtlMs/ListCacheScope properties; sample dpr sets 300000/public; library default 0/private); ReadResource: Params nil / uri not string / empty => EMCPError.InvalidParams; URI syntax check (TMCPUriUtils.IsValidUri, RFC 3986 scheme) at RegisterResource and read; exact lookup, then first IMCPResourceTemplate whose Matches succeeds; not found => EMCPError.ResourceNotFound(uri, Era) (-32602 modern with data {uri}; -32002 legacy; HTTP 200 in both); read exceptions propagate as -32603 (no text swallowing); contents via IMCPResourceReader (TArray<TMCPResourceContents> with Text or Blob base64 single-line) else the legacy single-text path; modern ttlMs/cacheScope from IMCPCacheableResource (default 0/private); MRTR (EMCPInputRequired) modern only. ListResourceTemplates emits registered templates. TMCPResourceBase<T>: protected FTtlMs (0), FCacheScope (csPrivate), FTitle, FSize (-1), FAnnotations, FIcons, FMeta exposed through additive IMCPCacheableResource/IMCPResourceMetadata; TMCPBinaryResourceBase for bytes. TMCPResourceTemplateBase: RFC 6570 level 1/2 matching compiled to TRegEx with named groups; TMCPRegistry.RegisterResourceTemplate/RegisterPrompt. Built-ins: project://info/readme => 3600000/public; logs://recent and server://status => 0/private and registered only when Settings.ExposeDiagnosticsResources (default True for the standalone exe; documented for library use); drop the access-log side effect in TLogsRecentResource.GetResourceData.
architecture.rationale: resources.mdx § Error Handling: 'If the requested resource does not exist, servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 ... SHOULD return -32603 for internal errors ... MUST NOT return an empty contents array'; legacy revisions say 'Resource not found: -32002'. Today an unknown URI yields a 200 result whose text is 'Error: Resource not found' (ResourcesManager.pas:165-170), read exceptions are swallowed into text (:158-163) and Params is dereferenced without a nil check (:134). ReadResourceResult.required includes ttlMs/cacheScope/resultType (schema.json 2026-07-28). IMCPResource.Read returns a single string (Resource.Base.pas:17) so blob contents ('Binary data MUST be properly encoded') are impossible without an additive interface. TBase64Encoding default inserts CR/LF every 76 chars, which would corrupt blob.

architecture.change: New src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.Base: IMCPPrompt {Name, Title, Description, Arguments: TArray<TMCPPromptArgument>, Get(Arguments: TJSONObject; Messages: TMCPPromptMessages; Ctx): string}; TMCPPromptBase and generic TMCPPromptBase<T: class, constructor> deriving arguments from T's string properties via RTTI reusing [SchemaDescription]/[Optional]; TMCPPromptMessages fluent builder (AddText/AddImage/AddAudio/AddResourceLink/AddEmbeddedResource with role user|assistant; resource_link only for >= 2025-06-18). New src/Managers/MCPServer.PromptsManager: 'prompts/list' (ordered, paginated, modern ttlMs/cacheScope) and 'prompts/get' (-32602 unknown prompt with data {name}; -32602 missing required argument; arguments values must be strings; EMCPInputRequired => input_required (modern) / -32603 (legacy); no ttlMs/cacheScope on GetPromptResult); capability {listChanged:false}. New src/Managers/MCPServer.CompletionManager: 'completion/complete' with ref/prompt (name) and ref/resource (uriTemplate or exact uri) → IMCPCompletable.Complete(ArgumentName, Value, ContextArgs) → {completion:{values (max 100), total?, hasMore}} (no caching fields); capability {} only when registered; per-remote token bucket shared with the rate limiter. Sample src/Prompts/MCPServer.Prompt.SummarizeLogs embedding logs://recent. Register in dpr, dproj, build.bat search path (src\Prompts).
architecture.rationale: Prompts are MAY, but prompts/get is one of the three MRTR-capable methods (mrtr.mdx § Supported Requests) and the frozen conformance server sets for 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 include prompts-list, prompts-get-* and completion-complete, so a 100% score needs them. prompts.mdx: 'Servers that support prompts MUST declare the prompts capability'; 'Invalid prompt name: -32602; Missing required arguments: -32602'. Sharing pagination/caching/error plumbing with tools/resources keeps each capability small.

architecture.change: New MCPServer.Mrtr: TMCPInputRequests (AddElicitationForm(key, message, schema), AddElicitationUrl(key, message, url), deprecated AddSampling/AddRoots; key uniqueness enforced) ; EMCPInputRequired(InputRequests owned, RequestState) ; TMCPInputResponses wrapper over params.inputResponses (TryGetElicit(key, out TMCPElicitResult{Action accept|decline|cancel, Content}), malformed => -32602, unknown keys ignored). Managers (tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get only) catch EMCPInputRequired: modern => verify each inputRequests method against Ctx.ClientCapabilities (elicitation.form / elicitation.url; empty elicitation object == form; sampling(.tools); roots) else raise EMCPError.MissingRequiredClientCapability (-32021/400) with data.requiredCapabilities in schema shape; require at least one of inputRequests/requestState; emit {resultType:'input_required', inputRequests?, requestState?} with no ttlMs/cacheScope; legacy => isError text ('This tool requires interactive input (MCP 2026-07-28 elicitation); supply the information as arguments'). New MCPServer.Elicitation: TMCPElicitSchemaBuilder (flat primitive properties only), TMCPElicitation.Form/Url (url must be absolute; https required unless Settings.AllowInsecureElicitationUrls), TMCPElicitSchema.Validate for returned content. New MCPServer.RequestState (Core): TMCPRequestStateCodec with Keys {Kid, Bytes} loaded from [Security] RequestStateKey (base64, 32 bytes) and RequestStateKeyPrevious (rotation); if absent generate per process and TLogger.Warning('requestState will not verify on other instances'); Pack(Payload, Ctx, TtlSeconds default 600) => base64url(json{kid, sub: principal or '', exp, m: method, h: SHA-256 of tool name + canonical arguments (or uri/prompt name), n: 128-bit nonce, d: payload}) + '.' + base64url(HMAC-SHA256 via THashSHA2.GetHMACAsBytes); Open => constant-time MAC compare (hand-written), exp, m, h, sub checks; failure => EMCPError.InvalidParams('Invalid requestState') (never a -32000..-32019 code); optional IMCPRequestStateStore hook for single-use nonces. Tool authors: raise EMCPInputRequired from ExecuteWithContext; read Ctx.InputResponses/RequestState; helper Ctx.RequireClientCapability('elicitation.form').
architecture.rationale: mrtr.mdx: 'Servers MUST send server-to-client requests ... using the MRTR pattern'; 'MUST include at least one of inputRequests or requestState'; 'MUST NOT send an inputRequests that the client has not declared support for'; 'MUST treat requestState as an attacker-controlled input ... MUST protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and MUST reject state that fails verification'; SHOULD embed principal, TTL and originating-request identifier; 'MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult responses on any other client requests'. The server never initiates JSON-RPC requests today (stdio only writes responses; POST SSE emits exactly one event), so MRTR is the only path to elicitation. A shared key is the only way requestState survives load balancing without sticky sessions; legacy clients must never see resultType input_required ('Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated', 2025-06-18 lifecycle.mdx § Operation).

architecture.component: Pluggable HTTP authorization hook and principal
architecture.change: New MCPServer.Authorization (Core): IMCPPrincipal {Subject, Scopes, Claims (clone), no raw token}; TMCPAuthChallenge {Scheme='Bearer', ResourceMetadataUrl, Scope, Error, ErrorDescription}; TMCPAuthDecision=(adAllow, adUnauthorized, adForbidden, adBadRequest); IMCPAuthorizer {Authorize(BearerToken, HttpMethod, Path; out Principal; out Challenge): TMCPAuthDecision; HasScopes(Principal, Required): Boolean}. TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer (token list from [Auth] BearerTokens or a file; constant-time compare). TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer (abstract ValidateToken(Token; out Claims) — introspection RFC 7662 via System.Net.HttpClient provided; JWT verification left to a sample unit) with mandatory ExpectedAudience (aud must contain it; exp checked) and scope hierarchy ([Auth] ScopeHierarchy=files:admin>files:write>files:read). TMCPIdHTTPServer.Authorizer property: invoked after Origin/health/PRM/endpoint checks, not for OPTIONS; token read only from Authorization header ('Bearer ' case-insensitive), never from query; 401 => WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<url>"[, scope="..."] (offline_access filtered out with a warning); 403 => error="insufficient_scope", scope="...", resource_metadata; 400 malformed; id-less JSON-RPC error body. RFC 9728 document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource<Endpoint> from [Auth] ResourceUri, AuthorizationServers (https or loopback only), ScopesSupported, bearer_methods_supported:['header'], Cache-Control max-age=3600, served unauthenticated with CORS. [RequiresScope('a b')] attribute on tool classes checked in CallTool => EMCPHttpError 403 with the full required set. Principal flows into TMCPRequestContext (Ctx.Principal), into requestState (sub), and flips default cacheScope to private. Never wired into TMCPStdioTransport. Optional token bucket per RemoteAddress/principal ([Http] RateLimitPerMinute, 0=off) => 429 + Retry-After with an implementation error code outside -32768..-32000 (e.g. -31029) in the JSON-RPC body.
architecture.rationale: 'Servers SHOULD implement proper authentication for all connections' (streamable-http.mdx § Security & Endpoint) and 'Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification' (authorization/index.mdx). Once auth exists: 'MCP servers MUST implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC9728)', tokens 'MUST' be validated with audience binding, 'Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive a HTTP 401', 403 for insufficient scope, 'MUST NOT pass through the token' (authorization/index.mdx; security-considerations.mdx). README advertises --header Authorization (README.md:353) but nothing reads it; no code path sets WWW-Authenticate. Error-code policy: 'New error codes ... SHOULD be allocated outside the JSON-RPC reserved range' (basic/index.mdx § Error Codes).

architecture.change: TMCPSettings new keys (all with defaults; existing ini files keep loading): [Server] BindAddress=127.0.0.1, BindIPv6=0, MaxConnections=0, Instructions=, Title=, Description=, WebsiteUrl=, DiscoverTtlMs=3600000, EmitServerInfo=1, ExposeDiagnosticsResources=1, ShutdownDrainSeconds=5; [Protocol] SupportedLegacyVersions=2025-11-25,2025-06-18, AdvertiseLegacyInDiscover=0, LenientModernPing=0, Accept2025-03-26Batches=0, SortListsByName=0, ToolsListTtlMs=300000, ResourcesListTtlMs=300000, PromptsListTtlMs=300000, DefaultCacheScope=auto (public when no authorizer, else private); [Http] HealthPath=/healthz, SseKeepAliveSeconds=15, RateLimitPerMinute=0; [Stdio] MaxConcurrentRequests=4; [Security] AllowedOrigins=(defaults to CORS list + loopback any-port), AllowedHosts=, RequestStateKey=, RequestStateKeyPrevious=, RequestStateTtlSeconds=600; [Auth] Enabled=0, Mode=bearer|oauth, BearerTokens=, ResourceUri=, AuthorizationServers=, ScopesSupported=, RequiredScopes=, ScopeHierarchy=; [Logging] Level=Info, Format=text|json, LogBodies=0. TLogger: Format=json emits one JSON object per line on stderr with ts, level, msg, and structured fields taken from TMCPRequestContext.Current (era, protocolVersion, method, name, requestId, traceId/spanId parsed from traceparent, remoteIp, clientInfo.name, durationMs, status, errorCode); RedactJson blanks params._meta, requestState, inputResponses and keys matching (?i)token|secret|password|authorization; Authorization header values never logged; StdoutReserved guard. Access log line per request at Info (no bodies).
architecture.rationale: Operators need the era/bind/origin/key/TTL knobs without recompiling; TMCPSettings today has only Server/CORS/SSL (Settings.pas:83-95). Full request/response bodies are logged at Info (IdHTTPServer.pas:331, :555; StdioTransport.pas:62, :70) and re-exposed via logs://recent — once Authorization, requestState and elicitation answers exist that leaks secrets/PII ('Log messages MUST NOT contain credentials or secrets', logging.mdx § Security; token 'cached or logged on the server' is an explicit threat, security-considerations.mdx). W3C trace context in _meta is reserved for OpenTelemetry propagation (basic/index.mdx § _meta) and is the natural correlation key for stderr logs; stdio logging to stderr is the migration path the spec recommends (logging.mdx Warning).

architecture.change: tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj (DUnitX, console runner) with fixtures: Golden (request+hints => expected body/status per era, JSON files under tests/golden/{legacy-2025-06-18,legacy-2025-11-25,modern-2026-07-28}), EraDetection, Headers (SEP-2243 tables), Envelope, Errors, Pagination, Serializer/SchemaGenerator/Validator, RequestState (tamper/expiry/principal/rotation), Authorization (challenge builder, PRM, static bearer), Origin, Concurrency (TParallel 50 threads), Stdio framing (in-process pipe stream), IndyIntegration (start TMCPIdHTTPServer on port 0/ephemeral, THTTPClient for statuses/headers/202 body emptiness/SSE stream reads/405/Origin 403). scripts/run-conformance.ps1 and .sh (start exe, wait for /healthz, run npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --requirements 2026-07-28 --expected-failures ./conformance-baseline.yml, then --requirements 2025-11-25), scripts/inspector-smoke.ps1 (npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli --config ./ci-servers.json --server delphi-modern|delphi-legacy --method tools/list --format json; auth case expects exit code 3), ci-servers.json with protocolEra modern/legacy/auto, package.json pinning tool versions, .github/workflows/conformance.yml for a self-hosted Windows runner; build.bat reads DELPHI_PATH from env/rsvars and adds src\Prompts.
architecture.rationale: The repo has no tests or CI (only LICENSE, README.md, build.bat, generate-ssl-cert.bat, settings.ini.example, src). The processor becomes fully transport-independent through TMCPTransportHints, so every era/header/status rule is testable without Indy; the conformance suite is the community yardstick (docs/community/sdk-tiers.mdx: 100% for Tier 1) and its 2026-07-28 server set scores dns-rebinding-protection, caching, input-required-result-tampered-state and the prompts/completion scenarios this plan adds.

phases.name: Phase 0 — Groundwork: typed errors, constants, thread-safety, JSON-RPC hygiene, test scaffold
phases.goal: Remove the hazards every later phase would inherit (string-based error mapping, duplicated constants, races, id:null handling) and stand up the DUnitX harness before any wire behaviour changes.
steps: Create MCPServer.Errors (EMCPError with Code/Data/HttpStatus and factories; EMCPToolError; EMCPInputRequired placeholder) and move JSONRPC_* to MCPServer.Types with the -32020/-32021/-32022 additions; keep aliases in MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor; delete the duplicates in IdHTTPServer.pas:94-99.

In ProcessRequest: catch EMCPError before the generic handler and emit code + data; ExecuteMethodCall raises EMCPError.MethodNotFound; managers' 'not handled' branches raise EMCPError.MethodNotFound; remove Pos('not found') heuristic; add data parameter to CreateErrorResponse.

Structural validation: jsonrpc='2.0', method non-empty string, id tri-state (absent/valid/invalid) => -32600 with null id for null/bool/object/array/fractional ids; params non-object => -32602; Empty result => {}; string result => parsed object or {"value"} wrapper with warning; client-sent responses (no method, result/error present) ignored on stdio / 202 legacy HTTP.
AtomicIncrement/AtomicDecrement in TServerStatusResource; class constructor for TMCPRegistry dictionaries plus registration-order lists; document read-only-after-Start for registries.
Remove FEventIDCounter/GetNextEventID and 'id:' SSE lines (ids optional legacy, removed modern).
Stdio outer except: log only; terminate on stdout failure; no id:null -32603 on stdout.

Create tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj with fixtures for error mapping, id handling, constants, atomic counters (TParallel), and a golden-file runner skeleton (legacy-2025-06-18 expectations captured from the current build so Phase 1 can prove byte-identical legacy output).
deliverables: tests/ DUnitX project with ~40 tests and legacy golden baseline
risks: Golden baseline must be captured on a real Delphi build (no compiler in the analysis sandbox); block Phase 1 until it exists.
Changing 'Method [x] not found' text/code for custom-manager exceptions is visible to consumers who matched on the message.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Dual-era core: request context, era detection, server/discover, negotiation, modern envelope, status policy, stateless sessions
phases.goal: Make the processor serve 2026-07-28 statelessly next to 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 without changing a byte of legacy output; make HTTP requests routable to any instance.
steps: Add MCPServer.RequestContext (IMCPRequestContext, TMCPRequestContext + threadvar Current, TMCPTransportHints, TMCPProcessResult, IMCPNotificationSink) and TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx; keep ProcessRequest as wrapper; add Create(Registry, Settings) overload.

Implement BuildRequestContext era detection exactly as in compatStrategy (initialize => legacy; modern _meta => modern with -32022/-32602/logLevel checks; header-only rules deferred to Phase 2 but hint fields already present); legacy-only method gate (-32601) for modern requests; LenientModernPing setting.
Add IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityDeclaration, IMCPManagerEnumerator; processor dispatch prefers ExecuteMethodEx; TMCPManagerRegistry implements the enumerator.

TMCPCoreManager: server/discover (DiscoverResult with supportedVersions, capabilities from TMCPCapabilityBuilder, instructions, ttlMs, cacheScope, _meta.serverInfo); initialize negotiation (echo supported legacy version else 2025-11-25); legacy-shaped capabilities from the builder; remove sessionId/supportsProgress/supportsCancellation; delete FSessionID write; warn on deprecated client capabilities.

Envelope injection in the processor for modern results (resultType, serverInfo, default ttlMs 0/cacheScope private on the six cacheable methods) and status policy (-32020/-32021/-32022 => 400; -32602 from validation => 400; -32601 => 404 modern only; -32700/-32600 => 400; legacy otherwise 200).

Transports: TMCPIdHTTPServer passes Settings to the processor, sets ResponseNo := Res.HttpStatus, stops echoing/minting Mcp-Session-Id, removes sessionId scraping; TMCPStdioTransport gets a Settings overload and the NegotiatedLegacyVersion side-slot (initialize writes it, later legacy requests read it).

Settings: Instructions/Title/Description/WebsiteUrl/DiscoverTtlMs/EmitServerInfo/SupportedLegacyVersions/AdvertiseLegacyInDiscover/LenientModernPing; Resource.Project reports the version list; README version section.

Tests: era-detection matrix, discover happy path, initialize negotiation for 2025-03-26/06-18/11-25/garbage/2026-07-28, missing clientCapabilities => -32602/400, unknown version => -32022/400 with data, modern unknown method => 404 vs legacy 200, modern ping strict/lenient, envelope presence modern-only, legacy golden files unchanged except initialize (documented diff), 50-thread concurrent initialize + tools/call.
deliverables: golden fixtures for modern-2026-07-28 and legacy-2025-11-25
risks: Legacy initialize output changes (negotiated version may now be 2025-11-25 for clients asking for it; sessionId removed) — verify with Claude Code, Codex, Inspector legacy mode.
Threadvar Current must be cleared in finally on every path or a pooled stdio thread leaks context into the next request.
If supportedVersions lists legacy versions, modern clients may retry with _meta protocolVersion 2025-11-25 and get -32022 — decide before shipping (open decision).

phases.name: Phase 2 — HTTP transport hardening for gateways and load balancers
phases.goal: Make TMCPIdHTTPServer spec-exact on the wire: validated routable headers, correct statuses and empty 202 bodies, Origin/bind/CORS hygiene, 405 for GET/DELETE, notification dispatch, health endpoint, redacted structured logs.
steps: MCPServer.HttpHeaders (DecodeMcpHeaderValue strict Base64 sentinel, ValidateStandardHeaders) and hint population from RawHeaders; processor applies header rules for modern requests: MCP-Protocol-Version absent/mismatch => -32020/400; header names modern version but no _meta => -32602/400; legacy header unknown => 400/-32600.

Reorder HandleHTTPRequest: ValidateOrigin (always) → AllowedHosts → /healthz → endpoint 404 → OPTIONS (reflect requested headers, Vary) → GET/DELETE 405 + Allow → POST pipeline; 202/204 with ContentLength 0 (curl -i verification of Indy default body); notification dispatch to managers before 202; array bodies => 400/-32600 unless Accept2025-03-26Batches; client-sent response bodies => 400/-32600 modern, 202 legacy.
Accept parsing across all Accept lines with q-values; default application/json; SSE only when needed (Phase 5) — for now JSON always.
Bindings: BindAddress (default 127.0.0.1, ::1 optional), MaxConnections; warning on 0.0.0.0 without auth/allow-list.
TLS: TLS 1.2+ only in the OpenSSL-1.0.2 branch; USE_TAURUS_TLS moved to src/MCPServer.inc.
Logging: Format=json with request fields from TMCPRequestContext.Current (traceparent parsed), RedactJson, bodies only at Debug with LogBodies=1; access log line per request; never log Authorization.
Settings/ini/README: [Security] AllowedOrigins/AllowedHosts, [Http] HealthPath/SseKeepAliveSeconds, [Server] BindAddress/MaxConnections/ShutdownDrainSeconds, [Logging].

Tests: Origin 403 with CorsEnabled=0; loopback any-port accepted; header case-insensitivity, TOOLS/CALL rejected, whitespace trimmed, bad Base64 padding => 400/-32020; no header + no _meta served legacy; 202 has Content-Length: 0; GET/DELETE 405 with Allow; unknown legacy header => 400; Indy integration run with THTTPClient.
risks: Indy internals (default 202 body, TIdHeaderList case-insensitivity, Bindings behaviour, WWWAuthenticate property) are asserted from memory — verify on the Windows build with curl before finalising.
Binding to loopback by default breaks existing remote/container deployments that relied on 0.0.0.0 — CHANGELOG + explicit BindAddress.
Inspector web client does not send Mcp-Param-* (documented in inspector docs) — only standard headers are enforced in this phase; Mcp-Param-* enforcement (Phase 7) is gated on tools that opt in.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Tools and resources conformance: errors, envelopes, schemas, ordering, pagination, caching, blobs, metadata
phases.goal: Make tools/* and resources/* results schema-valid in both eras with deterministic, cacheable lists and correct error codes; keep TMCPToolBase/TMCPResourceBase consumers compiling.
steps: TMCPToolsManager: -32602 for unknown tool / malformed params (HTTP 200); empty-object arguments; content always present (text fallback for structuredContent); ordered list; cursor pagination with stateless fingerprinted cursors (-32602 on invalid); ListTtlMs/cacheScope policy (public unless authorizer/filter); OnBeforeCallTool/OnAfterCallTool; EMCPToolError; LegacyErrorPrefixDetection flag; era shaping of definitions/results.
MCPServer.Tool.Result + IMCPContextAwareTool + IMCPToolMetadata + ExecuteWithContext virtual on the three base classes; annotations/icons/_meta emission; tool-name validation.

Schema generator: integer, Boolean by TypeInfo, TDateTime format, recursive nested/array/set/record schemas, additionalProperties:false for empty classes, new attributes (SchemaTitle/Format/Minimum/Maximum/MinLength/MaxLength/Pattern/Default/Name). Serializer: StrictMode required/type enforcement, nil-safe, full ConvertValueToJson coverage. MCPServer.Schema.Validator for hand-written tools.

TMCPResourcesManager: -32602 modern (data.uri) / -32002 legacy for unknown URI; -32602 for missing uri/nil params; -32603 on read exception; URI validation at registration; IMCPResourceReader (blob/multi-part, single-line base64), IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceMetadata; optional fields omitted when empty; pagination + modern ttlMs/cacheScope on list/templates/read; ExposeDiagnosticsResources; drop the logs://recent access-log side effect.
Shared MCPServer.Pagination unit; SortListsByName option.

Tests: unknown tool => -32602/200 both eras; tools/call without arguments on get_time; required param missing => isError; integer schema; nested schema; structuredContent validates against outputSchema; list order stable across 100 calls; invalid cursor => -32602; resource not found code per era; blob round-trip; read exception => -32603; legacy golden files updated only where the spec requires (documented).
risks: Behaviour changes visible to legacy clients (unknown tool/resource now JSON-RPC errors; required params enforced) — spec-mandated but must be tested with Claude Code/Codex.
Schema text changes (integer, additionalProperties) break consumers' snapshot tests.
TValue.AsBoolean on non-Boolean enums (Serializer.pas:346-356) behaviour depends on RTL version — confirm on a real build.

phases.name: Phase 4 — stdio: concurrent reader/worker/writer, cancellation, progress, UTF-8, graceful shutdown
phases.goal: Make the stdio transport honour cancellation, legacy ping, interleaved modern requests and UTF-8, and exit promptly on EOF/SIGTERM.
steps: Replace Text I/O with THandleStream + UTF-8 line splitter and byte writes; TMCPStdioWriter (locked, flush per line) implementing IMCPMessageWriter/IMCPNotificationSink.

Reader thread + bounded worker pool (StdioMaxConcurrentRequests, default 4; 1 = sequential) + TMCPInflightRegistry; notifications/cancelled => cancel flag, reason logged, response suppressed; unknown/late cancels ignored.
ReportProgress on IMCPRequestContext (token cloned from params._meta.progressToken, monotonic, throttled, stops after completion/cancel) writing notifications/progress lines before the response.

Shutdown: EOF/Stop drains with bounded wait; dpr stops installing SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers in stdio mode (or closes fd 0 from the handler); ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown never in stdio/Release; TLogger.StdoutReserved guard; UseStdErr forced in Create.

Tests: in-process pipe harness feeding lines and reading stdout; non-ASCII echo round-trip; cancel mid-tool suppresses response; ping answered during a slow tool; 200 interleaved requests with MaxConcurrentRequests=4 all answered exactly once; EOF exits within drain timeout; Windows manual run with 'é'/emoji.
risks: Consumer tools now run on worker threads on stdio; non-thread-safe tools must set MaxConcurrentRequests=1 (documented).
Signal semantics differ across Linux/macOS/Windows; test SIGTERM escalation on Linux64 explicitly.
Closing fd 0 from a signal handler is platform-sensitive; the simpler default-terminate approach is preferred.

phases.name: Phase 5 — Real SSE streaming in Indy: request-scoped notifications, disconnect = cancel, subscriptions/listen, drain-aware Stop
phases.goal: Deliver progress over HTTP, treat client disconnect as cancellation (modern), keep long-lived listen streams alive through proxies, and shut down gracefully.
steps: MCPServer.SseWriter (WriteHeader + IOHandler writes, keep-alive comments, IsConnected probe, write-failure => cancelled in modern era, logged in legacy).

HandlePostRequest streaming model: buffering sink, lazy switch to text/event-stream on first notification when the client accepts SSE, final response as last event, close; JSON fallback when SSE not offered.

TMCPSubscriptionsManager + TMCPSubscriptionRegistry: subscriptions/listen (modern only) with ack-first, agreed-subset semantics, subscriptionId tagging, keep-alive loop, disconnect teardown, completion result on shutdown; stdio path writes notifications/cancelled then the completion result on EOF/Stop; IMCPSubscriptionSource hook for future list_changed/updated publishers (capabilities stay false until a source is registered).
Stop(): shutdown event, bounded drain, forced disconnect, then Active := False; MaxConnections documented for pinned threads.

Tests: Indy integration — SSE stream receives notifications/progress then the response; listen stream receives acknowledged first and ':' keep-alives; closing the client socket marks the context cancelled within one keep-alive interval; Stop with an open listen stream returns within ShutdownDrainSeconds and the client sees the completion result; legacy request disconnect is logged, not cancelled.
risks: Indy has no built-in chunked writer for handler-driven streaming; Connection: close is used for streamed responses — verify proxies (nginx/Cloudflare) keep the stream open and that X-Accel-Buffering: no is honoured.
Each open listen stream pins one Indy thread; a misbehaving client can exhaust MaxConnections — expose the limit and a per-remote cap.
Ack-then-empty-subset behaviour (nothing advertised) is legal but must not be mistaken for a bug by operators; log at Debug.

phases.name: Phase 6 — Prompts, completion, resource templates
phases.goal: Add the remaining MAY capabilities required for a 100% conformance score and for MRTR on prompts/get, sharing the pagination/caching/error plumbing.
steps: MCPServer.Prompt.Base (IMCPPrompt, TMCPPromptBase, TMCPPromptBase<T>, TMCPPromptMessages, TMCPPromptArgument) and TMCPRegistry.RegisterPrompt/GetPromptNames/CreatePrompt.

TMCPPromptsManager: prompts/list (ordered, paginated, modern ttlMs/cacheScope), prompts/get (-32602 unknown/missing args; content-block builders; era gating of resource_link/title/icons; no caching fields), capability {listChanged:false}.
TMCPResourceTemplateBase (RFC 6570 level 1/2 via TRegEx), RegisterResourceTemplate, templates/list emission, read-through matching; sample logs://{level}.
TMCPCompletionManager: completion/complete with ref/prompt and ref/resource, IMCPCompletable, values capped at 100 + hasMore, capability {} when registered.
dpr/dproj/build.bat/README updates; sample prompt embedding logs://recent.
Tests: prompts/list envelope per era; prompts/get unknown => -32602; missing required argument => -32602; embedded resource shape; template match/percent-decoding; completion capping.
risks: Templates change resources/read lookup semantics (exact then template) — ensure exact URIs still win and templates cannot shadow registered resources.
Completion is a disclosure vector; keep it off unless registered and rate-limited.

phases.name: Phase 7 — MRTR, elicitation, HMAC requestState, x-mcp-header mirroring
phases.goal: Expose the only sanctioned modern elicitation path to tool/resource/prompt authors, with integrity-protected state that survives load balancing, and finish header mirroring for custom parameters.
steps: MCPServer.Mrtr (TMCPInputRequests, EMCPInputRequired, TMCPInputResponses/TMCPElicitResult) and MCPServer.Elicitation (schema builder, Form/Url builders, response validation).

MCPServer.Crypto (CSPRNG: BCryptGenRandom / /dev/urandom / OpenSSL RAND_bytes when TaurusTLS loaded; constant-time compare; base64url) and MCPServer.RequestState codec (kid rotation, sub/exp/m/h/n, TTL, optional single-use store).

Managers catch EMCPInputRequired only in tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get: capability gating (-32021/400 with data.requiredCapabilities), at-least-one-field rule, modern input_required (no caching fields) vs legacy isError/-32603 conversion; processor treats a stray EMCPInputRequired as -32603.

IMCPRequestContext exposes InputResponses/RequestState/RequireClientCapability/HasClientCapability; TMCPToolBase<T>.ExecuteWithContext sample tool (elicit a confirmation, then complete) and README section 'Elicitation (MCP 2026-07-28)' with the dual-era caveat and security rules (no secrets via form mode; never pre-authenticated URLs).

x-mcp-header: [SchemaHeader('Region')] emission with registration-time constraint validation; transport-side ValidateParamHeaders against cached per-tool bindings (numeric/boolean comparison, null/absent => header not expected, missing/mismatch/invalid chars => -32020/400); Access-Control-Allow-Headers reflection already covers Mcp-Param-*.

Tests: tampered/expired/wrong-principal/wrong-method requestState => -32602; key rotation accepts previous kid; missing elicitation capability => -32021/400 with schema-shaped data; legacy client gets isError text; multi-round retry with accumulated state; Mcp-Param-* tables from SEP-2243; conformance scenarios input-required-result-* green.
risks: Per-process generated keys silently break MRTR behind a load balancer — the warning must be loud and the README explicit (RequestStateKeyRequired option).
Enforcing Mcp-Param-* rejects the Inspector web client for tools that opt into x-mcp-header (documented client limitation); CLI/TUI are fine.
Elicitation URL flows need user binding (principal) that only exists with Phase 8 authorization; document that URL mode without an authorizer is development-only.

phases.name: Phase 8 — Pluggable authorization hook, RFC 9728 metadata, scopes, rate limiting
phases.goal: Give HTTP deployments a spec-shaped authorization surface (bearer today, OAuth resource-server base for consumers) whose principal flows into tools, cacheScope and requestState; keep stdio untouched.
steps: MCPServer.Authorization (IMCPPrincipal, IMCPAuthorizer, TMCPStaticBearerAuthorizer, TMCPOAuthResourceServerAuthorizer with mandatory audience/expiry checks and RFC 7662 introspection helper; JWT verification as a sample unit only).

TMCPIdHTTPServer.Authorizer: 401/403/400 with WWW-Authenticate challenge builder (resource_metadata, scope, error=insufficient_scope; offline_access filtered), id-less JSON-RPC body, Expose-Headers WWW-Authenticate; PRM document at both well-known forms; RequiresScope attribute + hierarchy in CallTool via EMCPHttpError 403.

Principal into TMCPRequestContext; default cacheScope flips to private when an authorizer is set; requestState sub binding; README 'Security' section (no token passthrough; tools must obtain their own upstream credentials).
[Http] RateLimitPerMinute token bucket per remote/principal => 429 + Retry-After with an implementation code outside the JSON-RPC reserved range; [Auth] settings and dpr wiring.

Tests: static bearer accept/reject (constant-time), 401 challenge format, 403 insufficient_scope with hierarchy, PRM JSON shape and https enforcement, OPTIONS unauthenticated, stdio unaffected; Inspector CLI exit code 3 without token, success with --header.
risks: Server-side OAuth behaviour is not machine-scored by the conformance suite (its auth scenarios are client-leg) — acceptance is DUnitX + Inspector OAuth run against a test authorization server.
Bearer token lists in settings.ini are a foot-gun; prefer file/env and document.
2025-03-26 clients used a different (server-hosted AS) auth model — declared unsupported for authenticated deployments.

phases.name: Phase 9 — Conformance automation, Inspector matrix, docs, release
phases.goal: Prove both eras against official tooling, document the dual-era behaviour and the library extension points, and ship.
steps: scripts/run-conformance.{ps1,sh}: build Release Win64 (and Linux64 via PAServer), start exe, wait on /healthz, run the conformance CLI with --requirements 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25 against the same endpoint with conformance-baseline.yml (initially listing tasks-* and any disputed scenario); tier-check invocation documented.

Inspector smoke: ci-servers.json with delphi-modern/delphi-legacy/delphi-auto (HTTP and stdio entries); --cli --method tools/list, tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get, server/discover; manual web/TUI checks of Subscribe (acknowledged), per-request logLevel silence, MRTR rounds.

Manual client matrix: Claude Code (HTTP, legacy path today; re-test when it moves to 2026-07-28), Codex (stdio, legacy), Claude Desktop, VS Code; Windows 11 + Ubuntu 22.04; behind nginx (X-Accel-Buffering) and Cloudflare Tunnel (SSE keep-alive).

README rewrite: badge 2026-07-28 dual-era; 'Protocol versions and era detection' (HTTP + stdio tables, status mapping, curl examples per era); 'Using as a Library' additions (IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityDeclaration, EMCPError, TMCPRequestContext.Current, ExecuteWithContext, TMCPToolResult, prompts, elicitation, stdio checklist incl. UseStdErr and MaxConcurrentRequests); 'Operations' (BindAddress, AllowedOrigins, health path, keep-alives, MaxConnections, RequestStateKey sharing, JSON logging, redaction); 'Security'; 'Conformance testing'; CHANGELOG with every wire-level change.
CI: .github/workflows/conformance.yml for a self-hosted Windows runner (build.bat + DUnitX + conformance + Inspector smoke); nightly Linux64 job; build.bat env-driven DELPHI_PATH.
risks: Exact conformance CLI flags/version must be checked against the conformance repository README at execution time (not part of the spec clone).
No Delphi on GitHub-hosted runners — a self-hosted Windows runner is a prerequisite for CI.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequest(const RequestBody, SessionID: string): string
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Kept as a wrapper over ProcessRequestEx with default hints (transport unknown, no header layer); SessionID is ignored and documented as deprecated. Returned body may now carry a JSON array only when Accept2025-03-26Batches is enabled.

publicApiChanges.item: New TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx(Body; Hints: TMCPTransportHints): TMCPProcessResult and constructor overload Create(Registry; Settings)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Additive; Create(Registry) still compiles (no serverInfo/instructions emitted without settings).

publicApiChanges.item: JSONRPC_* constants moved from MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor/IdHTTPServer to MCPServer.Types; new MCP_ERROR_* and version constants
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Aliases with identical names re-exported from MCPServer.JsonRpcProcessor for one release; IdHTTPServer copies were implementation-private.

publicApiChanges.item: MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION ('2025-06-18')
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Kept with value unchanged and marked deprecated; new MCP_LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION / MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS / MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS added.

publicApiChanges.item: IMCPCapabilityManager, IMCPManagerRegistry, IMCPTool, IMCPResource (GUIDs and members)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Frozen. New optional interfaces (IMCPCapabilityManagerEx, IMCPCapabilityDeclaration, IMCPManagerEnumerator, IMCPContextAwareTool, IMCPToolMetadata, IMCPCacheableResource, IMCPResourceReader, IMCPResourceMetadata, IMCPResourceTemplate, IMCPCompletable, IMCPPrompt) are discovered with Supports().

publicApiChanges.item: Custom IMCPCapabilityManager implementations now receive notifications via ExecuteMethod (return ignored) and see resultType/_meta/ttlMs/cacheScope injected on modern results
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Injection only adds absent keys; managers that raise on unknown notification methods now produce a logged error instead of silence (documented).

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPCoreManager.SessionID property and initialize result shape (sessionId, supportsProgress, supportsCancellation removed; protocolVersion negotiated; instructions/title added)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Property retained (returns ''); removed keys are not defined by any ServerCapabilities/InitializeResult schema; wire change listed in CHANGELOG; legacy golden tests document the exact diff.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPToolsManager.CallTool: unknown tool / malformed params => JSON-RPC -32602 instead of isError text; required params enforced (TMCPSerializer.StrictMode)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Spec-mandated (tools.mdx § Error Handling). TMCPSerializer.StrictMode := False restores lenient deserialization; LegacyErrorPrefixDetection keeps the 'Error:' convention; CHANGELOG entry and test coverage with Claude Code/Codex.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPResourcesManager.ReadResource: unknown URI => -32602 (modern) / -32002 (legacy) error with data.uri; read exceptions => -32603; missing uri => -32602
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Spec-mandated; clients previously received a 200 text 'Error: Resource not found'. No compile impact; behaviour documented.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPToolBase / TMCPToolBase<T> / TMCPToolBase<T,R>: new virtual ExecuteWithContext(Params; Ctx): TMCPToolResult (default wraps ExecuteWithParams), new protected metadata fields, implements IMCPContextAwareTool/IMCPToolMetadata
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Existing overrides of ExecuteWithParams compile unchanged; Execute(Arguments) signature unchanged.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPResourceBase<T>: new protected fields FTtlMs/FCacheScope/FTitle/FSize/FAnnotations/FIcons/FMeta and additive interfaces
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Defaults (0/private/empty) emit nothing new for legacy and safe values for modern.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPSchemaGenerator output: Integer/Int64 => "integer", nested object/array detail, additionalProperties:false for empty param classes, new attributes
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Only the emitted JSON text changes; deserializer accepts the same inputs. Consumers with schema snapshot tests must update; noted in CHANGELOG.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPRegistry: duplicate RegisterTool now warns (raises when StrictToolNames=True); RegisterResource validates URI syntax (raises EArgumentException on invalid scheme); new RegisterPrompt/RegisterResourceTemplate
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Default remains permissive for names; invalid resource URIs fail fast at startup with a clear message (previously would never be readable via a conformant client anyway).

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPIdHTTPServer behaviour: binds BindAddress (default 127.0.0.1) instead of all interfaces; GET/DELETE => 405; Mcp-Session-Id never minted/echoed; SSE event ids dropped; Origin validated regardless of CorsEnabled; HTTP statuses 400/404/202-without-body; new properties Authorizer, BindAddress, MaxConnections; Stop drains streams
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Remote deployments must set [Server] BindAddress=0.0.0.0 explicitly; AllowedOrigins='*' remains the explicit opt-out (with warning); all listed in CHANGELOG with migration notes. Public methods Start/Stop and properties Port/Active/ManagerRegistry/CoreManager/Settings unchanged.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPStdioTransport: Create(Registry, CoreManager) kept; new Create(Registry, CoreManager, Settings); Run now uses a reader thread + worker pool (StdioMaxConcurrentRequests, default 4), forces TLogger.UseStdErr, writes UTF-8 LF-only lines; new Stop
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Tools are already executed concurrently on HTTP, so thread-safety is the existing contract; MaxConcurrentRequests=1 restores sequential dispatch. LF-only output is accepted by all known stdio clients.

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPSettings: many new properties/ini keys; existing properties unchanged
