publicApiChanges.mitigation: All reads use TIniFile defaults, so old settings.ini files keep loading; CreateDefaultSettingsFile writes the new sections.

publicApiChanges.item: TLogger: new Format (text|json), RedactJson, StdoutReserved; request/response bodies logged at Debug only
publicApiChanges.mitigation: API additive; operators who relied on Info-level body logging set [Logging] LogBodies=1 and Level=Debug.

publicApiChanges.item: TServerStatusResource counters become atomic; server://status and logs://recent registration gated by ExposeDiagnosticsResources (default True)
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Class API unchanged; JSON field names unchanged (activeConnections semantics documented as in-flight requests).

publicApiChanges.item: TMCPCapabilities / TMCPToolsCapability / TMCPInitializeResponse / TMCPPingResponse / TMCPTool / TMCPToolsResponse in MCPServer.Types
publicApiChanges.mitigation: Left in place for source compatibility, marked deprecated; TMCPToolsCapability gains ListChanged. Not used by the server.

plans.testing: 1. UNIT TESTS (DUnitX, tests/MCPServer.Tests.dproj, Win32/Win64/Linux64). The processor is transport-independent after Phase 1: every test drives TMCPJsonRpcProcessor.ProcessRequestEx(Body, Hints) against an in-memory TMCPManagerRegistry with the real managers plus stub tools/resources/prompts, asserting JSON (parsed and compared with a normaliser that ignores timestamps/uptime) and HttpStatus. Fixtures: EraDetection (initialize with _meta => legacy; modern _meta => modern; header-only modern => -32602/400; no header no _meta => legacy 2025-03-26 handling; unknown legacy header => 400/-32600; stdio side-slot), Discover (required members, ttlMs>=0, cacheScope, serverInfo), Negotiation (2025-03-26/06-18/11-25/garbage/2026-07-28 => expected protocolVersion), Envelope (modern-only resultType/serverInfo/ttlMs/cacheScope defaults; manager-provided values untouched; input_required untouched), Errors (every EMCPError factory; data shapes for -32021/-32022; status matrix per era; no -32000..-32099 outside defined codes), Headers (SEP-2243 tables: name case-insensitivity, TOOLS/CALL reject, whitespace trim, Base64 sentinel decode incl. UTF-8 and bad padding, Mcp-Name vs params.uri, Mcp-Param-* numeric/boolean/null/absent/missing), JsonRpcHygiene (id null/bool/fractional => -32600 null id; missing jsonrpc; params non-object; client-sent response ignored), Tools (unknown tool -32602; absent arguments; required/type strictness; integer schema; nested schema; structuredContent validates against outputSchema; content always present; annotations/icons; deterministic order over 100 calls; cursor validity and fingerprint mismatch), Resources (not found per era with data.uri; -32603 on read exception; blob single-line base64; templates matching; metadata omission), Prompts/Completion, Pagination, Serializer/SchemaGenerator/Validator, RequestState (tamper, expiry, principal, method/args digest, key rotation, single-use hook), Authorization (constant-time compare, challenge string, PRM JSON, scope hierarchy), Origin/Host matching, Concurrency (TParallel.For 50 threads mixing initialize/tools/call/server/discover; no AV, counters exact), Stdio framing (in-process pipe: UTF-8 round trip, LF-only, cancel suppresses response, ping during slow tool, 200 interleaved requests answered once, EOF drain). 2. GOLDEN PROTOCOL TESTS PER ERA: tests/golden/<era>/<case>.json holding request, hints and expected response/status; the legacy-2025-06-18 set is captured from the pre-upgrade build in Phase 0 and must stay identical except for the documented initialize diff; legacy-2025-11-25 and modern-2026-07-28 sets are hand-written from the spec examples (schema/2026-07-28/examples/*.json for DiscoverResult, HeaderMismatchError, UnsupportedProtocolVersionError, MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError, SubscriptionsAcknowledgedNotification, SubscriptionsListenResult). Optionally validate modern responses against schema/2026-07-28/schema.json with the DUnitX validator subset. 3. INDY INTEGRATION TESTS (same project, tag 'integration'): start TMCPIdHTTPServer on an ephemeral port with test settings; use System.Net.HttpClient to assert: 202 with Content-Length: 0 for notifications; 400/404 bodies; GET/DELETE 405 + Allow; Origin 403 with CorsEnabled=0; loopback any-port allowed; OPTIONS reflection; SSE stream ordering (progress events then response); listen stream ack-first and keep-alive comment within SseKeepAliveSeconds; closing the socket flips IsCancelled; Stop() completes within ShutdownDrainSeconds with the completion result delivered; 401/403 challenge headers; PRM document; /healthz. 4. OFFICIAL TOOLING: (a) MCP conformance CLI (repository modelcontextprotocol/conformance; SEP-2484 names `npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance`): run `server --url http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp --requirements 2026-07-28` and `--requirements 2025-11-25` against the same endpoint with an expected-failures baseline (tasks-* and disputed scenarios); target 100% on both; verify exact flags against the conformance README at execution time. Note that server-side auth is not scored (auth scenarios are client-leg). (b) MCP Inspector (docs/docs/2026-07-28/tools/inspector): config entries with protocolEra legacy/auto/modern for HTTP and stdio; CLI `--cli --config ci-servers.json --server <name> --method tools/list|tools/call|resources/read|prompts/get|server/discover --format json`; web/TUI manual checks of Subscribe (acknowledged badge), logLevel Off silence, MRTR rounds, mid-session 401/403 step-up, exit code 3 without a token. 5. MANUAL CLIENT MATRIX (each release): Claude Code over HTTP (legacy path; re-run when it adopts 2026-07-28), Codex over stdio (legacy; non-ASCII echo; cancel), Claude Desktop, VS Code Copilot; on Windows 11 and Ubuntu 22.04 (Linux64 build via PAServer); behind nginx and Cloudflare Tunnel for SSE keep-alive/no-buffering; two instances behind a round-robin proxy with shared RequestStateKey to prove stateless routing (initialize on instance A, tools/call on B, MRTR retry on B). 6. CI: self-hosted Windows runner executing build.bat Release Win64, the DUnitX console runner (unit + integration), the conformance script and the Inspector smoke; nightly Linux64 job; all wire-level changes require a golden-file update reviewed in the PR.
risks: Indy internals could not be verified in this sandbox (no Indy source; no Delphi compiler): default HTML body on empty 202/204, TIdHeaderList case-insensitive Values lookup, Bindings default 0.0.0.0, WriteHeader + IOHandler streaming with ContentLength -1/CloseConnection, TIdHTTPResponseInfo.WWWAuthenticate — each is a Phase 2/5 spike with curl -i / curl -N before finalising.

Era misdetection edge cases: a modern client that omits MCP-Protocol-Version but sends _meta gets -32020 (recognised modern error, fine); a legacy 2025-06-18 client that sends the header on initialize would still be treated legacy (rule 1 wins). Any change to the ordering of checks must keep every 4xx to a modern request carrying a recognised modern error body or dual-era clients fall back to initialize.

Legacy-visible behaviour changes (unknown tool/resource become JSON-RPC errors, required params enforced, initialize result shape, GET 405, loopback binding) are spec-driven but could surprise Claude Code/Codex users; mitigated by the golden legacy suite, StrictMode/LegacyErrorPrefixDetection flags and CHANGELOG.
Concurrency on stdio changes the execution model for consumer tools; non-reentrant tools need MaxConcurrentRequests=1. Shared state in TMCPRegistry/managers is assumed read-only after Start.

Streaming responses use Connection: close; HTTP keep-alive is lost for streamed requests only, and each open subscriptions/listen stream pins an Indy thread (MaxConnections must be sized; per-remote cap recommended).
requestState HMAC key must be shared across instances; a per-process key silently breaks MRTR retries behind a load balancer (warning logged; RequestStateKeyRequired option).

Removing sessions means legacy per-client state (logging/setLevel, initialized flag) cannot exist; acceptable because none is implemented, but revisit if legacy server-initiated features are ever wanted.
x-mcp-header enforcement rejects the Inspector web client for annotated tools (its browser SDK skips Mcp-Param-*); only opt-in tools are affected.
TLS 1.0/1.1 removal in the OpenSSL-1.0.2 branch and the .inc-based define move could break consumers who edited the library unit; documented.
Conformance CLI flags/versions and Inspector behaviour evolve; scripts pin versions and must be refreshed.

Delphi RTL differences (TValue.AsBoolean on enums, TBase64URLEncoding availability, threadvar with interface references requiring explicit nil in finally) must be confirmed on Delphi 12 during Phase 0/1.
Total effort (~56 senior-dev days) is an estimate from code reading; Phases 5 and 7 carry the most uncertainty.
openDecisions: Legacy sessions: never mint Mcp-Session-Id in either era (recommended default; spec MAY; keeps every request routable to any instance and removes the FSessionID race) vs. an HTTP-transport session store with 400/404 obligations.

2025-03-26 support: recommended default — accept its initialize but negotiate to 2025-11-25 (allowed by lifecycle 'MUST respond with another protocol version it supports'), do not list it in SupportedLegacyVersions, reject JSON-RPC batch arrays with 400/-32600; alternative is Accept2025-03-26Batches=1 with array processing.

server/discover supportedVersions content: recommended default ['2026-07-28'] only (versions servable via per-request _meta); AdvertiseLegacyInDiscover=1 appends legacy versions for informational purposes with a documented -32022 'Legacy versions require the initialize handshake' answer to _meta requests naming them.
BindAddress default: recommended 127.0.0.1 (spec SHOULD) with explicit 0.0.0.0 for containers/remote; alternative: derive from Settings.Host to avoid breaking current remote users.
AllowedOrigins='*' semantics: recommended keep as explicit opt-out with a startup warning; alternative: deprecate and require an explicit list.

HTTP status for application-level -32602 (unknown tool/resource, invalid cursor, unknown prompt): recommended 200 (only _meta/header failures mandate 400; a 400 with a non-modern error body would trigger legacy fallback in dual-era clients).
Modern 'ping': recommended strict -32601/404 (removed in 2026-07-28) with LenientModernPing=0; set to 1 for transitional clients.
stdio MaxConcurrentRequests default: recommended 4 (1 = sequential compatibility mode).
Disconnect = cancellation for legacy requests: recommended log-only (legacy SHOULD NOT interpret disconnect as cancel); modern always cancels.
SSE framing: recommended Connection: close per streamed response; alternative chunked transfer-encoding hand-framed to keep HTTP keep-alive.
Default cacheScope for lists: recommended 'auto' (public when no authorizer or filter hook, private otherwise); alternative always private.
RequestStateKey provisioning: recommended require a configured key when [Auth] Enabled=1 or RequestStateKeyRequired=1, else generate per process with a warning.

Diagnostics resources (logs://recent, server://status) registered by default: recommended keep for the standalone exe behind ExposeDiagnosticsResources=1, off by default for library builds (documented), and never when an authorizer is configured unless explicitly enabled.

Scope of MAY features in this release: recommended include prompts, completion and resource templates (needed for 100% conformance and MRTR on prompts/get); alternative ship Phases 0-5 first as 2.0 and 6-8 as 2.1.
CI strategy: recommended self-hosted Windows runner with build.bat + DUnitX + conformance; alternative manual release checklist until a runner exists.
JSON-RPC error code for rate limiting (429): recommended an implementation code outside -32768..-32000 (e.g. -31029) per basic/index.mdx guidance; alternative omit the JSON-RPC body on 429.
outOfScope: Acting as an OAuth authorization server (authorize/token/register endpoints, DCR, CIMD): the spec places AS implementation outside the MCP server role; the plan ships only the resource-server hook and RFC 9728 metadata. 2025-03-26 clients (server-hosted AS model) are served unauthenticated only.
JWT signature verification in core: no JOSE in the Delphi RTL; provided as a sample authorizer unit, core offers RFC 7662 introspection and the abstract ValidateToken.

Tasks extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks): optional, opt-in per request, requires a durable task store and background execution; rated XL and deferred (tasks-* scenarios go into the conformance baseline).

Deprecated features: logging capability / logging/setLevel / notifications/message emission, roots/list and sampling/createMessage (SEP-2577 'New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt'); only per-request logLevel validation and deprecation warnings are implemented; deprecated MRTR builders AddSampling/AddRoots are marked deprecated.
HTTP+SSE transport (2024-11-05) and SSE resumability/Last-Event-ID/event ids: deprecated or removed; not implemented.

Legacy server-initiated requests over SSE (elicitation/sampling for 2025-xx clients): would require session-scoped correlation and blocked Indy threads; legacy clients get an isError explanation instead.
Legacy standalone GET SSE stream and list_changed/updated delivery to legacy clients: capabilities stay false; GET answers 405 (allowed).
Unix domain socket / TCP variants of the stdio framing: possible later reuse of the line transport, not planned.
Full JSON Schema 2020-12 validator (network $ref, all composition keywords): a bounded subset with same-document $ref only; never dereferences network URIs (spec MUST NOT).
MCP Apps / other extensions and the extensions negotiation beyond advertising an empty-by-default map.
Multi-instance shared caches or persistent task/subscription state: the design is stateless by construction; subscriptions are per-connection and re-established by clients after restart (spec).

strengths: Era detection is exact and in one function: initialize always legacy (versioning.mdx §Compatibility Matrix 'An initialize request selects legacy semantics'), _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion'] string → modern, header-only rules gated on HasHeaderLayer (stdio.mdx §Request Metadata 'There is no header layer'); check ordering (-32020 header presence/mismatch before -32022 before -32602 clientCapabilities before logLevel -32602 before legacy-method gate -32601) matches streamable-http.mdx §Protocol Version Header + basic/index.mdx §_meta + logging.mdx §Error Handling.

Status policy is era-gated and exactly right: modern -32020/-32021/-32022/-32602(_meta) → 400 (schema.ts HeaderMismatchError/UnsupportedProtocolVersionError/MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError 'MUST be 400 Bad Request'; basic/index.mdx §_meta), -32601 → 404 (streamable-http.mdx §Protocol Version Header); legacy always 200 because 2025-11-25 transports.mdx §Session Management item 3 makes 404 mean 'session terminated'; legacy invalid header → 400 (2025-06-18 transports.mdx §Protocol Version Header 'MUST respond with 400').

Only plan with a dedicated Phase 0 golden capture from the CURRENT binary before any change, plus MaxConcurrentRequests=1 default on stdio (today's sequential order, StdioTransport.pas:54-71) while still draining stdin so notifications/cancelled and legacy ping (2025-11-25 ping.mdx 'MUST respond promptly') are observed.

Legacy-only heuristic preserved: Pos('not found') → -32601 (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215) kept for legacy-era requests only, removed for modern where -32601 → 404 would make a probing client misdetect the server as legacy (stdio.mdx §Backward Compatibility).

Strict Base64 sentinel decoding (alphabet/padding/Length mod 4 before TNetEncoding) matches SEP-2243 §Conformance Test Cases ('Invalid Base64 padding =?base64?SGVsbG8?= → 400 + HeaderMismatch'); case-insensitive names/case-sensitive values per streamable-http.mdx §Case Sensitivity.

MRTR gating is correct: EMCPInputRequired caught only in tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get (mrtr.mdx §Supported Requests 'MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult responses on any other client requests'), capability check → -32021/400 (mrtr.mdx server req. 7), at-least-one-field rule (req. 6), HMAC requestState with principal/TTL/digest (req. 4-5), legacy clients get isError text (2025-06-18 lifecycle.mdx §Operation 'Only use capabilities that were successfully negotiated').

Caching hints on exactly the six methods of caching.mdx §Cacheable Results with a processor safety net (ttlMs 0 / private) so third-party managers become schema-valid (schema.json 2026-07-28 ListToolsResult.required=[cacheScope,resultType,tools,ttlMs]).
Every phase lists closed gap ids and is independently shippable; Phase 1 alone makes a 2026-07-28 client work on stdio and HTTP happy path.
weaknesses: 2025-03-26 clients are effectively not served by default: initialize answers 2025-06-18 and batch arrays get -32600 unless [Protocol] LegacyBatch2025_03_26=1 (Phase 4); a genuine 2025-03-26 client 'SHOULD disconnect' when it does not support the answered version (2025-03-26 lifecycle.mdx §Version Negotiation) and 2025-03-26 basic/index.mdx §Batching says 'MUST support receiving JSON-RPC batches'. The task lists 2025-03-26 as a revision to keep serving.
x-mcp-header / Mcp-Param-* validation is declared out of scope; acceptable (MAY) but leaves the 'integer' schema fix as the only groundwork.

Strict required-parameter validation stays off (TMCPSerializer.StrictRequired=False) although tools.mdx §Security Considerations 'Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs' and the generated schema already advertises 'required' (Schema.Generator.pas:93-94); Serializer.pas:130-131 silently defaults.
42 days is optimistic for eight phases that include Indy SSE streaming, subscriptions/listen, MRTR, prompts/completion and an OAuth resource-server base.

Legacy 'byte-identical' promise is stronger than what Phase 3 delivers (registration-order lists, 'integer' schema type, additionalProperties:false all change legacy tools/list bytes; only 'error paths' are listed as golden updates).
factualErrors: Internal contradiction on legacy version negotiation: the Core-manager component says 'Negotiated := Requested if in MCP_SERVED_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS else MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION' (= '2025-11-25') and in the same sentence 'anything else (2025-03-26, 2026-07-28, garbage) answers 2025-06-18 exactly as today'; Phase 1 step 7 repeats 2025-06-18. Answering 2025-06-18 while 2025-11-25 is served contradicts 2025-11-25 lifecycle.mdx §Version Negotiation 'Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports. This SHOULD be the latest version supported by the server.'

server/discover 'params may be nil or contain only _meta': a nil params request lacks the required _meta fields and basic/index.mdx §_meta says 'A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602'; under the plan's own rule (no _meta → legacy) it would instead be dispatched to Discover() and return a DiscoverResult, which the spec does not permit.

MCP_LEGACY_ONLY_METHODS lists 'roots/list' (and 'notifications/initialized') as legacy client→server methods; roots/list is a server→client request in every legacy revision (2025-11-25 client/roots.mdx) and notifications/initialized is a notification that never gets a response, so gating them as 'methods' is meaningless (harmless).

CORS Access-Control-Allow-Methods advertises 'POST, GET, DELETE, OPTIONS' while the same phase makes GET/DELETE answer 405 (streamable-http.mdx §Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions) — inconsistent, harmless.
Bookkeeping: GAP-BP-20 is listed as closed in both Phase 1 and Phase 7.

strengths: Only plan that serves all three legacy revisions named in the task by default: MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS includes 2025-03-26, initialize echoes it, and JSON-RPC batch arrays are processed element-by-element for legacy requests at 2025-03-26 (2025-03-26 basic/index.mdx §Batching 'MUST support receiving JSON-RPC batches'), while arrays are -32600 (400) in the modern era (streamable-http.mdx §Sending Messages item 4 'MUST be a single JSON-RPC request or notification').

Version fallback follows the SHOULD: unsupported requested version → MCP_LATEST_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSION '2025-11-25' (2025-11-25 lifecycle.mdx §Version Negotiation); LegacyEnabled=False makes initialize fail with a message naming supported versions (versioning.mdx 'SHOULD name the protocol versions it supports in any error it returns to an initialize request').

Eight-stage pipeline puts every modern MUST at one place: TMCPRequestId tri-state (basic/index.mdx §Requests 'the ID MUST NOT be null'), resultType decoration (basic/index.mdx §Result Responses), safety-net ttlMs/cacheScope for the six caching.mdx methods, status mapping identical to the spec (400 for -32020/-32021/-32022/_meta -32602, 404 for -32601, legacy 200).

x-mcp-header is implemented (SchemaHeader attribute + IMCPHeaderBindingSource + Mcp-Param-* numeric/boolean comparison, null/absent → header not expected) exactly per streamable-http.mdx §Server Behavior for Custom Headers table and §Schema Extension constraints; SEP-2243 §Conformance Test Cases edge tables become unit tests.
Strict input validation on by default (TMCPSerializer required/type enforcement) honours tools.mdx §Security Considerations 'Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs'.

Correct subscriptions/listen semantics: ack-first per subscription id, subscriptionId on every notification, graceful-closure result with required _meta.subscriptionId (schema.ts SubscriptionsListenResultMetaObject), disconnect = cancellation only in the modern era (streamable-http.mdx §Cancellation vs 2025-06-18 transports.mdx line 114 'Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling').
Modern goldens validated against schema/2026-07-28/schema.json with an ajv Node script — the only compiler-free conformance check proposed.
weaknesses: Phase 1 is a big bang: 12 steps, 42 gap ids and the whole spine (context, pipeline, errors, era detection, discover, decoration, batches, capabilities) in one 7-day release; no separate Phase 0 safety-net release (legacy goldens are captured 'before Phase 1' but not shipped as their own release).

Default behaviour changes are larger than the other plans: TMCPStdioTransport runs consumer tools on worker threads by default (MaxConcurrentRequests=4; today strictly sequential, StdioTransport.pas:54-71), TMCPSerializer.StrictMode=True by default (previously silent defaults, Serializer.pas:130-131), the 'not found' → -32601 heuristic (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215) is removed in the legacy era too; several of these are labelled breaking:false.
Legacy 'byte-identical' assertion coexists with deliberate list-order and schema-text changes; the allow-list of permitted legacy diffs is not enumerated.
Phase 5 streaming (7 days) and Phase 1 (7 days) are the riskiest and both are estimated tightly; total 42 days optimistic.
factualErrors: 'GET and DELETE ⇒ 405 … permitted by 2025-11-25 transports.mdx §Listening item 3 and required for modern-only traffic': the modern text is a SHOULD, not a requirement — streamable-http.mdx §Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions: 'A server that supports only this revision … SHOULD respond as follows: HTTP GET or DELETE to the MCP endpoint: respond with 405'.

compatStrategy applies the '2025-03-26 if nothing else is known' default on stdio too ('else TMCPTransportSession.NegotiatedLegacyVersion … else 2025-03-26'); that assumption is an HTTP header rule (2025-06-18 transports.mdx §Protocol Version Header 'if the server does not receive an MCP-Protocol-Version header … SHOULD assume protocol version 2025-03-26') and has no basis on stdio, where it would enable batch arrays and drop resource_link for pre-initialize stdio requests.

Removal of the Pos('not found') heuristic for legacy requests (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:214-215) changes the code custom managers get for Exception('... not found') from -32601 to -32603, but publicApiChanges does not list it (only the risks section alludes to it).

Pipeline order in the Indy component puts 'Authorizer (phase 8)' before path/OPTIONS dispatch while Phase 8 says the authorizer is 'not [applied] to OPTIONS or the well-known path' — internally inconsistent ordering.

Phase 1 gapIdsClosed includes GAP-MRTR-04/05 (era gating of input_required) and GAP-HTTP-13 (batch handling) although MRTR does not exist until Phase 6 and the HTTP batch path is only wired in Phase 2 — bookkeeping ahead of implementation.

strengths: Richest and most concrete Delphi authoring surface: TMCPOptionalBool tri-state annotations, TMCPIcon, IMCPToolMetadata/IMCPToolContextAware, [ToolAnnotations]/[ToolIcon]/[RequiresScope]/[SchemaHeader] attributes, ExecuteWithParamsEx on both generic bases (returning TMCPToolResult / R), a worked 'deploy' example showing annotations, x-mcp-header, output schema, progress and elicitation without touching ExecuteWithParams or IMCPTool (Tool.Base.pas:11-25,44-77).

Phase 0 golden baseline plus an explicit 'legacy diff allow-list' and tests/README contractual list; MIGRATION.md enumerating every behaviour change with its escape hatch (LegacyNotFoundHeuristic, LenientModernPing, EndpointInfoPath, AllowedOrigins '*', BindAddress, StrictRequiredArguments, LegacyErrorPrefixDetection, MaxConcurrentRequests, EmitServerInfo).

Wire details correct: -32020/-32021/-32022/_meta -32602 → 400, -32601 → 404 modern only, application-level -32602 stays 200 with the right reasoning (streamable-http.mdx §Backward Compatibility: a 400 without a recognized modern error body pushes dual-era clients to initialize); sessions never minted (2025-11-25 transports.mdx §Session Management MAY; streamable-http.mdx 'do not mint or echo').

Era gating of optional fields by legacy revision is explicit (title/_meta ≥ 2025-06-18, icons ≥ 2025-11-25, resource_link absent in 2025-03-26 — 2025-06-18 changelog.mdx items 3 and 7), and legacy MRTR fallback (isError text / -32603) is defined.

x-mcp-header with registration-time constraint validation (RFC 9110 tchar, uniqueness, primitive types, root properties chain) per streamable-http.mdx §Schema Extension, plus IMCPRequestStateStore hook for single-use enforcement (mrtr.mdx Warning 'MUST enforce that invariant server-side').
Realistic effort (64 days) that matches the scope of ten phases.
weaknesses: Contradicts its own 'zero breaking changes' lens on stdio: MaxConcurrentRequests defaults to 4, so consumer tools that were strictly sequential (StdioTransport.pas:54-71) now run on worker threads unless the consumer sets 1.

Drops 2025-03-26 (answers 2025-11-25, batches → -32600) yet labels header-less legacy requests as '2025-03-26' — a request served under 2025-03-26 semantics MUST accept batches (2025-03-26 basic/index.mdx §Batching).
Keeps ValidateRequiredArguments=False by default, deferring the tools.mdx 'Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs' MUST to a later major.
Phase sizes are large (Phase 1 8d, Phase 2 7d, Phase 3 9d) and Phase 6 (MRTR on prompts/get) precedes Phase 7 (prompts manager).
factualErrors: Era rule 4 assigns '2025-03-26' to header-less legacy HTTP requests while MCP_LEGACY_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ('2025-11-25','2025-06-18') and ProcessRequestEx answers every TJSONArray with -32600 'Batching is not supported'; 2025-03-26 basic/index.mdx §Batching: 'MCP implementations MAY support sending JSON-RPC batches, but MUST support receiving JSON-RPC batches' — the label and the behaviour are inconsistent (should be documented as 'served with 2025-06-18 semantics').

Phase 2 test 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 1900-01-01 => 400/-32022 with data.supported' contradicts the plan's own rule for a header value in neither list ('legacy header sanity: unknown version => 400 + -32600 body'); -32022 only applies when the body carries modern _meta naming that version (streamable-http.mdx §Protocol Version Header), which the test does not state.

Phase 6 'integrate EMCPInputRequired handling into … TMCPPromptsManager.GetPrompt' references a manager that is only created in Phase 7 (prompts), so Phase 6 cannot be released as written for prompts/get.
publicApiChanges marks TMCPStdioTransport 'breaking: false' although default MaxConcurrentRequests=4 changes the execution model for every stdio consumer (today one thread, StdioTransport.pas:54-71).
Summary says 'Nine phases' but the plan lists ten (Phase 0–9); cosmetic.

A modern-only method (server/discover, subscriptions/listen) sent without _meta falls into the legacy branch of every plan's era rule and is answered -32601 (or, in plan A, even served); basic/index.mdx §_meta requires -32602 'A request missing any required field is malformed'. Every plan promises byte-identity yet none enumerates the complete allow-list of permitted legacy diffs; the golden normaliser will otherwise fail on Phase 3.

From OPERATIONS: stateless pagination cursors that embed a list fingerprint so a cursor issued by one instance is validated (and rejected with -32602 when the list changed) by another.
From ARCHITECTURE-FIRST: validate the modern golden files against schema/2026-07-28/schema.json with a small Node/ajv script where a Node toolchain exists, in addition to DUnitX equality checks.
commonBlindSpots: All four plans promise 'no failures on both frozen requirement sets' while declaring logging/setLevel + notifications/message, resources/subscribe|unsubscribe + notifications/resources/updated, and legacy server-initiated sampling/elicitation over the POST SSE stream out of scope. Per the gap report's scenario list, the 2025-11-25 required server set scores logging-set-level, tools-call-with-logging, tools-call-sampling, tools-call-elicitation, elicitation-sep1034-defaults, elicitation-sep1330-enums, resources-subscribe and resources-unsubscribe — 100% on the legacy set is unattainable with every plan's stated scope; the baseline must list them as expected failures or the scope must grow (legacy in-stream elicitation needs a process-wide pending-request table keyed by JSON-RPC id, feasible in Indy but blocks a worker thread per pending request).

Nobody read the conformance scenarios themselves (the repo is not cloned here), yet every plan defaults POST responses to application/json and only upgrades to SSE lazily. Scenarios such as server-sse-multiple-streams (in both required sets) and caching may assert SSE framing or specific ttlMs expectations; the 'JSON by default' choice is unverified against the scored checks.

Header-less legacy HTTP requests: a non-initialize POST without MCP-Protocol-Version is by definition a 2025-03-26 client (2025-06-18+ clients MUST send the header). Three plans (A: assume 2025-06-18; C, D: assume 2025-03-26 but reject batches by default) silently downgrade or contradict the assumed version; only B is internally consistent. No plan states the consequence: either advertise and implement 2025-03-26 (batching) or reject header-less non-initialize requests explicitly.

The 202 'no body' gap is live TODAY, not just a future risk: HandlePostRequest (IdHTTPServer.pas:343-352) and the 204 path (:524-528) set only ResponseNo, so Indy's WriteContent emits its default '202 Accepted' page; and the manual 'Connection: keep-alive' CustomHeaders at :286/:307/:482/:531 duplicate/contradict the Connection header Indy manages itself (and will contradict CloseConnection := True on SSE streams). No plan removes those custom Connection headers.

Shared RTL assumption stated as fact: 'non-ASCII responses are not UTF-8 on Windows'. TJSONAncestor.ToJSON (default options) escapes code points >127 as \uXXXX, so every response built via ToJSON (JsonRpcProcessor.pas:202) is ASCII-safe already; the real defect is Readln input decoding (StdioTransport.pas:57) plus raw E.Message text in error paths. The fix is the same, but the stated test expectation ('emoji echo response corrupted') is likely wrong.

cancellation.mdx L10-13 states transport-agnostically that a server MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing the subscriptions/listen id when it tears the stream down; all four plans resolve the tension with subscriptions.mdx by sending it on stdio only and just closing on HTTP, without flagging that this is an interpretation a conformance scenario could disagree with.

TMCPRegistry is mutable after managers are built: TServerStatusResource.SetNamePrefix (Resource.Server.pas:72-76) re-registers a URI at runtime, and TMCPToolsManager/TMCPResourcesManager snapshot the registry in their constructors (ToolsManager.pas:46-51, ResourcesManager.pas:41-46). None of the plans define what happens to registrations after Start (ignored silently today) or tie it to the listChanged/OnChanged design they introduce.

TMCPSettings.Create writes settings.ini next to the executable on first start (Settings.pas:69-73) and logs while doing so — in stdio mode launched from a read-only install dir or as a library this is a side effect every plan inherits; only D's health/observability work touches settings and none addresses ACreateFile defaults for embedded use.

The HTTP transport parses every body twice (IdHTTPServer.pas:341 and JsonRpcProcessor.pas:48/164); all plans keep ProcessRequestEx taking a string, so the double parse and the IsRequestOnlyNotificationsOrResponses pre-check remain separate from the processor's structural validation — two sources of truth for 'is this a notification'.

No plan bounds request body size, in-flight SSE streams per remote address, or handler execution time; with long-lived subscriptions/listen pinning one Indy thread each, a single client can exhaust MaxConnections (D exposes the setting but no per-remote cap; the streamable-http security section's 'proper authentication' SHOULD is the only mitigation offered).

All plans assume TIdHeaderList.Values is case-insensitive and that Indy runs exactly one connection per thread (true for the default TIdSchedulerOfThread, and thread reuse under TIdSchedulerOfThreadPool is safe only because they clear the threadvar in finally) — none verifies the scheduler assumption or Indy's handling of repeated Accept header lines, which RawHeaders.Values collapses to the first occurrence.
